items.title: The nightly pin is held for a formatter this repository forbids running
items.why:
rust-toolchain.toml pins this workspace to nightly, and its own comment gives one reason: rustfmt Allman brace_style option is unstable. The gate repeats that reason at its Show toolchain step.

That reason is spent. README.md and rustfmt.toml both record that cargo fmt cannot produce this workspace style and damages the tree when run, and that cargo fmt --check is deliberately not a gate step because a gate containing two contradictory checks can never be green. So the toolchain is pinned to nightly to enable an option belonging to a command nobody is allowed to run.

The cost is not theoretical and it is what makes this worth an item rather than a comment. Because every build here and in CI used nightly, no older compiler was ever pointed at this tree, which is exactly why rust-version could sit at 1.85 for as long as it did while being false. An unpinned reason is how P11-MSRV-UNCHECKED came to exist.

Measured under P11-MSRV-UNCHECKED at 3cd2261: the workspace compiles on stable 1.88.0, cargo check --workspace --all-targets, exit 0, zero errors. So the pin is not load-bearing for compilation.
items.done_when:
rust-toolchain.toml states a reason that is true of a command this repository permits, or the pin is removed.

Three answers and the record says which and why. Keep nightly for a reason other than rustfmt, and name it. Keep nightly for rustfmt and lift the ban on running it, which contradicts README and rustfmt.toml and is a larger decision than this item. Or drop to stable, which the measurement above shows compiles.

What the choice costs the losing side is stated. Dropping the pin changes the compiler every contributor and every gate step runs, and nightly-only behaviour that nobody has looked for would surface as a finding rather than as this item failing.

Anything the pin is silently buying is found by looking rather than assumed absent: a nightly-gated feature, a lint, or a dependency that resolves differently. The item reports what it found, including nothing.

items.title: Every public API change is committed in a snapshot and nothing has asked whether a record accompanied one
items.why:
Every check in this repository inspects one tree. Nothing compares a run against the runs before it, and a whole class of claim is only visible across revisions: a regression accumulated in small accepted steps, a finding corrected and reintroduced, a dependency removed by a decision and quietly returned, an API behaviour that changed with no corresponding record or version transition.

The last one is the case where the evidence already exists and is unused. tests/contract/surface holds a committed snapshot of every exported declaration per crate, and P9-PUBLIC-API made re-blessing it a deliberate act that rewrites and then fails. So every public API change in this workspace's history is recorded, in git, with the commit that made it - and nothing has ever asked whether a given one was accompanied by a governing record. The join exists and no query runs it.

The reason this is not simply a matter of writing that query is that the temporal subject is undecided. Nomos stores facts pinned to a workspace state - P8-PIN removed the workspace state from fact identity deliberately - and nothing says whether a fact from an earlier state is retained, how a series is addressed, or what identity makes two facts from different revisions the same fact. Without that, a comparison across revisions has no key, which is precisely the failure crates/contracts/nomos-contracts/src/identity.rs says the prototype died of: every comparative feature - diffing, history, trajectories, co-change, transformation tracking - turned out to be a join with no key.

That module doc names history as one of the five features that failed, and this is the item where it either gets a key or stays unavailable.
items.done_when:
A registered governing record states whether facts from prior revisions are retained, what addresses a series across revisions, and what identity makes two facts from different revisions comparable - the key the identity module says every comparative feature needs.

It says what a temporal claim is evidence of and what it is not, since a trend over accepted revisions is not the same kind of statement as a fact about the current tree, and reporting them identically would let a historical inference block a change on evidence about other changes.

It names the comparison the existing surface snapshots already permit - a public API change with no accompanying record - as the worked case, because it is the one where both sides are committed today and the only missing thing is the question.

Adding a governing record leaves both required projections stale, so both are re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones this commit publishes.

items.title: Two language providers here are two answers to one language, so nothing has tested whether facts compose across two
items.why:
crates/languages holds nomos-lang-rust and nomos-lang-rust-scan, and they are two providers of one language rather than two languages. The bands table in tests/contract/tests/boundaries.rs puts them at the same band deliberately and forbids an edge between crates at one band, with the reason stated in the file: two providers that shared a parser could not disagree.

That is the right rule for two answers to one question. It says nothing about two languages, and the questions worth asking there are all about the seam between them. Ownership compatibility across an FFI boundary. Agreement between a serialized producer and its consumer. Error propagation across a protocol. Threading assumptions that hold on one side and not the other. Version compatibility between components built separately.

None of those belongs to either language's tooling, and that is the structural point rather than a convenience argument: a Rust language server cannot see the Python process, a Python type checker cannot see the C library's ownership contract, and no single-language tool is wrong for failing to - the claim is about the join and neither side holds it.

Provider-neutral facts are what make the claim possible at all, and this repository has the mechanism and no second language to test it with. Whether canonical facts from two different language providers actually compose into one claim is unproven, and it is the same generalization test the capability architecture already faces from a second provider - P8-SECOND-PROVIDER proved two providers of one capability can disagree, which is the neighbouring property and not this one.
items.done_when:
A registered governing record states what a cross-language claim is, what facts it composes, and what has to be true of two providers for their facts to be comparable at all - since two providers normalizing into the same fact type is not by itself evidence that a claim spanning both means anything.

It names the claim families above and says which of them are reachable with syntactic facts and which require the resolution levels that have no producer yet, so the record is honest about what is available now.

It states what a cross-language check reports when one side has no provider, using Applicability rather than silence, because the common real case is a stack where exactly one language is covered.

Adding a governing record leaves both required projections stale, so both are re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones this commit publishes.

items.title: The editor surface is the second adapter and the first that does not exit, and the easy version makes rendered text a protocol
items.why:
An editor surface is the second adapter P10-SERVICE-SEAM is about, and it is the worst-case one on both counts that record raises. It duplicates platform choice, verb execution and rendering if the seam is not fixed first, and unlike the CLI it does not exit - so it is also the first surface that can accumulate the privileged state P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE exists to forbid.

It is worth deciding rather than deferring because the interesting content is already built and is currently unreachable. Finding, EvidenceClass, Guarantee, Applicability, the requirement registry, the record set, the work ledger and the projection profiles all exist. What none of them has is a way to be looked at from inside the code they are about. Hovering a symbol and being told the architecture component, the governing requirement, the record that decided it, the evidence behind it and the open item that touches it is not new analysis - it is a projection of state this repository already holds, onto a subject the editor already knows.

The same is true of the actions. Moving a dependency behind a canonical capability, creating a missing trace entry, replacing a leaked vendor type, opening a correction item - each is an engineering refactoring rather than a syntactic one, and each is an existing command with a subject the editor can supply.

The failure to avoid is the obvious first implementation: an adapter that shells out to the CLI and parses its rendered output. That makes the CLI's presentation a protocol, which is the third duplication in P10-SERVICE-SEAM's list arriving as an integration rather than as a copy, and it is very hard to undo once an editor depends on the text.
items.done_when:
A registered governing record states what an editor surface is in this architecture: which canonical services it consumes, that it consumes them as services rather than by invoking and parsing a rendered surface, and that it holds no state the services cannot rebuild.

It states what a diagnostic carries beyond a message and a span - the finding, the rule, the governing requirement or record, the evidence class and guarantee, and the correction if one exists - since a diagnostic that carries only text is a linter's diagnostic and gives up everything this repository has that a linter does not.

It says which navigations and actions are in scope and which are explicitly not, with the negative half stated: this does not reimplement completion, type information or responsiveness that a language server already provides, and it composes with one rather than replacing it.

It cites OD-HOST-001 for the seam and OD-HOST-002 for the state rule rather than re-deciding either.

Adding a governing record leaves both required projections stale, so both are re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones this commit publishes.

Declined.reason: Depends on P10-SERVICE-SEAM (declined, superseded by Done P10-SERVICE-SEAM-2) and P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE (declined for the same reason, superseded by P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE-2). Re-authoring as P12-EDITOR-PROJECTION-2 against both actual successors so the dependency chain can resolve once P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE-2 finishes.

items.title: Three clippy findings are suppressed by a compatibility floor that is false, and the gate reddens the moment it is corrected
items.why:
clippy reads its MSRV from Cargo.toml rust-version, because clippy.toml sets no msrv key here. rust-version says 1.85, and clippy therefore withholds every suggestion that would require a newer language feature. collapsible_if is one of those: collapsing `if let Some(x) = e { if cond { } }` needs a let chain, which stabilized in 1.88.

So three findings are currently invisible, and they become errors under the gate `-D warnings` the moment the floor is corrected to the number that actually compiles this workspace:

  crates/spec/nomos-spec-ingest/src/restore/extract.rs:139
  tests/contract/src/gates.rs:384
  tests/contract/src/gates.rs:760

Measured as a control rather than inferred, in a detached worktree at 3cd2261 with one variable changed and nothing else: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings exits 0 with rust-version 1.85 and exits 101 with rust-version 1.88, reporting exactly those three sites.

This is why P11-MSRV-UNCHECKED could not land its own measurement. It reserves Cargo.toml and the workflow, and neither of these two files, and a floor correction that reddens the gate is not a correction anybody can commit.

Hazard for whoever takes this. extract.rs is under a live peer uncommitted module-split edits as of this writing and still carries the pattern at the same site. Territory is declared and not enforced, so claiming this item does not stop that work; check git status before touching that file and take gates.rs first if the peer is still in flight.
items.done_when:
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings exits 0 with rust-version set to 1.88, and the item reports that run rather than asserting it.

The floor itself is not changed here. Cargo.toml belongs to P11-MSRV-UNCHECKED and this item raises it only as a measurement, in a worktree, and reverts it. An item that lands the bump has done the other item work inside a territory it does not hold.

The three sites collapse into let chains, which is what clippy asks for and what the nine chains already in this workspace look like. Collapsing them is correct under the current declared floor too: nothing checks feature usage against rust-version, and the pinned nightly compiles either form.

Not closed by adding an allow attribute at the three sites. That converts a finding into a suppression and leaves the next author to discover the same class again, which is the shape P12-UNENFORCED-DECLARATION is open against.

items.title: A verification record says when it ran and never what it ran against, so still-verified and verified-against-something-else read the same
items.why:
OD-ANALYSIS-001 decides what identifies a fact, and the reasoning is that a key carrying the wrong thing defeats the reuse the key exists for. Nothing in this repository decides what identifies run evidence.

VerificationRecord in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/verification_record.rs carries argv, exit_code, output_tail, verified_at and gate. There is no revision, no tree digest and no reference to the territory the item reserved. So the ledger records that a predicate exited 0 at a wall-clock instant, and every reader has to supply the missing half themselves.

The consequence is not hypothetical and this board has it today. An item finished at unix N against a tree, then the tree moves under it -- a peer lands a module split, a record is amended, the item's own files are edited by the next item that reserves them -- and work show reports exactly what it reported before. 'Verified' and 'was verified once, against something else' are the same three words. That is OD-GATE-001's shape moved from a test that read nothing to a record that means nothing in particular: both report a pass while the thing the pass was about is absent.

It is also the gap under the gate half. Since OD-LEDGER-003 the record carries the gate's own outcome, because 'this item was verified' is only true of a tree the gate also accepted. That reasoning is exactly right and it stops one step short: a tree is what both halves are about, and neither half names one.

The precedent for how to add it is in the same struct. gate is Option<GateOutcome> with serde default, None on every record written before the gate was part of finishing, and the doc comment says that is a fact about those records and is left visible rather than backfilled. A revision field is the same shape and should be the same shape deliberately.

HAZARD, and it is the reason this item is larger than its diff. VerificationRecord is serde deny_unknown_fields, so a binary built before the new field refuses to read a ledger containing it -- that refusal is P10-STALE-WRITER working as designed. SCHEMA_VERSION at crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/store.rs:52 must rise from 3 to 4 in the same commit as the code, and every live session's copied binary starts refusing every work verb until it is rebuilt. ea3c167 did this accidentally and left dev unusable. Do it in one commit, and say so where sessions will read it.
items.done_when:
A verification record names what it was verified against, and work show can distinguish a record that still describes this tree from one that does not.

What identifies a tree is the decision, and it is not obvious. A git revision is cheap, is what CI and every reader already speaks, and is wrong in the one case that matters most here -- a dirty working tree, which is the normal state of this repository and the state most finishing happens in. A digest over the item's own territory is honest about what the predicate could have been affected by and says nothing about the rest of the workspace, which is where a peer's breakage comes from. A whole-tree digest is the strongest and the most expensive, and it changes on every untracked scratch file unless it is scoped.

The record says which, and says what the losing options give up rather than only what the winner buys. A record that only reports the field was added has not answered this.

Staleness is reported, not merely storable. A field nothing reads is a comment with a serializer: work show must say something different about a record whose revision no longer matches, and the item shows that output for both cases.

SCHEMA_VERSION rises to 4 in the same commit as the code that understands it, and the migration is stated where a session running an older copied binary will meet it -- the refusal already names the two versions.

Records written before the field are None and stay None. Backfilling a revision nobody measured would manufacture the exact claim this item exists to stop.

Not closed by storing the revision and leaving every existing caller printing the same sentence.

items.title: The report that decides what a run found never reads the enum whose first sentence is that unknown is not pass
items.why:
Applicability in crates/contracts/nomos-contracts/src/applicability.rs opens by calling itself the load-bearing expression of the product's first principle: unknown is not pass. A region no analyzer could read is not healthy, it is unknown, and the two must never render the same. Eleven variants carry that distinction and 189 occurrences across 30 files consume them - the registry, the analysis reader, the rules mirror, coverage and coverage_gap in the kernel.

crates/host/nomos-cli/src/check/report.rs contains the word zero times.

The report is not naive about the general problem, which is what makes the gap specific rather than an oversight. Its Examined struct carries two denominators deliberately, and its doc comment gives the reason: 0 findings over 400 files and 0 findings over 400 files none of which produced a fact are different claims, the second is a broken run, and the prototype reported the first shape for a check that had walked nothing. So the argument that a bare finding count is a lie has already been made here and acted on - and it stops one step short of the variant set that exists to finish it.

The consequence is that the surface a person reads can distinguish a clean tree from a broken walk and cannot distinguish a clean tree from an unexamined one. A subject whose provider is missing, whose toolchain is absent, whose parse failed or which needs a model contributes nothing to either denominator and produces no line, so it is reported by silence - which is exactly the rendering the enum's first sentence forbids.

It is worth doing now rather than with the next capability because every capability added from here makes the silence larger, and because the vocabulary needs no design work: the answer is to read a type that is already exhaustive, already has no Default, and already refuses to give a consumer a lenient arm.
items.done_when:
The check report carries applicability, so a run says what it could not judge and why, not only what it found and over how much.

A subject that produced no judgment appears in the report with its Applicability variant rather than by omission. Grouping is by whatever makes the answer readable at scale - per capability, per language, per variant - and the record says which, but a subject falling into MissingCapability, DependencyUnavailable, ProviderUnavailable, Unparseable, AnalysisFailed or AgentRequired must not be indistinguishable from a subject that was judged clean.

The run carries a roll-up verdict saying whether the claim is complete, and the exit code contract states what an incomplete claim exits with. This is the decision rather than the rendering: complete-and-clean and incomplete-and-nothing-found currently share an exit code, and whether they should stop sharing one is what the record settles.

Examined grows or is replaced. Two integer denominators cannot express eleven reasons, and adding a third integer is the shape this item exists to stop.

The negative control is the one that matters: a test in which a provider is absent must fail if the report renders that subject the same as a clean one.

items.title: The numbers in this workspace say what they are and not what they mean
items.why: A number written into an expression says what the value is and never what it means, and the second place the same number is typed is the place that will not be updated when it changes. The clean-file phase of the code-standards suite reads 187 of them in this workspace's production code: SQL column ordinals threaded from a SELECT list to a row reader lines away, exit codes spelled as bare discriminants, and real thresholds -- an hour in seconds, a digest's hexadecimal length, an excerpt width -- that no reader can recognize on sight.
items.done_when:
check-literals from the code-standards suite reports no finding in this workspace's production code, and the other five checks of its rust clean-file phase -- nested-call, nesting-depth, function-size, parameter-count, intrafile-duplication -- stay at no findings. Every positional column access reads through a named ordinal that sits beside the query it indexes, so the SELECT list and its reader can no longer drift apart silently. cargo test --workspace stays green and the gate's lint step stays clean.

Findings inside inline #[cfg(test)] modules are out of scope: the check's own --include-tests flag is off by default and only governs tests/ directories, so it cannot see that an inline module is test code.

Declined.reason: Ending the item, not just the claim: its 28-file territory and workspace-phrased done_when no longer describe live reality (see the abandonment just recorded for the fresh measurement). The part of it that was real -- 9 findings across spec/exit_code.rs and check/exit_code.rs are a documented cross-binary ExitCode enum's own discriminants, which check-literals' Rust front end cannot recognize as already named (rust_Literal_Context has no case for NODE_CONST_ITEM/NODE_STATIC_ITEM on an enum variant) -- is carried forward as a permanent, stated exception in OD-GATE-013 rather than left as an undocumented gap somebody keeps re-discovering. Reissued as P12-NAMED-LITERALS-2 with a territory sized to what a claimant can actually close: the three ExitCode-shaped files the exception covers plus the record and its registration. identity.rs needs nothing further (already fixed, re-verified). The newly discovered debt outside the old territory -- request.rs's splitn field count, check/report.rs's private array-length, and store/write.rs's SQL column ordinals plus its own unrelated function-size/parameter-count findings -- is left unclaimed on the board rather than folded into this item's reissue.

abandoned.reason:
Claim released, not the item. The session holding this committed its first pass at 77906ff and did not return; check-literals still reads 151 findings in this workspace, so the done_when is unmet and the item stays on the board for whoever takes it next.

The claim is released because its territory -- 28 files across the spec band, the CLI and substrate -- is most of what the decompose-file sweep must split, and a lease running to a wall-clock hour is not evidence a session is alive behind it. Confirmed stale with the operator before releasing.

check-literals over the 28-file territory now reports 0 findings in 26 of 28 files (test-code findings excluded per done_when; read.rs/rows.rs/table.rs/snapshot.rs findings all sit inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests). identity.rs's one production finding is fixed and committed (408499a): Digest128's tuple field now spells its length as Digest128::BYTE_LENGTH, an already-public const, instead of a bare 16; nomos-contracts surface snapshot re-blessed and public_surface suite green. The remaining 9 findings -- spec/exit_code.rs (6) and check/exit_code.rs (3) -- are ExitCode enum discriminants that already carry a doc comment per variant explaining the cross-binary meaning of each number. check-literals' rust front-end has a documented gap (rust_Literal_Context has no case for NODE_CONST_ITEM/NODE_STATIC_ITEM discriminants, confirmed in team notes and by 77906ff's prior session deliberately leaving these exact two files untouched for the same reason). Naming a const per discriminant would only mirror the variant name the enum already provides, which is the anti-pattern the checker's own --help text warns against ('the name is exactly what a tool cannot supply'). A suppressions.json waiver does not fit either: it needs standards.json plus a bounded expiry, and this is a permanent considered decision, not temporary debt. items.title: A file here can hold twenty-four types, so its name stops saying what is in it
items.why:
A file is the unit a reader navigates by, and this workspace has files whose names no longer say what they hold. crates/spec/nomos-spec-bundle/src/model.rs declares twenty-four public types; crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/src/authoring.rs declares eleven across 1789 lines; crates/spec/nomos-spec-model/src/submission.rs declares nine across 973. A reader looking for Blob, StagedEdit or Severity cannot find it by filename, an import pulls in twenty-three types it did not want, and no reviewer can hold the surface of such a file in one reading.

The decompose-file phase of the code-standards suite reads three of its five checks red against this workspace: check-one-public-type 66 findings across 19 files, check-responsibility-extraction 16 across 12, check-file-size 12 across 12. The other two, check-class-size and check-extractable-subset, are already clean, so the defect is file boundaries and not type cohesion. The three overlap by construction: the same twenty-four-type file is one finding for its type count, one for its public surface breadth, and one for its length.

Two earlier sweeps did this for the substrate band -- 43c5a63..ef1c93f, Give
items.done_when:

Every type the split moves keeps the path it is imported by, so no caller outside its crate changes: a file that becomes a directory re-exports its parts from the module that replaced it. The three public-surface snapshots under tests/contract/surface stay byte-identical unless a name genuinely left the surface, and any that changes is committed with the change that caused it.

A file kept whole against the rule carries a reasoned marker naming the coupling that keeps it together, not a bare one, and the reason names the algorithm or the locality rather than restating the size.

cargo test for every crate the split reaches stays green, and the gate lint step stays clean. Findings inside inline #[cfg(test)] modules and under tests/ are out of scope: the checks skip test sources by default and this item does not turn that off.

Its harness discharges a cross-environment scope claim by spawning the same test binary with --exact, and --exact matches the module path, so every name Test_Name_For returns is now domains::Test_... A bare name selects no test: the child exits zero having printed nothing, and the failure arrives as a missing digest line, which names the wrong cause. Any future split of a suite that spawns itself has the same trap. Confirmed by running the CrossBinary domain with --nocapture and watching the child's digest come back.

SECOND, AND IT DECIDES HOW THE REST OF THIS ITEM GETS DONE: the corpus-gate derivation is scoped to one file, and it says so itself at tests/contract/src/gates.rs -- A

items.title: nomos-corrections: CorrectionCandidate, CorrectionPlan, and the deterministic stage-preview-commit-rollback door the domain table already prices
items.why: The determinism domain table in nomos-contracts (crates/contracts/nomos-contracts/src/determinism.rs line 38) already prices a Correction planning and staging row as StateTemporal / CrossRun / BitIdentical, and tests/contract/tests/determinism_declarations.rs records it UNOCCUPIED on purpose: nothing in this tree plans or stages a correction. nomos-rules judges and reports; the step that would apply a fix does not exist, so there is no domain to declare and a declaration would be a promise about code nobody has written. A repository-wide search confirms it: no nomos-corrections crate, no CorrectionCandidate, CorrectionPlan or ChangeSet type anywhere, and the word correction appears only in two doc comments describing future intent (nomos-contracts finding display_label, and nomos-model artifact_kind GeneratedOutput). The project's own planning document (advisory only, per D-132) puts this capability directly after gate semantics and states plainly: start deterministic, and do not add an agent executor until the mutation and validation contract is solid. The ledger already carries P11 items that build an agent-coordination harness for sessions working this repository; that is a different concern from an AgentExecutor that would apply a correction inside an end user's repository, and building the second before the first deterministic contract exists would be building on an unproven mutation path.
items.done_when: A nomos-corrections crate occupies the Correction planning and staging row of the domain table: it exposes CorrectionCandidate, CorrectionPlan and ChangeSet types and a deterministic preview, stage, validate, commit and rollback lifecycle over a workspace change, with no dependency on an agent executor or model backend. The UNOCCUPIED entry naming that row is removed from tests/contract/tests/determinism_declarations.rs, the crate's own tests pass, and its public surface is snapshotted at tests/contract/surface/nomos-corrections.txt.

items.title: A dependency that will never finish is reported as a queue, so an agent is told to wait for declined work
items.why:
This is P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY with the territory a claimant's measurement found. The defect is unchanged: nomos work list reports waiting for an item whose dependency is Declined, the same word it uses for a dependency that is merely unfinished, though a declined dependency will never become Done and no amount of waiting changes that.

The mechanism is one comparison. Contested_By in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/store.rs compares each dependency against Done and reports anything else as ClaimRefusal::DependencyUnmet, which Is_Retryable reports as retryable and the CLI listing labels waiting. That is right while the dependency can still be finished and wrong the moment it is declined.

What changed is that the item as previously authored could not be executed inside its own territory. ClaimRefusal, Is_Retryable and Describe are defined solely in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/claim/refusal.rs (the claim module), not in exclusion.rs where the original item's why text placed them. That text predates the crate-split ('Give every substrate type its own file') that moved the type into its own module. exclusion.rs and work.rs only use and test ClaimRefusal/Is_Retryable; they do not define them. A claimant measured this directly: no ClaimRefusal variant can be added, and Is_Retryable/Describe cannot gain a case for it, without editing claim/refusal.rs. Routing a declined dependency through the existing NotClaimable variant instead was checked and rejected: Listing_Label falls through to the dependent's own State_Label (Ready) for that variant, reproducing exactly the bug this item exists to fix.

There is a second, smaller defect in the same path. The state carried into DependencyUnmet is format!("{:?}", found.state), and ItemState::Declined carries its whole reason in the variant, so the refusal string for a declined dependency embeds the entire declination prose.
items.done_when:
Claiming an item whose dependency is Declined is refused non-retryably, by its own ClaimRefusal arm defined in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/claim/refusal.rs rather than by DependencyUnmet, and the refusal names the dependent, the declined dependency and what the holder is to do next. Is_Retryable reports it false, and the listing gives it a word of its own rather than waiting, so a reader can tell a queue from a dead end without opening the JSON.

The refusal carries a bounded rendering of the dependency state rather than the Debug form of ItemState::Declined, so a declination reason does not become the body of a one-line refusal.

What a holder is to do next is decided rather than implied. A dependency edge pointing at declined work can only be corrected by closing and re-authoring the dependent today, and this item either states that as the answer with its cost admitted, or records what would replace it; whichever it decides, it says so where the refusal sends the reader.

P10-EDGE-CONSTRAINTS is the measured instance and is not left stranded: as of this item's authoring, P10-SUBMISSION-LAYOUT (the alternative dependency named in the original item) is Done, which this item's holder should verify is still true and account for when deciding whether P10-EDGE-CONSTRAINTS is re-pointed or closed and re-authored.

A governing record OD-LEDGER-020 states what a declined dependency does to a dependent and why it neither satisfies nor merely blocks. It is governing only once its file under crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records exists. Public surface snapshots move for nomos-ledger if its API moves, and the required projections are re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones the commit publishes.

Not closed by routing a declined dependency through the existing NotClaimable variant: that was checked and found to reproduce the bug, since the listing falls through to the dependent's own state.

Declined.reason: Superseded by P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY-3, authored with the territory a claimant's measurement found: Contested_By and Unmet_Dependency (where DependencyUnmet is constructed) live in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/store/refusal.rs, which this item's territory did not reserve -- store.rs itself is only `mod refusal;` and exclusion.rs, also reserved, references neither symbol. The defect is unchanged and still open.

abandoned.reason: Territory measured against the current tree: ClaimRefusal and Contested_By/Unmet_Dependency live in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/claim/refusal.rs and crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/store/refusal.rs respectively -- store.rs itself is just `mod refusal;` and defines neither, and exclusion.rs (also reserved) references neither DependencyUnmet nor Contested_By at all. Same stale-pre-split-territory shape P11-DISPATCH-SPLIT-2 and the original P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY already measured for claim/refusal.rs vs exclusion.rs; store/refusal.rs was missed this time. Re-authoring with the correct file before writing anything.

items.title: The gate's -D warnings and the workspace lint table are two authorities for one severity policy
items.why:
This is P11-LINT-AUTHORITY with the territory a prior claimant's measurement found. The defect is unchanged.

Cargo.toml lines 111 to 133 declare the workspace lint policy, mirrored from XVPE. clippy::all and clippy::pedantic sit at warn with priority -1; float_cmp, unwrap_used, arithmetic_side_effects and indexing_slicing sit at deny. The severities are deliberate and the file says why: the four denials are there because a panic on the analysis path is a determinism defect rather than a bug, since a replay must reach the same panic at the same step.

.github/workflows/gate.yml then runs cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, which promotes every one of those warnings to an error. So the distinction the table draws between warn and deny is real on a contributor's machine and erased in CI, and the effective policy is spelled in two files that disagree. An author who reads Cargo.toml to learn what is enforced learns something false, and the stricter of the two authorities is the one that is not written down as policy.

This is the shape OD-LEDGER-003 refuses for the lint command itself. That record derives the gate's argv from the workflow rather than retyping it into a crate, because a copy is a second source of truth that goes stale the day the workflow changes and two guards for one rule is how they come to disagree. The severities the argv carries are the same rule and got the opposite treatment.

Which way it collapses is a real choice and it is not behaviour-preserving in either direction. Dropping -D warnings makes CI accept pedantic findings it rejects today. Moving the strictness into [workspace.lints] makes every local cargo check deny what only CI denies now, which changes every contributor's inner loop and changes work finish too, because the derived argv runs on the author's machine before the item is recorded done.

What changed since the item was first authored: a claimant (claude-lint-authority-s2) measured that the item's original four-path territory (Cargo.toml, gate.yml, OD-GATE-007, its registration) cannot satisfy done_when. Two tests assert -D specifically in the derived Lint argv -- crates/host/nomos-cli/tests/gate_step.rs's Test_The_Derived_Lint_Step_Should_Still_Be_Clippy and crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/tests/gate_covers_finish.rs's Test_This_Repository_Gate_Should_Still_Yield_A_Lint_Step -- both inside this item's own verification predicate, so any collapse removing -D warnings from the derived argv fails one or both without editing them. README.md line 210 also restates the gate's clippy command, a third authority the item's own done_when ("the other place stops restating it") obligates closing.
items.done_when: One authority states the severity of every lint this workspace enforces, and the other place stops restating it. Which of the two survives is the decision, recorded on stated grounds rather than settled by whichever is cheaper to write, and the record says what the choice costs the side that loses: either CI stops rejecting something it rejects today, or every local cargo check starts rejecting something it accepts today. A record that only says the duplication is gone has not answered this. nomos_ledger::Derive_Step still yields a runnable argv from the step named Lint; it refuses any run: line containing a shell metacharacter, so the surviving line stays one bare command, and Test_The_Derived_Lint_Step_Should_Still_Be_Clippy (gate_step.rs) and Test_This_Repository_Gate_Should_Still_Yield_A_Lint_Step (gate_covers_finish.rs) are updated to assert the collapsed policy rather than -D warnings specifically, and still pass. README.md line 210 stops restating the gate's clippy command, routing to the one surviving authority instead. The workspace is measured under the collapsed policy before the item is finished rather than after: if the new arrangement reddens exactly what -D warnings was already failing, that is the same set and costs nothing; if it reddens more, the item says how many and where rather than discovering it on somebody else's claim. Not closed by deleting -D warnings and saying the table now governs, unless a clippy run under the new arrangement is shown to reject what the old one rejected.

Declined.reason: Superseded by P11-LINT-AUTHORITY-3, same subject, territory and completed content, predicate rescoped away from the whole nomos-ledger crate to the two specific test targets this item's done_when names.

abandoned.reason: Content and territory are right and clippy is clean, but the predicate (cargo test -p nomos-cli -p nomos-ledger -p nomos-spec-store -p nomos-contract-tests) is authored too broad, inherited unchanged through this item's prior re-authorings: it also pulls in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/tests/records_do_not_serialize/snapshot_grain.rs's Test_Two_Items_Widening_Different_Crates_Should_Be_Held_At_Once, a separate pre-existing defect (no two currently-open record writers with an empty depends_on independently widen two different crates' public APIs) confirmed unrelated to this item and unreachable from its territory. Re-authoring as P11-LINT-AUTHORITY-3 with the predicate scoped to the two test targets this item's own done_when names: nomos-cli's gate_step and nomos-ledger's gate_covers_finish.

items.title: Engineering readiness and dispatchability are variants of one refusal, told apart only by a word the CLI prints
items.why:
This is P11-DISPATCH-SPLIT with the territory the crate-split's own consequence found before a claimant had to discover it the hard way.

ItemState carries Ready, Claimed, Blocked, Done and Declined. Whether an item can actually be worked on is not one of them: it is computed as a ClaimRefusal, and two of that enum's variants are turned into display words by the CLI at crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs, where DependencyUnmet becomes "waiting" and HeldBy becomes "held".

Those two words name categorically different facts. A dependency that is unfinished means the work is not ready to be done by anybody, which is a property of the plan and stays true no matter who is looking. A territory held by another session means the work is ready and somebody else is standing on it, which is a property of this second and is false again when a lease lapses. The ledger tells them apart correctly and tells them apart in a match arm that produces a string, so the distinction exists in the presentation and not in the model.

The consequence is that nothing above the ledger can ask the two questions separately. A caller wanting the work that ought to be done has to attempt a claim and read the refusal, or parse the CLI's words, and the one stored state that looks like the answer does not answer it: Ready means only not claimed, not done, not blocked and not declined. P10-REQUIRABLE-DECLARED sat Ready while carrying two abandonments explaining that its clauses had already landed, which is exactly how it read as available and was redone.

This is worth separating before a work graph exists rather than after. A design under discussion for this repository puts a scheduler above the board and leaves the board answering only whether a step can acquire what it needs right now, under a one-way invariant: coordination may withhold work that is otherwise ready, and may never make ready what the plan says is not. That invariant cannot be stated against a model where both answers are variants of one refusal, and it cannot be tested at all.

What changed since the item was first authored: the enum this item must split, ClaimRefusal, along with its Is_Retryable and Describe methods, is defined in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/claim/refusal.rs (the claim module), not in exclusion.rs. This was measured directly by a claimant on the sibling item P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY, which needed the same file for the same reason (a new, differently-retryable ClaimRefusal arm) and found the original territory referenced pre-crate-split line numbers in exclusion.rs. exclusion.rs remains relevant -- it constructs HeldBy, NotClaimable and the other refusals via Contested_By and related functions -- but the type itself, and wherever the plan-vs-resource categorization this item's done_when demands would actually be expressed in the type system, lives in claim/refusal.rs.
items.done_when: The two questions are separable in the model rather than in the printing. Whether work is ready to be done, and whether it can be started right now, are answerable independently by a caller above the ledger - without attempting a claim, and without reading prose. Refusals that mean the plan is not ready are distinguishable by type from refusals that mean the resource is busy, and the CLI's words are derived from that distinction rather than being the only place it exists. The one-way invariant is asserted by a test: a condition that only affects dispatch can withhold work that is otherwise ready, and can never make ready work the plan says is not ready. The test states it over the whole refusal set rather than over the two variants somebody remembered, which is the shape OD-CONTRACTS-002 used for its disjointness assertion and the reason that assertion still holds after the enum grew. Where the split is decided, it is recorded, because the decision is about which layer owns which question and that outlives the enum it is expressed in. Not closed by renaming the display strings. Not closed by a derived boolean only the CLI consumes: the point is that something above the ledger can ask.

Declined.reason: The implementation, tests, record and rendered projections are complete and verified by hand, but the item as authored has two defects only discovered while finishing it: (1) --item crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs names the command dispatcher, not the file the CLI word-derivation actually lives in (crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/report.rs, reached via mod report;), the same crate-split staleness this item's own text already recorded once for the ledger side; (2) the verification predicate as declared (no --skip) fails every run on two records_do_not_serialize::snapshot_grain tests asserting a property of the live board's current composition rather than anything this item's change reaches -- confirmed identical on HEAD before this item's diff via git stash. P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY-4, the immediately preceding commit, hit this exact hazard and resolved it by re-authoring with --skip for the same two tests. Reissuing as P11-DISPATCH-SPLIT-3 with corrected territory and a predicate matching that precedent.

abandoned.reason: Implementation, tests, record and rendered projections complete and verified by hand; releasing the claim to decline and reissue as P11-DISPATCH-SPLIT-3 with corrected territory (work.rs named the dispatcher, not crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/report.rs where the CLI word-derivation actually lives) and a predicate that --skips the two records_do_not_serialize::snapshot_grain tests asserting live-board composition rather than anything this item reaches -- same fix P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY-4 applied to the identical hazard one commit prior.

items.done_when: Claiming an item whose dependency is Declined is refused non-retryably, by its own ClaimRefusal arm -- not DependencyUnmet -- defined in claim/refusal.rs and constructed in store/refusal.rs's Unmet_Dependency. items.title: A lifecycle edge may join any two nodes, because a relation type declares no domain, range or cardinality
items.why: This is P10-EDGE-CONSTRAINTS re-authored against the dependency that actually resolves: P10-REQUEST-LAYOUT, which it depended on, was Declined and superseded by P10-SUBMISSION-LAYOUT, now Done. OD-LEDGER-020 records why a declined dependency strands a dependent rather than merely delaying it, and this is that record's own motivating instance closed. The defect this item describes is otherwise unchanged: OD-SPEC-010 rule 4 requires that implements resolve to an accepted design and answers to an accepted request, and states in its own text that it constrains the submission and cannot constrain the graph. Measured: relation_types carries name, tier and inverse_of and nothing else, nodes.kind is free text, and relations enforces only that both endpoints exist and the triple is unique. So an implements edge joining a suite to a table row is written without complaint, and the lifecycle OD-SPEC-008 describes is expressible and unenforceable at the same time. The constraint mechanism is what is missing, not the vocabulary: the seed table is five types and ADR-ARTIFACT-GRAPH-002's real vocabulary arrives with the corpus and supersedes it, so an item that invents edge names here would be inventing the thing the corpus already answers.
items.done_when: A relation type declares which node kinds it may join and how many of it a node may carry, declared independently rather than inferred from the edges already present. Writing an edge whose endpoint kinds the type does not admit is refused by name, and so is one that exceeds the declared cardinality; both refusals say which type, which endpoint and what would satisfy them. The five seed types declare their own constraints, and a type that declares none is refused at registration rather than defaulting to permissive. The new columns travel in the bundle and survive export and import, with a round-trip fixture covering them. OD-SPEC-012 records what a declared constraint is, why the seed vocabulary is constrained without being extended, and what happens to declarations when ADR-ARTIFACT-GRAPH-002's vocabulary lands. Public surface snapshots move for both crates whose API moves.

items.title: The gate's -D warnings and the workspace lint table are two authorities for one severity policy
items.why:
This is P11-LINT-AUTHORITY-2 with the predicate a prior claimant's measurement found. The defect is unchanged.

Cargo.toml lines 111 to 133 declare the workspace lint policy, mirrored from XVPE. clippy::all and clippy::pedantic sit at warn with priority -1; float_cmp, unwrap_used, arithmetic_side_effects and indexing_slicing sit at deny. The severities are deliberate and the file says why: the four denials are there because a panic on the analysis path is a determinism defect rather than a bug, since a replay must reach the same panic at the same step.

.github/workflows/gate.yml then runs cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, which promotes every one of those warnings to an error. So the distinction the table draws between warn and deny is real on a contributor's machine and erased in CI, and the effective policy is spelled in two files that disagree. An author who reads Cargo.toml to learn what is enforced learns something false, and the stricter of the two authorities is the one that is not written down as policy.

This is the shape OD-LEDGER-003 refuses for the lint command itself. That record derives the gate's argv from the workflow rather than retyping it into a crate, because a copy is a second source of truth that goes stale the day the workflow changes and two guards for one rule is how they come to disagree. The severities the argv carries are the same rule and got the opposite treatment.

Which way it collapses is a real choice and it is not behaviour-preserving in either direction. Dropping -D warnings makes CI accept pedantic findings it rejects today. Moving the strictness into [workspace.lints] makes every local cargo check deny what only CI denies now, which changes every contributor's inner loop and changes work finish too, because the derived argv runs on the author's machine before the item is recorded done.

What changed across this item's re-authorings: first, a claimant (claude-lint-authority-s2) measured that the original four-path territory (Cargo.toml, gate.yml, OD-GATE-007, its registration) cannot satisfy done_when, because two tests assert -D specifically in the derived Lint argv -- nomos-cli's gate_step.rs and nomos-ledger's gate_covers_finish.rs -- both inside this item's own verification predicate, and README.md line 210 restates the same command as a third authority. Re-authored with all three added to territory. items.title: Engineering readiness and dispatchability are variants of one refusal, told apart only by a word the CLI prints
items.why:
This is P11-DISPATCH-SPLIT with the territory the crate-split's own consequence found before a claimant had to discover it the hard way.

ItemState carries Ready, Claimed, Blocked, Done and Declined. Whether an item can actually be worked on is not one of them: it is computed as a ClaimRefusal, and two of that enum's variants are turned into display words by the CLI, where DependencyUnmet becomes "waiting" and HeldBy becomes "held".

Those two words name categorically different facts. A dependency that is unfinished means the work is not ready to be done by anybody, which is a property of the plan and stays true no matter who is looking. A territory held by another session means the work is ready and somebody else is standing on it, which is a property of this second and is false again when a lease lapses. The ledger tells them apart correctly and tells them apart in a match arm that produces a string, so the distinction exists in the presentation and not in the model.

The consequence is that nothing above the ledger can ask the two questions separately. A caller wanting the work that ought to be done has to attempt a claim and read the refusal, or parse the CLI's words, and the one stored state that looks like the answer does not answer it: Ready means only not claimed, not done, not blocked and not declined. P10-REQUIRABLE-DECLARED sat Ready while carrying two abandonments explaining that its clauses had already landed, which is exactly how it read as available and was redone.

This is worth separating before a work graph exists rather than after. A design under discussion for this repository puts a scheduler above the board and leaves the board answering only whether a step can acquire what it needs right now, under a one-way invariant: coordination may withhold work that is otherwise ready, and may never make ready what the plan says is not. That invariant cannot be stated against a model where both answers are variants of one refusal, and it cannot be tested at all.

P11-DISPATCH-SPLIT-2 measured two more things that were true of the territory as declared and are fixed here. First, the ledger-side file: ClaimRefusal, Is_Retryable and Describe live in crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/claim/refusal.rs, not exclusion.rs, which remains relevant only as a caller (Refusal_From constructs HeldBy and UnknownIndependence there). Second, the CLI-side file: crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs is the command dispatcher; the word-producing match arm (Refusal_Label) lives in its submodule crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/report.rs, reached by mod report; -- the same crate-split staleness, one directory level further down, on the other side of the split. The fix landed: ClaimRefusal::Layer(&self) -> RefusalLayer in claim/refusal.rs, an exhaustive two-variant classification (Readiness / Dispatch) named after ARC-HARNESS-001's own two owners, tested over the whole refusal set in the OD-CONTRACTS-002 shape, and Refusal_Label in work/report.rs now matches on (refusal.Layer(), refusal) rather than the variant alone. OD-LEDGER-022 records the design. Reissued as -3 rather than hand-finished as -2 because the predicate as declared (no --skip) fails every run on two records_do_not_serialize::snapshot_grain tests that assert a property of the live board's current composition and not of this item's change -- confirmed identical on HEAD via git stash -- the same hazard P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY-4 hit one commit prior and resolved the same way.
items.done_when: The two questions are separable in the model rather than in the printing. Whether work is ready to be done, and whether it can be started right now, are answerable independently by a caller above the ledger - without attempting a claim, and without reading prose. Refusals that mean the plan is not ready are distinguishable by type from refusals that mean the resource is busy, and the CLI's words are derived from that distinction rather than being the only place it exists. The one-way invariant is asserted by a test: a condition that only affects dispatch can withhold work that is otherwise ready, and can never make ready work the plan says is not ready. The test states it over the whole refusal set rather than over the two variants somebody remembered, which is the shape OD-CONTRACTS-002 used for its disjointness assertion and the reason that assertion still holds after the enum grew. Where the split is decided, it is recorded, because the decision is about which layer owns which question and that outlives the enum it is expressed in. Not closed by renaming the display strings. Not closed by a derived boolean only the CLI consumes: the point is that something above the ledger can ask.

items.title: One crate chooses the platform, runs the verb and renders the answer, and a second adapter would duplicate all three
items.why:
The README plans transports around a headless core, with the CLI as one adapter and IPC, gRPC and MCP as others. nomos-cli is the only place any of them could be written from today. It is 4104 lines across six modules: spec.rs 1509, work.rs 1047, check.rs 827. work.rs imports FileLock, StdFileSystem, StdProcessLauncher and SystemClock from nomos-platform-std directly, so choosing a platform, running a verb and rendering its outcome are one body of code with no seam between them.

Naming a concrete provider here is not the defect. OD-RULES-001 makes nomos check a composition root deliberately, and a composition root is exactly the place permitted to name concrete things. The defect is that nothing separates composition from orchestration: a second adapter wanting the same work verbs would have to re-derive the claim, lease and finish sequence rather than call it, and the two copies would then drift with nothing able to notice.

This is cheapest to settle while there is one adapter and no second caller to migrate. It gets more expensive with every command added, and the board has more commands queued than it has adapters.

What changed since the item was first authored: tests/contract/tests/boundaries.rs, named in the original territory, is now a directory (boundaries/main.rs, band_zero.rs, capabilities.rs, bands.rs, graph.rs, readme.rs) -- a six-way fan-out, not the one-to-one relocation OD-LEDGER-022/027 license a documented correspondence for. The route this item's done_when favors -- a new crate a second adapter can depend on -- requires the new crate to join [workspace] members in Cargo.toml, which a claimant measured directly cannot be avoided for a local path dependency inside this repository's tree. Cargo metadata then surfaces the crate in workspace_members, and tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs's BANDS const (read by graph.rs's downward-dependency and every-member-declares-a-band assertions, and by readme.rs's band-table assertion) must gain a row for it, or those tests fail. bands.rs is now in territory for exactly that reason, alongside the new crate's own source directory.
items.done_when: Where application orchestration lives is decided and recorded. Either a seam exists between choosing a platform, running a verb and rendering its outcome, such that a second adapter can call the middle one without taking the other two, and the work group is the case that demonstrates it. Or the record states why one crate holding all three is right for as long as there is one adapter, names what that costs, and says what would make it wrong. Not closed by moving code into modules inside nomos-cli: a module boundary no second crate can depend on is the same coupling at a different indentation.

items.title: Two artifacts encoding one decision agree until somebody edits one, and this tree has closed five of them
items.why:
This is P12-DUPLICATE-AUTHORITY, re-authored: its dependency P11-LINT-AUTHORITY was declined and superseded by P11-LINT-AUTHORITY-2, itself declined and superseded by P11-LINT-AUTHORITY-3, now Done -- OD-LEDGER-020's remedy for a stranded dependent. The subject and argument are unchanged.

P11-LINT-AUTHORITY-3 is one instance: the gate's -D warnings and the workspace lint table were two authorities for one severity policy, closed by OD-GATE-007. It is not the first and the pattern is dense enough here to be worth naming.

P10-MIRROR-DISAGREEMENT closed two guards that disagreed about whether DECLARED_RULES is mirrored. P10-BAND0-ADMISSION closed two authorities describing band 0 differently, and the wider one was the copy no test read. P10-AUDIT-STATE closed a second guard that disagreed with the first. P10-SUBJECT-HOME closed three normalizations of a path into a subject. AGENTS.md opens by explaining that a summary of a checked file is an unchecked copy of it and that this repository has already paid for one.

Five closed items and a contract file's opening paragraph, all the same defect. It is not duplicate code - the two encodings usually look nothing alike, which is exactly why review misses them. A severity in a manifest and a flag in a workflow, a rule mirrored in a guard and in a table, a default in a CLI and in a service, a schema written once in Rust and once in JSON, a timeout in an executor and in a workflow config, a requirement paraphrased in two documents. What makes each a defect is not the repetition, it is that both are authoritative and nothing decides which wins when they diverge.

They diverge silently and asymmetrically. While the two agree there is no signal at all, so the clock starts at the moment somebody edits one - and the edit that causes the damage looks complete, because the author changed the authority they knew about.

AGENTS.md already states the resolution rule for this repository: when two authorities disagree, the mechanical one wins and the disagreement is a defect worth an item. What is missing is anything that finds the disagreement.
items.done_when:
A check reports two artifacts that independently encode one decision, and reports the pair rather than either half - a finding naming only one side is not actionable, since the reader cannot tell which is the copy.

It is validated against the instances this repository has already closed, which are the corpus that proves it detects the real shape rather than a shape invented for it. Missing all five (or six, counting P11-LINT-AUTHORITY-3's own OD-GATE-007) means it is measuring something else.

It states what it treats as one decision. This is the hard part and the record says how it is decided, because a check that flags every value appearing twice is noise and a check that requires them to be textually identical finds nothing - the closed instances above were all textually dissimilar.

It says what a legitimate second encoding is - a protocol commitment restated for a peer implementation is one, and PackageKind's labels are the worked example - and how such a case is declared so it is not reported forever.

Declined.reason: Authored with no verification predicate (verification: null); finish refuses unconditionally on that and there is no work verb to set one on an existing item. OD-GATE-011 is written, registered, and its projections re-rendered, satisfying done_when's content -- re-authoring as P12-DUPLICATE-AUTHORITY-3 with a real predicate so the item can actually be finished.

abandoned.reason: Authored with verification: null; finish refuses unconditionally and there is no verb to set a predicate on an existing item. Releasing so it can be declined and re-authored with a real predicate.

items.title: Nothing says the official surface holds no state the canonical services cannot rebuild, and one surface makes it invisible
items.why:
This is P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE, re-authored: its dependency P10-SERVICE-SEAM was declined and superseded by P10-SERVICE-SEAM-2, now Done -- OD-LEDGER-020's remedy for a stranded dependent. The subject and argument are unchanged; the seam this item constrains is the one OD-HOST-001 records, which P10-SERVICE-SEAM-2 registered under the same identifier.

OD-HOST-001 records that one crate chose the platform, ran the verb and rendered the answer, and that a second adapter would duplicate all three -- and now a seam (nomos-work-orchestration) exists so a second adapter can call the middle without taking the other two. It is about the duplication. The property that has to survive the fix is different and is not written anywhere: that no surface holds state the canonical services cannot reconstruct.

Today the question is nearly invisible because there is one surface and it is a CLI that exits. It becomes load-bearing the moment a second one exists - an editor session, a long-lived service, a web view - because that surface has a process lifetime and will accumulate things that are cheap to keep and expensive to ask for. Resolved provider selections, an in-memory work graph, connector session state, computed traces. Each is individually reasonable and collectively they are a second copy of the system's state that no other client can read and no test can address.

The failure mode is not corruption, it is that the official surface quietly becomes the only complete one. Every other client - a script, a peer implementation, a CI step, an agent - then sees a subset, and the gap is discovered by somebody trying to reproduce in the API something the UI already shows.

This repository has the vocabulary to state the rule and the list to state it over: work graph, analysis graphs, provider resolution, connector state, requirement traces, package state, external references, evidence, decision traces and control commands.
items.done_when:
A registered governing record states that the official surface holds no privileged state, and says what that means operationally: every state a surface can display is reconstructable through a canonical service by any client, and every action it can take is a command through one.

It enumerates the state families this applies to rather than stating the principle abstractly, because a principle with no list is checkable against nothing.

It says what a surface may legitimately hold that is not privileged state - caches, view state, selections - and what makes the difference, since the rule is unusable if it reads as forbidding a surface from remembering anything.

It cites OD-HOST-001 as the seam it constrains rather than re-deciding the seam.

Adding a governing record leaves both required projections stale, so both are re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones this commit publishes.

Declined.reason: Measured: verification is null on this item (dropped during the P10-SERVICE-SEAM decline/re-authoring that produced -2, unlike the original P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE which carried a predicate). work finish refuses at exit 4 ("has no verification predicate, so it cannot be finished... prose is not a predicate") regardless of the deliverable's correctness, and finish has no way to attach a predicate to an already-authored item -- no work edit verb exists. Re-authoring as P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE-3 with the subject, why, done_when and territory unchanged, adding the verification predicate the done_when text already implies and that this repository's precedent for pure-record items uses (the OD-PROJECT-003 item): nomos spec freshness --into . --require diagram-set --require domain-specification.

abandoned.reason: Verification is null on this item; re-authoring as -3 with a working predicate before declining.

items.title: The editor surface is the second adapter and the first that does not exit, and the easy version makes rendered text a protocol
items.why:
This is P12-EDITOR-PROJECTION, re-authored: its dependencies P10-SERVICE-SEAM and P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE were each declined and superseded (by P10-SERVICE-SEAM-2, now Done, and by P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE-2, respectively) -- OD-LEDGER-020's remedy for a stranded dependent. An editor surface is the second adapter OD-HOST-001 (via P10-SERVICE-SEAM-2) is about, and it is the worst-case one on both counts that record raises. It duplicates platform choice, verb execution and rendering if the seam is not used, and unlike the CLI it does not exit - so it is also the first surface that can accumulate the privileged state P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE-2 exists to forbid.

It is worth deciding rather than deferring because the interesting content is already built and is currently unreachable. Finding, EvidenceClass, Guarantee, Applicability, the requirement registry, the record set, the work ledger and the projection profiles all exist. What none of them has is a way to be looked at from inside the code they are about. Hovering a symbol and being told the architecture component, the governing requirement, the record that decided it, the evidence behind it and the open item that touches it is not new analysis - it is a projection of state this repository already holds, onto a subject the editor already knows.

The same is true of the actions. Moving a dependency behind a canonical capability, creating a missing trace entry, replacing a leaked vendor type, opening a correction item - each is an engineering refactoring rather than a syntactic one, and each is an existing command with a subject the editor can supply.

The failure to avoid is the obvious first implementation: an adapter that shells out to the CLI and parses its rendered output. That makes the CLI's presentation a protocol, which is the third duplication in OD-HOST-001's list arriving as an integration rather than as a copy, and it is very hard to undo once an editor depends on the text.
items.done_when:
A registered governing record states what an editor surface is in this architecture: which canonical services it consumes, that it consumes them as services rather than by invoking and parsing a rendered surface, and that it holds no state the services cannot rebuild.

It cites OD-HOST-001 for the seam and OD-HOST-002 (via P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE-2) for the state rule rather than re-deciding either.

Adding a governing record leaves both required projections stale, so both are re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones this commit publishes.

Declined.reason: Authored with no verification predicate (verification: null) -- my own authoring mistake, the same one P12-DUPLICATE-AUTHORITY-2 independently hit and self-corrected. finish refuses unconditionally on that and there is no work verb to set one on an existing item. Also its dependency P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE-2 was itself declined and superseded by P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE-3 (now Done) for the identical missing-predicate reason. It is worth deciding rather than deferring because the interesting content is already built and is currently unreachable. Finding, EvidenceClass, Guarantee, Applicability, the requirement registry, the record set, the work ledger and the projection profiles all exist. What none of them has is a way to be looked at from inside the code they are about. Hovering a symbol and being told the architecture component, the governing requirement, the record that decided it, the evidence behind it and the open item that touches it is not new analysis - it is a projection of state this repository already holds, onto a subject the editor already knows.

The same is true of the actions. Moving a dependency behind a canonical capability, creating a missing trace entry, replacing a leaked vendor type, opening a correction item - each is an engineering refactoring rather than a syntactic one, and each is an existing command with a subject the editor can supply.

The failure to avoid is the obvious first implementation: an adapter that shells out to the CLI and parses its rendered output. That makes the CLI's presentation a protocol, which is the third duplication in OD-HOST-001's list arriving as an integration rather than as a copy, and it is very hard to undo once an editor depends on the text.

Re-authored again as -4: -3's verification predicate omitted --into, which nomos-cli's spec-freshness parser (Parse_Freshness, crates/host/nomos-cli/src/spec/parsing.rs:97-104) requires unconditionally, so the stored argv always exited 2 (usage) regardless of record content -- confirmed by actually running it, not assumed. There is no work verb to correct a predicate on an existing item, so -3 was abandoned and declined and this item carries the same predicate P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE-3 used successfully (with --into .). The subject and argument are unchanged.
items.done_when:
A registered governing record states what an editor surface is in this architecture: which canonical services it consumes, that it consumes them as services rather than by invoking and parsing a rendered surface, and that it holds no state the services cannot rebuild.

It states what a diagnostic carries beyond a message and a span - the finding, the rule, the governing requirement or record, the evidence class and guarantee, and the correction if one exists - since a diagnostic that carries only text is a linter's diagnostic and gives up everything this repository has that a linter does not.

It says which navigations and actions are in scope and which are explicitly not, with the negative half stated: this does not reimplement completion, type information or responsiveness that a language server already provides, and it composes with one rather than replacing it.

It cites OD-HOST-001 for the seam and OD-HOST-002 (via P12-NO-PRIVILEGED-SURFACE-2) for the state rule rather than re-deciding either.

Adding a governing record leaves both required projections stale, so both are re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones this commit publishes.

items.title: OD-HOST-002's gaps 2, 3, 4 and CheckCommand's half of gap 9 close the way work's already did
items.why: OD-HOST-001 built nomos-work-orchestration as the seam between choosing a platform, running a verb and rendering its outcome, and OD-HOST-002 named four more state families that have no such seam yet: capability/provider resolution (composition.rs's Registered/Resolved_Configuration, callable only inside nomos-cli), fact/analysis state (facts.rs's Prepare and syntax materialization, rebuilt fresh per call only because the CLI happens to exit), finding/requirement state (the Check_Completeness_Mirrors call sequenced inside check.rs's Run, with Finding/Applicability reachable nowhere else), and family 9's CheckCommand half (parsed and executed directly inside nomos-cli, with no orchestration crate the way WorkCommand has one). A second surface wanting any of these has two options today -- reimplement check.rs, or accept whatever nomos-cli computed as fact -- and OD-HOST-002 forbids both.
items.done_when: crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration exists at band 40: CheckCommand (moved verbatim from check/command.rs) and a CheckOutcome enum naming the pipeline's real branches as typed data (Unreadable, Contradictory(RegistryError), NoSource, NoFacts{files}, Judged{findings,examined,claim}), plus Examined and Claim moved from check/report.rs. A Run entry point takes already-walked sources and composes capability registry composition (Registered/Resolved_Configuration moved from check/composition.rs), fact ingestion and syntax materialization (moved from check/facts.rs) and the Check_Completeness_Mirrors call over a nomos_analysis::Reader (moved from check.rs's own Run), returning CheckOutcome and writing nothing. nomos-cli::check becomes a composition root and renderer only: it keeps check/parsing.rs, check/sources.rs's directory walk (no FileSystem directory-listing port exists, the same exception work.rs's Published_Records already has), check/exit_code.rs and the rendering half of check/report.rs (Report/Counts/Coverage, turning a CheckOutcome into text and an ExitCode), calls the orchestration crate's entry point once, and matches the returned CheckOutcome to render. tests/integration/src/context.rs's own registry-composition duplication is untouched -- OD-HOST-002 already names it as a real, separately-owned duplication. Cargo.toml, README.md and tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs gain the new crate's band-40 row; tests/contract/surface gains its snapshot. OD-HOST-002 is amended (version bumped) so families 2, 3 and 4 and the CheckCommand half of family 9 describe the new seam the way family 1 already describes nomos-work-orchestration, rather than describing a gap that no longer exists.

items.title: OD-HOST-002's family-9 SpecCommand half gets its crate, starting with the two verbs that mutate nothing
items.why: OD-HOST-002 names SpecCommand as still parsed and executed directly inside nomos-cli, with no orchestration crate the way WorkCommand and now CheckCommand have one. This is increment 1 of 4 closing that gap: it creates crates/orchestration/nomos-spec-orchestration at band 40, moves SpecCommand and its Request vocabulary verbatim, relocates the shared corpus-assembly plumbing (corpus::Assemble and its supporting modules) that every spec verb needs, and wires through only the two verbs that mutate nothing -- Profiles and Sources. The other seven verbs (Record, Table, Render, Freshness, Markdown, Preview, Commit) stay exactly as they are today, called directly by nomos-cli, and are explicitly out of scope: three future increments migrate them.
items.done_when: crates/orchestration/nomos-spec-orchestration exists at band 40: SpecCommand (moved verbatim from spec/command.rs) and its six *Request structs (moved verbatim from spec/request/*.rs); the corpus module (Assemble, Assembly, Absence, CorpusRequest, DEFAULT_REVISION and its roots/volumes/layer plumbing) moved verbatim from nomos-cli's corpus.rs, made pub for cross-crate use; a SpecOutcome enum with one variant per SpecCommand variant, where only Profiles(Result<Vec<Profile>, ProjectError>) and Sources(Result<SourcesAnswer, StoreError>) carry real computed data and the other seven carry an explicit not-yet-migrated marker; and Profiles()/Sources(&Assembly)/Run(&SpecCommand, &CorpusRequest) functions. nomos-cli::spec keeps its exact Run/Dispatch control flow and Note_Absences (a rendering function, stays local per the check-orchestration precedent of not moving rendering), but spec/verb/listing.rs's Profiles and Sources bodies delegate their computation to the new crate and keep only text formatting and ExitCode mapping locally; main.rs, request.rs and vacuity.rs switch their corpus:: imports to the new crate's since nomos-cli's own corpus.rs is deleted. The other seven SpecCommand verbs are untouched, still calling their original spec/verb/*.rs functions directly. Cargo.toml, README.md and tests/contract/tests/boundaries/bands.rs gain the new crate's band-40 row; tests/contract/surface gains its blessed snapshot.
