items.title: nomos-api gains a twelfth real seam: Work's Add verb, closing Work entirely
items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names CLI/API/MCP projections as a near-term-tier item. nomos-api has now proven a second real caller for every WorkCommand verb except Add: List, Show, Validate, Audit, Claim, Renew, TakeOver, Abandon, Decline, Finish. This item closes Work entirely.

Checked before authoring: crates/orchestration/nomos-work-orchestration/src/run.rs's own Add_Outcome calls ledger.Add(item, "nomos work add", &published(), amending) -- the holder string is a literal hard-coded there, not a caller-supplied value, so this item does not invent a holder parameter either. published is the one input every other seamed verb's own Territory::Of_Files(std::iter::empty()) closure never had to compute for real: crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs's own Published_Records(directory) walks directory.parent()/docs/records and lists every file there as a Territory, the enumeration nomos_work_orchestration::Run's own doc says a composition root supplies because "that port is read, atomically-replace and exists, not a directory walk" (nomos_platform::FileSystem has no listing operation). This item ports that same function into nomos-api, the same "deliberate twin, not a shared dependency" choice sources.rs already makes for gate's own directory walk, because OD-HOST-002 treats a walk as a composition-root concern every composition root re-implements rather than shares.

LedgerItem, ItemId, ItemKind, ItemOrigin and Territory all already derive Serialize (checked -- all four are stored directly in ledger.json), so WorkCommand::Add's own item and amending fields need no twin types; a caller constructs a real nomos_ledger::LedgerItem directly, the same "the orchestration crate's real input type, not a re-export" precedent Handle_Work_Show's ItemId and Handle_Gate_Explain's FindingQuery both already set. AddRefusal does not derive Serialize and has Describe() but no single Is_X()-style method the way ClaimRefusal/FinishRefusal do -- crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/report.rs's own Code_For_Refusal maps its six variants across three different exit codes with no one boolean capturing that split -- so this item's Refused variant carries only cause: String, the same choice WorkListResponse::Unreadable and WorkValidateResponse::Invalid already made for LedgerError, which has no such method either. Inventing a categorization AddRefusal itself does not expose as a method would be a second, uncanonical implementation of a distinction only nomos-cli's own Code_For_Refusal currently draws -- the same "two implementations of one rule is how they come to disagree" reasoning crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/report.rs's own Blocking_Refusal doc already states for a different refusal type, applied here to the same shape of risk.

items.title: nomos-api gains a thirteenth real seam: Spec's Sources verb
items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names CLI/API/MCP projections as a near-term-tier item. nomos-api has proven a second real caller for the whole of Gate and Work, and for Spec's simplest verb, Profiles (which nomos_spec_orchestration::Run special-cases to skip corpus assembly entirely). Every other SpecCommand verb, including Sources, goes through Assemble(request: &CorpusRequest) first. This item takes Sources, the next-simplest of the eight remaining Spec verbs: it takes no request fields of its own beyond the shared CorpusRequest (SpecCommand::Sources is a unit variant) and, unlike Record/Table/Render/Freshness/Markdown/Preview/Commit, needs nothing keyed to a specific record, table or edit.

Checked before authoring: crates/host/nomos-cli/src/main.rs's own Corpus_Request(rest) builds { variable: "NOMOS_V14_CORPUS", root: --corpus flag or that env var, revision: --corpus-revision flag or nomos_spec_orchestration::corpus::DEFAULT_REVISION }, and its own doc says "Both are optional: neither being given is a supported state and produces an absence rather than an error, because the governing records are embedded and there are real questions this binary can still answer." nomos-api has no argv, so Handle_Spec_Sources builds the same CorpusRequest reading only the environment variable, the same "no invented shape ahead of a real body" choice Handle_Gate_Run already makes for GateCommand's own scope/rules selectors -- CorpusRequest's fields are configuration (which corpus, which revision), not a per-call identifier the way FindingQuery or ItemId are, so this seam does not take one as a parameter.

nomos_spec_orchestration::run::Sources(&Assembly) -> SourcesAnswer and Run's own Sources_Outcome wrap it as SpecOutcome::Sources(Result<SourcesAnswer, StoreError>). Neither SourcesAnswer nor its own Absence field derives Serialize (checked crates/orchestration/nomos-spec-orchestration/src/outcome/sources.rs and corpus/absence.rs); nomos_spec_store::StoreError derives none either but does implement Display (checked crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/src/store/error.rs), the same shape LedgerError already has that WorkListResponse::Unreadable's error.to_string() already exploits.

The v14 corpus's WF-008 through WF-012 (WorkflowStep, immutable artifacts, deterministic branch/merge, versioned definitions with pinned replay, retry/compensation) remain exactly as unbuilt as OD-WORKFLOW-001 found them. ARC-ROADMAP-001's near-term tier is unchanged, and the adjacent near-term-tier work landed since OD-WORKFLOW-001 (OD-PACKAGE-010's ModelBackendPackage first manifest, four new nomos-api Work/Spec seams) touches model/agent package infrastructure and the application-service boundary respectively, and neither references RunId, WorkflowStep, or the WF-* family anywhere -- checked directly by grep and by reading nomos-api's response.rs and lib.rs in full. items.why: OD-ROADMAP-001 retires the wait-for-a-second-consumer caution for the corrections cluster. items.why: Commit order confirms OD-PACKAGE-011's v2 amendment (0fca7d1, P13-PACKAGE-011-MODEL-ROUTE-001-036-SURVEY) landed BEFORE OD-ROADMAP-001 (0449e7f, P13-ROADMAP-001-POPULATION-CAUTION-RETIRED). Unlike the six sibling records OD-ROADMAP-001 explicitly amended to point to it (ARC-ROADMAP-001, OD-PACKAGE-006/008/010/012, OD-CORRECTIONS-001), OD-PACKAGE-011 was never touched in that pass -- its 34-of-36 'no real case' finding for MODEL-ROUTE-001 through 036 was reached using the old wait-for-a-consumer methodology (grep for a real ModelExecutionProfile/telemetry/dispatch consumer) the same session's own OD-ROADMAP-001 retires for this exact requirement family. This is the same staleness a fresh corpus re-read already found and corrected for AGT-010/012/018/AGT-EXEC-003 this session (P13-AGT-010-012-018-EXEC-003-KNOWLEDGE-AUTHORITY). A second live session (nomos-b7) independently read OD-PACKAGE-011 v2 and, reasonably, treated its 'no real case' finding as still current and blocking; this amendment settles the question with per-id evidence rather than leaving two sessions to disagree about a record's freshness. The amendment does not simply retire OD-PACKAGE-011's finding wholesale: MODEL-ROUTE-037's nine-state catalog shape and 038-049 genuinely differ (resolving an EXISTING loose Catalog(Vec<String>) field into a taxonomy with no real provider/catalog to check it against -- OD-PACKAGE-011's own RustEdition counter-example), and stay 'no real case' under OD-ROADMAP-001 too, since that override licenses building from real corpus-given shape, not inventing shape the corpus never closes. A per-id review (already run this session via a design-workflow audit over all of MODEL-ROUTE-001-036) separates ids with a genuine closed enumerated list directly transcribable from corpus text (e.g. MODEL-ROUTE-014's ten-item FallbackAdmissibility, MODEL-ROUTE-029's twelve-field ModelInputAssemblyIdentity, MODEL-ROUTE-034's nine-reason RuntimeCandidateDisqualification) from ids that are genuine narrative/process description with no data shape (e.g. MODEL-ROUTE-006/008/019/020/024/033) or that share MODEL-ROUTE-037's resolve-an-existing-loose-field problem.

items.title: nomos-corrections gains COR-EXEC-001: a declared or derived read/write set at its own resolution tier
items.why: OD-ROADMAP-001 retires the wait-for-a-second-consumer caution for the corrections cluster. COR-EXEC-001 names seven resolution tiers in order (artifact, symbol, configuration, generated-source, dependency, provider-state, semantic) and, for a derived set specifically, four provenance fields (provider, guarantee, confidence, invalidation basis) -- directly transcribable, the same declared-not-computed pattern already used for RankingCriterion and RollbackBoundary. The provenance half reuses real, already-band-legal types rather than inventing parallel ones: nomos_contracts::ProviderId and nomos_contracts::Guarantee, both already imported by this crate (committed.rs, staged.rs, validated.rs already use ProviderId in tests and SnapshotId/MutationClass from the same crate). Guarantee is a semantic fit, not a coincidental one: COR-EXEC-001 asks what a derived sets provenance claims about itself, and Guarantee is already this workspace own answer to what a provider promises about the facts it produces -- soundness, completeness and incremental granularity apply to a derived read/write set exactly the way they apply to any other derived fact. confidence and invalidation basis have no existing reusable type and no shape or range named by the corpus, so both are plain declared strings, the same placeholder pattern CorrectionChoice already uses for predicted_side_effects/unresolved_tradeoffs/verification_obligations. This type is free-standing -- referencing nothing from CorrectionCandidate and not threaded into its constructor -- the same shape CorrectionChoice and CorrectionDecision already took, so no existing call site changes.

items.title: nomos-api gains a fourteenth real seam: Spec's Record verb
items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names CLI/API/MCP projections as a near-term-tier item. nomos-api has proven
a second real caller for the whole of Gate and Work, and for Spec's Profiles and Sources.
Record is the next verb: unlike Sources it is not a unit SpecCommand variant, it takes a
RecordRequest{id, revision}, and its own outcome is Result<RecordAnswer, RecordRefusal>
rather than a single-shape answer.

Checked before authoring: RecordAnswer{id, document: DocumentSource} and
RecordRefusal{NotFound{id, revision, node: Option<NodeSummary>}, Ambiguous{id,
documents: Vec<DocumentSource>}, Store(StoreError)} (crates/orchestration/
nomos-spec-orchestration/src/outcome/record.rs and outcome/record/record_refusal.rs) --
none derive Serialize. DocumentSource{uid: i64 (never exported, its own doc comment says
so), path, revision, content_hash, text} and NodeSummary{node_id, kind, authority,
representation, title} (crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/src/read/document_source.rs and
read/node_summary.rs) are both flat String-only structs, neither derives Serialize.
StoreError has no Serialize but does implement Display, the same shape
SpecSourcesResponse::Unreadable already exploits.

run::record::Record(assembly, request) -> Result<RecordAnswer, RecordRefusal> takes no
FileSystem parameter and never touches one -- run.rs's own doc names only Render, Freshness,
Preview and Commit as the four verbs generic over FileSystem "for real"; Record is not one of
them. The shared entry point Handle_Spec_Sources already uses,
Run<F: FileSystem>(command, request, filesystem), is still generic across all nine variants
uniformly, so Handle_Spec_Record still supplies &StdFileSystem as plumbing even though
Record's own code path never reads it -- the same "no invented shape ahead of a real body"
composition Handle_Spec_Sources already established, extended to a verb that also carries a
request payload instead of being a unit variant.

D-132 is a real, embedded governing record (crates/orchestration/nomos-spec-orchestration/
src/tests.rs:109-124 already resolves it with no corpus), so a real end-to-end test needs no
scratch directory and no NOMOS_V14_CORPUS to be set, the same zero-setup shape
Handle_Spec_Sources's and Handle_Spec_Profiles's own tests already have.
items.done_when:
nomos-api gains a new public function Handle_Spec_Record(request: &RecordRequest) ->
SpecRecordResponse in spec.rs, following Handle_Spec_Sources's exact composition: builds the
same CorpusRequest from NOMOS_V14_CORPUS, calls
nomos_spec_orchestration::Run(&SpecCommand::Record(request.clone()), &corpus_request,
&StdFileSystem), matches SpecOutcome::Record via an irrefutable let-else with unreachable!
on the wrong-variant arm, converts through SpecRecordResponse::From.

SpecRecordResponse is a new tagged enum: Resolved{id: String, document:
DocumentSourceResponse}, NotFound{id: String, revision: Option<String>, node:
Option<NodeSummaryResponse>}, Ambiguous{id: String, documents: Vec<DocumentSourceResponse>},
Unreadable{cause: String} (Store(StoreError) collapsed via .to_string(), the same shape
SpecSourcesResponse::Unreadable already uses).

DocumentSourceResponse{path, revision, content_hash, text} is a new public struct, a

items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names CLI/API/MCP projections as a near-term-tier item. nomos-api has proven
a second real caller for Gate, Work, and Spec's Profiles, Sources, Record, Table and
Markdown. Freshness is the next verb: FreshnessRequest{into, profile, require}, answered as

Checked before authoring: run::freshness::Freshness<F: FileSystem> is one of the four verbs
generic over FileSystem (crates/orchestration/nomos-spec-orchestration/src/run/freshness.rs),
but its own module doc says it plainly: "Reads through FileSystem::Read_To_String rather
than raw std::fs" -- the function body calls Read_To_String exactly twice (a rendered body

record and can delete a vacated one), Freshness never writes -- so exposing it over

Checked before authoring: run::preview::Preview<F: FileSystem> is generic over FileSystem
(crates/orchestration/nomos-spec-orchestration/src/run/preview.rs) for exactly one reason,
stated in its own module doc: `--from` names a file at an author-chosen path, and
Read_To_String's shape does not care who chose it. Reading the function body confirms this
is its only filesystem contact -- Staged_Text calls filesystem.Read_To_String(from) once,
and everything after (Previewed) is an in-memory assembly.store operation
(Claim_For_Edit -> Stage -> Preview). Preview never calls Replace_Atomically, std::fs::write
or std::fs::remove_file. Unlike Render (which places/overwrites two files) and Commit (which
writes a committed record and can delete a vacated one), Preview never writes, so exposing
it over nomos-api carries none of the "does a wire call write to this host's disk" hazard
those two do -- the same reasoning already given for Freshness by P13-API-SPEC-FRESHNESS-SEAM.

this crate cannot reach them directly; it reads through EditPreview's own public accessors
(Node_Id, Rename, Blocks, Identity, Relations_Added, Relations_Removed, Statements, Markdown,
Path, Wording_Moved, Changes_Nothing) instead. Blocks/Identity/Relations/Statements each
carry a further non-Serialize type -- BlockChange (5-variant enum), IdentityChange (3 flat
String fields), RecordRelation (2 flat String fields, already Deserialize in
nomos-spec-model but not Serialize), NormativeMovement (2 String fields plus a nested
NormativeOutcome, itself a 4-variant enum) -- none of which derive Serialize, all confirmed

normative_movement,normative_outcome}.rs and crates/spec/nomos-spec-model/src/record/
relation.rs. This item twins RecordRelation locally (nomos-api's own established
DocumentSourceResponse/NodeSummaryResponse precedent) rather than adding Serialize to it in
nomos-spec-model, keeping this item's territory to crates/host/nomos-api alone; the crate
gains nomos-spec-model as a new direct dependency (previously only transitive) the same way
nomos-spec-store was added as a direct dependency for P13-API-SPEC-SOURCES-SEAM.

record with no corpus needed -- Handle_Spec_Markdown (this crate's own seam) supplies the

items.title: nomos-api gains a nineteenth real seam: Spec's Render verb
items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names CLI/API/MCP projections as a near-term-tier item. nomos-api has proven
a second real caller for Gate, Work, and Spec's Profiles, Sources, Record, Table, Markdown,
Freshness and Preview -- all read-only or write-nothing so far. Render is the next verb, and
the first here that writes: RenderRequest{profile, into, subject}, answered as
Result<RenderAnswer, RenderRefusal>.

User decision (asked explicitly via AskUserQuestion, since Render/Commit are the two
FileSystem-generic verbs that actually write, distinct from Freshness/Preview which only
read): build both Render and Commit now. Checked before authoring: run::render::Render<F:
FileSystem> (crates/orchestration/nomos-spec-orchestration/src/run/render.rs) places a built
projection's body and its sidecar under request.into via exactly two
filesystem.Replace_Atomically calls, unconditionally overwriting whatever was there --
confirmed by reading the whole function. nomos-api already performs real, unauthenticated
StdFileSystem-backed writes over a wire call today: Handle_Work_Claim (crates/host/
nomos-api/src/work.rs) writes a real ledger.json at a caller-named directory. request.into
here plays the same "caller-named root" role Work's directory parameter does, with the leaf
path chosen by this crate's own store/profile machinery rather than by the caller -- so this
is not a new category of risk for this crate, only its first Spec verb to exercise the write
half of a pattern Work already established. Unlike Commit's vacate step, Render's write is
never destructive of the governing record itself: a rendered projection is a derived,
regenerable artifact that a later render call simply rebuilds.

RenderAnswer{id: String, body: PathBuf, sidecar: PathBuf, stamp: nomos_spec_project::Stamp}
(crates/orchestration/nomos-spec-orchestration/src/outcome/render.rs) needs no twin at all:
checked that Stamp derives Serialize directly (crates/spec/nomos-spec-project/src/build.rs)
along with its own nested Format/Input fields, and PathBuf/String already serialize natively
-- the first Ok-side answer in this file reused whole rather than twinned.
RenderRefusal{NoSuchProfile{requested,known}, Project(ProjectError), Unwritable{path,error:
FileSystemError}, Store(StoreError)} -- Project and Store both collapse to the same
Unreadable{cause} shape every other verb in this file already uses; Unwritable keeps its own
path (via .display().to_string(), the same shape PreviewRefusal::Unreadable's own path
field already uses) alongside a collapsed cause.

"domain-specification" builds from the embedded governing records alone (the same profile
nomos_spec_orchestration's own tests.rs and crates/host/nomos-cli/tests/read_surface.rs both
use for the same reason), so a real end-to-end test against a fresh, unique scratch
directory needs no corpus and can assert the body/sidecar bytes actually landed on disk.

items.title: nomos-api gains a twentieth real seam: Spec's Commit verb, closing SpecCommand
items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names CLI/API/MCP projections as a near-term-tier item. nomos-api has proven
a second real caller for Gate, Work, and Spec's Profiles, Sources, Record, Table, Markdown,
Freshness, Preview and Render. Commit is the last of the nine SpecCommand verbs:
CommitRequest{edit: EditRequest, into: PathBuf}, answered as Result<CommitAnswer,
CommitRefusal>.

User decision (same AskUserQuestion as P13-API-SPEC-RENDER-SEAM, presented together): build
both Render and Commit now. Checked before authoring: run::commit::Commit<F: FileSystem>
(crates/orchestration/nomos-spec-orchestration/src/run/commit.rs) writes the committed
record's bytes at request.into.join(&report.path) via filesystem.Replace_Atomically -- the
same shape Render's own write already has, confirmed by reading the whole function -- and,
on a rename, removes the vacated old path via a raw std::fs::remove_file call OUTSIDE
nomos_platform::FileSystem entirely (deletion is not one of the port's three declared
operations, by that port's own documentation). The module's own doc comment and the Vacate
helper both name the real failure mode directly: if that removal fails, "two files now
declare this record." Unlike Render's write (a derived, regenerable projection), Commit's
write replaces the governing record's own bytes -- the same docs/records/-equivalent prose
this repository's README tables, contract tests and every session's own context treat as
ground truth for the spec store's own records.

CommitAnswer{preview: EditPreview, report: CommitReport, destination: PathBuf, vacated:
Option<Vacated>, reproduction: Result<Reproduction, EditError>} and CommitRefusal{kind:
CommitRefusalKind (Unreadable{path}, Edit, Refused{preview}, Unwritable{preview,report,
path}), error: CommitRefusalError (FileSystem(FileSystemError), Edit(EditError))} (crates/
orchestration/nomos-spec-orchestration/src/outcome/commit.rs and its four submodules) --
none derive Serialize. EditPreview is read through its own public accessors, the same
approach P13-API-SPEC-PREVIEW-SEAM already established (a fresh CommittedPreviewResponse
type here rather than reusing SpecPreviewResponse's own payload shape, since that type's
wire shape is already fixed by its own finished item and this item does not widen it).
CommitReport is five usize/bool/String fields, trivial to twin. Vacated/VacateOutcome and
Reproduction are small, already fully understood from CommitAnswer's own fields; Reproduction
's own Result<_, EditError> splits into three outer variants (Matched, Mismatched,
Unverifiable{cause}) the same way VerdictResponse::Compared already splits Verdict::
Compared's Result. CommitRefusalError has no Display impl of its own (only Debug); each of
its two wrapped types (FileSystemError, EditError) does, so a small CommitRefusalError ->
String helper matches on both arms directly rather than adding a Display impl to an
orchestration-crate type this item's territory does not include.

D-132 commits cleanly with the same canonical heading rename Preview already stages
(nomos_spec_orchestration's own Test_Run_Of_Commit_Should_Write_The_Record_And_Close_The_
Round_Trip proves this exact edit round-trips), so a real end-to-end test against a fresh
scratch directory needs no corpus, writes real bytes, and can assert them read back
unchanged.

items.title: nomos-api gains a twenty-first real seam: Submit, closing nomos-spec-orchestration entirely
items.why:
ARC-ROADMAP-001 names CLI/API/MCP projections as a near-term-tier item. nomos-api now seams
all nine SpecCommand verbs. Submit is the last verb nomos_spec_orchestration answers and the
last one nomos-api had not yet seamed: SubmitRequest{kind, id, by, state, contract_version,
fields, gaps, submitted_through, into: Option<PathBuf>}, answered as Result<SubmitAnswer,
SubmitRefusal>.

Checked before authoring: nomos_spec_orchestration::Submit is NOT a SpecCommand variant --
crate lib.rs's own "A second command group" section and OD-HOST-005's resolution are explicit
that a nomos request submit invocation is not a nomos spec verb by the CLI's own naming, so
Submit is a sibling of Run over its own SubmitRequest/SubmitAnswer/SubmitRefusal, taking an
already-assembled &mut Assembly directly (crates/orchestration/nomos-spec-orchestration/src/
run/submit.rs) rather than being dispatched through Run/SpecCommand. Confirmed against
nomos-cli's own crates/host/nomos-cli/src/request.rs: it calls
nomos_spec_orchestration::corpus::Assemble(request) then nomos_spec_orchestration::Submit(&mut
assembly, submit, &StdFileSystem) directly, the same two-step composition this item's
Handle_Spec_Submit uses.

SubmitAnswer{submission: Submission, uid: i64, written: Option<RenderAnswer>} and
SubmitRefusal{Store(StoreError), Refused(Refusal), Written(RenderRefusal)} -- none derive
Serialize. Submission and everything it carries (SubmissionKind, SubmissionState, FieldValue,
Origin, DecisionGap, Severity, all in nomos-spec-model) need twins, all confirmed flat/trivial
by reading crates/spec/nomos-spec-model/src/submission.rs and its submodules plus
crates/spec/nomos-spec-model/src/failure.rs and its submodules. Refusal{submission, failures:
Vec<Failure>} is NOT collapsed to a plain cause string the way most other refusals in this
file are: it carries the exact per-field validation detail (field, rule, remedy) a real form
submission endpoint exists to surface, so RefusalResponse/FailureResponse twin it structurally
instead -- the one deliberate departure from this file's usual collapse-to-string default,
made because here the granular data is the whole point of the verb rather than incidental
error detail. SubmitRefusal::Written(RenderRefusal) collapses via a new Render_Refusal_Cause
helper (RenderRefusal itself has no Display, only its own parts do -- ProjectError,
FileSystemError and StoreError's Display are each used directly). RenderAnswer's own fields
are reused via a new RenderedProjectionResponse (kept separate from SpecRenderResponse::
Placed's own payload for the same already-shipped-shape reason CommittedPreviewResponse is
kept separate from SpecPreviewResponse's).

Submit calls run::render::Render internally when request.into is given, so it writes real
bytes through StdFileSystem exactly like P13-API-SPEC-RENDER-SEAM's own Handle_Spec_Render --
already covered by that item's own precedent discussion and the AskUserQuestion answer
("build both now") that also covered Render/Commit; Submit's write is the same shape as
Render's (a derived, regenerable subject-dossier projection), not a new category.

nomos_spec_orchestration's own tests.rs proves a complete FeatureRequest (title, goal,
behaviour, acceptance, invariants fields) accepts from the embedded records alone with no
corpus, and an incomplete one refuses naming "goal" -- the same fixtures this item's own
tests reuse.

items.title: OD-ANALYSIS-009: whether nomos-check-orchestration's Run should read a persistent fact store instead of constructing MemoryFactStore fresh per invocation
items.why: nomos-analysis's generation/invalidation/dependency-tracking machinery is real and tested, but Run (crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/src/run.rs) still calls MemoryFactStore::New() fresh on every invocation, so incrementality is never exercised across process boundaries -- edit one file, run check twice, and the second run repeats every materialization the first one already did. An external architecture review independently named this the largest gap between the incremental substrate that exists and what nomos check actually does today.

items.title: ARC-CONNECTOR-001 amended: invariant 1 conflated an external artifact's identity with the Nomos subject it concerns
items.why: Invariant 1 said an external item's identity 'must be derived from what the item is about' -- one identity slot answering two questions that do not move together (which external row this is, versus what Nomos currently understands it to concern). It is also unimplementable as stated: a specific external record must be nameable before any semantic meaning has been derived from it, just to track whether it has been seen before. Worked through directly with the user: the external artifact's identity is an honest OD-MODEL-002/D-137-shaped mint from the authority's own stable key, never a derived digest; a locator that can change independently of the artifact is provenance beside that identity, the same split OD-ANALYSIS-001 already made for a fact's snapshot; and what the artifact bears on is a separate, independently evidence-bearing relation to an ordinary Nomos identity, never folded into either endpoint. Invariant 2's 'no canonical type may name a vendor' wording is tightened to distinguish vendor identity as provenance data (allowed) from vendor ontology in canonical schema (forbidden), since provenance must be able to say which external authority was observed.
items.done_when: ARC-CONNECTOR-001 is version 2. Invariant 1 states the corrected rule: external artifact identity is an honest mint from the authority's stable key, canonically constructed by Nomos; a locator is provenance beside that identity, not part of it; what the artifact bears on is a separate, independently evidence-bearing relation to an ordinary Nomos identity. Invariant 2 is tightened to vendor-identity-as-provenance-data (allowed) versus vendor-ontology-in-canonical-schema (forbidden). Invariants 3 and 4 are unchanged. A named non-goals list states explicitly what stays undecided: the concrete ExternalArtifact type, canonical spelling syntax, the eventual correlation representation (Relation<T> / EGRAPH / other), correlation discovery algorithms, vendor-specific stable-key-versus-locator definitions, migration/transfer semantics, and any connector implementation. The record is registered and both required projections are current.

items.title: OD-GATE-016's CoveragePolicy: the first real increment, consulted by Run_Gate
items.why: A gate run reports Passed even when scope went unanalyzed or unsupported. OD-GATE-016 names the first real increment to build (a require-completeness CoveragePolicy recomputing Claim over the rule-and-scope-selected findings) but nothing builds it yet, and a fresh language provider is about to make partial coverage a routine, not an edge, case.
items.done_when: A CoveragePolicy type exists in nomos-gate-orchestration, default unset. When a caller sets it to require completeness, Run_Gate recomputes Claim over the rule-and-scope-narrowed findings (not the whole-run check_outcome claim) and returns GateRunOutcome::Indeterminate whenever that recomputed claim is Incomplete, never silently Passed. Unset behavior is provably unchanged from today. Tests cover both the set and unset paths. Public-surface snapshots for nomos-gate-orchestration and nomos-cli are reblessed if their exports move.

items.title: OD-GATE-017: whether Run gains a real per-call rule subset now, or waits for a caller that needs one
items.why: OD-GATE-014 built ScopeSelector and RuleSelector but was explicit that RuleSelector only narrows disposition after Run returns; nomos_check_orchestration::Run still executes every registered rule unconditionally, and its own text calls a real per-call rule subset a new question for a new record, not a reopening of itself. New rule and language packages are the first real candidate for a rule meant to run only for some invocations, so this measures whether that trigger has actually fired rather than leaving the caveat undecided.
items.done_when: A new accepted decision record, measured against the real code at HEAD, that checks whether any concrete caller (the incoming Go language/rule work, this repository's own CI, or elsewhere) genuinely needs Run to skip a rule's computation rather than the rule self-filtering the SourceFiles it is handed, and decides on that evidence whether to build a Run signature change now or decline with a named future trigger, at the same rigor OD-GATE-014/OD-PACKAGE-006/OD-PACKAGE-008 already apply. Registered as governing via its own spec-store registration file.

items.title: OD-RULES-010: a ToolProvider's output is a fact a native rule judges, not a Finding a tool emits directly
items.why: PackageKind::ToolProvider is one of twelve still-unconsumed package kinds. Every real Finding today traces to exactly one RuleId -- a native rule judging a materialized fact -- and EvidenceClass::Authoritative is declared with zero real usages anywhere. A tool like cargo clippy produces diagnostics that are already verdicts, not raw material, which forks the first real ToolProvider two ways: (a) treat the tool's output as a fact a thin native rule then re-emits as Finding(s), matching today's only existing shape; or (b) let ToolProvider emit Finding(s) directly, which needs a new Finding attribution field beyond RuleId and would give Authoritative its first real use. Which shape the first real ToolProvider takes is undecided.
items.done_when: OD-RULES-010 exists, is registered, and decides (a): a ToolProvider's output is materialized as a fact behind a real capability contract, and a native nomos-rules function reads that fact and emits Finding(s) the same way every existing rule does -- Check_Dependency_Direction's own Require/judge/emit shape. The record states why (b) -- widening Finding's attribution shape and giving Authoritative a first real use -- is premature for one tool (N=1), the same discipline OD-PACKAGE-011 and OD-WORKFLOW-002/003 already apply elsewhere, and names the real precedent this decision's own first increment will mirror: nomos-lang-rust-cargo's subprocess-backed provider (metadata.rs) paired with nomos-capability::Registry::Declare_And_Offer.

items.title: OD-CAPABILITY-009: whether Registry::Resolve owes subject-partitioned same-capability providers a rule beyond guarantee-strength ranking
items.why: nomos-lang-go offers nomos.cap.syntax.items with Assurance::Sound on both axes -- strictly stronger than nomos-lang-rust's Sound/Unknown -- but answers only about Go files, disjoint from nomos-lang-rust's Rust files. Registering it in nomos-check-orchestration::Declare_Syntax_Capability was tried and reverted: Registry::Resolve ranks purely by guarantee strength with no notion of which subjects a provider can even attempt, and nomos_rules::Syntax_Requirement's own deliberately-unpreferenced resolution silently picked nomos-lang-go to answer for .rs files too, since its guarantee dominates. Four real tests in nomos-check-orchestration's own tests.rs went from green to DependencyUnavailable findings -- empirical, not theoretical. OD-CAPABILITY-006 does not cover this: it is explicit that its cross-language case is two DIFFERENT languages' subjects joined by a declared correspondence, and states plainly that two same-capability offers ranked by strength is OD-CAPABILITY-001's case, not its own. This is neither: one capability, offers that partition by subject rather than compete over one, and no existing record states what Resolve owes that shape.
items.done_when: OD-CAPABILITY-009 exists, is registered, and decides whether nomos_capability needs a subject/domain-scoping mechanism (on ProviderOffer, Requirement, or elsewhere) before a second same-capability provider covering disjoint subjects can be safely registered in one Registry, or whether the real fix lives above the registry entirely -- e.g. a composition root that resolves per-Recognition before ever calling Resolve, leaving the registry's own guarantee-strength ranking untouched and reserved for genuine same-subject competition. The record states its answer against the concrete failure in this item's own why, not hypothetically, and says whether nomos-lang-go's registration is unblocked by it or still waits on a further increment.

items.title: nomos-lang-go-modules: the Go provider of nomos.cap.dependency.edges
items.why: nomos-lang-rust-cargo is the one provider of dependency edges for Rust, reading cargo metadata and composed into nomos-check-orchestration::Declare_Dependency_Capability so Check_Dependency_Direction sees Rust's real module graph. Without a Go equivalent, a Go-analyzed repository gets syntax facts from nomos-lang-go but no dependency-direction enforcement. Registering a second nomos.cap.dependency.edges offer is attempted here against Declare_Dependency_Capability, the same site nomos-lang-go's own syntax offer was tried and reverted at -- OD-CAPABILITY-009 (accepted this session) already measured why a same-capability, subject-partitioned second offer breaks every subject the wrong provider gets picked for, so this item can try the registration knowing the mechanism rather than rediscovering it, and must honestly document whichever way the attempt actually goes.
items.done_when: A new crate crates/languages/nomos-lang-go-modules reads go.mod and go list -m output through nomos-platform's ProcessLauncher port (never raw std::process::Command), exports PROVIDER, Declared_Guarantee(), Provider_Offer() and Materialize(...) per the nomos-add-plugin skill's convention, with its own Declared_Guarantee tests proving the guarantee neither vacuously satisfies nor vacuously fails. README's band table gains its row (band 25, peer to nomos-lang-rust-cargo), bands.rs recognizes it, and a fresh public-surface snapshot exists. Declare_Dependency_Capability (composition.rs) gains a Registry::Offer attempt for it: if nomos-check-orchestration's own tests stay green with it registered, it stays: if OD-CAPABILITY-009's measured hazard reproduces (a subject the wrong provider answers for), the offer is reverted and composition.rs's own doc says so, citing OD-CAPABILITY-009, the same honest-revert shape nomos-lang-go's own syntax offer already carries. Either outcome satisfies this item; silence about which one happened does not.

items.title: OD-WORKFLOW-004: the first real agent executor is not yet a real instance of WF-006's task/result protocol
items.why:
OD-WORKFLOW-002 (v2) named three conditions that would decide the workflow tier's next real increment, one being "ModelBackend/AgentExecutor infrastructure reaches a real executor ... giving WF-006's 'API-hosted, subscription-agent, human, and recorded-replay executors' a first real instance to check a shared task/result protocol against." Since that record was accepted, P14-AGENT-EXECUTOR-CLAUDE-FIRST-INCREMENT shipped nomos-agent-executor's real Execute function and P14-CLI-AGENT-EXECUTE gave it a real CLI caller -- an executor now genuinely exists, at the letter of the condition's wording, and the user directing this session's work explicitly asked for exactly this kind of audit: an accepted record's named "wait until X" condition checked against the current tree for whether X has actually arrived.

Checked directly rather than assumed. nomos-agent-executor's own module doc (crates/agent/nomos-agent-executor/src/lib.rs) states plainly: "It does not assemble a nomos_agent_contracts::WorkResult" -- it reads TaskEnvelope.goal and .effort and returns AgentExecutionOutcome, a free-text result, never the WorkResult type WF-006's "task/result protocol" names on its result side. OD-CONTRACTS-003 (accepted the same window nomos-agent-executor shipped) already measured this precisely and left it open on purpose: "It does not decide how nomos-agent-executor or any other caller assembles the rest of a WorkResult from an executor's free-text response ... not answered here." Grepped across the whole workspace (crates --include=*.rs) for every real WorkResult construction site: the only two are nomos-agent-contracts' own unit tests (work_result.rs, both inside #[cfg(test)]); zero production constructors exist anywhere, including in nomos-cli's own two real callers of the executor (agent execute, and the in-progress agent judge-role, both of which say directly in their own comments that they do not assemble one). WF-006's own corpus text names four executor kinds -- API-hosted, subscription-agent, human, recorded-replay -- sharing one protocol; grepped for every one of those four terms across crates and docs/records, the only hits are WorkflowStep's own module doc quoting WF-006's list verbatim (OD-WORKFLOW-003's vocabulary admission), not an implementation of any of the four. Exactly one executor kind (subscription-agent, dispatching to a local Claude Code subprocess) has a real instance, and that instance realizes only the task half of the named protocol.

The other two conditions were re-verified unchanged rather than assumed stale: nomos_gate_orchestration::Run_Gate still has exactly the same two real callers OD-WORKFLOW-002 found (nomos-cli's gate.rs, nomos-api's lib.rs), grepped directly; and a word-boundary grep for phase/Phase across crates/orchestration/nomos-gate-orchestration/src and crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/src still returns zero matches in either, so Gate still has no phase concept.

So the honest finding is not "the trigger fired, build the engine" -- it is that condition 3, read at the letter OD-WORKFLOW-002 wrote it, is now trivially satisfiable by any single tool-dispatching executor regardless of whether it ever produces a result, which is not the substance the record's own reasoning was reaching for (a first real instance "to check a shared task/result protocol against"). Leaving the condition worded that loosely risks a future session reading "a real executor exists" and starting the WF-009..012 engine on the strength of one half-protocol, one-executor-kind instance. This record re-surveys all three conditions against the live tree, finds none has produced a genuine second increment yet, and sharpens condition 3's wording with the evidence this audit found, the same self-correcting discipline OD-WORKFLOW-001 already used twice on its own first-increment plan.
items.done_when: docs/records/OD-WORKFLOW-004-the-first-real-agent-executor-still-has-no-real-workresult-so-wf-006s-trigger-is-half-fired.md exists, accepted, authority canonical-normative-record, and states: (1) nomos-agent-executor's Execute is a real, shipped executor satisfying condition 3's literal wording, but its own module doc and OD-CONTRACTS-003 both confirm it does not construct a WorkResult, so WF-006's task/result protocol has a real instance only on its task side; (2) grepped directly, WorkResult has zero production construction sites anywhere in the workspace, only its own crate's unit tests; (3) grepped directly, none of WF-006's other three named executor kinds (API-hosted, human, recorded-replay) has any implementation anywhere, only WorkflowStep's own doc comment quoting the list; (4) Run_Gate still has exactly the same two real callers OD-WORKFLOW-002 found, re-verified by grep; (5) Gate still has no phase concept anywhere, re-verified by a word-boundary grep across nomos-gate-orchestration/src and nomos-check-orchestration/src returning zero matches; (6) the finding is therefore that no genuine second increment has yet arrived, and condition 3's wording is sharpened so a future check requires a real WorkResult-producing executor, not merely a real executor, before treating the trigger as fired. crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/OD-WORKFLOW-004.record registers the record's path so it is governing. docs/records/OD-WORKFLOW-002-the-workflow-tiers-second-increment-has-not-arrived-since-runids-first-consumer-shipped.md is amended in place: version bumped to 3, a relates-to relation to OD-WORKFLOW-004 added, and an "Amendment (OD-WORKFLOW-004)" section appended narrating the sharpened condition 3 text, following the exact precedent OD-WORKFLOW-003's own amendment of this same file already set -- narrowing wording, not reversing the prior finding. diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md (both halves plus sidecars) are re-rendered from a clean detached worktree carrying exactly this commit's registered records (per OD-GATE-005) and pass nomos spec freshness --require diagram-set --require domain-specification. No code anywhere in the workspace is touched by this item.

items.title: nomos-lang-go-package: the first real second consumer of nomos-package's generic core
items.why: OD-PACKAGE-006/007 built nomos-package (band 24) as the language-agnostic manifest core specifically so a second language's package crate could depend on it directly rather than on the Rust-specific nomos-lang-package wrapper, and OD-PACKAGE-006's amendment retired waiting for a real second language before trusting that split. Nothing has ever actually built that second consumer. nomos-lang-go existing (P14-LANG-GO-SYNTAX-PROVIDER) supplies the real PROVIDER constant this crate needs to be more than a hypothetical.
items.done_when: A new crate crates/packages/nomos-lang-go-package, band 26 (peer to nomos-lang-package, both wrapping nomos-package's band-24 core), depends on nomos-package directly and never on nomos-lang-package. It invents its own Go version-label domain (mirroring nomos-lang-package's RustEdition, not reusing it), builds its provider allowlist through nomos_package::KnownProviders populated with nomos_lang_go::PROVIDER, and its reader refuses a manifest naming an unlisted provider the same way nomos-lang-package::reader does. A real packages/nomos.lang.go.json manifest exists, the same real corpus role packages/nomos.lang.rust.json already carries, and this crate's own tests round-trip it. README's band table gains its row, bands.rs recognizes band 26 for it, and a fresh public-surface snapshot exists.

ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 already names the work ledger as one of three subsystems whose 'current placement does not prove ownership,' framed as an open disjunction -- 'either repository bootstrap machinery or a generic coordination primitive' -- and explicitly declines to settle which, or to move anything. Fresh evidence bears on that disjunction directly: OD-WORKFLOW-001 and OD-WORKFLOW-002 each had to correct an accidental conflation between nomos-ledger's own Run_Gate_Step and the product's real nomos_gate_orchestration::Run_Gate, meaning the two vocabularies have already collided by name-fragment accident and been explicitly un-conflated twice; nomos-api::work.rs's own module doc frames its ledger-verb exposure as 'a second real caller of orchestration seams nomos-cli otherwise has to itself,' an architectural-seam exercise, not a stated product surface, the same framing check/gate/spec verbs get there. This is new evidence ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001's own open disjunction invites, not yet checked against it.
items.done_when: A new record decides the disjunction ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 left open for the work ledger specifically -- bootstrap machinery or generic coordination primitive, and states which, with the evidence: no product surface (check, gate) depends on nomos-ledger; TaskEnvelope/WorkResult are declared bundling types with no real Workflow engine to converge with; OD-WORKFLOW-001/002's two corrected conflations are evidence the vocabularies must stay apart, not evidence they are converging. Names nomos-api::work.rs's full 11-verb exposure at band 90 as the real trigger to revisit this on, precisely if nomos-api ever becomes a real external product surface rather than a seam-exercise caller. Does not move any file and does not change nomos-ledger's or nomos-work-orchestration's code. spec/domain-specification.md and diagrams/relations.mmd re-rendered from a tree whose registered records are exactly the ones this commit publishes.

items.why: External review's package-materialization framing led to reading ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001's adopted D-091 clause directly rather than trusting ARC-ROADMAP-001's own paraphrase of it. items.title: OD-GATE-018 phase 3: real fixes for check-condition-shape, check-atomic-ordering, and check-error-info's structural exception
items.why: Following P16-EVERYTHINGELSE-CATEGORY1-WAIVERS's test-code sweep, three of phase 3's checks had small, fully-scoped production remainders. check-condition-shape (3, code-shape phase) each named the whole && / || chain as a local predicate -- a caller-invisible extraction. check-atomic-ordering (4, concurrency-and-unsafe phase, one of the thirteen safety-critical checks) are all a per-process AtomicU64 counter used only to make two calls pick different numbers, the exact 'statistics-only counter' case the check's own message names as legitimate -- justified with the in-code // atomic-ordering: allow marker this check honours under the shipped safety-only policy, matching the precedent already in nomos-platform-std/src/launcher/drain.rs. check-error-info's 2 remaining findings (errors phase) are crosslang/reading.rs's Payload_Of, whose caller silently drops an unreadable source by crosslang.rs's own documented design (lines 47-51: reporting an unreadable source is Check_Completeness_Mirrors/Check_Naming_Convention's job, not this rule's) -- threading a Finding through would fabricate diagnostic content this rule intentionally never emits, so it is waived individually citing that design rather than forced into the sibling Payload_Of shape.
items.done_when: check-condition-shape, check-atomic-ordering and check-error-info all report zero findings against crates tests (default run). cargo build --workspace --all-targets stays green. The two check-error-info waivers in suppressions.json name their own reason (crosslang.rs's documented silent-absence design), not the OD-GATE-018 category-1 test-code reason.

items.title: OD-GATE-018 phase 3: check-trailing-whitespace fixed and check-explicit-return's divergent-tail false positive waived
items.why: formatting phase's check-trailing-whitespace (2 findings, both in crates/spec/nomos-spec-bundle/src/row.rs) took the tool's own --fix cleanly. check-explicit-return (6 findings) all turned out to be the same shape: a tail-position match or loop where every reachable arm already exits via its own explicit return, so the construct as a whole diverges. Applying the tool's own --fix (wrapping each in an outer return) and rebuilding produced five real rustc unreachable_code warnings -- confirmed, then reverted -- because an outer return over an already-fully-divergent match/loop is redundant, not a fix. All six are waived individually with that reasoning; per-arm return already gives this check's own stated goal (a visible return-point landmark).
items.done_when: check-trailing-whitespace and check-explicit-return both report zero findings against crates tests (default run). cargo build --workspace --all-targets produces no new warnings relative to before this item (in particular, no unreachable_code warnings). git diff for crates/spec/nomos-spec-bundle/src/row.rs touches only trailing whitespace.

items.title: OD-GATE-018 phase 3: close check-closure-bounds and check-lifetime-discipline
items.why: concurrency-and-unsafe's check-closure-bounds (5) and check-lifetime-discipline (1) are neither test code nor one of the thirteen safety-critical checks whose in-code marker this repository's safety-only policy honours -- two of the six findings already carried an in-code // rust-closure: allow / // rust-lifetime: allow marker that check.exe reported as not honoured. All six bounds are structurally required (Send by std::thread::scope(..).spawn(..) in nomos-ledger's interleaving test harness and by std::thread::spawn in nomos-platform-std's Drain::Reading; Fn as the minimal, deliberately-chosen bound in tests/integration/src/verification.rs's Verify), so each is waived in suppressions.json with its own reason, per OD-GATE-018's stated remedy for an unhonoured marker (move it to the ledger). The two ineffective in-code markers were reworded as plain comments pointing at the waiver, so a reader does not mistake them for working suppressions.

items.why: P16-EVERYTHINGELSE-CATEGORY1-WAIVERS's test-code classification only recognized an inline #[cfg(test)] mod tests { } block in the same file as the finding. This workspace also declares whole sibling files as test-only via #[cfg(test)] mod X; in a parent file (38 such declarations found under crates/, e.g. nomos-api's src/work.rs declaring #[cfg(test)] mod tests_support;, or nomos-spec-store's lib.rs declaring #[cfg(test)] mod registration; over a file whose own doc comment says 'the library itself never calls' it). Re-running the five checks phase 3 has already measured against this corrected file set found 23 findings that were counted as production remainder but are actually file-scoped test code: check-vertical-organization 93->92, check-allman-braces 55->50, check-closing-brace 45->40, check-tuple-return 9->4, check-error-values 8->1 (7 of those 8 were nomos-api's tests_support.rs, the same file already read while triaging check-error-info).

items.title: OD-GATE-018 phase 3: close check-panic-primitives, finishing concurrency-and-unsafe
items.why: check-panic-primitives (24 findings, one of the thirteen safety-critical checks whose in-code marker this repository's safety-only policy honours) flagged every unreachable!/panic! this workspace has in production reach, and every single one already carried its invariant in prose -- 19 nomos-api handlers share one unreachable!("Run always returns the ... variant naming the ... it was given") after destructuring WorkOutcome/SpecOutcome, and the remaining five (tests/contract's module_tree.rs, tests/integration's slice.rs x2, slice/dispatch.rs, slice/edit.rs) already had a full explanatory comment right beside the panic. None needed a code change: check-panic-primitives does not read a panic!'s own message string or a plain comment as satisfying it, only the // rust-panic: allow: <reason> marker syntax, so each site's existing reasoning was promoted into that marker (word-for-word where a comment already existed, restated concisely for the 19 handlers whose reasoning lived only inside the unreachable! string). This closes concurrency-and-unsafe (check-borrowing/move-out-of-mut/closure-bounds/lifetime-discipline/smart-pointer/channels/async-blocking/lock-across-await/blocking-under-lock/atomic-ordering/panic-primitives/drop-panics/unsafe-justification/unsafe-send-sync/ffi/sql-injection/secret-in-url/hardcoded-secret/tls-verification/boundary-in-loop all now report zero).
items.done_when: check-panic-primitives reports zero findings against crates tests (default run). cargo build --workspace --all-targets stays green. cargo test -p nomos-api, -p nomos-contract-tests and -p nomos-integration-tests all pass. No production behavior changes -- every edit is a comment.

items.title: Decide: a rule's parameters are a fact a repository declares, not a compiled constant
items.why: Every casing/threshold rule in nomos-rules hardcodes its convention in Rust while standards.json already declares a schema-validated naming block nothing reads, and two shipped Go casing rules drifted from the exact vocabulary their own rule id names (upper-snake vs screaming-snake, confirmed against code-standards' own case_validation.go). The user asked for rules to be generalized/multidimensional rather than hardcoded.
items.done_when: OD-RULES-011 is registered, its markdown round-trips through the store, and both diagram-set and domain-specification projections are re-rendered and fresh against the record set this commit publishes.

verified.output_tail:
are each their own future instance of this same
decision, not decided here.

It does not give `nomos-rules` general file-system access or a second way to read
`standards.json` outside the capability/provider seam `OD-RULES-010` already established —
a rule still takes only `&[SourceFile]` and a `FactReader`, per `crates/rules/nomos-rules/
src/lib.rs`'s own stated invariant, and the provider is still the only place in this
increment that touches a path.

It does not compose the new provider into `nomos-check-orchestration::Run`. Several rules
in this crate already ship additive and unwired for one build cycle before composition
follows (`Check_Declared_Role_Matches_Surface`, `Check_Cross_Language_Correspondence` at
their own first landing); this capability follows the same sequencing, as its own later
item.

It does not decide anything about a repository that declares a case style outside the
eight code-standards names — such a value is a load error at the provider, the same
"a casing scheme this check cannot read is one it would silently ignore" refusal code-
standards' own `spec.go` already states for the identical reason.

items.title: OD-RULES-011 v2: how a rule reacts to an absent optional capability
items.why: Designing the casing-rule refactor onto nomos.cap.naming.policy surfaced a real gap in OD-RULES-011 v1: it never said how a rule should react when the capability is unconfigured or unwired. OD-CAPABILITY-004 already decided the general question (an absent optional capability must never be reported through Applicability); v2 cites it rather than re-deciding it, so the six-rule refactor has a settled read-side contract to implement against.
items.done_when: OD-RULES-011 is at version 2, its markdown round-trips through the store, and both diagram-set and domain-specification projections are re-rendered and fresh against the record set this commit publishes.

n stated invariant, and the provider is still the only place in this

Thirteen text-only rules (no FactReader, taking only sources) were candidates; checked against a real gate run --root . over this tree first, three (no-decorative-section-dividers, unwrap-expect-discipline, panics-are-justified-documented-and-validated) currently produce 71 real Blocking findings across this repository and wiring them in now would turn every session's Rules step red. The other ten are already clean.
items.done_when: nomos-check-orchestration::run_context::RULE_COUNT rises from 8 to 18, composing NO_TRAILING_WHITESPACE, TODO_FORMAT, DEPRECATION, A_RUST_PATH_STAYS_WITHIN_ITS_OWN_SUBTREE, SHARED_INTERIOR_MUTABILITY_SAYS_WHY, EVERY_ALLOW_CARRIES_A_JUSTIFICATION, UNSAFE_JUSTIFICATION, SCRIPTS_USE_A_PORTABLE_SHEBANG, A_SCRIPT_DECLARES_ITS_PURPOSE and NO_MOD_RS_FILES; a real gate run --root . over this repository (nomos-cli's Test_Host_Variant_Should_Compose_Into_A_Real_Run_That_Judges_This_Workspaces_Own_Tree) still passes with the ten newly composed; and cargo test -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-cli --lib --bins passes. Deliberately out of scope: composing the three rules this tree currently violates (a separate, larger repository-wide cleanup, not a wiring task), and updating nomos-gate-orchestration::Registered to report these ten -- the same check::Run-wiring-precedes-Gate-registration split OD-GATE-019-REGISTRY-COHERENCE followed (P13-DEPENDENCY-WIRE-1 composed DEPENDENCY_DIRECTION into Run; P13-GATE-REGISTRY-THIRD-RULE registered it with Gate later, as a separate item).

items.title: Import the error-message text hygiene family into a new error_text.rs
items.why: Three code-standards Rust error-handling rules decidable from raw text: lowercase-first-letter and no-trailing-punctuation (one Go tool, check-error-message, judging a #[error("...")] attribute's message content) and eager-vs-lazy-context (check-context-laziness, judging a same-line .With_Context(...) call whose argument allocates). Real breadth -- nothing already converted touches Display-message wording or Result-context allocation timing. Scoped narrower than the Go tool in one respect: the Go tool also judges write!/writeln! literals inside a hand-written impl Display block via real parsing, which this crate's text-only convention cannot soundly bound without brace-depth block tracking this crate has consistently declined to build (the same choice already made for concurrency_text's file-level test exemption) -- left unattempted rather than guessed at, matching the deprecation rule's own same-line-only precedent.

items.why: Nine rule modules decide their own applicability by sniffing file extensions -- go_text.rs (Is_Go_Source), naming/go_data_names.rs, naming/go_function_names.rs, naming/go_type_names.rs, rust_text.rs, concurrency_text.rs, placement.rs, structure.rs and function_shape.rs all match on .go or .rs or call extension(). nomos-rules deliberately names no language crate: its Cargo.toml argues at length that a rule states a capability floor and the registry chooses who answers it, and OD-CAPABILITY-009 kept SourceFile::preferred_syntax_provider opaque for the same reason -- the three call sites that read it pass it straight to Syntax_Requirement_For and never compare it to a provider identity. So a text-only rule that must apply to Go alone has no non-regressing way to ask the question today: sniffing the extension is a second answer to a convention the composition root owns, and comparing preferred_syntax_provider against nomos_lang_go::PROVIDER would put a band-30 rule back in the business of knowing which languages exist. An external review flagged the sniffing on 2026-09-01; it did not notice that the obvious fix is the thing OD-CAPABILITY-009 rejected. The count is what makes this worth deciding rather than tolerating: it was one module and is now nine.

items.title: Whether a repo-tooling verb may be projected through the band-90 API host
items.why: README lines 34-36 mark four rows [repo tooling] -- nomos-ledger, nomos-work-orchestration, nomos-spec-orchestration and nomos-surface-provenance -- and say they exist to run this repository, not to answer a question an end-user repository would ask Nomos. nomos-api sits at band 90 and now projects work (List, Show, Validate, Audit) and spec (Profiles and further verbs) beside gate. Its own module doc gives a coherent reason: it exists as a second real caller, proving Run_Gate, nomos_work_orchestration::Run and nomos_spec_orchestration are genuinely callable without nomos-cli, which is a real architecture test and was the stated point of the crate. So this is not obviously a defect. But nothing in the workspace records which of those two readings governs, and the two disagree about what nomos-api is: a seam prover may freely reach repo tooling, whereas the product API named in ARC-ROADMAP-001 CLI/API/MCP projections may not without dissolving the distinction README just drew. An external review read the crate the second way on 2026-09-01 and called it product surface leaking repository infrastructure. The question is cheap to answer now and expensive once a transport exists and the projected verbs have external callers.

items.title: Route the spec-commit rename vacate through nomos-platform rather than raw std::fs
items.why: nomos-spec-orchestration::run::commit calls std::fs::remove_file directly to unlink the old path a record rename vacated, and both its module doc and VacateOutcome say so on purpose. The stated reason is not architectural: it is that nomos_platform::FileSystem declares three operations (read, atomically replace, exists) and "extending nomos-platform is out of this crate territory". That is a territory constraint on whoever wrote it, not a finding that the port should stay small -- so the half-abstraction persists because no item ever reserved both crates at once, which is exactly the kind of gap the ledger can close by reserving them together. The consequence is real and already written down in the code: a failed unlink leaves two files declaring one record (VacateOutcome::Failed), on a path the platform seam otherwise exists to make testable and swappable. An external review flagged it on 2026-09-01 as an abstraction leak; it did not notice the doc already concedes the point and names the reason.

items.title: OD-RULES-014 put the carried language type in the wrong crate
items.why: OD-RULES-014 constraint 2 says the carried type lives in nomos-contracts, the way RuleId and ProviderId do. Implementing it exposed that this fails nomos-contracts own admission test. OD-CONTRACTS-001 admits a type when it crosses a subsystem, process or plugin boundary and the parties on both sides need one stable shared representation, and its stated deciding question is whether a peer that never compiles the crate would be unable to agree with us without it. Nothing exchanges a language identifier with a peer today: nomos_package::PackageManifest carries language_versions but no language name, so a LanguagePackage manifest does not declare which language it is for. The parties that must agree are the three language crates, nomos-rules and nomos-check-orchestration, all inside this workspace. That is exactly the worked counter-example nomos-contracts own module doc gives for refusing a type: nomos-cap-syntax SyntaxPayload is a real shared representation read by more than one provider, and it lives at band 23 rather than band 0 because the parties that must agree are the providers of one capability rather than every peer that speaks to Nomos. A language identity has the same shape. It is also measurably free to put it at band 23: all five parties already depend on nomos-cap-syntax, so the move adds no dependency edge at all. No mechanical test catches this, which is why it needs a record rather than a silent correction.

items.title: Carry a language on SourceFile and delete the eleven private extension classifiers
items.why: OD-RULES-014 as amended decided the mechanism and its Status says the implementing change needs its own item. Third scoping of that item: -1 reserved nomos-contracts before the amendment moved the type to nomos-cap-syntax, and -2 reserved the eleven classifier sites without the two files the change provably also needs. checks/naming.rs holds the Source test helper that five Go naming tests use, and they fail once the rules stop sniffing extensions because the fixture never sets the carried field. composition.rs holds Recognized_Syntax_Provider, the one function that recognizes a path against every registered provider, and language recognition belongs beside it -- putting it in run_context.rs instead would be the second answer to one convention that this whole record exists to remove. Both were found by building and running, not by reading.
items.done_when: nomos-cap-syntax exposes the opaque carried language type; nomos-lang-rust, nomos-lang-rust-scan and nomos-lang-go each declare a LANGUAGE constant beside PROVIDER, the two Rust crates declaring the same value; nomos_rules::SourceFile carries the field and nomos-check-orchestration populates it in the same enrichment pass that sets preferred_syntax_provider, recognizing the language beside Recognized_Syntax_Provider rather than in a second place; all eleven classifiers are deleted and their call sites compare the carried field, with FunctionAritySource::Extension becoming a language variant; nomos-rules/Cargo.toml gains no language-crate dependency; a test proves the language names nomos-rules states agree with what the language crates declare, since nomos-rules cannot depend on them to check; and every affected surface snapshot is re-blessed.

items.title: Thread a FileSystem port through Run/Run_Gate, and wire naming-policy materialization as its first consumer
items.why: OD-RULES-011's four capability families (naming/limits/scripting/words) are library-complete but nomos-check-orchestration::RunContext has no FileSystem port at all -- only ProcessLauncher -- so no rule package's own facts.Require for its policy capability ever succeeds in a real run; every one silently falls back to its hardcoded default (OD-CAPABILITY-004's optional-capability design working exactly as designed, just against a fact nobody ever offers). nomos_repo_standards::Materialize_Workspace (and the limits/scripting/words siblings) all need a FileSystem to read standards.json. This is one shared prerequisite for all four, not four independent ones -- confirmed with a peer session already mid-scope on limits/scripting/words, who is deliberately waiting on this rather than risk an incompatible RunContext shape. Landing naming's own Declare+Materialize wiring in the same item proves the new port has a real consumer rather than shipping an unread field.
items.done_when: RunContext and GateEnvironment both carry a Fs: FileSystem generic and a filesystem field, threaded through Run/RunEnvironment/MaterializationEnvironment/Materialize_Capabilities in nomos-check-orchestration and through Judged_Sources/Run_Gate/Explain_Gate in nomos-gate-orchestration, with nomos-cli::check.rs/gate.rs and nomos-api's two gate response call sites supplying nomos_platform_std::StdFileSystem and every test call site (nomos-check-orchestration's tests.rs/run_seam.rs, nomos-gate-orchestration's tests.rs/check_orchestration_seam.rs) updated to pass one. A new Declare_Naming_Policy_Capability offers nomos_repo_standards against nomos_cap_naming_policy in composition.rs, and a new Materialize_Naming_Policy call (gated on any of NAMING_CONVENTION/DATA_NAMES_STAY_LOWER_SNAKE/EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS_USE_UPPER_SNAKE_CASE/UNEXPORTED_FUNCTIONS_LOWERCASE_ONLY_THE_FIRST_LETTER/TYPES_USE_UPPER_CAMEL_CASE_LOWER_CAMEL_CASE being selected) writes the fact into the store before those rules run, with a new integration test proving a real standards.json naming override actually changes a real Run's findings (not just that the plumbing compiles). Both crates' public surface snapshots re-blessed, and cargo test -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-gate-orchestration -p nomos-cli -p nomos-api passes.

Declined.reason: territory list omitted crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/src/tests.rs, which also constructs RunContext directly (14 call sites) -- re-adding with it included

items.title: An MCP projection fires OD-LEDGER-036 and OD-HOST-006's shared trigger, reopening what nomos-api may project
items.why: AGT-006.assessment is the only requirement assessment in the registry that calls its gap total: 'MCP tools is a clean, total gap: nomos-api's own module doc states outright it does not read argv, listen on a socket, or speak MCP's JSON-RPC framing, and no MCP transport or tool surface exists anywhere in the workspace.' ARC-ROADMAP-001 names CLI/API/MCP projections as a near-term-tier item, not a proposal. OD-ROADMAP-001 already licenses building ahead of a caller. It blocks more than its own crate: work finish runs the gate lint step and then the item's predicate, so any item whose predicate names -p nomos-cli cannot finish while this is red, whatever it changed. It refused OD-LEDGER-AMENDS-PATH-ECHOED-VERBATIM-2, whose own five files carry no finding. The census by rule, since the shape matters more than the total: file-name-matches-declared-type is 53 of the 78 Blocking findings, parameter-count 7, scripts-use-a-portable-shebang 3, every-allow-carries-a-justification 3, a-script-declares-its-purpose 3, todo-format 2, data-names-stay-lower-snake 2, unsafe-justification 1, relaxed-not-used-when-ordering-matters 1. The dominant rule is mostly right: only 4 of its 53 are tests/corpus fixtures it should exempt, and the other 49 are real workspace files whose declared type does not match their stem. items.title: Compose nomos.cap.limits.policy and nomos.cap.scripting.policy into Run
items.why: Five OD-RULES-011 families have a contract and a provider; composition.rs declares only naming's. Six rules already composed into Rule_Findings read the other two capabilities and get nothing back. items.title: file-name-matches-declared-type disagrees with the OD-RULES-011 family layout ten times over
items.why: Measured 2026-09-01 and confirmed independently by a second session. Ten of the 48 remaining file-name-matches-declared-type findings are one repeated layout, not ten independent misnamings: five crates/capabilities/nomos-cap-<X>-policy/src/payload.rs each declaring <X>PolicyPayload, three of them also declaring Refusal, and five crates/repository/nomos-repo-<X>/src/reading.rs each declaring <X>PolicyError. Every OD-RULES-011 family lands this way, so the rule and the family layout disagree as a matter of design, and each new family adds two more findings. An early reading held that splitting these types into per-type files would break the one-public-type-per-module property the surface snapshot depends on; that reading was retracted after checking. The real constraint is that a type's public functions, inherent and trait impls alike, must stay in the module the pub use route names -- moving a type together with its impls is safe, and these payload types are derive-only structs with no inherent impls. Check_One_Public_Type_Per_File is in this rule set and would want the split. So the argument for the layout is the five families' coherence, which is a real argument but a much weaker one than a mechanical constraint, and it is the argument this item has to weigh.
items.done_when: Either the ten files carry one public type each and the findings are gone, or the layout is exempted in the rule with its reason recorded, or the disagreement is declined with a reason naming which of the two authorities gives way. Whichever is chosen holds for the next family without a further decision. cargo test -p nomos-rules is green and tests/contract/surface snapshots are unchanged or reblessed with the change that moved them.

Declined.reason: Superseded by P27-SELFCHECK-FILENAME-FAMILY-LAYOUT-2, which reserves the rule file and the record the decision needs. The measurement is unchanged and is carried over.

abandoned.reason: Territory is the ten family files, but the remedy the measurement supports is a change to the rule, in crates/rules/nomos-rules/src/checks/naming/file_names.rs, plus a record. Neither is reserved here. Re-added as -2 with the territory the decision actually reaches.

items.title: Check_Abbreviations judges trait-impl method names the author cannot rename
items.why: Measured before composing the rule into a real run: an approximation over this workspace's declarations reports about 165 findings, and 104 of them are the single word fmt -- the required method name of core::fmt::Display, which no author picks and none can change without abandoning the trait. Ten more are impl and six are fn, the same shape. code-standards' own sibling check-generic-parameter-name states the carve-out this rule is missing in as many words: the one thing it skips is a declaration whose name was not the author's, because a trait that fixes its implementers' shape also fixes what they may call things. Until that carve-out exists, composing Check_Abbreviations into nomos-check-orchestration::Run would add roughly a hundred findings nothing can act on, which is why OD-RULES-011-COMPOSE-GOALS deliberately leaves the words family unwired: materializing nomos.cap.words.policy for a rule that cannot be composed would be wiring a fact nobody reads.
items.done_when: Check_Abbreviations does not report a name declared inside an impl block that serves a trait, distinguishing it from an inherent impl through the TRAIT/INHERENT shape nomos-cap-syntax already records on the enclosing impl item -- the payload carries the distinction on the block rather than on its members, so the rule has to correlate a member with the block that encloses it. A unit test covers a trait-impl member being skipped and an inherent-impl member of the same qualified name still being judged, and cargo test -p nomos-rules is green.

items.why: 85477f14 composed the rule and declared sdk, std and str approved, which leaves 42 Blocking findings over 36 names in the self-check. They are not 42 renames and should not be batch-renamed. Reading them rather than counting them, roughly two thirds are names that quote a term they are about -- Check_Eager_Vs_Lazy_Context is a rule about eager versus lazy, Check_No_Mod_Rs_Files is about .rs files, SENSITIVE_URL_PARAMS is about URL parameters, CHK_003 is a requirement identifier, and others quote Rust itself: Rc, core::cmp::Ordering, the env shebang, LF line endings, ms for milliseconds. Renaming those would make them worse. The rest would genuinely read better spelled out -- Temp_Dir, Temp_Db and TempWorkspace across five test files, Doc and Docs where documentation is meant, len, and a Stds that looks like a slip. The repository owner has already ruled that vs, rs, chk, rc and the banned truncations are not to be approved as words, so the answer for the first group is not the words capability either; it is either a narrower rule or an accepted cost, and that is the decision this item exists to take.

items.title: Check_Abbreviations still blocks 30 findings that quote a term they are about, and the exemption to narrow it is not obvious
items.why:
The 11 findings P27-SELFCHECK-ABBREVIATION-FINDINGS's own territory could reach are renamed and committed (e3c091ca); it was declined once spent. These 30 remain, all in crates/rules/nomos-rules (error_text.rs, structure.rs, security_text.rs, concurrency_text.rs, script_discipline.rs, rust_text.rs), tests/contract/tests/requirement_trace/committed.rs, crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust/tests/corpus/claims.rs, crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/tests/{submission/tests.rs,governing_records_are_present/supersession.rs}, crates/spec/nomos-spec-project/tests/projections/determinism.rs, crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust-deny/tests/integration_seams.rs and crates/agent/nomos-agent-executor-claude-code/src/agent_execution_outcome.rs -- none reserved here, since which of them a rule change can even reach is exactly the open question.

Unlike Check_Abbreviations' two existing exemptions (a trait-fixed method name, a use-binding naming another crate's declaration), none of these 30 is a name the author did not choose -- every one is a freely-authored test/const/struct name that happens to contain a banned or vowelless word because that word is what the code is about. That is a fuzzier category with no existing structural signal to key an exemption on, which is why this is a decision and not a mechanical extension of OD-RULES-015/016's precedent.

Roughly six shapes, by inspection of the 2026-09-02 run:
- CHK_003 (3 findings, committed.rs): quotes a fixed external requirement id.
- Vs / Eager_Vs_Lazy (7, error_text.rs): a rule's own canonical name, quoted by its own derived test names.
- Rs / Mod_Rs (5, structure.rs): a rule about the .rs extension, same shape as Vs.
- param/params / SENSITIVE_URL_PARAMS (4, security_text.rs): may in fact be a safe, ordinary rename (PARAMETERS) with no semantic cost -- not obviously in the "leave alone" class the other five are.
- Rc, cmp::Ordering, an env shebang, LF, duration_ms, Nth (7, scattered): each quotes a std type, a POSIX convention, a line-ending term, an established _ms suffix convention, or an ordinary English ordinal.
- Docs/Doc quoting "doc comment", Rust's own term of art (4, claims.rs/supersession.rs/concurrency_text.rs): same shape as Rc.

Checked whether "accepted cost" (a waiver) is available instead of a rule change: it is not. crates/host/nomos-cli/src/gate/parsing.rs:120-123 states plainly that no flag authors a Suppression, a BaselineDebt or a RuleCalibration yet, and hardcodes SuppressionPolicy::default() -- nomos_gate_orchestration::SuppressionPolicy/Suppression/SuppressionDisposition exist and are tested in isolation, but nothing in this workspace can apply one to a real finding today. Building that CLI surface is a real increment of its own, not a substitute for this decision, and OD-GATE-015's suppression/baseline/adoption records (already Accepted) may already cover deciding whether it should exist -- worth reading before assuming it needs a fourth record.

Check_Abbreviations (or a caller) changes to match, with a test proving each side (matching OD-RULES-016's own "two tests hold the two sides" pattern). cargo test -p nomos-rules is green. Whatever is left unaddressed by the record is either a plain rename (if the decision concludes one is safe, e.g. the param/params group) executed at its own site, or is named explicitly as still open with a reason, not left silently unequal to the other 29.
