items.title: Superseded mechanisms are kept beside their replacements and narrated as increments
items.why: Several of the most mature modules describe themselves as a sequence of increments, and the gate crate is the clearest case: an old mechanism, a transitional one, and a current one all still present and all still reachable. That narration is valuable history and it belongs in the decision records, which already exist for these choices. What should not persist is the code: a compatibility layer nobody needs is a second way to get an answer, and a reader cannot tell which path is authoritative. A consolidation pass after a concept has survived several increments is what stops the architecture becoming a museum of its own stages.
items.done_when: In the gate crate, every mechanism a later increment superseded is deleted rather than left reachable, module documentation describes the current design rather than its history, the history it removes is present in the governing records, and no test still exercises a path no caller can reach.

Declined.reason: OD-GATE-023. No superseded reachable mechanism is found in nomos-gate-orchestration; the one candidate, the post-hoc rule filter, is redundant rather than superseded. The half of its done_when that is real, module documentation describing history rather than the current design, is now governed by OD-AGENT-004, which decided it on a measured population of fifteen stale sites.

items.title: Build-everything and finish-the-seam-first now disagree, and nothing says which wins
items.why: OD-ROADMAP-001 retired the population-of-zero caution and licensed building ahead of consumers, and that licence has been reaffirmed repeatedly. The architectural review now asks for the opposite in three named places: no new model-routing vocabulary, no new gate policy increments, and no further one-off capability orchestration until the planner seam exists. These are not the same question and both can be right, which is exactly why the board should not be left to resolve them by whichever item somebody claims next. The distinction worth recording is that OD-ROADMAP-001 answers whether a thing may be built before it has consumers, while this answers whether it may be built before the mechanism it will have to be rewritten onto exists.
items.done_when: A record decides how the build-ahead licence and the finish-the-seam-first constraint compose, names which of the two governs each of model routing, gate policy and capability orchestration, states what unblocks the paused work, and amends OD-ROADMAP-001 so the two records do not have to be read against each other.

items.title: Nothing constructs a non-empty suppression, baseline, adoption or coverage policy
items.why: The internal semantics of suppressions, baselines, adoption and calibration, and coverage are real and tested, but GateCommand documents repeatedly that nothing builds a non-empty one. A policy that only ever arrives empty is a policy nobody can use, and the tests that exercise it are exercising a shape no caller can reach. What is missing is the authoring and configuration surface: a declared, readable source a real run resolves these four policies from, so that suppressing a finding, adopting a baseline, or demanding a coverage floor is something a person can express rather than something only a unit test constructs. Sequenced after the gate selection collapse so that policy authoring is written against one resolved run plan rather than against the transitional two-selection design.
items.done_when: A real gate run resolves all four policies from a declared configuration source rather than from defaults, a non-default coverage floor and at least one suppression and one baseline entry are exercised end to end, and GateCommand no longer documents that nothing constructs a non-empty policy.

Declined.reason: Stranded behind P41-GATE-SELECTION-COLLAPSE, which is itself stranded behind the declined P41-RUN-PLANNER. That dependency is inherited rather than load-bearing, confirmed with nomos-dd who held the OD-RULES-009 recheck: constructing a non-empty suppression, baseline, adoption or coverage policy needs a readable configuration source and a resolver, and neither needs a resolved analysis DAG. The original sequencing note said policy authoring should be written against one resolved run plan rather than the transitional two-selection design, but OD-RULES-009 declines the planner across eight rounds, so waiting for it means waiting forever. Re-added as -3 with no dependency. Territory also corrected. The original reserved gate_command.rs and policy.rs only, which cannot satisfy its own done_when: the four no-constructor doc claims are spread across gate_command.rs and the four policy type files, Run_Gate lives in gate_environment.rs, an end-to-end exercise belongs in tests.rs, a file shape needs serde in the crate manifest and a new module, the public surface snapshot must be re-blessed, and nomos-api-transport gate_parameters.rs carries a doc that names this very item as the reason it omits four wire fields.

items.title: Declared phases, thresholds and approvals are named as unbuilt WF-001 gate semantics
items.why: The gate module names declared phases, thresholds and approvals among the parts of WF-001 it does not implement. A gate today is one undifferentiated pass over every selected rule: there is no way to say that one group of checks must pass before another is even attempted, no numeric threshold a run is judged against, and no approval that a human or an agent supplies to let a run proceed despite a finding. These are what turn a gate from a single verdict into a policy a team can adopt incrementally. Sequenced after the gate selection collapse, since a phase is a partition of the selected rule set and partitioning a set that is resolved in two places would inherit that ambiguity.
items.done_when: A gate run can declare ordered phases whose later phases do not run when an earlier one fails, judge a numeric threshold, and record an approval that changes a disposition, each covered by a test and each reachable from the gate orchestration seam.

Declined.reason: OD-GATE-023. Re-authored as P40-GATE-PHASES-APPROVALS-3 without the planner dependency. The item stated its own sequencing reason: a phase partitions the selected rule set, and partitioning a set resolved in two places would inherit that ambiguity. OD-GATE-017 resolved selection in one place, so the condition this item set for itself is met.

items.title: Five TaskEnvelope fields are accepted and ignored, so the contract is ahead of enforcement
items.why: TaskEnvelope carries goal, scope, knowledge_context, applicable_rules, prohibited_changes, available_tools, expected_output_schema and effort. The Claude Code executor consumes goal and effort and documents that it accepts and ignores the other five, matching what OD-EXECUTOR-001 already found. So an executor is bounded by a fresh isolated working directory, a tool allow-list, one turn, a budget ceiling and a timeout, all of which are real, but not by anything the task itself declared: scope does not constrain what it can reach, prohibited_changes does not contain what it may not touch, available_tools does not shape its capability surface, and applicable_rules bounds neither its context nor its validation. The code is commendably explicit that these do not work yet, which is why this is a gap to close rather than a defect to report.

items.title: A requirement assessment can contradict the tree for weeks and nothing notices
items.why: Found by hand, and it is the motivating case rather than a hypothetical. The committed assessment of AGT-001 says no single typed envelope bundles goal, scope, prohibited changes, tools and output schema into one artifact. TaskEnvelope has carried exactly those since 2026-08-24, in a commit named P13-AGT-001-002-TASK-ENVELOPE-WORK-RESULT, and its own test says it closes AGT-001. The assessment was last touched on 2026-09-01 by a sweep that fixed 72 stale citations across 26 assessment files and did not catch this one, because that sweep checked whether cited paths still exist and not whether the prose still holds. A ledger item was then authored on the false premise, which is the cost. Nomos already has the shape that would catch it: a declared claim plus an observed fact judged by a rule. The trace is the declared claim and the tree is the fact.
items.done_when: A rule judges committed requirement assessments against the tree they describe, reports an assessment whose cited sites or gaps no longer match what is there, the AGT-001 case is caught by it, and the rule is composed into a real run rather than only unit tested.

items.title: Nomos has no editor surface, and the backend it would project already exists
items.why: There is no language server anywhere in this workspace. That is the largest missing presentation surface, and the important point is what it should not be: not another analyzer. Facts, rules, findings, declared architecture, requirements, work state and evidence all already exist behind canonical services, so an editor surface is a projection and a transport over them. What it buys that no ordinary linter can is the walk outward from a diagnostic: which rule governs it, which facts support it, which requirement and which architectural component it belongs to, how strong the evidence is, and what correction is available. One current design point must survive the crossing: LintDiagnostic deliberately carries only the tool reported line and refuses to invent an editor-grade span, so precise locations are combined at projection time from the language provider rather than by widening that fact contract.
items.done_when: A language server exposes Nomos findings as diagnostics over canonical services with no analysis logic of its own, a diagnostic can be walked to its governing rule, supporting facts and subject, the LintDiagnostic contract is unchanged, and the server is a thin adapter that owns no product semantics.

Declined.reason: declared territory (a single crates/host/nomos-lsp/src/lib.rs) was too narrow for a new crate, and investigation found two of the five walk-outward targets the item's own done_when named (supporting facts, the requirement link) are OD-HOST-003's own two open gaps from before nomos-check-orchestration had a caller-callable Run, unclosed since. Reauthored as P42-LSP-PROJECTION-2 with the complete territory and a scope that builds the three targets that are real (governing rule, architectural component, available correction) while OD-HOST-010 records the other two as undecided rather than forced.

items.title: Dependency direction is the only declared-architecture rule, and authority has none
items.why: Check_Dependency_Direction already proves the shape this system is for: a declared architecture beside an observed fact, judged into a finding. Nothing else uses it. Two authority questions are the nearest and most valuable extensions, and both are things this repository has already been bitten by in prose rather than mechanically. Declared component ownership against the actual public and dependency surface answers whether a component owns what it claims. A declared service authority against observed mutation paths answers whether a second write door exists, which is exactly the property nomos-store was built around and which nothing currently checks. These belong as additional rules over existing facts, not as a parallel architecture-analysis subsystem.
items.done_when: Two rules judge declared ownership against the observed surface and declared write authority against observed mutation paths, both read facts that already exist or a fact family added for them, both are composed into a real run, and their finding counts over this workspace are measured before composition rather than after.

Declined.reason:
Investigated both halves before writing code. Write authority is real and buildable: only
nomos-workspace depends on nomos-store today (grepped every Cargo.toml and every real
import site), and Check_Dependency_Direction already reads the one fact
(nomos.cap.dependency.edges) a write-door allow-list check would need -- no new fact
family, no new wiring beyond composing a third rule the way the first two already are.

Ownership is not ready. The only concrete, checkable reading of "declared ownership against
the actual public and dependency surface" -- no two crates define a same-named top-level
type -- was checked directly against every committed surface snapshot: Refusal is
independently defined in nine different crates, Visibility/Scope/Reading/PayloadRefusal/
Member/ManifestError/ItemKind/Item/Disposition each in three. This is ordinary, idiomatic
Rust naming, not drift -- a rule built on this reading would report roughly two dozen false
positives on its first real run. Nothing in this workspace declares ownership as a
structured claim to check a real fact against (README's own Owns column is prose,
OD-PROJECT-001 already decided it stays hand-authored for exactly that reason), so
"decided" here would mean inventing the declaration format under this item's own single-file
territory rather than deciding it as its own question first.

Declining the combined two-rule framing and re-authoring as a decision that closes write
authority concretely and leaves ownership named but undecided, rather than shipping a rule
against a definition already shown wrong or silently dropping half of what was required.

items.title: Nothing judges declared topology against the observed graph, or catches provider representation leaking
items.why: The second pair of declared-architecture rules. Declared topology against the observed call, data and dependency graph is architecture drift, which is the question a band table answers only for direction and not for shape. A canonical provider boundary against actual type flow is representation leakage: a provider specific type reaching a consumer that was promised only the capability contract. This workspace already cares about the second one in prose, which is what makes it a rule rather than a preference, and it is the mechanism that keeps a capability contract from being a boundary only by intention.
items.done_when: Two rules judge declared topology against the observed graph and canonical provider boundaries against actual type flow, both are composed into a real run, and each rule finding count over this workspace is measured before composition so that composing it does not redden the gate by surprise.

Declined.reason: neither rule is buildable against an existing fact: architecture drift needs a call-graph/data-flow capability that does not exist, and representation leakage needs a widened syntax payload or a provider-identity fact nomos-rules cannot read without crossing into the Provider zone. Reauthored as a Decision item citing OD-RULES-024, which measures both gaps directly against the real capability set and surface snapshots.

abandoned.reason: pivoting to build OD-RULES-023's already-decided write-authority rule first, so a decision actually ships as code before this session accumulates a fifth undelivered decision in a row

items.title: Nothing detects the same engineering decision encoded independently in two places
items.why: This is not source duplication, which ordinary tools already find. It is two artifacts that independently determine the same behaviour, where one should have been a projection of the other. This repository has paid for exactly that shape more than once: a band table maintained by hand in three places with a fourth checking it, and a measured figure restated in a comment that then drifted from the guard that declares it. The general class reaches far past code into configuration, schemas, package metadata, generated documentation, editor and agent configuration, and external system mappings. It is a strong candidate for a rule because neither a linter nor a language server has the normative project knowledge to know which of two artifacts is meant to be canonical.
items.done_when: A rule reports two artifacts that independently determine one behaviour where one is declared canonical, at least one real instance in this workspace is found by it, and a declared projection relationship suppresses the finding rather than a per-file exemption.

Declined.reason: not buildable against an existing fact: the nearest mechanism (Check_Completeness_Mirrors) only resolves whether a named check exists, never extracts or compares a value. Duplicate authority needs a value-extraction-from-prose fact, a list-length-as-observed-fact, and an undesigned canonical/projection annotation with its own suppression semantics. Reauthored as a Decision item citing OD-RULES-025, which also records a real live instance: nomos-rules' own rule-count prose (67) disagrees with both DESCRIPTORS.len()/RULE_COUNT (65) and the raw Check_ function count (84).

items.title: A semantic review tool has no capability to answer under, and lint is the wrong shape for it
items.why: The tool-provider seam is already right: a tool produces a fact and a native rule judges it, so no external tool emits a Nomos finding directly. What is missing is a second contract for tools whose output is not lint-shaped. The lint contract is deliberately narrow, carrying level, optional lint identifier, message, repository-relative file and line, and that narrowness is correct for a compiler diagnostic. A semantic review tool such as CodeRabbit can report a multi-file issue, a change-level observation, a suggested correction, pull-request context, a requirement relationship, a review thread and a confidence. Flattening those into the lint payload would destroy them, so the governing rule should hold: normalize to the lowest canonical contract that truthfully represents what the provider produced, rather than normalizing every tool into lint.
items.done_when: A review capability contract carries what a semantic review tool actually produces rather than a lint-shaped subset, at least one provider answers under it, a native rule judges its facts into findings, and nothing about the lint contract changed to accommodate it.

Declined.reason: declared territory (one new crate, nomos-cap-review) presumes the wrong shape. OD-EXECUTOR-006 already decided a CodeRabbit-style tool is connector-shaped (ARC-CONNECTOR-001), not a same-band ToolProvider capability crate, and explicitly deferred the fact-contract question until a second connector exists. A second connector -- nomos-connector-coderabbit, contract+provider+fixture, real gh api integration -- already exists in full on the unmerged track-c-external-kwb branch (commit d85a22a0), 342 dev commits stale (predates the zone migration and crate reorg). Reauthoring as a port-and-adapt item with corrected territory rather than a from-scratch nomos-cap-review crate.

items.title: One agent executor exists, so nothing has shown which of its choices are the contract
items.why: The Claude Code executor is properly bounded: fresh isolated working directory, strict tool configuration, a structural allow-list, one turn, a budget ceiling, timeout and stall handling, and structured parsing rather than trusting prose. A second executor over a richer session or harness runtime, of which Clay is the motivating example, would be an adapter rather than a new execution architecture. Its value is evidence: with one implementation nothing distinguishes what the canonical task contract requires from what one vendor happened to need. It is deliberately sequenced after the envelope constraints and the canonical result, so the second executor is written against the contract as enforced rather than inheriting the first executor accepted-and-ignored fields. A harness executor gets no scheduler authority, no work-graph authority and no rule authority.
items.done_when: A second executor satisfies the same task contract with the same enforced constraints and produces the same canonical result type, what the two implementations disagree about is recorded, and no scheduling, work-graph or rule authority moved into either.

items.title: knowledge_context is a declared field with no acquisition, provenance or promotion path
items.why: TaskEnvelope carries knowledge_context as a list of knowledge references, and the executor ignores it. That field is the anticipated seam to KWB, and the seam being anticipated structurally is genuinely most of the design work, but nothing acquires a context, records where it came from, selects what is relevant to a task, or promotes anything back. ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 is explicit that what a source or a decision claimed is KWB and not Nomos, so this bridge is where the boundary is honoured or quietly crossed. Two committed requirement assessments already name the knowledge reference identifier as their gap.
items.done_when: A task envelope knowledge context is acquired from a real source rather than constructed by a caller, each item carries provenance, selection for a task is a decision the system makes rather than a caller guessing, promotion back across the boundary is either implemented or recorded as refused, and no normative authority moves out of Nomos.

Declined.reason: not buildable: KWB itself has no exposed interface yet. Verified directly against f:/repos/kwb -- every one of its ten crates is an unimplemented scaffold (kwb-cli/kwb-mcp print 'nothing wired yet', kwb-platform-std says 'nothing implemented yet', kwb-contracts stays deliberately empty pending a decision KWB has not made about its own citation-identity shape). D-137 already says 'nothing yet produces or consumes' KnowledgeReferenceId, and ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 states plainly 'no KWB or XVPE integration is implemented, and none is scheduled here.' Building nomos-knowledge-context now would mean inventing both ends of a protocol against a peer that doesn't have one. Reauthored as a Decision item citing OD-EXECUTOR-009, which records promotion as honestly refused (nothing exists to promote) while leaving acquisition and selection blocked on KWB's own progress.

items.title: Every fact family is syntactic, so no rule can ask a question that needs resolved semantics
items.why: The fact substrate is ready for more than it carries: identity, keys, payloads, readers, dependency tracking, invalidation reports, rematerialization groups and condensation all exist and are structural rather than embedded in individual checks. What it holds is syntax, dependency edges, control flow, and two external tool reports. Ownership, borrowing, allocation and escape, effects, and concurrency and synchronization are the families that would let a rule ask a question no syntax scan can answer, and each is provider-neutral in the same way syntax already is. Sequenced after the first compiler-backed provider because these need resolved semantics as their source, and building the family before anything can produce it would be a contract with no provider.
items.done_when: One new semantic fact family from that list is a real capability with a real provider and a declared guarantee, at least one rule judges it and could not have been written without it, and the family is provider-neutral rather than shaped around the one compiler that produces it.

items.title: Every rule judges the tree as it is now, with no runtime evidence and no history
items.why: This is where Nomos can be qualitatively different from static analysis rather than incrementally better at it. A declared zero-allocation path judged against runtime allocation evidence, a performance requirement judged against benchmark history, and a previously removed dependency reappearing as an architectural regression are all the same declared-constraint-plus-observed-fact shape the dependency direction rule already proves, with the observation coming from a run or from the past rather than from the current source. Neither a linter nor a language server can ask these, because neither has the normative project knowledge or the retained history. The fact substrate already carries generations and invalidation, which is most of what a historical claim needs.
items.done_when: A rule judges a declared constraint against evidence from a real run or from retained history rather than from current source, the evidence family it reads is a real capability with a provider, and a regression it reports is reproducible rather than dependent on one machine.

Declined.reason: None of the three worked examples is a real, reproducible, buildable increment today. Runtime allocation evidence and benchmark history each need an evidence-capture category this workspace has zero instance of (no runtime observation port beyond one-shot ProcessLauncher, no benchmarking convention anywhere in Cargo.lock); the first also reaches into territory ARC-ROADMAP-001 already deferred on purpose (runtime/debug intelligence under Deferred consuming systems). A previously-removed dependency reappearing is not a gap: it is already a live, composed, reproducible check -- DEPENDENCY_POLICY, cargo deny check bans against deny.toml's committed ban list, composed in run_context.rs -- and on inspection its evidence was never historical, only a static current-graph-vs-committed-list comparison; the one way to make it genuinely historical (querying git log live) is exactly what OD-STORE-002 and nomos-surface-provenance already decline to wire into a gate, confirmed against gate.yml's own shallow (unset fetch-depth) checkout. OD-RULES-026 records this measurement and its evidence; a future explicit decision to accept git history or runtime observation as gate input, if this workspace's boundary or CI checkout depth ever changes, is not foreclosed.

abandoned.reason: Investigated all three worked examples directly against the real tree. Runtime allocation evidence: ProcessLauncher is one-shot/run-to-completion only, no provider crate observes a judged repository's own running code, and ARC-ROADMAP-001 already places runtime/debug intelligence under Deferred consuming systems. Benchmark history: no criterion dependency, no benchmark-results convention anywhere in this workspace -- nothing to extend. A previously-removed dependency reappearing: already shipped as DEPENDENCY_POLICY (cargo deny check bans against deny.toml's committed ban list of wgpu/egui/winit/ash/naga), composed into run_context.rs today -- and its evidence was never historical, it is a static current-graph-vs-committed-list comparison, the same shape dependency-direction already proves. The one way to make it genuinely historical (a live git log query) is exactly what OD-STORE-002 and nomos-surface-provenance already decline to wire as a gate input, confirmed against gate.yml's own unset fetch-depth (shallow CI checkout). The item's own premise that generations are 'most of what a historical claim needs' is also directly contradicted by OD-STORE-002, which predates it. Declining with a decision record (OD-RULES-026) rather than abandoning for someone else to retry the same three examples.

items.title: No agent run reaches a validated correction, so agent output is never checked before it lands
items.why: A Claude Code executor and an Ollama backend both really run, and typed agent contracts exist, but nothing carries what an agent produced into a correction the system validates before committing. The game plan is explicit that an agent executor should not precede a solid mutation and validation contract; the executor was built first, so closing this restores that ordering rather than adding to the inversion. Sequenced behind the canonical correction seam because a workflow or agent tier calling into a CLI module would invert the layering, and behind the canonical result because the executor does not construct one yet, so this path would otherwise be built on a vendor-shaped response.
items.done_when: An agent run produces a canonical WorkResult that becomes a correction candidate, that candidate goes through Preview, Stage, Validate and Commit, a validation failure leaves the tree untouched, and a test covers both outcomes.

Declined.reason: Stranded on P42-AGENT-STRUCTURED-WORKRESULT, which is Declined and was re-authored under a renamed id rather than a -2 suffix: P42-EXECUTOR-WORKRESULT-MECHANISM, Done, recorded as OD-EXECUTOR-008. That successor is a decision whose own title ends in the words before code, so it does not by itself satisfy this item's stated precondition of a canonical result the executor actually constructs. The missing implementation is now filed as P42-EXECUTOR-WORKRESULT-IMPLEMENTATION. Re-added as -3 depending on that implementation and on P40-CORRECTIONS-CANONICAL-SEAM. Territory also corrected: the original reserved only nomos-agent-contracts work_result.rs, which defines the type rather than carrying it into a validated correction, and which the implementation item now reserves. The real seam is in nomos-agent-orchestration, which cannot reach corrections today, so the crate manifest and the zones edge table are reserved alongside it.

items.title: The AGT-001 assessment says no typed task envelope exists, and one has for eleven days
items.why: The committed assessment states that no single typed envelope bundles goal, scope, prohibited changes, tools and an output schema into one artifact, and names Claim and WorkflowStep as its gaps. TaskEnvelope carries all seven AGT-001 parts and has since 2026-08-24. The assessment was last touched on 2026-09-01 by a sweep that fixed 72 stale citations across 26 files, which checked whether cited paths still exist rather than whether the prose still held, so this survived it. The verdict is load-bearing: these assessments are how remaining work is chosen, and a ledger item was authored against this one and then declined. Fixing the file is the correction; making the class impossible is a separate rule.
items.done_when: The AGT-001 assessment describes the tree as it is, names TaskEnvelope as a site rather than asserting no envelope exists, its verdict is whatever the corrected reading supports, and the sibling AGT and AGT-EXEC assessments are checked for the same staleness rather than only this one.

items.title: A rule is a bare function, so the engine has to learn each one individually
items.why: A rule today is a function the composition root names, plus a RuleId, plus membership in a hand-written mapping from rule to the capability materialization it needs. Nothing about a rule declares its own subjects or its required facts, so that knowledge lives centrally and grows once per rule: 56 composed entries, and nine separate selection predicates deciding which capability families to materialize. The package specification says applicability is derived from canonical capability requirements rather than duplicated support information, which is the opposite of what the code does. A descriptor is the prerequisite for the planner, because a planner with nothing to plan from would only relocate the same table. This item delivers the descriptors and proves them complete; deleting the central mapping is P41-RUN-STOPS-NAMING-EVERY-RULE, where both sides of that edit are in one territory.
items.done_when: Every composed rule has a descriptor declaring its identifier, the subject kind it judges, and the capability facts it requires; a contract test proves the descriptor identifier set equals the Composed_Rules set nomos-check-orchestration already exports, so a rule added on either side without the other fails; and the declared capability requirements are stated to match the nine existing selection predicates, which the migration item then makes mechanical.

Declined.reason: Territory reserved only the new descriptor file and the new contract test. A new module cannot exist without a declaration in crates/rules/nomos-rules/src/lib.rs, and adding a public type re-blesses tests/contract/surface/nomos-rules.txt. Both were outside what it reserved, so it could not be finished honestly either. Re-added as -3 with all four paths, determined by reading how lib.rs declares modules and confirming the surface snapshot exists, rather than by guessing a second time.

items.title: The API cannot express gate scope or rule selection, so its gate run is not the gate
items.why: nomos-api reaches the canonical orchestration seams for the gate verbs, the work ledger verbs and the spec surface, which is what makes the second host real. Its own documentation records that the request surface does not expose gate scope or rule selection, and the committed requirement assessments name Handle_Gate_Run as a gap for exactly that reason. ScopeSelector and RuleSelector are real, and OD-GATE-017 drove selection down into check orchestration so an unselected rule can skip its materialization entirely. An API caller that cannot select is therefore not merely less expressive than the CLI, it is paying for every expensive provider on every call. Re-issue of P40-API-GATE-SELECTION-SURFACE: that item reserved only src/lib.rs, which merely re-exports; Handle_Gate_Run itself lives in src/response/gate_run_response.rs, its one real call site outside this crate's own tests is tests/integration_seams.rs, and changing its parameter from root: &Path to command: &GateCommand rewrites the line tests/contract/surface/nomos-api.txt records for it.
items.done_when: Handle_Gate_Run takes a &GateCommand instead of a bare root, so an API caller can set scope and rules exactly as GateCommand already carries them through to Run_Gate; a test proves a deselected rule's finding does not exist in the response rather than being filtered from it after the fact; the existing call site and the public surface snapshot are updated to match; and cargo test -p nomos-api -p nomos-gate-orchestration is green.

items.title: Four registered rules judge scripts the walker never collects, so the gate reports them clean
items.why: Measured 2026-09-05 against the built binary at 21e77900. Every walker in both hosts admits only .rs and .go (check/sources.rs, gate/sources.rs, correct/sources.rs and nomos-api sources.rs each carry the same literal). Four composed rules judge files that are neither: scripts-use-a-portable-shebang, a-script-declares-its-purpose and executed-scripts-set-nounset judge any file whose first line is a shebang, and declared-tooling-language-for-scripts judges a path ending in an extension this repository declares forbidden, which its own standards.json lists as .ps1 .psm1 .bat .cmd and .sh. The intersection of what those rules judge and what the walk collects is empty, so all four are unable to report anything. Demonstrated directly: a directory holding deploy.sh with a hardcoded interpreter shebang, asked for exactly that rule, answers 0 findings and exit 0. All four are advertised by gate plan, counted in Composed_Rules and asserted by the plan-run parity test, none of which observes reachability. Their unit tests are green because every fixture names scripts/check.sh or tooling/deploy.ps1, paths the product cannot produce, which is this repository's own a-test-that-cannot-find-its-corpus-passes hazard recurring at the rule and walk boundary. P27-SELFCHECK-RULES-JUDGING-NON-SCRIPTS narrowed these rules off Rust lib.rs files and promised no file that really is a script stops reporting; that held at the rule and was never checked at the composition. P41-WORKSPACE-DISCOVERY-SERVICE names the hardcoded extension list as a design defect and is gated behind platform directory enumeration; this item is the live false pass underneath it and does not wait for that refactor.
items.done_when: A shebang script with a hardcoded interpreter path and a file with a forbidden extension, both under a walked root, are reported by the rules that exist to catch them, proven by a test that runs a real walk and judgement over a fixture tree containing both rather than over a hand-built SourceFile. The self-check finding delta from widening the walk is measured and stated before the change lands, so newly reachable text rules reporting on newly walked files is a counted outcome and not a surprise. No rule that judges Rust or Go changes what it reports.

items.title: A rule that judged nothing reports exactly as a rule that judged clean
items.why: The system reports honestly one layer down and not at this one. When a capability cannot be materialized the run says so: claim incomplete, ProviderUnavailable, and an Advisory finding naming the capability that went unanswered. When a rule runs against a subject population the walk never collected, the run says nothing at all, and the output is indistinguishable from that rule having judged the tree and found it clean. CheckOutcome::NoFacts covers exactly one instance of this shape, zero syntax facts, and its message is the whole principle stated out loud: a clean result here would mean only that the walk found nothing. Nothing generalizes it. P43-SCRIPT-RULES-CANNOT-FIRE is the first measured consequence and is a correction to one walker; the reason it was silent rather than loud is this gap, and a second instance arrives with every language or artifact kind added ahead of its discovery. P41-APPLICABILITY-IN-THE-PLAN answers a different question, which subjects a rule declines once a plan exists, and is gated behind the planner; this asks what a run owes a reader about a rule whose population was empty, which holds with or without a plan and needs deciding before either is built on it.
items.done_when: A record states how a run distinguishes a rule that judged an empty population from one that judged clean, names where that verdict is computed and which existing outcome vocabulary it extends or replaces, says whether an empty population is Advisory the way ProviderUnavailable already is or a stronger disposition, and applies the test to the four rules P43-SCRIPT-RULES-CANNOT-FIRE names. No code moves under this item.

items.title: Agent is the one verb family with no orchestration seam, so only the binary can reach it
items.why: Work, spec, check, gate and workflow each have an orchestration crate that both hosts call, which is what makes the claim that a host owns no product semantics true for those five. Agent is the exception and nothing marks it as one. The whole family lives in nomos-cli agent.rs and its agent directory, 1135 lines that reach nomos-agent-executor-claude-code and nomos-model-package EffortLevel directly with no crate between, and nomos-api names neither dependency, so the second host cannot dispatch a task envelope, choose a backend or read a result at all. P40-CORRECTIONS-CANONICAL-SEAM records the identical hole for correction and was authored without noticing agent has it too; the two are the complete set of unseamed families, checked against the crate list and against nomos-api Cargo.toml rather than assumed. Every later consumer inherits it: P40-MCP-SURFACE, P40-API-TRANSPORT and P42-SECOND-HARNESS-EXECUTOR each need an agent seam that is not a CLI module, and P42-AGENT-STRUCTURED-WORKRESULT would otherwise land its canonical WorkResult inside the one host that cannot share it.
items.done_when: Agent dispatch and result handling are reachable through an orchestration seam both hosts call, nomos-cli agent is a thin renderer over it the way the gate verbs already are, nomos-api exposes the same verbs, and the new crate carries its band declaration, README row and contract-test harness entries rather than leaving them stale.

Declined.reason: Territory names one file in a crate that does not exist yet. The real, precedented shape (nomos-correction-orchestration + nomos-api/src/correction.rs + nomos-cli/src/correct.rs, the P40-CORRECTIONS-CANONICAL-SEAM sibling this item's own why cites) needs a whole new crate directory, the CLI module it thins (crates/host/nomos-cli/src/agent.rs and src/agent/), a new nomos-api/src/agent.rs, both hosts' Cargo.toml dependency edges, a zones.rs entry, a README crate-table row, and surface snapshots for the new crate and nomos-api -- not one lib.rs. Reauthoring with the full territory checked directly against the correction-orchestration precedent.

items.title: Consolidating the policy crates relocates five copies of the same scaffolding rather than removing them
items.why: Measured 2026-09-05 by diffing the five repository policy providers against each other. Across nomos-repo-standards, nomos-repo-limits, nomos-repo-scripting, nomos-repo-words and nomos-repo-goals, four of the six files are token-identical apart from the capability name and the error type: lib.rs, guarantee.rs, fact_context.rs and the XPolicyFactProduction strategy, roughly 330 lines each and about 1350 lines of five-way copy. Only reading.rs carries content that differs, and the one part already factored out, the standards.json read itself, is the smallest of them, sitting in nomos-repo-standards-document. P41-CRATE-BOUNDARY-REVIEW asks the right question about these crates but a different one, whether a crate buys independent versioning, isolation or installation, and P41-CAPABILITY-CRATE-CONSOLIDATION carries out its answer under a done_when that says no public type is renamed or removed by the move alone, which preserves every copy. Crate to module changes where the duplication lives and not that there is any, so the item that looks like it addresses this would close with all five copies intact. Kept separate because the two axes are independent: the duplication is worth removing whether or not any of these stays a crate, and removing it is a behaviour-preserving change reviewed on its own.
items.done_when: The scaffolding the five providers share is written once and each provider supplies only what genuinely differs, its own reading and its own error type. What each capability declares stays independently stated rather than derived, so a provider that should declare a different guarantee or granularity still can, and the deliberate duplication OD-CAPABILITY-008 defends for Encode_Payload is not folded in by the same move. No provider changes the fact it materializes, proven by the existing per-provider tests passing unchanged.

Declined.reason: Predicate names five pre-consolidation crates that no longer exist (nomos-repo-goals/limits/scripting/words/standards); P41-REPOSITORY-CRATE-CONSOLIDATION-2 already merged them into nomos-repo-policy's own modules before this item was authored. abandoned.reason: Predicate names the five pre-consolidation crates (nomos-repo-goals, nomos-repo-limits, nomos-repo-scripting, nomos-repo-words, nomos-repo-standards) by their old names; P41-REPOSITORY-CRATE-CONSOLIDATION-2 already merged them into nomos-repo-policy's own five modules before this item was authored, so cargo cannot resolve those package ids at all. The first is proven and the API seam is substantially built, which leaves MCP as the sharpest remaining hole in that row: nomos-api states plainly that it does not speak the JSON-RPC framing MCP requires, and the AGT-006 assessment calls MCP tools a clean, total gap. An MCP surface is what lets an agent consume Nomos as a tool rather than by shelling out to a CLI and parsing rendered text, which is precisely the coupling OD-HOST-003 rejects for the editor surface. Sequenced after the transport so that framing and serving are not designed twice. This is P40-MCP-SURFACE with its scope corrected to OD-HOST-007, accepted after that item was written, and with the territory a new workspace member actually costs.
items.done_when: An MCP server exposes the three Gate operations as tools over MCP JSON-RPC framing and exposes no handler belonging to a repo-tooling crate, an MCP client can run a gate and read typed findings without parsing rendered output, no product semantics live in the MCP crate, the crate declares a band in every table that carries one, and the AGT-006 assessment is re-measured against what actually shipped rather than left saying MCP tools is a total gap.

items.title: OD-HOST-007 says it stays open until a transport exists, and one will
items.why: OD-HOST-007 closes with: Open until the first transport exists. This record exclusion is a rule with no artifact enforcing it yet, and a contract test asserting a registry that does not exist would be the vacuous-truth trap OD-CONTRACTS-001 honesty vocabularies refuse. P40-API-TRANSPORT-2 builds that transport and the assertion the record was waiting for, at which point the sentence describes a state that has passed. This repository has already paid for the class twice this month: P43-CAPABILITY-008-TRIGGERS-FIRED found a record still saying neither of its revisit triggers had fired when both had, and four P42 assessment corrections were one stale citation each. A record whose own status is behind the tree is the same defect at the authority layer rather than the assessment layer.

items.title: The shared text substrate under the rules does not know what a string literal is
items.why: Measured 2026-09-05 against the built binary. Three defects, one layer, all reproduced against real fixtures rather than read. First, the comment stripper every text rule copies is a split on the two-slash sequence taking the first part, so a line whose string literal holds a URL is truncated at that URL and everything after it becomes invisible: two identical unsafe blocks were judged, and the one preceded on the same line by a string containing a scheme-and-double-slash was not reported while the other was. Second, there is no string-literal awareness at all, so violation-shaped text inside a string is judged as code: a string holding the text of an unsafe block, a string holding an atomic ordering, and a raw string holding both an unsafe block and an unbalanced quote were all reported as violations. Third, the self-exemption nine modules carry is keyed on a path suffix, so it exempts any file in any repository whose path ends the same way: two byte-identical files carrying the same live-looking token were judged, and the one at checks slash security_text.rs was silently skipped while the one at ordinary.rs was reported. The third is the urgent one and is separable from the other two. It is worth saying that security_text.rs is right about itself: its own doc comment argues that a general string-stripping fix would defeat a content-shaped rule whose violation is the text of a string, and that reasoning holds and must survive this change. What is wrong there is the mechanism, not the policy. A syntax-shaped rule wants the string blinded; a content-shaped rule does not; neither wants a path suffix a stranger can match.
items.done_when: One shared code-prefix helper exists, aware of line comments, string literals, raw strings and char literals holding a quote, and every syntax-shaped rule that keeps its own copy today uses it instead. A content-shaped rule still judges the text of a string, so the credential, sensitive-URL and disabled-verification rules keep reporting what they report now. No rule decides whether to judge a file from a path suffix a user repository can match: two files with identical content get identical verdicts unless the tree really is this one. The three fixtures above reproduce as tests, including a URL inside a string followed by real code, a char literal holding a double quote, and identical content at two paths.

Declined.reason: declared territory named 11 files sharing the naive Code_Prefix copy plus a new code_prefix.rs, but five more files carry the identical defect, measured directly: closure_bounds.rs, lifetime_discipline.rs, borrowed_container.rs, procedural_macro.rs, orphan_modules.rs. Also found mid-implementation that a first design (blanking every string/raw-string/char-literal body) broke three real, passing tests that read a specific literal's own value as syntax (#[path="value"], .expect("message"), t.Skip("reason")) -- reverted to comment-boundary-only correctness, documented in code_prefix.rs's own module doc. Re-authoring as P45-CODE-PREFIX-KNOWS-STRINGS-2 with the complete 16-file set and the corrected, narrower scope (comment-truncation and self-exemption fixes; blanket string-content blinding explicitly not attempted, named as a real but harder follow-up).

abandoned.reason: territory too narrow: closure_bounds.rs, lifetime_discipline.rs, borrowed_container.rs, procedural_macro.rs and orphan_modules.rs also carry the identical naive line.split("//").next() Code_Prefix copy, measured directly, not named in the original territory alongside the 11 that were. Re-authoring with the complete 16-file set.

items.title: The unsafe rule demands one comment spelling and rejects the one Rust actually uses
items.why: Measured 2026-09-05 against aho-corasick, 32 files and 20937 lines, a crate that documents its safety contracts carefully. The rule produced 219 blocking findings there. Checked against the source rather than counted: packed/ext.rs line 8 declares an unsafe fn with a rustdoc Safety section on the three lines directly above it and was reported as using unsafe without an adjacent justification; automaton.rs line 198 declares an unsafe trait whose own doc block carries the same section. The rule looks for one spelling, the two-slash SAFETY comment, which is the right artifact at an unsafe block and the wrong one at an unsafe fn, trait or impl declaration, where a rustdoc Safety section is the convention and is what rustc and clippy missing-safety-doc already ask for. Separately, a marker with nothing after it satisfies the rule, and so does one whose text is a placeholder, which is inconsistent with the sibling rules in this workspace that require a suppression or an exclusion to carry an actual reason. Both halves are one question and neither is answerable by editing the matcher alone: what artifact discharges a justification requirement, and does it have to say anything. A decision first, because the answer sets the shape of at least four rules that each ask for a justification today.
items.done_when: A record states which artifacts discharge a justification requirement, distinguishing the construct that takes an adjacent comment from the declaration that takes a documentation section, and states whether a justification must carry text beyond its marker and what the rule does when it does not. It applies the answer by name to the unsafe, inline-always, allow and suppression rules that each ask for one today, and says what changes for each. No rule code moves under this item.

items.title: Nothing measures the rule set against code this repository did not write
items.why: The eight gate phases were driven to zero findings against this workspace, and that is the only corpus the rule set has ever been measured on. Tuning a rule until its author's own tree is clean proves the tree is clean, not that the rule is right. Measured 2026-09-05 against aho-corasick, 32 files and 20937 lines: 483 blocking findings, of which 219 came from one rule and were checked individually against the source and found false. A further 612 advisories cited README.md's Conventions section, which is this repository's README and says nothing in the repository being judged. None of that was visible from inside, because from inside the number is zero. The gap is not any single rule; it is that no test exercises a rule against source written by someone who had never heard of it, which is the only condition under which a rule tuned to its own corpus reveals what it actually matches. This repository already knows the shape of the hazard: a test that cannot find its corpus passes, and the three existing corpora live outside the tree where CI cannot see them, so the fixture this item builds has to be committed rather than referenced.
items.done_when: A committed fixture of idiomatic third-party source, small enough to review and carrying its provenance and licence, is judged by the composed rule set in a test. The test asserts a stated expected verdict per rule rather than a total, so a rule that starts reporting on ordinary code fails it. Every finding the fixture does produce is either justified in the test as a true positive or is an open item naming the rule. A rule whose expected verdict cannot be stated honestly today is recorded as uncalibrated rather than given a number that matches whatever it currently does.

items.title: The syntax payload is a tab-separated index, so every rule needing structure re-parses the text
items.why: Measured 2026-09-05. Render_Payload writes one tab-separated line per item carrying ordinal, kind, visibility, qualified name, documentation and shape. A tab-separated line cannot express a tree, so the parse tree is flattened before it is ever stored, and five of those six fields are strings. syn builds the full tree and the provider walks it properly with a Visit implementation, then discards it: visit_item_enum records no shape at all while node.variants is in hand, Function_Shape keeps a parameter count and no names, types or return type, and Type_Shape collapses every type to either slice or value, so a struct field of u32 and one of String are recorded identically. The shape that does survive is a string that Struct_Fields and Function_Arity have to re-parse to get structure back. The consequence is that a rule needing anything more re-parses the raw text it was also handed: enum_shape re-derives variant members, constant_scope re-derives function and constant headers and visibility one line at a time, domain_type_alias keeps a second copy of the visibility stripper, facade re-derives re-exports. Those re-derivations are wrong the way hand parsers are wrong. Split_At_Top_Level_Commas was compiled verbatim and run: two plain members split correctly, a generic member with an inner comma splits correctly, and a member whose type contains a function arrow does not, because the arrow's closing angle decrements a bracket depth that never opened, so a variant holding a callback reads as one member instead of two. Its author did handle generic nesting, which is the point: careful hand parsing still loses to the parser that already ran. Two different gaps are being conflated. P42-SEMANTIC-FACT-FAMILY and P40-COMPILER-BACKED-PROVIDER name the absence of a semantic model, name resolution and symbols, and name it correctly. Nothing names the absence of typed syntax, which is far cheaper because syn already produces it in process on every run and the tree is thrown away about sixty lines before the rules that rebuild it from text. Worth noting alongside: kind and visibility being strings is exactly what Check_Domain_Values_Are_Distinct_Types exists to catch, and that rule is one of the nineteen built and never composed, so it has never judged the payload it would fail.
items.done_when: A record decides whether the syntax payload carries a typed tree or stays a flat item index. It states what a second language provider owes under that answer, since nomos-lang-go must produce the same shape from tree-sitter and nomos-lang-rust-scan must produce it without a parser at all. It states what happens to the content-addressed encoding and to the determinism declarations that depend on byte identity if the encoding changes. It names which of the four hand-parsing rules the answer removes and which keep their own parser and why. No code moves under this item.

items.title: Nineteen of seventy-five rules are exported and never composed, and nothing reports the gap
items.why: Measured 2026-09-05 by comparing the Check functions nomos-rules exports against the ones run_context composes: seventy-five declared, fifty-six composed, nineteen that judge nothing. Building a rule first and composing it in a later item is a deliberate and sensible pattern here, because composing an unmeasured rule can redden the gate by hundreds of findings, and this workspace has done it on purpose before, in OD-RULES-012-WIRE-CLEAN-TEXT-RULES and again in P27-RULES-TWO-MORE-UNCOMPOSED. The defect is not the pattern; it is that the gap is found by hand each time somebody happens to diff the two lists, and nothing reports it in between. A rule that is built, tested, documented and exported costs the same to maintain as one that runs, and reads to any reader of the crate as though it is in force. Two of the nineteen matter beyond bookkeeping. Check_Domain_Values_Are_Distinct_Types would judge the stringly-typed fields P46-SYNTAX-PAYLOAD-TREE-OR-INDEX is about, and has never run against them. The three facade rules are the only check on a boundary this workspace states as architecture. Composed_Rules already exists as the single authority on what a run judges, and nothing compares it against what the rules crate offers.
items.done_when: A contract test compares the rules nomos-rules exports against the rules a run composes and fails when the difference contains a rule nobody has accounted for. Every rule in the difference today is either composed or carries a stated reason it is not, so nineteen becomes a set of decisions rather than an unexamined number. A rule exported tomorrow without either falls out of the test rather than out of a future review.

items.title: ToolProvider is a declared package kind with two real instances and no manifest crate
items.why: Measured 2026-09-05. PackageKind declares ToolProvider as an external analysis or transformation tool wrapped behind a capability. Two real ones exist and OD-RULES-010 names them in exactly those words: nomos-lang-rust-clippy is called the first real ToolProvider and nomos-lang-rust-deny the second. Neither can be declared by any manifest, because every other populated package kind has a manifest crate and this one does not: LanguagePackage has two, RulePackage has nomos-rule-package, and the model and agent-executor kinds share nomos-model-package. The consequence lands on OD-PACKAGE-014, which decided a package's activation semantics are the conformance claim that its declared providers match what the registry actually offers. A Rust LanguagePackage cannot carry clippy without contradicting its own stated meaning, recognition and canonical mapping for one language, so the allowlist admitting only the two syntax providers is correct rather than stale. What is missing is the kind that should carry them. Until it exists the conformance claim can never cover a linter or a dependency-policy tool, which are the two providers most likely to drift, since each shells out to an external binary whose version is exactly what ProviderRegistration's tool_version field was designed to record. The other unpopulated kinds, MetricProvider, RepositoryProvider and RuntimeProvider, have no instances and no case; this one has two.
items.done_when: A ToolProvider manifest crate exists as a peer of nomos-rule-package and nomos-model-package, wrapping nomos-package's generic core rather than depending on a sibling package crate, and admits the two real ToolProviders this workspace has by their own provider identities. It settles, and states, which side of the line a dependency reader falls on: nomos-lang-rust-cargo shells out to cargo metadata while nomos-lang-go-modules reads go.mod text directly, and only one of those looks like an external tool, so the answer decides whether Go's own language package should have admitted its modules reader all along. The crate carries its band declaration, README row and contract-test harness entries.

Declined.reason: Authored before the Go predecessor's kernel/toolspec was read, and its done_when asks a question that package now answers differently. It asks which side of a line a dependency reader falls on, cargo metadata shelling out against the go.mod reader not, which treats delivery as the dividing axis. The predecessor divides by family, what kind of question a tool answers, and makes delivery an orthogonal in-process against external axis, under which that question does not arise. Building a ToolProvider manifest against the delivery axis would bake in the split this workspace should probably not have. Re-added as P47-TOOLPROVIDER-HAS-NO-PACKAGE-2, same subject and territory, depending on P54-TOOL-FAMILY-TAXONOMY so the axis is decided before the crate is written.

items.title: OD-PACKAGE-014 decided what a package manifest is for and nothing has ever read one
items.why: OD-PACKAGE-014 decided that a language package's activation semantics are the conformance claim that its declared providers match what nomos_capability::Registry actually offers for each one's capability, checked and reported, never enacted. It measured at the time that nothing outside the package crates calls Parse_Manifest or Read_Manifest, and that is still true on 2026-09-05: no crate in this workspace depends on nomos-lang-rust-package or nomos-lang-go-package at all. So the one thing a manifest is for has never been done, and four manifest formats now exist that nobody reads. Every input the check needs is already present. ProviderRegistration carries the provider identity and the tool version, Registry::Offers answers for any capability exactly which providers are registered, and OD-RULES-003 already designed this composition for architecture, declared data compared against an observed reality and judged into a Finding, with P14-RULES-DEPENDENCY-COMPLETENESS applying the same shape a second time. This is that shape a third time. Note what it must not become: OD-HOST-004 forecloses a manifest that causes composition to add or omit an offer, and D-091 puts the installer and materializer mechanism on the other side of the ecosystem seam, so the answer is a report and never an action.
items.done_when: A manifest's declared providers are compared against what the registry actually offers, and a mismatch in either direction is reported: a package claiming a provider that is not registered, and a registered provider that no read manifest claims. The comparison runs from a real caller rather than a test, over the manifests a caller names, and reports rather than changes what composes. A run with no manifest to read says so instead of reporting agreement, since nothing read is not the same as nothing wrong.

items.title: A language server answers the semantic questions no fact family has, and nothing says whether it may
items.why: P42-SEMANTIC-FACT-FAMILY says every fact family is syntactic, so no rule can ask a question that needs resolved semantics, and P40-COMPILER-BACKED-PROVIDER says no provider uses a real compiler semantic API. Both are open and both assume the answer is a compiler integration per language. A language server is the other candidate and nothing has weighed it. The shape fits what a provider already is: a subprocess behind a capability, which nomos-lang-rust-cargo, nomos-lang-rust-clippy and nomos-lang-rust-deny all are today. What it answers is exactly what is missing, type at a position, definition of a symbol, references to it, the symbol hierarchy of a file. And unlike a compiler front end it is one interface rather than one integration per language, since rust-analyzer, gopls, the Roslyn server and pyright all speak it, so a single adapter shape would reach every language this system ever adds rather than one. Two existing records bear on this and neither settles it. OD-ANALYSIS-010 declined embedding rustc, rust-analyzer, Roslyn, Clang or any LSP server for one fact, control-flow reachability, and was explicit that it forecloses nothing for a future rule whose subject genuinely needs a compiler front end. P42-LSP-PROJECTION is the opposite direction, Nomos serving an editor rather than consuming one, and says nothing about this. The question is worth deciding before either open semantic item is claimed, because the two would be built differently.
items.done_when: A record decides whether a language server may be a provider, and if so what it is a provider of: which capability contracts a language-server-backed fact would answer, what guarantee it may honestly declare given that a server answers from its own index rather than from a compilation this system controls, and what IncrementalGranularity it sits at given that a server is long-lived where every provider today is a one-shot subprocess. It states the relationship to OD-ANALYSIS-010's decline, which covered one fact rather than the class, and says whether P40-COMPILER-BACKED-PROVIDER is satisfied by this route or remains separate. No provider is built under this item.

items.title: An unreferenced Rust source file compiles into nothing and no rule notices
items.why: code-standards' check-orphan-modules (rules/language-specific/rust/checks/check-orphan-modules, main.go plus module_reachability.go) reports a .rs file under a crate's src/ that no mod declaration reaches. Rust compiles only what the module tree names, so such a file is never parsed: it does not compile, its tests never run, its lints never fire, and nothing says so. It reads as finished work. Go compiles every file in a package directory and C# globs the project, so Rust is unusual in needing this at all, and nomos is a sixty-crate Rust workspace with no rule that asks the question. Verified against the real Go implementation rather than its prose: resolution tries the sibling file name.rs before the directory module name/mod.rs, an inline mod name { } is excluded by requiring the terminating semicolon, mod r#name is backed by name.rs with the raw-identifier prefix dropped, and a hash-bracket path attribute resolves against the directory the DECLARING FILE sits in while the file it names then owns the directory it lands in rather than a subdirectory named after it. Those last three are each recorded there as a false positive on real code, the third having reported all thirty-nine files of one live crate as orphans. Measured against this workspace before writing anything: sixty crates, zero orphans, so composing it costs the gate nothing today.
items.done_when: nomos-rules exports a rule for no-orphan-modules that resolves mod declarations against the sources it was handed rather than the filesystem, honoring the sibling-file and mod.rs layouts, the raw-identifier prefix, the semicolon that excludes an inline module, and the path attribute's declaring-file-relative resolution. It is composed into nomos-check-orchestration's Run behind the same per-call selection every other rule sits behind, carries a descriptor saying it reads source text and needs no fact, and the crate's blessed public surface names it. cargo test -p nomos-rules -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: OD-HOST-004 said hand-written composition holds until a rule runs conditionally, and one does
items.why: OD-HOST-004 decided Run stays hand-written for as long as every rule it calls runs unconditionally, and named the exact event that flips it: Run flips the first time a rule is meant to run for some check invocations and not others, selected by something the request states. That has happened. nomos_check_orchestration Run now takes selected as a slice of RuleId, OD-GATE-017 made a non-empty selection narrow what Run computes at all, and nomos gate run --rule reaches it from the command line. The answer given at the time was a filter over a fixed array: run_context.rs holds RULE_COUNT equal to fifty-seven and its own doc calls the accompanying structure a fixed, hand-written mapping from RuleId to the fact or facts it needs. That is a declaration doing registry work inside a function body, which is the accretion OD-HOST-004 exists to head off. Meanwhile nomos-rule-package already parses a manifest carrying exactly that per-rule information, measured field by field against four real rules by OD-PACKAGE-008, and nothing in this workspace depends on it: grepped 2026-09-05, its only appearances outside its own directory are two band tables and one doc comment. Seventy-five rules are exported and fifty-seven composed, and the gap is invisible because there is no declaration to compare the array against. The porting target makes this structural rather than tidy: the Go predecessor declares one thousand one hundred and forty-three rules, and a hand-written array is not the shape that holds them.
items.done_when: A governing record decides whether rule composition resolves a declared rule package against a linked implementation, the way a provider offer already resolves through KnownProviders and the capability registry, or stays a hand-written array with a request-carried filter. It states what a rule package declares versus what only linked code can supply, since a manifest cannot conjure a function. It records that OD-HOST-004 named a trigger, that the trigger fired, and what became of it, rather than leaving that record describing a condition that has passed. It is registered under crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records and both required projections are re-rendered from the record set the commit publishes.

items.title: Three text-decidable Rust rules exist in the tool this ports and in no rule here
items.why: Of the twenty Rust-specific checks code-standards ships that nomos has not ported, thirteen are tree-sitter-backed and need structure the nomos.cap.syntax.items payload does not carry, which is P46-SYNTAX-PAYLOAD-TREE-OR-INDEX's own question and not this item's. Three of the remaining text-decidable ones were measured against this workspace before being chosen and each reports zero: check-borrowing (rules/language-specific/rust/borrowing-and-ownership/borrowing, a borrowed owning container in a signature -- ampersand-String, ampersand-Vec, ampersand-PathBuf, ampersand-Box -- where the unsized view is what the caller can supply without allocating), check-lifetime-discipline (rules/language-specific/rust/lifetimes/lifetime-discipline, two or more distinct single-letter lifetimes on one declaration, and a static bound with no justification), and check-proc-macro (rules/language-specific/rust/structure/proc-macro, a function-like procedural macro with no justification, deliberately not the derive and attribute forms the rule sanctions). Zero was checked for vacuity rather than trusted: each was run against a hand-written positive fixture and fired, so the clean result is a real population judged clean and not the empty-population reading P43-EMPTY-POPULATION-IS-NOT-CLEAN names. Two neighbours were measured and rejected for cause and are not in scope: check-move-out-of-mut cannot fire on Allman-braced code at all, and a corrected version producing five findings against this tree was checked site by site and all five are reads the field must survive rather than moves out; check-closure-bounds reports four findings that would redden the gate and needs its own item.
items.done_when: nomos-rules exports four rules -- one for the borrowed owning container, one for terse multi-lifetime declarations, one for an unjustified static bound, one for the function-like procedural macro -- each in its own module named for what it judges, each judging only a line's own code the way this crate's sibling text rules already do. A static bound and a procedural macro are justified by an adjacent explanatory comment, the shape Check_Inline_Always_Justification already established here, rather than by one exact marker spelling. All four are composed into nomos-check-orchestration's Run behind the same per-call selection, each carries a descriptor saying it reads source text and needs no fact, the blessed public surface names them, and a real nomos check over this workspace reports zero findings from all four. cargo test -p nomos-rules -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

Declined.reason: Territory and verification predicate both omit crates/orchestration/nomos-gate-orchestration/src/composition.rs, the fifth registration site composing a rule costs -- the exact omission P47-ORPHAN-MODULES-HAS-NO-OFFERINGS-ROW had just corrected. items.why: HEAD e9b9363f composes no-orphan-modules into nomos-check-orchestration, raising RULE_COUNT to 57, and adds no row to OFFERINGS in nomos-gate-orchestration, which still lists 56. Two tests fail on a clean tree: composition::tests::Test_Registered_Should_Offer_Every_Composed_Rule and tests::Test_Registered_Should_Compose_Every_Rule_A_Check_Run_Composes. Verified by running the crate: 63 passed, 2 failed, and the assertion diff names exactly one identifier, no-orphan-modules. The parity test is doing its job; the composing item simply never ran it. P47-RULES-ORPHAN-MODULES is Done, and neither its territory nor its predicate reaches nomos-gate-orchestration: it reserved the rules crate, the check-orchestration run context and the surface snapshot, and it verified with cargo test over nomos-rules, nomos-check-orchestration and nomos-contract-tests. So the item went green while leaving a fourth crate red, and the workspace test step is red for every session until this lands. The recurrence cause is in the procedure rather than in that item's judgment. The nomos-add-plugin skill tells an author to compose a rule into nomos-check-orchestration's own composition and never mentions the gate's OFFERINGS table or the crate whose tests assert the two agree, so the next rule repeats this. items.title: A rule package cannot say whether anything mechanically judges the rule it declares
items.why: OD-RULES-022 decided that a declaration states its own judgment, and that this is what makes the resolution total: a declaration is either mechanical, in which case an implementation must exist and resolution fails if it does not, or model-judged, in which case there is none and the rule contributes nothing to a deterministic run. RulePackage carries no such field today. Its ApplicabilitySemantics is a different question entirely, AlwaysSupported against StructurallyPartial, which is about the subjects a judgment covers rather than whether a judgment exists. Without the distinction the resolution step has only two bad options for the Go predecessor population, where by its own rulespec doc 728 of 1116 rules are decided by a model rather than by a parser: refuse every one of them, or admit them as implementations that silently judge clean, which OD-GATE-001 already names as the defect the gate exists to prevent. The manifest already carries agent_guidance for exactly the rules this field would mark, and that field is empty for every shipped rule because no rule it was meant for can be declared yet.
items.done_when: RulePackage carries a declared judgment, its reader parses and refuses an unknown value the way it already refuses an unknown applicability semantics or evidence class, and a round-trip test covers both arms. The crate surface snapshot is reblessed. Nothing consumes the field yet: this item makes the distinction representable, and the resolution step that reads it is its own item.

items.title: Nothing judges how deeply a function nests, and the shared scanner that could is private
items.why: code-standards' check-nesting-depth (rules/general/style/checks/control-flow/readability/check-nesting-depth, judgment in the language-free shared package rules/general/style/shared/nesting) reports a function whose control flow nests deeper than three levels. Depth counts control-flow constructs and not braces: the first if, loop or match is level one, one directly inside it is level two, and a function reaching three is fine while one past it is reported once, at the first construct to cross. An else-if continues at its neighbour's level rather than deepening, and its own body still deepens as usual. Deep nesting is the readability signal an over-long function is, and the remedy is a guard clause or an extracted helper. Ported as a text rule rather than faithfully: the Go original reaches tree-sitter, but so does check-constant-scope, which this crate already re-decided as a text rule, and so does the single-line-body check it ships as NO_SINGLE_LINE_FUNCTION_BODIES. Whether a given one survives that translation is a per-rule question answered by prototyping, and it was answered twice here. It failed for allman-brace-placement, whose text prototype produced thirteen false positives in six structural classes against this workspace. It succeeded for this one: a prototype reached exact agreement with the real Go tool on the positive fixture and on six control probes covering if-else chains, items, nested blocks, match arms, closures and every governed loop form, and then reported zero over the whole of crates, which is what the Go tool reports. Zero was also checked for the two ways it lies: the prototype fires on a hand-written four-deep function, so the population is judged rather than empty, and the count is identical when the same sources are copied to a scratch path, so no waiver is doing the work.
items.done_when: nomos-rules exports a rule for nesting depth that counts control-flow constructs rather than braces, treats an else-if as continuing at its neighbour's level while still deepening its own body, reports a function once at the first construct past the limit, and resolves that limit through nomos.cap.limits.policy with three as the default the way the file-size rules already do. Brace counting reads only a line's own code through the cross-line literal-state scanner formatting.rs already owns, rather than a fourth private copy of a comment stripper. It is composed into nomos-check-orchestration's Run behind the same per-call selection, carries a descriptor naming the limits capability, has a row in nomos-gate-orchestration's OFFERINGS, and the blessed public surface names it. A real nomos check over this workspace reports zero from it, and the same binary reports it against a scratch crate that nests four deep. cargo test -p nomos-rules -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-gate-orchestration -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

The duplication that decision measured is still there. nomos-gate-orchestration composition.rs says why in its own module doc: this is not yet a shared derivation, the rows below are still authored, because a rule contract citation is knowledge no export carries. OD-GATE-020 named the same thing as the fix it did not build, and its stated revisit condition is a shared-derivation export being built.
