items.title: A rule names a capability but nothing names the kind of tool that answers it
items.why: Read out of the Go predecessor at C:/Users/kmett/source/repos/kevinmettias/code-standards on 2026-09-05. Its kernel/toolspec package carries a three-name model this workspace has two thirds of: FAMILY is what a check asks for, a type checker for TypeScript; TOOL is what can answer it, tsc or Roslyn or go/types or cargo or clippy; SELECTION is which one this repository chose. Its governing rule is that a check may name a family and must never name a tool, and it states why the family set is closed while a tool id is a plain string: the families are the engine's vocabulary and the tools are the world's. Twelve families are declared there, parser, semantic model, compiler, linter, type checker, formatter, language server, refactoring engine, indexer, test runner, documentation generator and package manager, with delivery a separate axis of in-process against external. That separation is what this workspace does not have, and the cost is visible in an item already on this board. P47-TOOLPROVIDER-HAS-NO-PACKAGE asks which side of a line a dependency reader falls on, since cargo metadata shells out to a subprocess and the go.mod reader does not, and under the predecessor's model that question does not arise: both are tools, their family is what they answer and their delivery is where they run. This workspace currently splits LanguagePackage from ToolProvider along delivery, which is the axis that does not matter, and has no name at all for the axis that does. A capability contract is not the same thing as a family and does not replace one: nomos.cap.lint.diagnostics is one fact shape, LINTER is a kind of tool that could answer several.
items.done_when: A record decides whether this workspace adopts a closed tool-family vocabulary above its capability contracts, and if so which families it declares and what a rule is allowed to name. It states the relationship between a family and a capability rather than conflating them, since a capability is a fact shape and a family is a kind of answering tool. It states whether delivery, in-process against external, becomes an explicit axis or stays implied by which crate a provider lives in. It applies the answer by name to the seven provider identities this workspace has today. No provider or package moves under this item.

items.title: A refusal says what is missing and never what to do about it
items.why: nomos_capability::Unmet is a closed set of typed variants, NoProvider, Undeclared, BelowRequirement with the closest offer, and VersionMismatch with what was offered. That is better than the bool the Go predecessor started with and this item keeps it. What it carries is what is wrong. What no path out of this crate carries is what a person could do about it. The predecessor arrived at the distinction the hard way and states it in kernel/toolspec's own package doc: every path out of that package that means no analysis happened carries a reason and a remedy, and they are separate fields on purpose, because the dotnet runtime is not on PATH is what is wrong while install dotnet 10 then run dotnet build in tools/cs-semantic is what to do, and a message that merges them tends to be neither. Its own reasoning ends on the part that matters here, that the remedy is the only half a user can act on. Its provider adapters carry this at the point of refusal rather than at the call site: cargoanalyzer's availability probe returns Absent_Because with the sentence naming cargo, chained to Fixed_By naming rustup. This workspace instead invents a sentence at each call site, which is the same failure that record names, and the sentence a user needs is the one nobody writes. Related to but distinct from P43-EMPTY-POPULATION-IS-NOT-CLEAN and its OD-ANALYSIS-012 record: that asks whether a gap is reported at all, this asks what a reported gap has to carry to be worth reading.
items.done_when: An unmet or refused capability carries a remedy alongside what is wrong, structured rather than prose, so a caller renders both without composing a sentence of its own. The existing typed variants survive; a remedy is added to them rather than replacing them with a string. A provider that can only be answered by installing or building something states that at the point it refuses, not at the point a report is rendered. Every existing caller that today invents its own sentence is changed to render the carried one, so a second wording of the same refusal does not survive this item.

items.title: ToolProvider is a declared package kind with two real instances and no manifest crate
items.why: PackageKind declares ToolProvider as an external analysis or transformation tool wrapped behind a capability. Two real ones exist and OD-RULES-010 names them in exactly those words: nomos-lang-rust-clippy is the first real ToolProvider and nomos-lang-rust-deny the second. Neither can be declared by any manifest, because ToolProvider is the one populated package kind with no manifest crate: LanguagePackage has two, RulePackage has nomos-rule-package, and the model and agent-executor kinds share nomos-model-package. The consequence lands on OD-PACKAGE-014, which decided a package's activation semantics are the conformance claim that its declared providers match what the registry actually offers. A Rust LanguagePackage cannot carry clippy without contradicting its own stated meaning, recognition and canonical mapping for one language, so its allowlist admitting only the two syntax providers is correct rather than stale. What is missing is the kind that should carry them. Until it exists the conformance claim can never cover a linter or a dependency-policy tool, which are the two providers most likely to drift since each shells out to an external binary whose version is exactly what ProviderRegistration's tool_version field records. This supersedes P47-TOOLPROVIDER-HAS-NO-PACKAGE, whose done_when asked which side of a delivery line a dependency reader falls on. P54-TOOL-FAMILY-TAXONOMY may answer that the axis is family rather than delivery, in which case what this crate admits and how it is named both change, so it waits on that record rather than guessing.
items.done_when: A ToolProvider manifest crate exists as a peer of nomos-rule-package and nomos-model-package, wrapping nomos-package's generic core rather than depending on a sibling package crate, and admits the two real ToolProviders this workspace has by their own provider identities. Its shape follows whatever P54-TOOL-FAMILY-TAXONOMY decided rather than re-deciding it: if a family vocabulary was adopted, a registration carries its family, and the crate admits providers by family rather than by whether they launch a subprocess. items.title: Nothing judges a closure bound that asks for more than the call site needs
items.why: code-standards' check-closure-bounds (rules/language-specific/rust/closures/closure-bounds, judgment in closure_Bounds/closure_Bounds_Line) enforces two rule ids: closure-bounds-are-minimal.md (a bound widened with Send, Sync, or 'static past what the call site uses, and a public function's own Fn/FnMut/FnOnce choice as an unverifiable API contract) and boxed-closures-are-justified-and-off-hot-paths.md (Box/Arc/Rc of dyn Fn*, a heap allocation plus an indirect call). A pure line scanner over Noisy_Lines_Blanked, not tree-sitter backed, matching the class this crate has already ported successfully (parameters-borrow-unless-ownership-is-taken, lifetime-discipline). Measured against the real corpus rather than assumed: the real check.exe over crates/ reports 0 findings at the real path but 4 waived-by-suppressions.json findings revealed by re-running a byte-identical scratch copy, all Send-only widenings in nomos-ledger's interleaving.rs (lines 197, 198, 236, 237), each already carrying a longer explanatory comment several lines above its enclosing multi-line signature -- out of the small look-back window this crate's justification rules already use, and out of the original Go marker-scan's reach too, which is why suppressions.json rather than an in-code marker was carrying it there. The public-API case and the boxed-dyn case were each checked for vacuity with a hand-written positive fixture (both fire) rather than trusted on their real zero: the public case is vacuous by construction over this workspace's multi-line Allman-braced signatures, which never put pub fn and an inline Fn* bound on one physical line; the boxed case is a genuine zero, since nothing here boxes or shares a closure.
items.done_when: nomos-rules exports Check_Closure_Bounds_Are_Minimal (covering the widened-bound and public-API shapes under closure-bounds-are-minimal) and Check_Boxed_Closures_Are_Justified_And_Off_Hot_Paths (boxed-closures-are-justified-and-off-hot-paths), both SourceText rules reading no facts, both accepting any adjacent explanatory comment as justification rather than the original's one marker spelling -- the same divergence lifetime_discipline.rs's static-bounds rule already made, and for the same reason: this workspace's four real instances each already carry a comment, just out of the small look-back window, and a literal port would report all four as unjustified with nowhere to say otherwise. Both rules exempt their own implementation file by path, the same way rust_text.rs's justification rules do, verified necessary by a real nomos gate run before the exemption existed. Composed into nomos-check-orchestration's Run, carry descriptors in rule_descriptor.rs, and the blessed public surface names all four new exports. interleaving.rs's four Send-bounded closure parameters each carry their own adjacent one-line reason so the ported rule reports the real population as justified rather than as four new findings. A real nomos gate run over this workspace reports zero blocking findings from either new rule, and the same binary reports findings against a hand-written positive fixture for every shape (widened bound, public API bound, boxed dyn). cargo test -p nomos-rules -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-gate-orchestration -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

Declined.reason: predicate argv corrupted by a misplaced --timeout flag; superseded by P55-RULES-CLOSURE-BOUNDS-2

abandoned.reason: authored with --timeout after the -- separator, which silently joined the predicate argv instead of setting nomos's own flag; re-adding as -2 with it placed correctly

items.title: One correction family exists, so nothing has yet shown what generalizes
items.why: The phantom-mirror vertical is a real end-to-end proof that a finding can reach a deterministic type-state lifecycle and a filesystem commit, and it deliberately handles only the first recognized finding and only one candidate per run. That narrowness means every generalization question is still unanswered by evidence: batching, ranking between competing candidates, and whether two families share a producer seam cannot be decided from a population of one. P40-CORRECTIONS-SECOND-FAMILY named this gap with territory under nomos-cli's own correct/ directory, written before P40-CORRECTIONS-CANONICAL-SEAM (08949b65) moved every real correction composition out of nomos-cli and into nomos-correction-orchestration, emptying that directory of the very logic a second family would extend -- declined and re-authored here with territory where the shared entry point (Run_Correction) now actually lives.
items.done_when: A second correction family over a different rule (no-trailing-whitespace) reaches Preview, Stage, Validate and Commit through the same nomos-corrections lifecycle, both families are produced by trying each family's own claim-recognizer against one shared Judged() result and then running one shared seed/stage/validate/commit pipeline over whichever matched -- not two bespoke pipelines -- and what the pair demonstrates about batching (multiple lines in one file as one candidate) versus what it leaves undecided about ranking between competing families is recorded in the orchestration crate's own module doc rather than assumed.

Declined.reason: Authored with an incomplete territory list (missing crates/orchestration/nomos-correction-orchestration/src/correction_outcome.rs); re-authoring as P40-CORRECTIONS-SECOND-FAMILY-3 with the complete list before any implementation began.

abandoned.reason: Territory list omitted correction_outcome.rs, which the shared-pipeline generalization also needs to touch (renaming the claimed field for family-neutral wording); re-adding with the complete list before implementing.

items.title: Materialize_Syntax's own skip made a fully-unchanged reused run report NoFacts
items.why: P40-INCREMENTAL-SKIP-UNCHANGED-SUBJECTS (8db1ae46) changed Materialize_Syntax's return value from a coverage count (how many sources now have a materialized fact, whether newly written or already current) to a newly-written count, so that skipped subjects would not inflate it. Nothing downstream of that return value was updated to match: run_context.rs's own Materialized_Syntax_Facts still treats a zero return as CheckOutcome::NoFacts (the vacuity gate), and Outcome_Of still files it into Examined.facts, a coverage statistic Claim_Of reads to judge completeness. A second Run over a store and workspace reused across two calls with zero content changes -- the exact usage pattern that item's own done_when asked callers to be free to adopt -- would today report NoFacts and an Incomplete claim over a tree every file of which has a perfectly good, current fact. No real caller has hit this yet: every current caller either passes a fresh store per call or always has at least one real edit between reused calls. It is latent, not yet observed wrong, and it is a landmine directly in the path of any future demand-driven recompute work.,
items.done_when: Materialize_Syntax's return value again means what Examined.facts and the NoFacts vacuity gate need it to mean -- the count of sources with a current materialized fact, whether skipped or newly written -- and the newly-written count P40-INCREMENTAL-SKIP-UNCHANGED-SUBJECTS's own test needs is read from MemoryFactStore::Materializations()'s own delta instead. A test proves a Run reused across two calls with zero content changes between them still reports CheckOutcome::Judged with Examined.facts equal to the file count, not NoFacts.

items.title: Only demanded invalidated facts are recomputed, and only affected rules are reassessed
items.why: The original item named nomos-analysis's invalidation.rs/propagation.rs as territory, but on investigation those own a different question (what happens to already-materialized dependents once a cause retires a fact) than the one done_when actually asks: whether a rule needs to run again at all. The facts half is effectively delivered already by P40-INCREMENTAL-SKIP-UNCHANGED-SUBJECTS (8db1ae46, fixed by 7b721edb): today's fact graph is entirely leaf/flat (every store.Materialize call across every provider passes dependencies: &[]), so 'facts reachable from a changed subject' already collapses to 'that subject's own fact', already skipped when unchanged. What remains unbuilt is the rule half: run_context.rs's own 64-entry Composed_Rules array invokes every selected rule's closure unconditionally on every call, over a MemoryFactStore::Materializations() count nothing reads to decide whether a rule's own required capability actually produced anything new since the last call over a reused store. nomos_rules::DESCRIPTORS already declares, per rule, which RequiredFact capability families it reads -- the one piece of declarative data a skip decision needs and does not yet have a consumer for.
items.done_when: A Run reused across two calls with zero content changes reassesses none of the selected rules a second time -- their prior findings are reused rather than recomputed -- and a Run reused across two calls where one subject changed reassesses only the rules whose own nomos_rules::RuleDescriptor.requires names a capability family that subject's change actually touched, proven by a test that counts real rule-closure invocations (not just materializations) against a one-file change in a many-file, many-rule tree.

Declined.reason:
Only Materialize_Syntax has a currency check. Read all nine other materializers this
crate composes (Materialize_Dependencies, Materialize_Lint, Materialize_Policy,
Materialize_Reachability in dependency_materialization.rs, and the five policy-family
functions in policy_materialization.rs): every one calls store.Materialize() unconditionally
whenever its section runs, with no Already_Current-shaped check first. A family other than
nomos.cap.syntax.items therefore reads as "changed" on every call it is selected for,
whether or not the run's inputs actually differ.

Syntax's own dedup is whole-call, not per-subject: Materialize_Syntax reports one count over
all of `sources`, so one changed file among many flips the same signal a hundred unchanged
files would leave untouched. There is no selection of real composed rules where one family
can be shown to have changed while another, also-selected family did not, for a one-file
change in a many-file tree -- the exact scenario this item's own done_when named as the
test. Building that honestly needs either per-subject syntax tracking (which the rule
closures cannot use today -- each one reads the whole `sources` list and returns one
Vec<Finding>, not a per-subject partial result) or a currency check added to each of the
other nine materializers first, and either is a larger, separate body of work.

Re-authoring the half that is real: zero content changes across two calls skips a rule
requiring only nomos.cap.syntax.items or nothing at all (a SourceText rule), and says
plainly that a rule needing any other family still reassesses every call until that
family's own materializer gets the currency check syntax already has.

abandoned.reason: Re-scoping before implementing: the done_when's second clause is not honestly demonstrable against real providers, per direct inspection of every materializer this crate composes.

items.title: A rule needing only syntax, or nothing, skips a call where nothing changed
items.why:
P40-INCREMENTAL-SKIP-UNCHANGED-SUBJECTS gave Materialize_Syntax a currency check, so a
reused store and workspace no longer re-parse a subject nothing touched. Nothing yet uses
that saved work above the materialization layer: Findings_For_Selected_Rules still runs
every selected rule's closure on every call regardless of whether anything it reads moved.

Only syntax has that currency check today -- direct inspection of Materialize_Dependencies,
Materialize_Lint, Materialize_Policy, Materialize_Reachability and the five policy-family
functions in policy_materialization.rs shows every one of them writes unconditionally
whenever its section runs, so their own family always reads as changed. A rule needing one
of those other nine families cannot be skipped honestly until its own materializer earns
the check syntax already has -- that is separate, later work, one materializer at a time.
What is real right now is the syntax-only and source-text case: a rule that reads nothing
but nomos.cap.syntax.items, or reads no fact at all and judges sources directly, has nothing
left to see when a second call over the same, unmoved sources runs.
items.done_when:
A caller that keeps a workspace, fact store and a new per-rule reassessment cache across
two calls to this crate's run pipeline, with the same selection and zero content changes
between calls, does not run the closure again for any selected rule whose own
nomos_rules::RuleDescriptor.requires names only RequiredFact::SyntaxItems, or names no
family at all (every SubjectKind::SourceText rule) -- its prior findings are reused
instead. A selected rule needing any other family still runs its closure again on the
second call, since that family's own materializer has no currency check yet. Existing
callers of the existing Run function, which construct a fresh cache per call, see no
behavior change at all. Proven by a test that counts real rule-closure invocations, not
just materializations, across a selection spanning both kinds of rule, over an
otherwise-identical second call: the syntax-only and source-text rules' counts do not
grow, the other kind's does.

items.title: Four surfaces widened and their snapshots were never blessed
items.why:
cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests --test public_surface's Test_Every_Crates_Public_Surface_
Should_Match_Its_Snapshot fails today for four crates -- nomos-api,
nomos-correction-orchestration, nomos-corrections and nomos-gate-orchestration -- each
exporting something its own committed snapshot under tests/contract/surface/ does not show.

Traced each to a real, already-committed change earlier in this session that never ran the
NOMOS_SURFACE_BLESS step afterward: nomos-correction-orchestration's and nomos-api's own
CorrectionOutcome/CorrectionResponse enums renamed a claimed field to summary; nomos-gate-
orchestration gained Compare_Gate_Runs, GateCompareResult, DispositionChange and
FindingDisposition (commit d99b689e, confirmed via git show --stat: it touched
gate_compare.rs and lib.rs and nothing under tests/contract/surface/); nomos-corrections
gained CorrectionCandidate::Read_Write and With_Read_Write. Each item's own predicate at the
time only named its own package, so none of them reached this suite and the gap went
uncaught until an unrelated item (P40-MCP-SURFACE-4) ran the whole contract suite and found
it red for a reason that was not its own change.

Nobody currently holds these four files; they are stale, not mid-flight.
items.done_when:
cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests --test public_surface passes, with
tests/contract/surface/nomos-api.txt, nomos-correction-orchestration.txt,

agree with what each crate really exports today, and nothing else in this workspace's real
public surface changed to make that comparison pass -- verified by re-reading each diff the
bless step would have compared away and confirming it matches only the additions this
item's own why already names (the claimed-to-summary rename, Compare_Gate_Runs and its
supporting types, and CorrectionCandidate::Read_Write/With_Read_Write), not a fifth,
unnoticed drift.

items.title: Two real blocking gate findings shipped with the rule-reassessment cache
items.why:
P40-INCREMENTAL-SKIP-UNCHANGED-RULES shipped two real blocking gate violations, both in
crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/src/run_context.rs and the file it added:
RuleReassessmentCache is public but lived in rule_reassessment.rs instead of
rule_reassessment_cache.rs (file-name-matches-declared-type), and adding the reassessment
cache and changed-families slice as direct parameters pushed Findings_For_Selected_Rules,
Judged_Findings, Judged_Over and Rule_Findings to arity 5 or 6 against a configured cap of
4 (parameter-count).

Neither was caught at the time: that item's own predicate named only nomos-check-
orchestration and nomos-rules, which runs no naming-convention or parameter-count rule
over its own source, and nothing in the loop re-ran the real workspace-wide gate (crates/
host/nomos-cli/src/check.rs's own real-tree integration test) until this session's next
item (P40-WORKFLOW-CLI-VERB) happened to depend on nomos-cli's own predicate reaching it.
items.done_when:
RuleReassessmentCache's own file is named rule_reassessment_cache.rs, every function whose
own arity exceeded the configured parameter-count cap of 4 is at or under it (grouping the
reassessment cache, the changed-families slice and the rule selection into named values the
same way this file already groups its other parameters), cargo test -p
nomos-check-orchestration passes, and a real gate run over this workspace's own tree no
longer names either finding.

items.why:
OD-PACKAGE-015 (v2) marked the repository-policy family for consolidation: six crates --
nomos-repo-standards-document and its five providers nomos-repo-standards, nomos-repo-limits,
nomos-repo-scripting, nomos-repo-words, nomos-repo-goals -- fail every clause of the
crate-boundary test (no independent versioning, no enforced isolation, and their only two
consumers, nomos-check-orchestration and tests/integration, already depend on all five
providers together every time). The record explicitly left carrying that verdict out to a
future item. This is that item.

A new crate nomos-repo-policy under crates/repository/ holds the former nomos-repo-standards-
document, nomos-repo-standards, nomos-repo-limits, nomos-repo-scripting, nomos-repo-words and

every public type any of the six exported is reachable from nomos-repo-policy under the same
name, only under a new crate-qualified path; nomos-check-orchestration and tests/integration
build and pass against the new crate; README.md's band table and Cargo.toml's member list
name nomos-repo-policy in place of the six; tests/contract's boundary/band tests and surface
snapshots reflect one crate instead of six, with no stale snapshot left for a deleted crate.

Its predicate, cargo test --workspace, is real and correctly scoped, but its 600-second

items.title: The filesystem port cannot list a directory, which is why every host walks the tree itself
items.why:
The port offers Read_To_String, Replace_Atomically, Exists and Remove_File and nothing
that enumerates a directory. Because of that omission every caller that needs to find
files reaches past the port to std::fs directly, and check orchestration documents the
walk staying outside for exactly this reason. That was defensible when one host walked;
it is now the mechanical cause of duplicated walkers in nomos-cli and nomos-api and of the
hardcoded extension lists in both. A port missing a capability that several real consumers
need is a gap in the port, not a reason to keep bypassing it.
items.done_when:
The filesystem port enumerates a directory, the standard implementation and the test
double both provide it, at least one existing caller that reached for std::fs directly now
goes through the port, and the decision is recorded.

Declined.reason:
A second territory gap, found only after the first correction: adding Read_Directory to
the trait and StdFileSystem widens both crates' public surface, and
tests/contract/tests/public_surface's own snapshot test refuses to pass until
tests/contract/surface/nomos-platform.txt and nomos-platform-std.txt are reblessed --
neither reserved by this item's territory, the same class of gap the prior decline named
for std_file_system.rs and work.rs. All code from the prior attempt carries forward
unreverted (the trait method, its default-refusal test, the standard implementation and
its two tests, the Published_Records migration and its two new tests, the check/sources.rs
doc correction, and the OD-PLATFORM-002 record and its registration all already exist on
disk and are unaffected by this decline).

abandoned.reason: re-authoring again to add the two surface-snapshot paths a widened trait requires blessing

items.title: The band table is maintained by hand in three places and a fourth checks it
items.why:
Whatever the zone decision concludes, the mechanism that enforces it is currently a
numeric table copied into the contract-test boundaries suite, into the dependency rule
inside nomos-rules, and into the README, with a real gate run checking the third copy
against the first two. Three hand-maintained copies of the architecture is the same
unchecked-copy defect this repository has paid for elsewhere, and it is why a band change
is remembered as touching three files rather than one. The migration should land the
decided model once and derive the rest.
items.done_when:
The dependency model is declared in one place, the enforcement rule and the contract-test
boundary suite both read that one declaration rather than their own copies, the README
table is derived or checked rather than maintained by hand, and a real gate run still
refuses a forbidden edge.

Declined.reason:
A fourth territory gap, found only after the code was already implemented and green:
adding ZONES, SAME_ZONE_EDGES and ALL as public constants to nomos-rules made them real
"declared universes" OD-COMPLETENESS-001's own scanner picks up, and
tests/contract/tests/completeness_universes/table.rs must classify each one (Standing::
Mirrored, naming the real test that checks it against reality) or the derivation test
refuses to pass -- a file this item's prior territory never named. All implementation
work is complete and independently verified before this decline: cargo test -p nomos-rules
-p nomos-contract-tests all green (583 + full contract suite passing, including the new
Test_Every_Same_Zone_Edge_Should_Be_A_Real_Dependency and Test_Every_Zone_Should_Be_
Matched_Exhaustively mirrors this table row needs), cargo build --workspace clean, cargo
clippy --workspace --all-targets clean, and the nomos-rules surface reblessed. Re-authoring
with the complete file list `git status --short` now shows rather than guessing again.

abandoned.reason: re-authoring once more to add tests/contract/tests/completeness_universes/table.rs, discovered mid-implementation; everything else already verified green

items.title: The shared text substrate under the rules does not know what a string literal is
items.why: Measured 2026-09-05 against the built binary: the comment stripper every text rule copies is a naive split on the first two-slash sequence, so a line whose string literal holds a URL is truncated at that URL and everything after it becomes invisible; a bare path-suffix self-exemption lets any repository whose file happens to end in the same path spoof exemption from the rule that would otherwise judge it. A single shared code_prefix.rs, aware of string, raw-string and char literals, replaces the identical naive copy this session found in sixteen files (eleven with a named Code_Prefix function, three with the same expression inlined, plus rust_text.rs and code_prefix.rs itself), and the ten self-exemption checks now compare a full repo-relative path exactly rather than a path suffix. A first design also blanked every literal's own body so a syntax detector's bare .contains("unsafe {") could not match a string that merely quotes the words; it broke three real, passing tests that read a specific literal's own value as syntax (#[path="value"], .expect("message"), t.Skip("reason")), so it was reverted in favor of comment-boundary correctness alone, documented in code_prefix.rs's own module doc as a real, narrower gap this item does not close.
items.done_when: code_prefix.rs exists with a real byte-level scanner aware of string literals, raw strings (including b-prefixed byte-string forms) and char literals holding a quote, distinguishing a char literal from a lifetime. Every one of the sixteen files that copied the naive line.split("//").next() shape uses it instead. Every one of the ten self-exemption checks compares a full repo-relative path exactly rather than by suffix. Three fixtures reproduce as tests: a URL inside a string followed by real code, a lifetime not misread as a char literal, and two files with identical content at two different paths getting identical verdicts. cargo test -p nomos-rules passes and cargo clippy -p nomos-rules introduces no new warning, including no indexing_slicing or arithmetic_side_effects violation (workspace deny-level lints).

items.title: A review finding carries no outcome, and there is only one provider to compare it against
items.why: CodeRabbit review findings enter this workspace through nomos-connector-coderabbit as FindingPayload, whose own doc comment says its eight fields are kept apart from any judgment about whether the finding is valid or what it bears on. Check_Review_Findings then relays that fact into the one Finding shape every rule in this workspace uses, and Finding carries rule, subject, subject_name, applicability, evidence, gate, summary and locations, with no field for what happened to a finding after a person or a correction looked at it. EvidenceClass already forbids the nearby shortcut: AgentJudged is a floor that cannot be promoted afterward, because promotion would have to happen somewhere that no longer holds the evidence. An external architectural review of this workspace, checked directly against the real tree rather than taken on faith, named the next stage past ingestion: whether a finding was accepted, rejected, judged a duplicate, superseded, or whether a correction built from it succeeded or failed, becoming benchmark evidence for comparing providers rather than mutating a rule automatically. Nothing in nomos-contracts, nomos-connector-coderabbit, or nomos-corrections carries that outcome today, and there is exactly one review connector in this workspace, so nothing yet needs comparing against it.

items.title: A review finding carries no outcome, and there is only one provider to compare it against
items.why: CodeRabbit review findings enter this workspace through nomos-connector-coderabbit as FindingPayload, whose own doc comment says its eight fields are kept apart from any judgment about whether the finding is valid or what it bears on. Check_Review_Findings then relays that fact into the one Finding shape every rule in this workspace uses, and Finding carries rule, subject, subject_name, applicability, evidence, gate, summary and locations, with no field for what happened to a finding after a person or a correction looked at it. EvidenceClass already forbids the nearby shortcut: AgentJudged is a floor that cannot be promoted afterward, because promotion would have to happen somewhere that no longer holds the evidence. An external architectural review of this workspace, checked directly against the real tree rather than taken on faith, named the next stage past ingestion: whether a finding was accepted, rejected, judged a duplicate, superseded, or whether a correction built from it succeeded or failed, becoming benchmark evidence for comparing providers rather than mutating a rule automatically. Nothing in nomos-contracts, nomos-connector-coderabbit, or nomos-corrections carries that outcome today, and there is exactly one review connector in this workspace, so nothing yet needs comparing against it.
items.done_when: A record measures the gap directly: confirms FindingPayload and Finding carry no outcome or disposition field today; states why a disposition must be a new fact rather than a rewrite of the original evidence class, citing the rule already in EvidenceClass against promoting a claim after the fact; names exactly what a disposition fact would need, a closed set of outcomes keyed to a durable identity for the finding rather than its file location, and a home for it, since nomos-contracts documents every field of Finding as load-bearing and none of the eight open a place for one; and states plainly that comparing providers needs a second real review provider before a selection mechanism is buildable, not merely a second finding. No code changes under this item. The record is both documented under docs/records/ and registered under crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/, per OD-SPEC-007.

items.title: Is_Unsafe_Declaration reads a string literal's own text as a real declaration
items.why: crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust-scan/src/item_kind.rs:70 is a string-literal table entry, ("unsafe impl", Self::Implementation), and unsafe-justification reports it as an unjustified unsafe fn/impl/trait despite a real // SAFETY: comment three lines above explaining exactly this: the rule is text-local and cannot see the keyword sits inside a string. Is_Unsafe_Declaration and Has_Unsafe_Construct (rust_text.rs) are both bare substring searches over Code_Prefix's own output, and Code_Prefix deliberately preserves a string's own body rather than blanking it (P45-CODE-PREFIX-KNOWS-STRINGS-2, reverted an earlier blanking design because other rules need a string's real value) -- so any file whose string literal happens to contain the phrase unsafe fn/impl/trait/unsafe { will misroute through Has_Local_Safety_Justification's declaration-vs-block dispatch. This file's own comment already correctly diagnoses the defect but could only add a workaround comment for the block-check path, not fix the declaration-dispatch misrouting the comment's own SAFETY marker cannot satisfy (Has_Rustdoc_Safety_Section wants a /// doc comment, not the // block this site has).
items.done_when: A rule judging unsafe-justification does not misclassify a string literal's own text as a real unsafe declaration or construct; item_kind.rs:70 is judged correctly (either as justified via its existing // SAFETY: comment, or the false trigger is gone), and a regression test proves the case: a string literal containing the exact phrase unsafe impl must not be read as a declaration.

items.title: single-letter-names reads a blanket impl's own generic Self-type parameter as a chosen name
items.why: P45-RULES-CALIBRATED-AGAINST-CODE-THEY-WERE-NOT-TUNED-ON's own third-party fixture (hex 0.4.3) surfaced this directly: impl<T: AsRef<[u8]>> ToHex for T reports T as an unjustified single-letter name. T is not a struct field or an ordinarily-declared item name a human carelessly abbreviated; nomos_lang_rust::syntax::walk's visit_item_impl records an Implementation item's own name as Type_Head(&node.self_ty), which for this common, idiomatic blanket-impl-over-a-generic-parameter shape is literally the generic parameter's own already-declared name, reached a second time through the Implementation item path. single_letter_names.rs's own module doc already states generic parameters are out of this rule's scope (left to a richer syntax shape) -- but that exemption does not reach this path, since the walker files this occurrence under the Implementation item's own name, not under the generic-parameter declaration site the existing exemption was written against. Invisible from nomos's own tree, which does not happen to write a blanket impl over a bare generic parameter this way.
items.done_when: single-letter-names does not report an Implementation item whose own name is a bare generic parameter already declared on that same impl (or the underlying Implementation-item-naming choice in the syntax walk is corrected so this case does not reach the rule as a chosen name). A regression test proves it: impl<T: AsRef<[u8]>> ToHex for T must not be reported, the same way a real, deliberately abbreviated single-letter binding elsewhere still is.

Declined.reason: Investigated the payload directly: PayloadItem (crates/capabilities/nomos-cap-syntax/src/payload_item.rs) carries only kind/visibility/qualified_name/documentation/shape, and an Implementation item's shape (nomos-lang-rust/src/syntax/shape.rs's Impl_Shape) is only ever TRAIT or INHERENT, computed from node.trait_.is_some() alone. The impl block's own generic parameter list (syn::ItemImpl::generics, read at the exact call site in walk.rs's visit_item_impl, right beside the unused node.generics field) is never threaded into the payload at all -- there is no existing signal single_letter_names.rs could read to tell impl<T: AsRef<[u8]>> ToHex for T (self-type is a bare, already-declared generic parameter) apart from impl Trait for X where X is a real, single-letter-named struct someone actually chose and still deserves the finding. A rule-side heuristic with no new data (e.g. exempting every single-uppercase-letter Implementation name) would hide that second, real case, which is worse than the gap this item names. Closing it honestly needs the payload's shape vocabulary extended to carry an impl's own generic parameter names -- a change spanning nomos-lang-rust's walker, nomos-lang-rust/src/syntax/shape.rs, and nomos-cap-syntax's payload shape encoding, the identical kind of payload-extension decision OD-CAPABILITY-011 made for three other named cases -- not a single-file Correction against single_letter_names.rs alone. Re-file as a Decision item scoped to that payload extension, with this Correction re-authored to depend on it once the extension exists.

abandoned.reason: investigated before deciding; the fix needs more territory than declared, see decline reason

items.title: cargo clippy, cargo metadata and cargo deny do not confine themselves to the judged root
items.why: P45-RULES-CALIBRATED-AGAINST-CODE-THEY-WERE-NOT-TUNED-ON measured this directly while building its own fixture. Pointed at a root nested inside a larger cargo workspace with no manifest of its own stopping cargo's upward search, cargo clippy --workspace and cargo metadata (nomos-lang-rust-clippy's and nomos-lang-rust-cargo's own Materialize_Lint/Materialize_Dependencies) silently escaped upward and judged the enclosing workspace instead -- 174 unrelated lint-diagnostics findings about crates the caller never named. Giving the judged root its own manifest closes that escape for cargo itself, but cargo deny's own config/manifest discovery is a second, independent escape the same fix does not close: nomos-lang-rust-deny's Cargo_Deny_Command sets only working_directory, never a --manifest-path or --config, so cargo deny walks upward past the judged root's own boundary regardless and picks up whatever deny.toml it finds first. Neither provider's own materialization confines the real subprocess it launches to the root a caller actually named; both rely entirely on that root already being a self-contained cargo workspace, which nomos's own tree always is and an arbitrary judged root is not guaranteed to be.
items.done_when: A rule judging a root that is not itself a cargo workspace root (nested inside a larger one, with no manifest of its own) does not silently report findings about the enclosing workspace instead. Each of the three affected commands (cargo clippy, cargo metadata, cargo deny) either is invoked with an explicit flag confining it to the given root, or the materialization refuses honestly when it cannot confirm the subprocess judged only what was asked. A regression fixture proves it: a directory with no cargo manifest of its own, nested inside a real workspace, must not produce a finding about anything outside itself.

items.title: nomos-cli's own gate::tests assert zero Blocking findings, which P45's fixture now permanently contradicts

P45-RULES-CALIBRATED-AGAINST-CODE-THEY-WERE-NOT-TUNED-ON (3be57464) deliberately committed tests/integration/fixtures/third-party/hex-0.4.3 with one permanent, accepted true positive (abbreviations: val, calibration.rs's own RuleVerdict table names it Expected::TruePositive(1)) plus single-letter-names: T, tracked separately by P70-IMPL-BLOCK-GENERIC-PARAMETERS-NOT-IN-PAYLOAD. Both are Blocking. Measured directly against the real tree at HEAD (31750a5e), independent of any uncommitted work: both gate::tests fail today, and neither test's own predicate has ever been named by an item's verification argv (every item this session named -p nomos-check-orchestration, -p nomos-rules, or -p nomos-cli --test check_command specifically, never -p nomos-cli --bin nomos), so this went unnoticed since P45 landed. Discovered independently in two unrelated worktrees (P47-TOOLPROVIDER-HAS-NO-PACKAGE-2's and P68-SUBPROCESS-PROVIDERS-ESCAPE-A-NESTED-ROOT's), each reproducing the identical failure with completely disjoint changes -- confirming it is neither item's own regression.
items.done_when: Both gate::tests pass again, honestly: either the test's own expectation is corrected to account for a real, permanently-accepted third-party calibration fixture that is not itself first-party code this workspace's own gate judges for cleanliness (excluding tests/integration/fixtures/third-party/ from what a real gate run over this workspace's own tree walks, if that is the right boundary -- OD-GATE-* precedent should be checked before deciding), or the assertion is corrected to name the exact accepted findings rather than asserting zero. Whichever is chosen, a future third true positive accepted the same deliberate way (a fourth calibration fixture, say) must not silently re-break this test a second time.

items.title: OD-RULES-025 records a live rule-count instance whose three figures have all moved

But the record also names 67, 65 or 84 as the three candidate values a future rule must choose between, which is now a list of three numbers none of which exists in the tree, and it presents them as what that rule should expect to find on its first run. This is an instance of the very defect the record defines, and the same shape as P72-STALE-PLATFORM-DIRECTORY-CLAIM, where an external reviewer read a stale figure out of committed prose and recommended the wrong thing.

The nomos-rules module prose is not hand-corrected: the record's own stated reason for declining to choose among the counts still stands.

items.title: nomos-lsp hardcodes the correction-family membership that correction orchestration keeps private
items.why: nomos-lsp answers whether a correction family exists for a finding by hardcoding two rule ids in available_correction.rs: COMPLETENESS_MIRROR and NO_TRAILING_WHITESPACE. The real membership is a private local array at nomos-correction-orchestration run.rs line 162, and that crate exports only CorrectionCommand, CorrectionOutcome, CorrectionEnvironment and Run_Correction, so there is no membership query for a host to call. A third correction family composed into run.rs would leave the LSP silently reporting no correction available for it, and nothing would fail: the two ids are real public constants of nomos-rules, so the duplication compiles, tests green, and drifts quietly. The crate module doc already states both the defect and its remedy, that a real fix is exporting that membership from nomos-correction-orchestration itself rather than inventing it in the host. This is a live instance of the duplicate-authority class OD-RULES-025 describes, sitting inside the one host OD-HOST-003 says must consume canonical services rather than hold engineering knowledge of its own.
items.done_when: nomos-correction-orchestration exports the set of rule ids it composes a correction family for; nomos-lsp AvailableCorrection resolves membership from that export instead of its own literal array; the committed surface snapshot for nomos-correction-orchestration records the new export; and a test fails if a rule id is added to the composed set in run.rs without the exported membership following it, so the next family cannot drift the two apart silently.

Declined.reason: Territory too narrow, caught before anyone claimed it. A definitive sweep for every site naming both correction-family rule ids found that crates/host/nomos-lsp/src/walk_outward.rs carries the tests asserting the correction answer this item changes, and it was not reserved. The minimal fix may leave those tests untouched, but that is the same assumption P72-STALE-PLATFORM-DIRECTORY-CLAIM made about its own population and paid for with two follow-up items. Re-authored as -2 with walk_outward.rs added. The sweep also confirmed the substance is right: the membership duplication is exactly two sites, available_correction.rs and run.rs line 162; the other seven files naming both ids are rule registration or fixtures, not membership.

items.title: The fact store dies with the process, so incremental work cannot survive an invocation
items.why: OD-ANALYSIS-009 already frames the question of whether Run should read a persistent fact store instead of constructing one fresh per invocation, and leaves it open. Skipping unchanged subjects and recomputing only demanded facts both buy nothing across process boundaries while the only store is in memory: every CLI invocation starts cold, which is the case that actually matters to somebody running the gate. This was originally sequenced after P40-INCREMENTAL-DEMAND-DRIVEN-RECOMPUTE, which was declined twice and never re-authored under that name; the currency machinery it was waiting for arrived instead as P40-INCREMENTAL-SKIP-UNCHANGED-SUBJECTS, P40-INCREMENTAL-SKIP-UNCHANGED-RULES and P40-INCREMENTAL-SKIP-COVERAGE-REGRESSION, all Done. What is worth persisting and what a cache entry must carry to be safely reused are answered by that landed work rather than guessed ahead of it. It also brings a lifecycle with it, since a durable cache needs eviction, a version boundary and a way to be invalidated wholesale when the build variant changes.
items.done_when: The persistence question OD-ANALYSIS-009 leaves open is decided and recorded, and if the decision is to persist, a store survives process exit, is keyed so a stale entry cannot be served across a build-variant or contract-version change, and has a stated eviction and invalidation lifecycle.

items.why: P42-AGENT-STRUCTURED-WORKRESULT was declined for an under-reserved territory and re-authored as a decision, P42-EXECUTOR-WORKRESULT-MECHANISM, whose own title ends in the words before code. items.why: A Claude Code executor and an Ollama backend both really run, and typed agent contracts exist, but nothing carries what an agent produced into a correction the system validates before committing. The game plan is explicit that an agent executor should not precede a solid mutation and validation contract; the executor was built first, so closing this restores that ordering rather than adding to the inversion. Sequenced behind the canonical correction seam because a workflow or agent tier calling into a CLI module would invert the layering, and behind the canonical result implementation because the executor does not construct one yet, so this path would otherwise be built on a vendor-shaped response. nomos-agent-orchestration is the seam that should carry this: it already dispatches an executor and it is the application-service peer of the correction orchestration it needs, but it does not name that peer today, so an explicit zone edge is part of the work rather than an accident of it.

items.title: One agent executor exists, so nothing has shown which of its choices are the contract
items.why: The Claude Code executor is properly bounded: fresh isolated working directory, strict tool configuration, a structural allow-list, one turn, a budget ceiling, timeout and stall handling, and structured parsing rather than trusting prose. A harness executor gets no scheduler authority, no work-graph authority and no rule authority.

items.title: Four hosts walk the tree themselves and each hardcodes the languages Nomos supports
items.why: nomos-api sources.rs calls itself a deliberate twin of the CLI walker, and measured directly at c0e5c79f there are four copies, not two: nomos-api sources.rs, nomos-cli check/sources.rs, nomos-cli gate/sources.rs and nomos-lsp sources.rs. That is four copies of the answer to which files Nomos analyses, in the layer that is supposed to be a thin adapter. The specification puts file and project recognition in LanguagePackage and says every user-visible action gets a canonical application service rather than client-specific logic; discovery is currently the clearest violation of both. Recognition should come from registered packages and providers so that adding a language does not require editing every host.

Abandoning to decline and re-author with both added, so the two now-dead use lines can be removed rather than left as debris this item's own edit caused.

items.title: A discovered file is a nomos-rules type, so discovery is owned by the layer that judges
items.why: SourceFile is declared in nomos-rules and it is what the API and CLI walkers return and what the whole orchestration passes around. That inverts ownership: a discovered artifact exists before any rule does, and making the rules package its owner means the workspace, analysis and discovery layers all depend on the judging layer to describe their own input. It also means a future consumer that never judges anything still links the rules package to name a file. A canonical source or artifact representation belongs to workspace, model or analysis, with rules consuming it. Sequenced behind P41-WORKSPACE-DISCOVERY-SERVICE-2 because that item removes four of this type's call sites and introduces the canonical service that is the natural owner, so migrating consumers before it lands would migrate a population about to change.
items.done_when: The canonical discovered-source type is owned by workspace, model or analysis rather than by the rules package, rules consume it rather than declaring it, and no crate depends on nomos-rules solely to name its input.

Declined.reason: Its done_when cannot be satisfied as written, measured rather than argued. It requires the canonical discovered-source type to be owned by workspace, model or analysis; SourceFile carries language: Option<Language> from nomos-cap-syntax, a Capability Contract crate, and nomos gate admits refuses all three candidates that edge -- nomos-model, nomos-workspace and nomos-analysis are Substrate, and Substrate may not name a Capability Contract, while nomos-rules is Rules and may. So the move the item asks for is refused by this workspace's own layering until something else changes first. Two other things about it were also stale or short. Its dependency named P41-WORKSPACE-DISCOVERY-SERVICE-2, which was declined for a territory reason and re-authored twice more to P41-WORKSPACE-DISCOVERY-SERVICE-4, now Done -- so the edge that stranded this item was stale and the sequencing it wanted is satisfied. And its territory reserved one file, crates/rules/nomos-rules/src/lib.rs, for a change reaching fifteen crates' imports and manifests. Superseded by P95-A-LANGUAGE-IDENTITY-IS-MISFILED-IN-A-CAPABILITY-CONTRACT, which decides the blocker; the ownership move follows that answer rather than preceding it.

items.title: A decision item satisfies its own done_when while leaving every dependent stranded behind it
items.why: Found twice in one sweep of the board, and both instances were invisible until every stranded edge was walked by hand. An item is declined for an under-reserved territory and re-authored as a decision whose title ends in the words before code. That decision is claimed, recorded and finished honestly: its done_when asked for a decided mechanism and it delivered one. But the items that depended on the original were never repointed, and repointing them onto the decision would not help, because a decision structurally cannot satisfy a dependent whose own precondition is working code. P42-EXECUTOR-ENVELOPE-MECHANISM and P42-EXECUTOR-WORKRESULT-MECHANISM are both Done and recorded as OD-EXECUTOR-007 and OD-EXECUTOR-008; P42-SECOND-HARNESS-EXECUTOR and P40-AGENT-WORKRESULT-VALIDATED-PATH-2 sat stranded behind them with no implementation item filed at all. The board reported next: nothing is eligible with thirteen items Ready, and none of the five stranded ones was missing work. Two further mechanics made this hard to see and are part of the same defect: a re-authored successor is sometimes renamed rather than suffixed, so a search by -2 suffix reports it absent, and one root was decomposed into three narrower items rather than re-authored under its own name. The ledger already knows how to say stranded; what it cannot currently say is that a dependency was answered by a decision that was never carried out.
items.done_when: It is decided whether the ledger should refuse or flag a decline whose stated remedy is a follow-up that is never filed, whether a decision item may be named as a dependency by an item needing code, and how a re-authored successor is discoverable from the id it replaces; and the decision is recorded.

Declined.reason: Scope was too narrow, found so within the session that authored it. Two things arrived after it was filed. First, a third instance: OD-GATE-022 is Done, its own What This Record Does Not Do section says it does not wire compare into any surface and that each is separate implementation territory, and Compare_Gate_Runs has zero callers -- filed as P73-GATE-COMPARE-HAS-NO-CALLER. Three instances is a shape, not a coincidence. Second, nomos-dd observed that a decline orphans a subtree the same way a decision-before-code item does, from the other direction, and demonstrated it in one write: declining P41-RUN-PLANNER stranded three dependents directly and left four more waiting behind those, with no warning at decline time and no prompt to repoint anything. Both are the same underlying defect -- an item can be ended honestly while silently making other items unreachable -- and their remedies are likely the same mechanism, so one record should name both rather than two records each seeing half. Re-added as -2.

items.title: Compare_Gate_Runs is exported, decided and reachable by nobody
items.why: Measured at ecfaf833: Compare_Gate_Runs has zero callers. The only two mentions outside its own module are its own re-export in lib.rs and a line of lib.rs prose describing it. The CLI refuses the verb outright -- gate/parsing.rs treats compare as an unknown verb and gate/tests.rs asserts that refusal -- so the one surface a user could reach it from is wired to say no. This is the third instance this session of a decided mechanism with no code behind it, after OD-EXECUTOR-007 and OD-EXECUTOR-008, and it is the cleanest: OD-GATE-022 is Done and its own What This Record Does Not Do section says in as many words that it does not wire compare into the CLI, nomos-api, nomos-api-transport or nomos-mcp, that each is separate implementation territory, and that each can now proceed without inventing its own answer. Its Status goes further and names the shape a first caller takes: two same-process walks of Run_Gate over two roots, two revisions or two policies produce the two GateRunResults it already takes, needing no new store and no new serializable type. Nothing was filed against that. P62-GATE-COMPARE-LIB-DOC-STALE corrected the lib.rs prose that said no increment implements compare, which left the documentation accurate and the verb still unreachable. This item takes the CLI only, because the record calls each surface separate territory.
items.done_when: nomos gate compare runs two real same-process walks and prints their difference; the CLI stops refusing the verb and the test asserting that refusal is replaced by one asserting the verb works; a second root is named by a decided argument shape; the disposition changes between the two runs are rendered; and no new serializable type is added to nomos-gate-orchestration to do it.

items.title: An item can be ended honestly and leave other items silently unreachable
items.why: Two shapes of one defect, both measured on this board in one session. Shape one, a decision that cannot satisfy its dependents: an item declined for under-reserved territory is re-authored as a decision whose title ends in the words before code. It is claimed, recorded and finished honestly, because its done_when asked for a decided mechanism and it delivered one. But a dependent whose own precondition is working code is not satisfied by it, and repointing onto it would not help. Three instances. P42-EXECUTOR-ENVELOPE-MECHANISM and P42-EXECUTOR-WORKRESULT-MECHANISM are Done as OD-EXECUTOR-007 and OD-EXECUTOR-008, and P42-SECOND-HARNESS-EXECUTOR and P40-AGENT-WORKRESULT-VALIDATED-PATH-2 sat stranded behind them with no implementation filed. OD-GATE-022 is Done and explicitly says it does not wire compare into any surface and that each is separate implementation territory, and Compare_Gate_Runs still has zero callers. Shape two, a decline that orphans a live subtree: declining P41-RUN-PLANNER stranded three dependents directly and left four more waiting behind those, in a single write, with nothing said at decline time about the seven items just made unreachable. The decline was correct on its merits and the cascade was still invisible. Two mechanics make both shapes hard to see afterward and belong to the same question: a re-authored successor is sometimes renamed rather than suffixed, so a search by -2 reports it absent -- this session reported two such successors as missing work before finding them by territory -- and one root was decomposed into three narrower items rather than re-authored under its own name. The ledger already knows how to say stranded. What it cannot say is that a dependency was answered by a decision nobody carried out, or that ending one item just ended six others.
items.done_when: It is decided whether the ledger should warn or refuse when a decline or a finish leaves dependents unreachable, whether a decision item may be named as a dependency by an item whose precondition is code, whether a decline whose stated remedy is a follow-up must file one, and how a re-authored successor is discoverable from the id it replaces; and the decision is recorded naming both shapes rather than one.

items.title: Whether a bundled contract crate doing real I/O may be classified Capability Contract zone
items.why: The eighth-round review's fourth point was the one this reconciliation left unrecorded, and it has substance the other nine did not. nomos-connector-coderabbit runs gh api as a subprocess and nomos-cap-requirement-trace reads arbitrary files through a FileSystem, and both are classified Capability Contract zone. OD-CAPABILITY-002 licenses the bundling and its one-provider criterion is untouched by this, but it decides nothing about the zone consequence. Two instances exist, so this is not a population of one.

items.title: gate plan describes the registry and does not vary with scope, rules or policy
items.why: The plan verb is the one place a person can ask what a gate would do before it does it, and it answers the same way regardless of root, scope, selected rules, suppressions, baseline or adoption. That is registry introspection wearing the name of a plan. GatePlan holds exactly one field, rules: Vec<RuleOffer>, and its own doc states it does not vary by GateCommand::root, scope or rules. Re-authored from P41-GATE-PLAN-IS-A-PLAN, which OD-GATE-023 measured and freed: the original waited on P41-GATE-SELECTION-COLLAPSE and through it on the declined planner, but making the plan vary needs only ScopeSelector and RuleSelector, both of which already exist and are already consulted by Run_Gate. The dependency was inherited from a sibling rather than required by the work.
items.done_when: Two gate plan invocations differing only in scope or selected rules produce different plans, and a test pins that correspondence. This does not require the plan to be the same resolved object a run executes, which was the original item's planner-shaped half and is not carried forward.

Declined.reason: Territory (gate_plan.rs alone) omits where the real fix lives: GatePlan's own struct shape (rules: Vec<RuleOffer>) does not need to change at all -- what needs to change is run.rs's Run(), which currently ignores command entirely (parameter named _command) and would need to read command.rules and filter registry.Offers() by it for two invocations to differ. lib.rs's own doc also states as fact that GatePlan does not vary by root/scope/rules/suppressions/baseline/adoption, which would go stale and undocumented once rules-filtering lands. Re-authored as P41-GATE-PLAN-IS-A-PLAN-3 with run.rs and lib.rs added, unchanged in kind, done_when and predicate. Caught by inspection before claiming, not mid-implementation, following the same lesson P40-GATE-PHASES-APPROVALS learned the hard way twice this session.

items.title: Declared phases, thresholds and approvals are named as unbuilt WF-001 gate semantics
items.why: A gate today is one undifferentiated pass over every selected rule: no way to say one group of checks must pass before another is attempted, no numeric threshold a run is judged against, no approval a human or agent supplies to let a run proceed despite a finding. These turn a gate from a single verdict into a policy a team can adopt incrementally. Re-authored from P40-GATE-PHASES-APPROVALS-2, which stated its own sequencing reason: a phase partitions the selected rule set, and partitioning a set resolved in two places would inherit that ambiguity. OD-GATE-023 measured that OD-GATE-017 already resolved selection in one place, so the condition the item set for itself is met and the planner dependency it inherited is gone.
items.done_when: A gate run can declare ordered phases whose later phases do not run when an earlier one fails, judge a numeric threshold, and record an approval that changes a disposition, each covered by a test and each reachable from the gate orchestration seam.

Declined.reason: Territory too narrow, caught before implementing rather than after (the same pattern P42-LSP-PROJECTION and P73-LSP-CORRECTION-FAMILY-DUPLICATED both hit). gate_phase.rs alone cannot even become part of this crate's compilation: nothing declares 'mod gate_phase;' anywhere, and only lib.rs can. Read against every prior single-concern increment in this crate (suppression, baseline, adoption, coverage), each wired its policy type into GateCommand (a new field), Run_Gate/gate_environment.rs (consultation) and GateRunResult (a carried field) -- the done_when's own 'reachable from the gate orchestration seam' asks for the same shape here, which this item's one-file territory cannot reach. Re-authored as P40-GATE-PHASES-APPROVALS-4 with gate_command.rs, gate_environment.rs, gate_plan/gate_run_result.rs, lib.rs and the surface snapshot added, unchanged in kind, done_when and predicate.

abandoned.reason: Territory reserves only gate_phase.rs, but a new module cannot even compile into this crate without a mod declaration in lib.rs, and real consultation (the done_when's 'reachable from the gate orchestration seam') needs GateCommand, Run_Gate and GateRunResult to carry it too -- the same too-narrow-territory trap P42-LSP-PROJECTION and P73-LSP-CORRECTION-FAMILY-DUPLICATED already hit. Abandoning to decline and re-author with the complete territory.

items.title: Nothing constructs a non-empty suppression, baseline, adoption or coverage policy
items.why: The internal semantics of suppressions, baselines, adoption and calibration, and coverage are real and tested, but GateCommand documents four times over that nothing builds a non-empty one. Measured at cff9df40: SuppressionPolicy, BaselinePolicy and AdoptionPolicy are constructed non-empty only inside nomos-gate-orchestration's own tests.rs, and CoveragePolicy has no non-default construction anywhere, including tests. A policy that only ever arrives empty is a policy nobody can use, and the tests exercising it are exercising a shape no caller can reach. nomos-api-transport gate_parameters.rs omits all four wire fields deliberately and names this item as the reason, on the grounds that a wire field a caller can set that changes no outcome is a promise the transport cannot keep. What is missing is the authoring and configuration surface: a declared, readable source a real run resolves these four policies from, so that suppressing a finding, adopting a baseline, or demanding a coverage floor is something a person can express rather than something only a unit test constructs. Two facts make this buildable now. Run_Gate already takes a FileSystem port and the root, so resolving there serves every caller at once rather than once per surface. And nomos_model::Subject_Of_Path is the kernel's canonical path-to-subject mapping that every real walker already uses, so a person can name a file path and the resolver can compute the SubjectId that suppression and baseline match on -- which is what makes a human-authorable file possible at all, since those two match on a digest nobody can write by hand.
items.done_when: A real gate run resolves all four policies from a declared configuration source rather than from defaults, a non-default coverage floor and at least one suppression and one baseline entry are exercised end to end, an absent source leaves every existing caller's behavior unchanged, a malformed source refuses rather than silently passing, GateCommand and the four policy types no longer document that nothing constructs a non-empty one, the transport doc that cites this item is corrected, and the public surface snapshot is re-blessed.

items.title: A person can author a suppression that silently matches nothing
items.why: P40-GATE-POLICY-AUTHORING-3 gave the four gate policies a declared source, and entries in it name a path because SubjectId is a digest nobody can write by hand. nomos_model::Subject_Of_Path turns that path into the identity a run matches on, calling the same kernel function every real walk uses. That works only for findings a rule addresses by the file's own subject. Measured directly against a real run rather than assumed: no-single-line-function-bodies and todo-format-is-todo-name-description-ticket address the file, so a path names them; completeness-mirror addresses the mirrored item and single-letter-names addresses the name, so a path names neither. The consequence is a silent one, which is what makes it worth an item: an author who writes a suppression for completeness-mirror gets no error, no warning and no effect, and the finding keeps blocking with nothing anywhere saying why the entry did not take. nomos-gate-orchestration tests.rs already documented the underlying fact before this file existed, in the comment on Test_A_Suppressed_Finding_Should_Not_Block, which reads its subject off a real run precisely because Subject_Of_Path does not name it. The fix is not a digest field in the file, which would reintroduce the unauthorable identity the design exists to avoid.
items.done_when: It is decided how a person names a sub-item finding in a declared policy, or that they cannot; if they can, a Finding carries an addressable name a policy entry can match and the resolver uses it; and either way an entry that matches nothing is reported rather than silently ignored.

items.title: The spec-change skill's render-tree rule names records but the inputs also cover source
items.why: The nomos-spec-change skill states the render-tree rule as a claim about records: the tree you render in holds exactly the registered records your commit will publish, no more and no fewer, and its worked example builds a detached worktree at HEAD and copies only the record files in. Measured on 2026-09-06 that is necessary but not sufficient. A worktree at 4bc9dc92 carrying the edited record rendered domain-specification cleanly there, freshness exit 0, and the identical bytes read stale with exit 8 against the shared tree at edd8f1c9. Both trees had byte-identical record files, byte-identical projection bodies and the same 216 registration files; the only difference was one peer commit touching gate-orchestration source and no records at all, plus one uncommitted source edit. The domain-specification input hash therefore covers repository source and not only the record set, so following the skill exactly still yields a stale projection whenever HEAD has moved on code, which is the common case in this tree. The skill's own reason for existing is that this step was absent for eleven commits, so an incomplete statement of it has the same cost.
items.done_when: The skill states that the render tree must hold what the commit publishes in source as well as records, gives the measured evidence that a records-only match is insufficient, and names the cheap correct path of rendering from the shared tree when git status shows it clean apart from the author's own change. The existing worktree recipe stays for the case where the shared tree is contaminated, with the added step of copying the source changes in and re-creating it if HEAD moves.

Declined.reason: Premise disproven by experiment. The domain-specification input digest does not cover repository source; it covers the record set only, and the staleness I attributed to a source-only commit was my own stale binary. nomos-ae reproduced the same symptom independently, found the cause, and caught it on a render diff of 85 insertions against 2180 deletions before publishing anything. Measured in a detached worktree at 5816c2bf with a binary built in that worktree: clean baseline exit 0; two source files appended to and rebuilt, still exit 0; a record body appended to and rebuilt, exit 8; that record reverted without rebuilding, still exit 8. Source does not stale it, records do, and a binary that was not rebuilt reports stale about a tree that is correct. My own error was exact: I built the worktree binary, then edited the record citation afterwards, then re-rendered without rebuilding, so the render emitted the superseded record text and mismatched the shared tree's correct binary. cargo does track docs/records as a build input, which is why a rebuild fixes it and why omitting one is silent. Nothing wrong was published: the committed projection carries edd8f1c9 twice and 4bc9dc92 zero times, and re-rendering it on a clean tree produces an empty diff. Superseded by P77-STALE-BINARY-RENDERS-A-TRUNCATED-PROJECTION, which records the real and sharper hazard.

items.title: A binary built before the last record edit renders a projection missing records, successfully
items.why: The spec-change skill says to build the binary in the render worktree, because a binary built in the shared tree has the wrong records compiled into it. It does not say what happens when the binary is right at build time and wrong afterwards, which is the common case: build the worktree binary, then edit the record again, then re-render. Record content is compiled in and cargo does track docs/records as a build input, so the second render silently emits the superseded text and every check around it passes. Two sessions hit this within an hour on 2026-09-06. One rendered a projection carrying a record citation it had already replaced, and read the resulting mismatch as evidence that repository source feeds the input digest, filing P77-SPEC-CHANGE-SKILL-RENDER-TREE-RULE-INCOMPLETE on that false premise; experiment later showed source-only changes leave freshness at exit 0 and only record changes stale it. The other, running a binary copied to a scratchpad at session start, re-rendered and produced a diff of 85 insertions against 2180 deletions, having dropped the projection entries for OD-GATE-023, OD-HOST-011, OD-HOST-012, OD-AGENT-004 and the amended OD-RULES-025, and caught it only by reading the diff. The render exits 0 and freshness then agrees with it, because both are computed from the same stale compiled-in record set. That is the shape this repository files items about: a check that passes by not looking.
items.done_when: The spec-change skill states that the render binary must be rebuilt after the last record edit and not merely built once in the worktree, gives the measured failure mode that a stale binary renders a projection with records missing while exiting 0, names reading the render diff as the check that catches it, and records that cargo tracks docs/records so a rebuild is sufficient. The measurements distinguishing record-fed from source-fed inputs are stated so the next session does not re-derive them from a symptom.

items.title: CorrectionFamily::ALL is a declared universe with no row, and it has reddened CI since 4bc9dc92
items.why: d92249e1 introduced CorrectionFamily::ALL, a const array enumerating the correction families this workspace composes. Declared_Universes scans it as a universe, so the completeness_universes suite now finds 28 scanned universes against 27 classified rows and fails on both platforms: these declared universes are not classified in UNIVERSES, naming correction_family.rs ALL Constant. It reproduces at HEAD locally, so it is committed rather than environmental, and it has failed every CI run from 4bc9dc92 onward. The item that introduced ALL passed its own gate because its predicate named two crates and work finish runs clippy as the lint step, so nothing in either reached the contract tests. This is the same trap P40-API-TRANSPORT-2 hit when a new crate's ServedMethod REGISTRY turned out to need a table row outside its territory. Six universes already establish the pattern for an All over a closed enum, including Kind All, ExitCode All, Family All, Restored All, Sibling All and RowKind All, each mirrored by an exhaustive match with no wildcard arm that fails to compile when a variant is added without acknowledgement. ALL should follow that precedent rather than raise UNMIRRORED_TOTAL, because the mirror is real and cheap and the alternative buys a hole for nothing.
items.done_when: CorrectionFamily::ALL carries a doc comment naming its mirror in the convention the scanner reads, an exhaustive-match test in its own file makes adding a variant a compile failure rather than a silent omission, UNIVERSES has a matching row whose by field names that test, UNMIRRORED_TOTAL is unchanged because the universe is genuinely mirrored, and the completeness_universes suite passes with 28 compared against 28.

items.title: A clippy discovery test roots itself at a Windows-only path, so it fails on ubuntu
items.why: Test_Discover_Workspace_Should_Read_A_First_Party_Package_From_The_Json_Stream in clippy_error.rs roots itself at Path::new of F:/repos/nomos and hand-types a matching package_id. On Windows that literal is absolute because of the drive letter, and the prefix match succeeds. On Linux it has no leading slash, so it is a relative path, and P36's own fix resolves a relative root against the real current directory before matching. The resolved root is then the current directory joined with F:/repos/nomos, which the hand-typed package_id cannot be under, so Discover_Workspace finds no first-party member and refuses. The test passes locally on Windows with 18 of 18 and fails on ubuntu-latest only. It was masked until now: earlier CI runs failed further up the pipeline, on the nomos-capability surface snapshot and then on the unclassified CorrectionFamily universe, and the ubuntu Test step never reached this crate. Fixing those two exposed it. The same file already carries the remedy and does not use it here: Package_Id_Uri builds a package id from a real PathBuf so a fixture can name a real absolute directory without hand-encoding a drive letter or separators, and both the P36 and P68 tests beside it use it with a real current directory or temp directory. Only this one test hand-types the literal in a position where the root must be absolute.
items.done_when: The test roots itself at a directory that is absolute on every platform and builds its package id through Package_Id_Uri rather than hand-typing one, the crate's tests pass on a path-independent basis rather than by virtue of the machine being at F:/repos/nomos, and the ubuntu Test step gets past nomos-lang-rust-clippy.
