items.title: Whether the specification store seals its rusqlite connection, given that 107 production call sites hold it
items.why: SpecificationStore::Connection(&self) -> &Connection is public, and measured 2026-09-12 there are 107 production calls to it outside the owning crate: nomos-spec-bundle 52, nomos-spec-ingest 34, nomos-spec-project 18, nomos-spec-validate 3 (137 including tests). Those four crates write SQL against SQLite's own handle and each names rusqlite in its manifest. OD-SPEC-001 says the test that keeps the store trait honest is store-backend equivalence, and that test is unreachable while callers hold the connection, because a query written against a rusqlite handle cannot be satisfied by any other backend. The record already declines to build Postgres and that is not in question; what is in question is whether the seam it names can exist at all in the current shape. Note the escape is a method on the store, not a mention of the library, so a grep for rusqlite double-colon undercounts it badly: that grep finds 65 sites where the real figure is 107. Re-authored from P87-THE-SPECIFICATION-STORE-HANDS-OUT-ITS-CONNECTION, which demanded a record and reserved no record identifier; OD-SPEC-015 was taken by an open peer item, so this reserves OD-SPEC-016.
items.done_when: A governing record, registered, stating whether the connection stays public, is sealed behind named operations, or is replaced by a narrower query seam -- and if it is to be sealed, what the first increment is and why 107 call sites is or is not worth paying. The measurement above is the input; the decision is which of those three the workspace takes, with the cost of each measured rather than implied. Sealing is not assumed to be the answer: a store that grows one method per query is a different problem, and the record says so if that is the conclusion.

items.title: Nothing can ask whether a dependency would be permitted before it is written, so the architecture answers only once the edge exists
items.why: Two independent brainstorming loops put the same step before implementation -- have Nomos validate the proposed dependency and policy impact -- and Nomos answers only retrospectively. Check_Dependency_Direction reads nomos.cap.dependency.edges, which nomos-lang-rust-cargo derives by running cargo metadata over manifests on disk, so an edge is judged once it has been written and never before. The primitives for a prospective answer are already public and total: Zone_Of maps a crate name to its zone, Permits answers a zone pair, SAME_ZONE_EDGES names the peer exceptions. Grepped, Permits has exactly two non-test callers -- violations.rs, judging an edge that already exists, and tests/contract/tests/boundaries/graph.rs, asserting the real graph -- and no host verb reaches it at all. nomos-lsp already names Zone_Of, but only to label which architectural component a finding falls in. The cost of learning late is recorded rather than imagined: OD-RULES-020 replaced the band table because a crate had to be renumbered more than once for a dependency nobody disputed, nomos-workflow-orchestration three times across two items in one session. The counter-argument belongs in the record rather than being hidden here: nomos check over this workspace already answers the question retrospectively in one run, so what is missing may be a convenience rather than a capability; and while the declaration is compiled into nomos-rules, which P95-ARCHITECTURE-DECLARATION-IS-COMPILED-AND-DUPLICATED puts in question, a prospective answer is only ever about this repository.
items.done_when: A new governing record under OD-GATE decides whether this workspace answers a prospective admissibility question -- may a crate in zone A name a crate in zone B, asked before any manifest carries the edge. If it does, it fixes three things: whose question it is (a fourth Gate verb beside Plan, Run and Explain, an LSP code action, or a seam with no host surface yet), what the subject of the answer is (a crate pair, a proposed manifest edit, or a planned change-set), and what the answer says when either endpoint has no declared zone, which is what Zone_Of already returns None for and the case a foreign repository is always in. items.title: The one required diagram is 243 nodes at a single resolution, and re-rendering it is the most-paid tax in this repository
items.why: diagrams/relations.mmd is one of the two committed projections and one of the two the freshness step requires. Measured: 1851 lines, 89473 bytes, 243 distinct nodes, 1612 edges, two subgraphs (Relations and Decisions), and 93 percent of those edges carry the single label relates-to, which is paired with itself, so each authored pair is drawn once in each direction. Measured on git history: 151 of the 830 commits in the last thirty days touched this file, so nearly one commit in five pays the re-render, and OD-GATE-005 requires that re-render to come from a worktree holding exactly the record set the commit publishes -- which is why this repository ships a skill for constructing one and why a stale pair is a recurring way CI goes red on a change that looks unrelated. So the most-paid tax here buys an artifact whose readability at that size nobody has measured. The README opens by claiming a canonical, multi-resolution model of software, and this projection has exactly one resolution: there is no aggregation anywhere in selection, no group-by and no rollup, so nothing can show how the OD-LEDGER decisions stand to the OD-GATE ones without drawing all 243 nodes. The one narrowing mechanism that does exist, Filter's identifier_prefix, is used by no shipped profile. OD-PROJECT-002 decided which projections are required and OD-PROJECT-003 what committing one costs; neither asked whether the required one can be read.
items.done_when: A new governing record under OD-PROJECT states the measurements above -- 243 nodes, 1612 edges, 89473 bytes, 151 of 830 commits in thirty days, 93 percent one label, identifier_prefix used by no profile, no aggregation in selection -- and decides what the required relation projection is for, reaching one of three answers. The diagram stays as it is, in which case the record names who reads it at this size and why the tax is worth paying. Or the required projection becomes a coarser one with the full graph still available unrequired through nomos spec render, in which case it names the resolution and says whether that needs aggregation in selection or is expressible with identifier_prefix alone. Or the requirement moves off the diagram, in which case it says what still catches a stale projection and answers OD-PROJECT-002's own reasoning for requiring one. It changes no profile, no selection code and not the required set itself: this item reserves the decision, not the implementation, and diagrams/relations.mmd is re-rendered only because registering the record changes the record set, never for a content reason of its own. Registered at crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/OD-PROJECT-006.record so it is governing rather than merely written, and cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-store -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: A governing record cites tests and files by name and nothing resolves them, so 14 test citations and 97 path citations point at nothing
items.why: mirror.rs resolves a declared mirror named in a code doc comment against real parsed test functions and reports a phantom when the name resolves to nothing, and D-134 decision 4 ranks that phantom Blocking while an admitted gap is only Advisory, because a false claim of coverage is worse than a hole somebody wrote down. Records carry the same kind of claim and get no such resolution. Censused over all 227 files in docs/records: 83 name at least one Test_ function in prose, 178 distinct names, of which 14 resolve to no fn Test_ anywhere in the workspace -- counted after discarding nine names this reading truncated at a line wrap and five whose own prose says outright that they do not exist. Of the 14, seven have an obvious renamed successor in the tree (a cited ..._Read_Off_The_Doc_Comment against the real ..._Read_Off_The_Documentation_Comment, which is OD-RULES-017's own abbreviation rename; a cited ..._Match_The_Manifesto against the real ..._Match_The_Manifest; a cited ..._Offer_All_Eight_Shipped_Rules against the real ..._Offer_Every_Composed_Rule), two are absences the code itself documents with a tombstone comment naming the old test, and five resolve to nothing anywhere with nothing noting it: OD-LEDGER-012, OD-LEDGER-013 twice, OD-GATE-004 and OD-ANALYSIS-006. Each of those five appears in exactly two files, its own record and spec/domain-specification.md, so the committed projection republishes the claim. File paths are the larger half: 273 distinct cited paths carry a file extension and 97 do not exist, from mixed causes rather than one. Some moved under a reorganized module (nomos-contracts src/finding/applicability.rs is now src/reporting/finding/applicability.rs). Some name a crate since renamed (nomos-agent-executor, nomos-agent-executor-ollama). Some name a file the architecture deleted (nomos-lsp src/server.rs, which OD-HOST-013 replaced when the protocol moved to the xvpe backend). Each is honest history from the record's side and a dead reference from a reader's, and AGENTS.md sends every agent to the records as the authority.
items.done_when: A new governing record under OD-SPEC states the census above and decides what a citation inside a governing record is owed, reaching one of two answers. Either a citation is a historical statement that may age, in which case the record says so plainly so no later reader treats a dead path as a defect, and says what a reader does when a cited site has moved. Or a citation is a live reference, in which case the record names which citation kinds are in scope (a test name, a path, a symbol) and which existing mechanism resolves them -- mirror.rs already resolves a test name against real parsed test functions, and tests/contract/tests/rule_contract_citation.rs already reads a record's own front matter from a test, so it picks one of those two shapes rather than inventing a third. Either answer disposes of the five fully-unresolved test citations by name, since a claim the committed projection republishes is the one case no reading of the question leaves alone. It states what it does not do: no record is edited, no citation is repaired, no rule and no test is written, and this item reserves the decision rather than the sweep that would follow it. Registered at crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/OD-SPEC-017.record so it is governing rather than merely written, and cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-store -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Five governing records assert coverage by a test name that resolves to nothing, and the committed projection republishes each one
items.why: OD-SPEC-017 censused every test name cited in prose across 229 records: 178 distinct names, 28 unresolved, of which nine are line-wrap truncations and five are prose-declared placeholders. Of the 14 real ones, six are renames with an obvious surviving successor and two are already annotated at the site they left. Five resolve to nothing and nothing anywhere notes it: Test_A_Lapsed_Item_Should_Refuse_A_New_Holder_And_Keep_The_Old_One_Visible in OD-LEDGER-012, Test_A_Held_Pattern_Should_Refuse_Every_Other_Claim_On_The_Board and Test_A_Pattern_Item_Should_Be_Unclaimable_Once_Anything_Is_Held in OD-LEDGER-013, Test_A_Phantom_Mirror_Should_Fail_The_Command in OD-GATE-004, and Test_No_Strength_Should_Refuse_A_Trace_Claim in OD-ANALYSIS-006. Each appears in exactly two files, its own record and spec/domain-specification.md, so the committed projection republishes the claim. D-134 already ranks a false claim of coverage above an admitted gap, and this is that claim one indirection further from the reader.
items.done_when: For each of the five, the citation is resolved: either the surviving test it became is named in an amendment to its own record, or the record says the test no longer exists and why, or the test is rebuilt. Which of the three is chosen is decided per citation by looking at what the cited test was asserting and whether that assertion still holds, not by one blanket edit. Both projections are re-rendered because record bodies moved. cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-store -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: OD-SPEC-017 requires a citation to be declared unresolvable at the citation and states no form for doing it
items.why: OD-SPEC-017 version 2 says the third exclusion cannot be inferred and has to be declared at the citation, and then names no way to declare it. The guard it specifies therefore has a requirement it cannot implement against anything. Measured 2026-09-13 there are 34 unresolved record-and-name pairs across 18 records once line-wrap truncations are set aside, and 12 of them are OD-SPEC-017's own, because that record quotes every example in its census tables. items.title: Nothing can show how one record family stands to another, because selection has no aggregation
items.why: OD-PROJECT-006 decided the required relation projection stays as it is -- it is a derived manifest spec freshness compares against, its 1,646 per-input hashes are the comparison, and the re-render tax it is blamed for is OD-GATE-005's worktree and build rather than the 495 milliseconds of rendering. It also named what the question really wanted and this repository does not have: a reader asking how the OD-LEDGER decisions stand to the OD-GATE ones has nothing. Measured, there is no aggregation of any kind in selection -- no group-by, no rollup -- and Filter::identifier_prefix, the one narrowing mechanism that exists, is used by no shipped profile and cannot express it: it narrows to one family, which draws that family's internal edges and every edge leaving it as a dangling end, rather than rolling families into nodes and edges between them.
items.done_when: Selection can roll a set of nodes into one by a declared grouping and emit the edges between groups rather than between members, and a profile renders that as a second relation view. The view is not added to the required set, for the reason OD-PROJECT-006 gives: a projection is required because it is a re-render obligation, and a reading aid nobody compares against the store has no obligation to discharge. A test proves a group's internal edges do not appear between groups and that an edge leaving the grouped set is not drawn as a dangling end. A test proves two renders of one store are identical, since a grouping with nondeterministic iteration would pass every other assertion. tests/contract/surface/nomos-spec-project.txt is re-blessed if the surface moves. cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-project -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

Declined.reason: Territory reserved five paths for a change reaching ten, measured before re-authoring rather than after. A new Content kind cannot ship without a profile selecting it -- catalogue.rs's Test_Every_Content_Kind_Should_Be_Reached_By_A_Shipped_Profile makes that a compile-and-test requirement, not a choice -- so the change reaches a new file under profiles/, its include_str registration in src/catalogue.rs, and tests/projections/selection.rs for the tests the done_when names. It also reaches tests/projections/rebuildability.rs twice, the way the one-hop traversal did: SEEDED_BY_RECORDS names the content kinds a records-only store answers for, and the shipped-profile sets name every profile by id. Re-authored as -2 reserving all of it.

items.title: Whether a language identity belongs to a capability contract, given that it blocks the discovered-source type from being owned below the rules package
items.why: P41-SOURCE-ARTIFACT-OWNERSHIP wanted the canonical discovered-source type owned by workspace, model or analysis rather than by the rules package, on the ground that a discovered artifact exists before any rule does and a consumer that never judges anything should not link the judging layer to name its input. Measured, that is true of exactly two crates today -- nomos-lang-rust-cargo and nomos-workspace-discovery use SourceFile and nothing else from nomos-rules, and nomos-workspace-discovery is the discovery layer itself, which is the inversion stated. Measured further, the move is refused: SourceFile carries language: Option<Language> from nomos-cap-syntax, and nomos gate admits refuses nomos-model, nomos-workspace and nomos-analysis that edge, because all three are Substrate and Substrate may not name a Capability Contract. nomos-rules is Rules and may, which is why the type sits where it sits. Language itself is a newtype over String with no syntax-specific structure, named by two crates, and structurally identical to ProviderId, SubjectId and CapabilityId, which all live in nomos-contracts at Protocol.
items.done_when: A new governing record under OD-RULES decides whether a language identity belongs to a capability contract crate or to the protocol crate, against the measurements above rather than by analogy. If it moves, the record names the zone consequence -- that Substrate may then name it and the discovered-source type stops being pinned to the rules package by one field -- and says whether the discovered-source move follows automatically or is its own decision. If it stays, the record says what that means for the ownership inversion P41-SOURCE-ARTIFACT-OWNERSHIP named, and whether the alternative OD-RULES-014 already refused -- a rule deriving its own language from the path, which that record measured as eleven copies of a three-line test across nine modules -- is genuinely the only other route. It states what it does not do: no type moves, no crate changes, no manifest is edited. Registered at crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/OD-RULES-030.record so it is governing rather than merely written, and cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-store -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

Declined.reason: Superseded by P95-THE-DISCOVERED-SOURCE-TYPE-STAYS-WHERE-TWO-RECORDS-PUT-IT, which asks the question that is actually open: not where the language identity belongs, which OD-RULES-014 decided and amended, but what follows for the ownership inversion P41-SOURCE-ARTIFACT-OWNERSHIP named, given that two accepted decisions together pin the discovered-source type to the rules package.

abandoned.reason: The question is already decided and I asked it again. OD-RULES-014's own amendment, headed The Carried Type Belongs At Band 23 Not Band 0, moved the language identity to nomos-cap-syntax deliberately: constraint 2 of that record had placed it in nomos-contracts, implementing it surfaced that this was wrong, and the amendment gives the reason -- a language identity fails OD-CONTRACTS-001's deciding question, whether a peer that never compiles the crate could not agree with us without the type. Nothing exchanges a language name with a peer; the five parties that must agree are all inside this workspace, which is the same shape as SyntaxPayload sitting at band 23 rather than band 0. So it is not misfiled, and a record asking where it belongs would re-decide what a record decided and amended.

items.title: Why the discovered-source type stays in the rules package, so the question stops being raised
items.why: P41-SOURCE-ARTIFACT-OWNERSHIP has been raised, stranded on a stale dependency edge, and declined once. Its complaint is real: SourceFile is declared in nomos-rules and is what every walker returns and every orchestration passes, so the discovery layer depends on the judging layer to describe its own input. Measured today, that is true of exactly two crates -- nomos-lang-rust-cargo and nomos-workspace-discovery name nothing else from nomos-rules, and the second is the discovery layer itself. But the move is refused by two accepted decisions acting together, and nothing records that, which is why the item keeps coming back. SourceFile carries language: Option<Language>, because OD-RULES-014 decided a rule's language restriction is carried rather than derived, having measured eleven copies of the same three-line extension test across nine modules. Language lives in nomos-cap-syntax because that record's own amendment moved it there, deliberately, on OD-CONTRACTS-001's peer-visibility test. And nomos gate admits refuses nomos-model, nomos-workspace and nomos-analysis the edge to nomos-cap-syntax: all three are Substrate, Substrate may not name a Capability Contract, and nomos-rules is Rules and may.
items.done_when: A new governing record under OD-RULES states the measurement chain above and decides whether the discovered-source type stays in the rules package. If it stays, the record says plainly that the ownership inversion is a consequence of two accepted decisions rather than an oversight, names what would have to change first for the move to become available, and says what a reader should conclude when they notice the inversion again -- so the next person to raise it finds the answer instead of re-deriving it. If it does not stay, it names which of the two decisions it reopens and argues against that record rather than around it. It states what it does not do: no type moves, no crate changes, no manifest and no zone table is edited. Registered at crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/OD-RULES-030.record so it is governing rather than merely written, and cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-store -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Two provider crates state a two-direction guarantee check as the convention, and nothing says the other nine owe it
items.why: nomos-lang-rust/src/guarantee.rs and nomos-lang-go/src/guarantee.rs open with the same sentence -- what this provider promises, stated as a value and checked in two directions -- and name both. Downward, nomos_capability::Registry refuses an offer claiming more than the capability ceiling permits, so a provider does not grade its own work. Upward, a test asserts one property per axis against what the provider actually emits, so the declaration is not merely permitted but true. The Rust one states the principle outright: a declaration nobody exercises is a comment rather than a fact. That convention lives in those two module docs and nowhere else -- no record carries it, grepped -- and the workspace does not follow it uniformly. Eleven crates declare a provider guarantee. nomos-lang-rust is the only one with a test file named for it, tests/guarantee.rs. nomos-lang-rust-compiler, nomos-repo-policy and nomos-connector-coderabbit have no tests directory at all; the first two assert their guarantee only as Ceiling().Satisfies of the declared guarantee and registry.Offer of the provider offer returning Ok, both of which are the downward direction, and the third asserts neither. What makes this worth measuring rather than shrugging at is what Sound buys: Assurance::Sound's own doc comment says the property is claimed and the claim is backed, and Satisfies_Requirement returns true for Sound alone, so Sound is the single value that clears a rule's requirement floor and nothing distinguishes a Sound an upward test exercises from a Sound that merely fits under its ceiling. The census is itself the work. A source scan counts 177 production Assurance::Sound occurrences, but that number mixes a contract's ceiling with a provider's claim, and telling a real upward property assertion from a plumbing test that only checks that an emitted fact carries the declared value needs each test read rather than grepped, which is why this item measures before proposing anything.
items.done_when: A new governing record under OD-CAPABILITY carries the census and the disposition. The census names, per guarantee-declaring crate, which direction is actually asserted, separating three things read from each test rather than grepped: a downward check (the ceiling admits the claim, the registry accepts the offer), a plumbing check (an emitted fact carries the declared value), and a real upward property assertion (the claimed property holds of what the provider emits). It also splits the raw Assurance::Sound count into contract ceilings and provider claims, since the single number answers neither question. The disposition decides whether the two-direction convention those two module docs state is a requirement every provider owes or a practice those two crates chose. If a requirement, the record names what enforces it and says whether the precedent is mirror.rs's own convention of naming the exercising test at the declaring site, a mechanism that already resolves a named test against real parsed test functions. If a practice, it says why Sound clearing Satisfies_Requirement without an upward test is acceptable, and amends both module docs so neither states a convention the workspace does not hold. It states what it does not do: no test is written, no guarantee is weakened, no provider and no contract changes. Registered at crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/OD-CAPABILITY-016.record so it is governing rather than merely written, and cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-store -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: An implementation block discards its own generic parameter list before the payload is written
items.why: OD-CAPABILITY-014 is accepted and unbuilt. It decided that an Implementation item own declared generic type-parameter names join OD-CAPABILITY-011 closed set of typed shape extensions, and nothing has built it: nomos-lang-rust visit_item_impl still reads exactly two things off the syn::ItemImpl it holds, Type_Head(&node.self_ty) and node.trait_.is_some(), and node.generics sits unread at that same call site. Impl_Shape is still a two-constant function returning the bare trait or inherent label. Until the fact reaches the payload, no consumer can ask whether an Implementation item own name is one of its own generics, which is the question P68 was declined for being unable to answer.
items.done_when: nomos-cap-syntax encodes an implementation block own declared generic type-parameter names alongside its trait-or-inherent label, and publishes a typed reader for each half, the way it already publishes Struct_Shape and Struct_Fields for a struct field list. An impl declaring no generics still encodes as the bare label, so its bytes do not move. nomos-lang-rust visit_item_impl reads node.generics rather than discarding it. Every site that recovered an impl trait-or-inherent label by comparing the raw shape string against TRAIT or INHERENT reads it through the typed reader instead, so a generic trait impl is still recognized as one; there are four such sites and a test proves each still answers the same for a generic impl. The payload own schema table names the new form. The surface snapshot follows. The determinism goldens are re-baselined if and only if the shared fixture own bytes actually moved, measured rather than assumed.

items.title: A benchmark with no correctness oracle is a real defect class with 266 subjects in the sibling workspace and none in this one
items.why: XVPE's own testing standard states a Benchmark Correctness Rule: every benchmark must exercise behavior covered by a correctness test or an equivalent pre-benchmark oracle, and results from an implementation that does not pass its oracle are invalid and must not participate in performance comparison or default selection. Nomos is the layer that would judge that and has no rule of the kind -- across every rule module under crates/rules/nomos-rules/src/checks the only occurrence of the word bench anywhere is a fixture string inside rust_text.rs. The mechanism is already built one scale over: mirror.rs reads a declared mirror off a doc comment, resolves the name against real parsed test functions, and reports a phantom when it resolves to nothing, which is the shape a bench-to-oracle correspondence needs. Population, measured rather than assumed, and this is the part that decides the item's shape. This workspace has zero bench targets, so the rule would be vacuous against nomos's own self-check and a green self-check would be no evidence at all -- the vacuity trap the corpus gates already warn about. The sibling xvpe checkout has 266 real bench targets (a crate benches directory holding .rs files with a manifest beside it) across 84 crates, of which 112 have no same-stem file under tests or src in the same crate. That 112 is a proxy and an upper bound rather than a finding count: a bench may be covered by a differently-named test, and a same-stem file does not prove the bench's own workload is asserted anywhere. And xvpe is a corpus CI does not have, so the only population able to exercise this rule is one no gate run will ever see.
items.done_when: A new governing record under OD-RULES decides whether a bench-to-correctness-oracle rule is built, against the population split above rather than against the standard's wording. If it is built, the record fixes four things: what declares which benches owe an oracle (a declared policy family in the OD-RULES-011 shape, or the mirror convention of naming the oracle at the bench site that mirror.rs already resolves, and not a compiled-in assumption about directory names); what the rule's subject is, given that a bench target is a file while its oracle may be a test function in another file; what it reports when it can see a bench and not its oracle, since absence must become neither a pass nor a failure per OD-RULES-001; and how it is verified at all, given a zero population here and a corpus-only population there that no predicate on this board can reach. If it is not built, the record declines against the 112 measured candidates rather than against the absence of a local population, since OD-ROADMAP-001 retired the population-of-zero caution and a decline on that ground alone would contradict it. It states what it does not do: no rule is written, no registration site changes, nothing is composed into a run. Registered at crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/OD-RULES-031.record so it is governing rather than merely written, and cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-store -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: The xvpe checkout declares 261 machine-readable rules, 224 of them enforced by nobody, and names nomos in none of them
items.why: The xvpe checkout beside this workspace -- the one OD-PLATFORM-003 made this build depend on, so it is always on disk -- ships a committed machine-readable standards corpus under docs/arch/standards: 375 markdown files behind a rule.schema.json requiring every rule document to declare id, severity, enforced_by and gate in YAML front matter, with prose in the body and, in the schema's own words, nothing guessed. Censused directly rather than assumed: 261 rule documents, 109 indexes, 5 references. Severity is 161 MUST, 5 MUST NOT, 83 SHOULD, 1 SHOULD NOT, 11 MAY. Gate is 224 review, 31 blocking, 6 unreachable -- so 86 percent of that corpus declares outright that no tool enforces it. The named enforcers are xvpe's own scripts: check-impact-map on 11 rules, then check-arch-doc-structure, check-strategy-docs, check-platform-boundaries, layering-direction, strategy-determinism-gate and a handful more. Nomos appears in enforced_by zero times. Set against what this repository already decided, that is the finding. ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 makes nomos the ecosystem's deterministic conformance layer. ARC-CONFORMANCE-001 argues that a check surface which cannot say what it is for keeps being filled with what is easiest to justify rather than with what only it can supply, and defines a conformance claim as the question a compiler, a linter and a language server cannot answer. A declared MUST rule whose own front matter says no tool enforces it is that question, 224 times over. And nomos-rules already reads this very doctrine once: Check_Declared_Role_Matches_Surface quotes xvpe's engineering doctrine on why some MUST rules are review-enforced, and produces Applicability::AgentRequired for exactly that category. So the category nomos built a state for is declared, enumerable and 224 rules long in a tree this workspace already requires, nomos's own rule set was ported from code-standards instead, and nothing connects the two.
items.done_when: A new governing record in the ARC-CONFORMANCE family decides what relationship nomos's rule set has to xvpe's declared standards corpus, against the census above rather than against the idea of an ecosystem. It reaches one of three answers. The corpus is an external declaration nomos reads as a capability fact, in which case the record names the contract, says what a rule does with a severity, a gate and an enforced_by value, and says what becomes of the 224 review-gated rules given Applicability::AgentRequired already exists for precisely that category. Or the corpus is xvpe's own to enforce and nomos's absence from enforced_by is correct, in which case the record says why the ecosystem's conformance layer is not the enforcer of its sibling's MUST rules, and what ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001's seam means if not that. Or the question waits, in which case the record names the trigger as a condition a later session can mechanically check rather than a judgement it would have to re-make. Either way it records the numbers it decided against -- 261 rules, the five-way severity split, 224 review-gated, 31 blocking, zero naming nomos -- so a later reader can re-measure rather than re-argue. It states what it does not do: no contract crate, no provider, no rule, no change to nomos-rules, and no edit anywhere in the xvpe tree, which this workspace does not own. Registered at crates/spec/nomos-spec-store/records/ARC-CONFORMANCE-002.record so it is governing rather than merely written, and cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-store -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.why: nomos gate run --root . exits 1 at HEAD, and the finding that blocks it is abbreviations against tests/integration/fixtures/third-party/hex-0.4.3/lib.rs -- a committed, unmodified excerpt of hex 0.4.3, vendored by P45 precisely so the composed rule set can be measured against code this repository did not write. 14 of the runs 232 findings are against that one file, and 13 of them are function-naming-convention findings whose stated reason is README.md Conventions section requires function names to be Pascal_Snake_Case: this repositorys own README, cited at a crate whose author never saw it. The fixture declares its own standards.json and calibration.rs measured that declaration working -- judged as its own root the same 13 names resolve clean, judged as part of this repository they do not, because the enclosing walk reads the repositorys standards.json and ignores the one beside the source. nomos_workspace_discovery::Read_Entry already refuses to descend into a nested git worktree for the same reason P67 gave, that it is not source anyone at this address authored, and OD-HOST-008 records that skip as part of what this walk is. A vendored tree that declares its own conventions is the same class and has no such skip.
items.done_when: A directory below the run root that carries its own standards.json is not descended into, and the reason is stated where P67 stated its own, beside the skip it sits next to. The marker is nomos_repo_policy::STANDARDS_JSON rather than a third copy of the literal -- gate admits reports the edge permitted, measured before the manifest carries it. A roots own standards.json still configures that root and does not make the walk skip itself, proved by a test over a scratch tree holding a root marker, a source beside it, a nested marker and a source beside that. README.md names the fourth skip in the row that already names the other three. nomos gate run --root . then exits 0 over this workspace and reports 218 findings, none of which can fail a build, and tests/integration/tests/calibration.rs still judges the fixture unchanged, because it names the fixture directory as its own root rather than reaching it through this walk.

Declined.reason: The done_when required the marker to be nomos_repo_policy::STANDARDS_JSON. It cannot be: standards_document is a private module of nomos-repo-policy (crates/repository/nomos-repo-policy/src/lib.rs line 28, mod standards_document with no pub), so the constant is unreachable from outside that crate even though gate admits reports the edge itself permitted. Reaching it means exporting it, which widens that crates public surface and its committed snapshot -- neither in this items territory, and OD-RULES-019/OD-PACKAGE-015 made that module private deliberately, so un-privating it is a decision rather than this correction. The dependency is not wanted either once the constant is out of reach. Re-authored with a local constant whose doc states why, the same shape nomos-rules checks/goals.rs DECLARATION_FILE already has, and with territory narrowed to the walk and README.md; Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock leave scope entirely.

items.title: Table_Rows scans a fenced code block for table rows, so ASCII art is read as a table
items.why: nomos_spec_model::Table_Rows walks a blocks text for pipe-shaped lines and never consults block.kind, even though Segment already classifies a fenced block as BlockKind::Code correctly. A diagram inside a triple-backtick fence in the v14 corpus game plan -- a box drawn with plus and minus borders and five lines reading pipe Request N pipe -- is therefore read as a five-row markdown table with no delimiter row, and Table_Defects refuses it: table 1 has 5 row(s) and no delimiter, so no row is a header. Six corpus-gated tests fail on exactly that message. Markdown has no tables inside a fence; every parser treats fenced content as literal. The defect reaches five call sites through this one function -- archaeology/sections.rs, restore/extract.rs, revisions.rs and both of nomos-spec-store write/blocks.rs -- so it is fixed once, here, rather than at each. Invisible until now because it only bites a corpus CI never has, which is OD-GATE-001 shape.
items.done_when: Table_Rows returns no rows for a block whose kind is Code, and the doc says why in terms of what a fence means rather than as a special case. A unit test builds a Code block whose text is pipe-shaped ASCII art and asserts no row comes back, and a second asserts a Prose block with the identical text still yields its rows, so the discriminator is the kind and not the text. The existing fixtures are unaffected and stay unaffected, measured: every SourceBlock in the affected suites is already BlockKind::Prose. cargo test -p nomos-spec-model -p nomos-spec-store -p nomos-spec-ingest passes. Note honestly that this predicate is green with no corpus set because the corpus-backed assertions return early; the corpus-backed half of this fix belongs to its successor item, which re-measures the counts this change moves.

items.title: The live v14 corpus has diverged from the archive whose figures the tests pin, and its own machine index is stale
items.why: Eight corpus-gated tests fail, and re-pinning the numbers is the wrong answer -- measured, not assumed. The archive nomos-spec-internal-artifacts-v14.36.zip is dated 2026-08-07 and still reproduces every pinned figure: tests/revisions.rs reads it and passes, 282 pipe lines, 258 non-separator rows, 234 content rows. The live directory NOMOS_V14_CORPUS points at answers 286 and 2535 instead, because five of its ten domain volumes were edited on 2026-08-17. So the live tree has moved past the archive it was cut from and no newer archive exists. Worse, the corpus is now inconsistent with itself: 02_machine/catalog/catalog.json is dated 2026-08-06, eleven days behind the markdown, and Test_I1_Should_Reproduce_Every_Recorded_Block reports 494 block-hash mismatches with 02-core-architecture-identity-and-configuration.md recording 202 blocks where segmentation produces 204. Two further tests report 18 and 103 preservation violations, blocks with neither a lineage disposition nor an omission -- content added without the lineage records the corpus own rules require. None of this is a regression here: running the identical tests at 515fc26a, the last commit known green from 2026-08-09, against todays corpus reproduces all of it. Bumping 282 to 286 would turn three of the eight green and pin figures measured against a corpus whose own index disagrees with its content, which is the number that matches whatever it currently does that this repository refuses elsewhere.
items.done_when: The divergence is resolved at its source before any figure in this repository moves, and which source is the decision: a v14.37 archive cut from the current live tree with 02_machine regenerated and V14_LAST re-pointed, or the live tree reconciled back to v14.36, or the lineage records the 18 and 103 preservation violations name being authored. Only then are the pinned figures re-measured, and each new number is recorded with what it was measured against and on what date, so the next reader can tell a deliberate re-measurement from a drift nobody noticed. If the resolution is entirely corpus-side and no figure in this repository changes, this item declines with that as its reason rather than being closed by editing a constant.

Declined.reason: Cannot be completed as authored, measured 2026-09-14 while holding it. Territory reserves two files, real_corpus.rs and table_rows/corpus.rs, and the eight failures live in five: family_counts/measurement.rs carries two, restoration.rs one, siblings.rs one, none reserved. The owner chose the third resolution the done_when lists, refreshing source-block-lineage.yaml, and that route needs a mechanism this workspace does not have. The lineage's authored fields are disposition, authority, target_volumes and stable_ids; its mechanical fields are block_ordinal, heading_path, block_kind, content_hash and normalized_hash. Only a segmenter agreeing with nomos can produce hashes Test_I1 accepts, and the corpus's own validate_bundle.py is not one: read at 05_tools/validate_bundle.py, editorial_source_errors checks only that an entry HAS a disposition, HAS both hashes and HAS a target volume, never recomputing or comparing them, which is why it reports ok while nomos reports 494 mismatches. No nomos verb emits block lineage: spec offers record, table, render, freshness, markdown, preview, commit, profiles, sources, and the only readers of source-block-lineage.yaml are three test files. Confirmed against the item's own why: the archive still reproduces every pinned figure (revisions.rs, 12 passed), no archive newer than v14.36 exists, and the cause is one act, cace351ac on 2026-08-17, whose volume 02 diff splits one service heading into two and one table row into three, taking that document from 202 recorded blocks to 204 and shifting every ordinal after it. The why's claim that catalog.json is eleven days behind the markdown is true by mtime and false by content: rebuild_bundle.py does not write catalog.json. Re-authored with measured territory rather than closed by editing a constant, which this item's own done_when forbids.

items.title: No nomos rule has been measured against a second repository's declared MUST list, and one sits on disk beside this one
items.why: This repository's bar for building anything is a real second party: OD-CAPABILITY-002 licenses a bundled contract only while there is one provider on each side, OD-PACKAGE-011 stands open because there is still no second case, and OD-RULES-010's whole reasoning is that a rule was a real second party from the day it was written. Eighty-five rule identifiers ship in nomos-rules, extracted from the RuleId constants under src/checks. None has ever been measured against another repository's own declared list of what must hold, and such a list is on disk: the xvpe checkout this build already requires declares 261 machine-readable rules under docs/arch/standards. Two overlaps are verified by reading, not matched on a name. First, xvpe's every-source-file-is-reachable (MUST, gate blocking, enforced_by check-orphan-modules) states that every .rs file under a crate's src must be reachable from its roots by following mod declarations, and argues it as a MUST because rustc never parses an orphan so its tests silently do not run -- which is nomos's own no-orphan-modules rule, shipped. Second, and sharper, xvpe's memory-ordering-in-security-code (MUST, gate review, enforced_by review) states that security-relevant atomics use the ordering their semantics require and default to sequentially consistent unless analysis shows a relaxation is safe -- a rule its own front matter says no tool enforces, while nomos ships three for it: atomic-ordering-choices-are-justified, relaxed-not-used-when-ordering-matters and seqcst-justified-explicitly. A third pairing is the same question over a different declaration: xvpe's engine-folder-tiers-and-dependency-direction and composer-dependency-direction, both MUST and blocking, are what nomos's dependency-direction answers. The census cannot be grepped, and that was measured rather than assumed: a token-overlap matcher over identifiers and titles proposed 23 candidate pairs of which most are false (trace-verification matched against certificate-verification-is-not-disabled, strategy-type-parameter-is-named-strategy against parameter-count) and it missed every-source-file-is-reachable entirely, the strongest real pair of the three.
items.done_when: A new governing record under OD-RULES carries the per-rule census, read from each xvpe rule's body rather than matched on its identifier. For each of the 261 it records exactly one of three dispositions: a nomos rule already answers it, naming the nomos rule identifier; nothing in nomos answers it and the question is inside nomos's domain; or the question is outside it, naming why (a UI spacing rule, a benchmark methodology rule, a documentation-topology rule about xvpe's own tree). items.title: Three guarantee declarations name what exercises them, and one stops claiming a check it does not have
items.why: OD-CAPABILITY-016 decided the two-direction guarantee check is a requirement, and that a Declared_Guarantee names in its own doc what exercises it or states that it cannot be exercised and why. It named the two module docs as the enforcing increments first job, one of them on accuracy grounds: nomos-lang-go/src/guarantee.rs asserts Upward, this crates own tests assert what it actually emits against the claim, and they do not. Re-checked before filing rather than trusted from the record: Test_Claiming_Resolution_Should_Be_Refused offers a fabricated offer to a registry and asserts refusal, which is the downward half; Test_Broken_Source_Should_Be_Unparseable_Rather_Than_Empty asserts a file that fails to parse yields Unparseable rather than an empty Parsed, which is OD-RULES-001 refusal honesty and the same class the record already carved out for nomos-lang-rust-deny, not an axis of this providers guarantee. Neither is an upward check. Separately nomos-lang-rust-scan holds the convention without stating it: its Declared_Guarantee doc says crate::Scan own tests enumerate the cases where it reports a declaration that is not there, and names none, so nothing resolves it. nomos-lang-rust already names tests/guarantee.rs truthfully and only needs to cite the record that now governs what it is doing.
items.done_when: No module doc or Declared_Guarantee doc in these three crates asserts an upward check that does not exist. nomos-lang-go says plainly that the downward half holds and the upward half is owed, names what the crate does have and what class that belongs to, and says which axes have no exerciser, so the gap is declared rather than silent. nomos-lang-rust-scan names Test_The_Declared_Unsoundness_Should_Be_Demonstrable by its function name so a resolver can find it, and says which of its four declared axes that test reaches and which it does not. nomos-lang-rust cites OD-CAPABILITY-016 beside the naming it already carries. No guarantee value changes, no test is written, no provider behaviour moves, and cargo test -p nomos-lang-rust -p nomos-lang-go -p nomos-lang-rust-scan passes. The mechanical resolver that would make a named exerciser fail when it resolves to nothing is OD-CAPABILITY-016 own follow-up and is not this item.

items.title: Nothing resolves a guarantee declaration to the test that exercises it
items.why: OD-CAPABILITY-016 made the two-direction guarantee check a requirement -- a Declared_Guarantee names what exercises it, or states that it cannot be exercised and why -- and decided the naming is enforced the way a declared mirror already is, by resolving a name declared at a site against real parsed test functions. It also left this increment three things to decide: the rules identifier, its gate category, and whether a missing exerciser is blocking or advisory. Nothing is built. The convention has now been found stated and unheld twice, in the two module docs that carried it, which is why that record chose a mechanism over prose; 6e2e2541 corrected the three declaration sites it named and left fifteen still naming nothing. Prose naming is not resolvable: what 6e2e2541 wrote is readable and true and a resolver cannot find it, because there is no marker. The resolver this needs already exists one scale over -- universe_kind.rs Claimed_Mirror reads the marker Mirrored by followed by a backticked name, refuses a marker followed by prose so it cannot invent a name out of the next word, and facts.rs Check_Names_In already indexes every function whose name starts with Test_ across the whole source set, which is exactly the index a cross-file resolution needs.
items.done_when: A rule in nomos-rules judges every Declared_Guarantee function the syntax payload carries, and reports one of three answers: it names an exerciser that resolves to a real test function in the source set, so nothing is reported; it names one that resolves to nothing, which is a finding; or it names nothing at all, which is also a finding. A declaration stating it cannot be exercised satisfies the rule, since OD-CAPABILITY-016 made that half of the requirement and not an escape from it. The marker vocabulary is decided here and stated in the rules own doc, reusing Claimed_Mirrors shape rather than inventing a second grammar, and a marker followed by prose rather than a name is refused the same way. The rule states its own Requirement floor rather than letting the composition root decide it. It is registered in DESCRIPTORS, which is now the single site both Composed_Rules and the gates own offering list derive from -- confirmed by reading both rather than from the skill, whose two-list instruction is stale -- and cites OD-CAPABILITY-016 at the version its front matter declares. The gate category is decided here and the doc says the reasoning, including what would change it. The finding count over this workspace is measured before composing and stated in the commit, so a rule that is clean for a bad reason is not mistaken for one that is clean. cargo test -p nomos-rules -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-gate-orchestration -p nomos-contract-tests passes, and nomos gate run --root . still exits 0.

items.title: The check verb's printed help names one rule of seventy while claiming it runs every one, and six of eight groups' help text has no mirror at all
items.why:
Measured on a quiescent tree at 3c728d31, with a binary built at HEAD. crates/host/nomos-cli/src/check/parsing.rs line 5 holds USAGE, the text nomos check prints. It says Runs every rule over the tree and reports what they find, and then opens a rules: section naming exactly one rule, completeness-mirror, with a three-line gloss. DESCRIPTORS in crates/rules/nomos-rules/src/rule_descriptor.rs line 245 holds exactly 70 entries, nomos gate plan --root . prints rules: 70, and a full-root nomos check --root . run today emitted 217 findings from 8 distinct rules: lint-diagnostics 190, dependency-policy 12, completeness-mirror 6, function-naming-convention 5, and one each from unread-reaches-finding, single-letter-names, data-names-stay-lower-snake and abbreviations. So a sentence promising every rule sits directly above a list wrong by 69, and any real run falsifies the list without anyone having to count DESCRIPTORS.

The mechanism that would have caught it is in the same file, written twice. check/tests.rs Test_All_Should_Match_The_Documented_Exit_Codes splits USAGE on exit codes:, parses the integers out of the prose, sorts both sides and asserts set equality against ExitCode::All(), and refuses to pass on an empty parse -- no exit code was parsed out of the usage text, so this compared nothing. gate/tests.rs Test_The_Documented_Exit_Codes_Should_Be_The_Ones_This_Group_Can_Exit_With is the same fifteen lines over Every_Exit_Code(). Its own doc comment states the general rule: USAGE is prose a person reads and ExitCode is what the process returns, the two were written separately, and a code added or renumbered in one of them and not the other is the failure that actually happens. That is exactly true of a rule added to DESCRIPTORS and not to the rules: section, and nothing checks that axis.

Eight groups print an exit-code list and each has its own ExitCode enum -- agent, check, correct, gate, request, spec, work, and workflow, whose enum and prose share workflow.rs. Two mirror it. The other six are correct today, verified variant by variant against each prose line (agent 0/2/5/6, correct 0/1/2/5/6, request 0/2/5/7/9, spec 0/1/2/5/6/7/8/9, work 0/1/2/3/4/5), so they are unguarded rather than wrong, which is worth saying rather than inflating. The same help text restates further compiled closed vocabularies with no mirror anywhere: work list's nine states, work add's five kinds and two origins, agent's six effort levels (its own text calls them MODEL-ROUTE-004's closed vocabulary), request's three kinds and two states.

The code side is already guarded, which is what isolates this. DESCRIPTORS is a declared universe in tests/contract/tests/completeness_universes/table.rs, Standing::Mirrored by Test_Every_Composed_Rule_Should_Have_A_Descriptor. Declared_Universes derives universes from pub const NAME: &[...] and Type::All(); USAGE is pub(super) const USAGE: &str, so an enumeration written as prose inside a string constant is structurally outside every completeness mechanism this repository has.

OD-AGENT-004 governs this and its own third revisit trigger is this instance: a checked artifact going stale anyway, which would mean the checks are narrower than the facts they appear to cover. USAGE is a checked artifact whose check covers one of the two lists it carries. That record's general objection -- that a restated-fact detector would need to know which facts have mechanical authorities elsewhere, which is not derivable from text -- does not bind here: these restatements name closed compiled vocabularies whose authority is a const in the same workspace, and the two existing tests are the proof the comparison is derivable. P96-THE-GATE-WORKFLOW-TELLS-A-READER-IT-RUNS-ON-NIGHTLY closed the same defect class in gate.yml this week.
items.done_when:
The check verb stops printing a rule list it cannot keep true, and OD-AGENT-004 says what a printed help text may declare.

OD-AGENT-004 is amended in place rather than answered by a second record, since it is the standing decision on restated prose. It records that its third trigger fired, names this instance -- one string constant carrying two declared lists, one mirrored and one wrong by 69 of 70 -- and extends its route-what-is-checked-elsewhere rule to the text a command prints, which its measured population (module docs, README.md, Cargo.toml) did not include. It states that rule as a condition a later author can apply rather than a judgement they must remake: a help text may enumerate a compiled vocabulary only where a test compares that enumeration against its authority, and otherwise routes to the verb that prints it.

check's USAGE stops naming one rule of seventy. Which shape replaces it is the implementer's call and both are admissible: routing to nomos gate plan, which already prints the real 70 out of DESCRIPTORS, or an enumeration generated from DESCRIPTORS and mirrored by a test. Hand-pasting 70 names is refused, because it recreates the same unguarded list one drift later. The sentence claiming it runs every rule stays true of what the verb does and stops standing above a list contradicting it.

The exit-code mirror is extended to the six groups lacking it -- agent, correct, request, spec, work and workflow -- as the same comparison those two tests already make, each against its own group's enum, each carrying the empty-parse guard so a group whose prose section is renamed fails rather than silently comparing nothing. All six pass unchanged against today's text, which is the point: they are correct now, and this is what keeps them correct.

Each new test is confirmed able to fail, by injecting a wrong code into that group's prose and observing red, not by reasoning that it would. A test that cannot fail is the defect this item is about.

Not closed by correcting check's list alone and leaving the eight-group population unguarded: one corrected list is the instance and the missing mirror is the shape. Not closed by widening Declared_Universes to parse string constants -- a prose list inside a string is not a declared universe in OD-COMPLETENESS-001's sense, and making it one would put every sentence of the CLI's help under a completeness guard.

diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md are both re-rendered from a tree holding exactly HEAD plus this item's amended record, per OD-GATE-005, and committed alongside.

items.why: b8cc19d6 composed guarantee-declares-its-exerciser and it reports 20 findings, 19 of them real declarations plus one unreadable corpus file. The fourth, nomos-lang-rust reachability, has only downward tests -- the offer is accepted, an offer claiming more is refused, the ceiling is satisfied -- and owes a stated absence rather than a name.
items.done_when: Each of the four declarations carries the marker the rule reads. Three name a test that resolves: the name is checked to exist rather than assumed, and each is a real assertion about what the provider emits rather than about the declared value. The fourth states it has no exerciser and why, which is the requirements other half and not an escape from it -- the reason names what a test would have to assert rather than merely recording that none exists. nomos gate run --root . reports exactly four fewer guarantee-declares-its-exerciser findings than the 20 b8cc19d6 measured, and the number is stated in the commit rather than left to be inferred. No test is written, no guarantee value changes, and cargo test -p nomos-lang-rust -p nomos-lang-rust-scan -p nomos-rules passes.

items.title: Five vocabularies a help text prints have nothing comparing them to their authority, and work's state list is already short the spelling it accepts
items.why:
Measured on a quiescent tree at e16060cf, with a binary built there. OD-AGENT-004 version 2 states the condition: a help text may enumerate a compiled vocabulary only where a test compares that enumeration against the vocabulary's own authority, in both directions, refusing to pass on an empty parse; otherwise it routes to the verb that prints the vocabulary. That amendment closed the exit-code axis -- all eight groups on this binary now compare their printed exit codes against their own ExitCode enum -- and named five printed vocabularies that meet the condition in no way at all. This item is those five. They are named in the record so that they read as not-yet-met rather than as satisfied, and this is the item the record says each of them is.

The population, measured across every nomos-cli test that reads a usage text (the complete set is: the eight exit-code mirrors, spec's Test_Usage_Text_Should_Name_Every_Command, and work's negative assertion that the text does not advertise --territory-pattern):

1. work list's states. VERBS in crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/parse.rs line 378 prints --state ready|waiting|held|snagged|stranded|claimed|blocked|done|declined. Nine. The authority is not one enum: nomos_ledger::item::State declares five variants (Ready, Claimed, Blocked, Done, Declined) and the other four are derived, produced by the refusal-to-label match in crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/report.rs around line 236. That match produces a tenth label the printed list omits: lapsed. It is not decorative. Listed_As in work/listing.rs filters by comparing the requested string case-insensitively against Listing_Label's output, so every label the match can produce is an accepted --state value, and nomos work list --state lapsed exits 0 today printing "no items are lapsed". So this list is not merely unguarded, it is already short by one, exactly the way check's rules section was -- found by measuring rather than by reasoning that it might be.

2. work add's five kinds and two origins, against nomos_ledger::item::Kind (5 variants) and nomos_ledger::item::Origin (2). Both closed sets OD-LEDGER-024 decided, both restated in prose, nothing comparing them.

3. agent's six --effort spellings, against nomos_model_package::EffortLevel. All six are exercised against the parser by EFFORT_SPELLINGS in agent/tests.rs and Test_An_Execute_Command_Parses_Every_Effort_Spelling, so the parser side is closed. Nothing compares that census to the list the help text prints, which is a different claim and the one the condition asks for.

4. request's three submission kinds and two states.

5. spec's nine command names. This one is compared, by Test_Usage_Text_Should_Name_Every_Command, but against Every_Spec_Command_Name, a hand-written array in the test file rather than a compiled authority -- and in one direction only, so a command the parser accepts and the text omits passes. The compiled vocabulary that would answer is nomos_spec_orchestration::SpecCommand.

The shape is settled and cheap: P96-THE-CHECK-VERBS-HELP-NAMES-ONE-RULE-OF-SEVENTY-AND-CLAIMS-IT-RUNS-EVERY-ONE built it six times in one sitting, and its commit e16060cf is the worked example for the census-in-the-test-file form, the empty-parse guard, the assertion that the test read its own group's text rather than a sibling's, and the injection that proves a new test can fail.
items.done_when:
Each of the five printed vocabularies either gains the comparison OD-AGENT-004 version 2 requires, or stops enumerating and routes. Which of the two is the implementer's call per vocabulary, and both are admissible; what is refused is leaving a list standing with nothing comparing it, since that is the state this item exists to end.

Each comparison is both directions -- a spelling in the text and not in the authority fails, and a spelling in the authority and not in the text fails -- and each carries the empty-parse guard, so a test whose prose section is renamed fails rather than silently comparing nothing. One direction is not enough and is the specific reason spec's existing check does not already close case 5.

work's --state list gains lapsed, or the implementer establishes that lapsed must not be an accepted filter value and narrows what Listed_As matches instead. Either closes it; printing nine while accepting ten does not. The authority for this one is the set of labels Listing_Label can return, which is nomos_ledger::item::State's variants together with the derived labels work/report.rs produces, so the comparison is against that set and not against State alone. A test asserting the printed nine against State's five would be wrong in both directions and is not what this asks for.

The other four compare against their own compiled authority: nomos_ledger::item::Kind and Origin, nomos_model_package::EffortLevel, request's submission kind and state types, and nomos_spec_orchestration::SpecCommand. For case 3 the existing EFFORT_SPELLINGS census is reused rather than a second one written; for case 5 Every_Spec_Command_Name is replaced by SpecCommand rather than kept beside it, because a hand array beside a compiled vocabulary is the second authority this whole record is about.

Each census that a test file has to carry, because the vocabulary's own declaration is not this item's territory, is paired with a wildcard-free match over that type, so a variant added to it fails this workspace to compile rather than to pass. The form is the one commit e16060cf uses in agent/tests.rs, request/tests.rs, spec/tests.rs and work/tests.rs; follow it rather than inventing a second.

Each new test is confirmed able to fail by injecting a wrong spelling into that vocabulary's own prose and observing red, not by reasoning that it would. A test that cannot fail is the defect this item is about.

OD-AGENT-004 needs no further amendment: its version 2 already states the condition and already names these five as not yet meeting it. Removing them from that list is part of the work, so the record stops describing a debt that has been paid -- that is an edit to the amendment's own What is compared section, and this item reserves the record for it.

Not closed by doing one or two of the five and filing the rest: the five were measured together and named together, and a partial pass leaves the record's list wrong in the other direction. If one of them turns out to need a decision this item cannot make, decline it with that reason rather than silently leaving it.

If the record is edited, diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md are both re-rendered from a tree holding exactly HEAD plus the amended record, per OD-GATE-005, and committed alongside.

items.title: README.md reprints five compiled vocabularies with nothing comparing any of them, and its state list is stale against the help text P97 corrected
items.why:
Measured on a quiescent tree at c1776c0c. OD-AGENT-004 version 2 states the condition: a help text may enumerate a compiled vocabulary only where a test compares that enumeration against its authority, in both directions, refusing to pass on an empty parse; otherwise it routes. P97 closed that across nomos-cli's five printed vocabularies and, in doing so, surfaced a copy the population it measured could not see, because that population was every nomos-cli test that reads a usage text and this artifact is not one.

README.md reproduces the work group's usage synopsis nearly verbatim and enumerates five compiled vocabularies inside it. Nothing compares any of them to anything:

  line 141  --state, nine words, against the label universe nomos-cli's Listing_Label produces
  line 144  --kind, five words, against nomos_ledger::item::Kind
  line 145  --origin, two words, against nomos_ledger::item::Origin
  line 174  --kind again, the same five words restated in prose two paragraphs below
  line 267  request submit --kind, three words, against nomos_spec_model::submission::Kind

The first is already wrong. P97 added lapsed to the help text because Listing_Label produces it and Listed_As accepts it as a filter value, so nomos work list --state lapsed works; line 141 still prints nine and is now inconsistent with the command it documents.

This bears directly on OD-AGENT-004 version 1's central measurement, which is why it belongs in an item rather than in a passing note. That measurement found fifteen stale restatements the day after a port changed, every one in module prose and none in README.md, and concluded README.md stayed correct because tests/contract/tests/boundaries/readme.rs asserts its tables against the real workspace, both directions. That test parses table rows and nothing else, and it says so in its own doc. A pipe-joined vocabulary inside a fenced command block is not a table, so none of the five above has ever been in its scope. The README is not correct because it is the README; it is correct where it is checked, which is version 1's rule holding at a finer grain rather than an exception to it.

What each case can be compared against differs, and the item should not pretend otherwise. nomos-ledger is already a dependency of tests/contract, so Kind and Origin are reachable from a contract test today. nomos_spec_model is not a dependency of that crate. The state label universe is not reachable at all: Listing_Label and Refusal_Label are private to the nomos-cli binary, which exports no library, so no external test can read the set P97's own test derives by running it.

Every one of the five enumerations above either gains a comparison against its authority or stops enumerating and routes, and which one is decided per case by what is actually reachable rather than by preference:

The two ledger vocabularies, --kind and --origin, are compared against nomos_ledger::item::Kind and nomos_ledger::item::Origin from tests/contract/tests/boundaries/readme.rs, which already depends on that crate. Each new comparison is confirmed able to fail by injecting a wrong word into README.md and observing red, not by reasoning that it would. Each routing case is confirmed by checking that the vocabulary it dropped is still reachable by a reader in one step, from the text that replaced it.

No figure moves anywhere else. This item does not touch the help text P97 already corrected, and README.md's zone table and every other table in it are outside what this changes.

OD-AGENT-004's amendment names this README copy in its Two further copies section. That entry is updated to say it is closed, or narrowed to whatever remains, and the record is reserved for it. If the record is edited, diagrams/relations.mmd and spec/domain-specification.md are both re-rendered from a tree holding exactly HEAD plus the amended record, per OD-GATE-005, and committed alongside.

items.title: The work verb list is compared against the usage text and the parser, and against the enum that actually changes when a verb is added it is not
items.why:
Measured on a quiescent tree at 7c45e019. This is the last instance in the population OD-AGENT-004 version 2's condition covers, and it is the weakest of them, which is why it is filed separately rather than folded into the items that closed the other seven.

crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/parse.rs line 522 holds Every_Verb, a hand-written list of eleven verb names, and Test_Usage_Text_Should_Name_Every_Verb_It_Accepts iterates it asserting two things per verb: the usage text names it, and the parser does not reject it as an unknown command. Both of those are real and neither is the direction that matters. The authority is nomos_work_orchestration::WorkCommand, a compiled enum with one variant per verb, and nothing compares the list to it -- so a verb added to the dispatch match in Work_Command_From_String_Arguments and not to Every_Verb is named by neither the test nor, necessarily, the usage text, and the suite stays green.

It is better than the two copies P97 has just closed, and that is worth saying rather than inflating the finding. It checks both the text and the parser, so it is two directions between those two artifacts. What it does not have is any tie to the enum, which is the thing that actually changes when a verb is added.

The comparison is buildable the way the seven already built are. The verb-to-variant mapping is not one-to-one in spelling -- claim, renew and takeover each parse to their own WorkCommand variant through a shared arm -- so the exhaustive match a census needs is over the enum and not over the strings, which is the same shape spec/tests.rs uses for SpecCommand.

A verb whose spelling differs from its variant name is handled by the match rather than by a second table. claim, renew and takeover share a parse arm and are three variants; nothing about that is a special case to write down twice.

The new comparison is confirmed able to fail by injecting a wrong verb into the usage text and observing red, not by reasoning that it would.

OD-AGENT-004 version 2 already states the condition this applies and its coverage section is about the copies it named, not about this one, so adding a line there would be a claim about scope the record never made. items.title: The reuse-equals-recomputation proof through Run covers one rule over caller-supplied source bytes, and eleven other fact families materialize beside it
items.why: Three tests in this workspace assert some form of incremental equivalence and none of them reaches the gap. crates/substrate/nomos-analysis/tests/recomputation_equivalence.rs proves it on a synthetic fixture built directly on MemoryFactStore's own Materialize/Invalidate/Current API, and its own module doc states it deliberately exercises store mechanics rather than any capability's business logic. crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust-cargo/tests/invalidation.rs proves an edited manifest's old edge fact does not survive the generation it was invalidated at, but never compares a reused run against a clean one through Run. Test_A_Store_And_Workspace_Reused_Across_An_Edit_Agrees_With_A_Clean_Recomputation, at crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/src/tests.rs:535, is the only test that asserts the invariant through the real Run pipeline on both claim and findings, and it selects exactly one rule: NAMING_CONVENTION, feeding on SyntaxItems and NamingPolicy. Materialize_Capabilities in run_context.rs materializes twelve RequiredFact families. The three families differ in where the input lives and what mutates it, and that is the axis the current proof does not cross: a source-derived fact comes from bytes the caller hands in, a workspace-derived fact comes from a subprocess reading a manifest tree under root, and a repository-derived fact comes from files under root that no caller passes at all. Reuse-equals-recomputation is proved only along the first. An under-invalidating family in the second or third class serves a stale fact, which is a wrong answer rather than a missing one, and it is silent in exactly the conditions the suite runs under.
items.done_when: crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/tests/incremental_equivalence.rs exists and proves the invariant for three rules spanning the three input classes named in the why: NAMING_CONVENTION for the source-derived class, DEPENDENCY_DIRECTION for the workspace-derived class (cargo metadata over a fixture tree whose manifest is rewritten between generations), and REQUIREMENT_TRACE_STALENESS for the repository-derived class (a file under root rewritten between generations). Each proof performs a G0 Run, mutates that family's own real input, performs a G1 Run reusing the same workspace and store, performs an independent G1 Run over a fresh workspace and store, and asserts the reused run equals the clean run on both claim and findings. Each of the three is separately confirmed able to fail by mutating the input and suppressing the invalidation, or by breaking the mutation, and observing red; the confirmation is stated in the commit message per rule, not as one blanket sentence. The item reports whether the three classes behaved identically. A family-by-family matrix over the remaining nine is NOT added by this item and is authored as a separate item only if this one measures a real difference in invalidation semantics between the classes; adding twelve copies without that measurement is explicitly out of scope.

items.title: Two accepted records state a single-adapter topology that was retired, and neither says what survived it
items.why: On 2026-09-10 the owner retired the boundary test that forbade any crate but one named adapter from reaching an xvpe- dependency. The tombstone in tests/contract/tests/boundaries/graph.rs gives the reason: nomos is built on top of XVPE, so a rule forbidding that dependency does not describe an architecture worth keeping. What that retired was the adapter-count restriction, that exactly one crate may name xvpe-. It did not retire D-130's separate clause that an XVPE dependency is never taken by path, and it did not retire D-130's Phase 5 adoption gate. Both records still describe the retired topology as current. D-130 is accepted at version 2 and its title still reads that nomos takes no XVPE dependency before Phase 5, and never by path. ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 is accepted at version 4 and states twice that D-130 fixes the mechanical form of this crossing as a single named adapter and no path dependency, and that D-130 is untouched and unweakened. No record supersedes either: all eight relations pointing at D-130 are relates-to or affects. Measured 2026-09-14 at 8503ddb3: eight workspace crates and the contract test crate carry sixteen relative path dependencies into a sibling checkout, so both records assert a mechanical claim the tree falsifies.
items.done_when: D-130 and ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001 each carry an amendment separating what was retired from what survives. The amendments record four things: that the sole-adapter restriction is retired; that the boundary against making nomos correctness or reproducibility depend on an unpinned sibling working tree is retained; that the Phase 5 adoption gate is retained unless separately superseded; and that each condition D-130's own 2026-08-18 amendment named is dispositioned individually against a measurement rather than lapsing with the adapter-count rule. Those dispositions are measured against the xvpe checkout and name its commit, covering at least whether xvpe has a storage crate, whether it has a package crate, whether xvpe-telemetry still names a desktop OS backend, and what nomos's real xvpe dependency closure contains. ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001's two statements about D-130 are corrected rather than left standing. If either amendment names the retired test, tests/contract/tests/record_citation.rs gains the matching declaration. Both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly these records, and cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes.
