items.title: Sixteen relative path dependencies crossed a boundary that no decision retired
items.why: D-130's path clause and its Phase 5 adoption gate both survive the 2026-09-10 retirement, which reached only the adapter-count restriction. Against that surviving boundary the tree has diverged, and the divergence is an implementation defect rather than stale prose. Measured 2026-09-14 at 8503ddb3: eight workspace members carry sixteen dependencies spelled as a relative path climbing out of this repository into a sibling directory named xvpe, so whether this workspace builds is a function of another product's working tree at whatever revision that tree happens to be sitting at, with nothing recording which revision that was. Three facts bound the fix. First, replacing them is available rather than theoretical: the sibling checkout has a real remote at github.com/kevinmettias/xvpe.git, sits on dev at commit 82a3c8fccf4ef7f3759f36d3f320a91d0f96341c with a clean tree, so a git and rev dependency of the form D-130 already names is fetchable today. Second, the adoption is narrower than D-130 feared: the whole workspace's xvpe closure is twelve crates and contains no GPU, windowing or UI crate, so the concern that a path dependency selects a game engine's entire workspace is not what the current adoption actually did. Third, two of D-130's stated gate conditions are unchanged, since xvpe still has no storage crate and no package crate, so Phase 5 has not opened and this adoption preceded it.
items.done_when: Either the sixteen relative path dependencies are gone, each replaced by a dependency that pins what it adopts by a git reference and an explicit commit in the form D-130 names, with Cargo.lock regenerated so the adopted revision is recorded rather than ambient; or, if replacing them is refused for a reason measured rather than assumed, a governing record adjudicates that refusal, states why a path dependency is the accepted form of this crossing, and supersedes D-130's surviving path clause explicitly instead of leaving it contradicted. That test's own module documentation states its limit in terms, saying the migration never touched the one place a band number also lived, and the phrase check it performs looks only at a description line. The population outside that one line was never measured and is not small. Measured 2026-09-14 at 8503ddb3: fifty-two band references survive in Cargo.toml comments, forty-seven of them in the root workspace manifest alone, and sixty-one survive in Rust module documentation across fifty-seven files. AGENTS.md names stale architectural language as something a reader should not have to mentally translate, and a later agent reading a Band 41 comment beside a zone table has no way to tell which of the two the workspace believes.
items.done_when: The guard no longer stops at a manifest description: it covers Cargo.toml comments and Rust module documentation as well, and the workspace is clean under the widened guard. The two contract tests that exist precisely to talk about bands, boundaries/band_zero.rs and boundaries/manifest_bands.rs, are exempt by a named exemption rather than by the guard failing to notice them, because a guard that cannot name its own subject is the vacuity this repository already writes records about. Every surviving reference is either replaced by the zone the crate actually sits in, read from nomos-rules' own ZONES rather than retyped, or removed where it carried no meaning beyond the number. cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes, and the run is checked against a quiescent tree rather than one a peer session is editing.

items.title: Whether bundling a provider with its contract lets a rule compile-link an external system past the Rules-may-not-name-Provider edge
items.why: nomos-rules names nomos-connector-coderabbit and nomos-cap-requirement-trace, and each of those crates carries a real provider beside its contract: the first has provider.rs, fetching.rs and translation.rs and reaches GitHub through gh api, the second has provider.rs and reads arbitrary files across the tree. Two questions about this are already settled and neither is the open one. OD-CAPABILITY-015 settles which zone such a crate belongs to, on the criterion that it declares a capability contract, and README.md states in terms that the classification is not made because nomos-rules needs to reach it, which would make the edge vacuous by relabelling whatever a rule turns out to need. OD-CAPABILITY-002 settles when a contract earns its own crate, and its criterion is provider contention: the moment a second provider exists, because the first can change the ceiling, the version or the schema its peer is bound by in a file the peer cannot open. A second consumer is not that, so the argument that nomos-rules reading a contract is itself the second party that forces a split misreads the record, and this item does not assume the split. What neither record reaches is narrower. The dependency model forbids Rules from naming Provider. Bundling puts a provider's implementation inside a crate the Rules zone may name, so nomos-rules acquires a compile-time link to external-system machinery while the declared edge still reads as a prohibition. Nothing has decided whether that is an accepted consequence of the bundling license or a backdoor the license did not intend to open.
items.done_when: A governing record decides what the Rules-may-not-name-Provider edge means when a provider is bundled into a crate the Rules zone may name. It answers, rather than assumes, three things: whether a compile-time link from nomos-rules to external-system machinery is an accepted consequence of OD-CAPABILITY-002's bundling license or something the license did not intend; if it is not accepted, what the remedy is and on what trigger, distinguished from OD-CAPABILITY-002's provider-contention trigger which this is not; and what a future bundled capability contract must satisfy before the Rules zone may name it, stated so that a later reader can apply it without re-deriving this argument. The record is registered rather than only written, both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly it, and cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: A local patch override needs a recorded status before it reads as the governing form of the XVPE crossing
items.why: The sixteen path dependencies are now pinned to a git reference and commit, which is the form D-130 requires, and the owner chose to keep the day-to-day loop by allowing an uncommitted local patch override redirecting those crates to the sibling checkout. That override is useful and it is also dangerous in a specific way. It makes every local build test something other than what the repository publishes, so a change that compiles here can fail in CI for a reason no local run can reproduce, which is the same class of silent divergence the pinning was adopted to end. Two mechanical facts sharpen it. There is no .cargo directory in this tree and nothing in .gitignore excludes one, so an override file would sit untracked in a working tree that AGENTS.md already warns is shared with live sessions, one git add away from being committed as though it were the governing form. And this tree is shared: an override appearing in it silently changes what every concurrent session builds against, with nothing telling a reader that their build is no longer using the pinned revision.
items.done_when: A governing record states the status of a local patch override: that the pinned git dependency is the only governing form of this crossing, that an override is a development convenience carrying no authority, what it may do and what it must never do, and how a reader determines whether one is active in the tree they are sitting in. The record is registered rather than only written. .gitignore excludes the local cargo configuration so an untracked override cannot be swept into a commit by a scoped add, which is the mechanical half the record cannot supply. Both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly this record, and cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Nothing asserts the committed lock still pins the XVPE crossing, and a local override silently un-pins it
items.why: OD-PLATFORM-004 names this debt and deliberately does not pay it. Measured 2026-09-14: with a local patch override active, a single cargo metadata call rewrote the tracked Cargo.lock and deleted the git source line from all twelve xvpe- packages, reporting nothing. Cargo.lock is the artifact that makes the adopted revision a recorded fact rather than an ambient one, which is the whole content of D-130's surviving clause. It is tracked on purpose, so gitignore cannot protect it the way it protects the override file, and the scoped git add that AGENTS.md asks for everywhere else is exactly the gesture that would publish an un-pinned lock. Every other clause of OD-PLATFORM-004 fails safely, because a wrong override breaks a local build and its author finds out immediately. This one fails silently, in the committed state, in the direction the pinning exists to prevent, and no test in this workspace reads Cargo.lock at all.
items.done_when: A contract test asserts that every package in Cargo.lock whose name begins with xvpe- carries a git source, and that the revision it names is the one the manifests name, so a lock rewritten by an active override fails the gate instead of being published. The failure message says what happened and how to restore, because the reader hitting it will usually be somebody who ran a build rather than somebody who edited a manifest. The guard is proven by injecting a lock that violates it and observing the failure, then restoring the file byte-identically, rather than being believed because it passes on a tree that already satisfies it. The boundaries module documentation, which already says eight properties while listing nine, is corrected to the real count rather than left one further behind. cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: The local override activates itself on every command, and sibling development should have to be asked for
items.why: OD-PLATFORM-004 permits a local substitution of the XVPE crossing and denies it any authority, and that decision is correct. Its activation semantics are not. The file it names is .cargo/config.toml, which Cargo discovers automatically, so every cargo command run anywhere in this tree opts into the substitution whether or not the person running it wanted sibling development -- including a concurrent session's commands, which never asked for it at all. The consequence is not hypothetical and was observed twice today: an ordinary command stripped the git source line from all twelve xvpe- packages in the tracked Cargo.lock, and at one point this working tree stood at zero of twelve pinned with the new guard failing. The guard is the right backstop and stays, but it catches the damage after the fact. The ergonomics are inverted: the reproducible form is what a build should fall into by default, and substituting a sibling checkout is the thing that should cost an explicit gesture. Cargo already supplies one, so this needs no new machinery: an extra configuration file passed by name is loaded only when it is named.
items.done_when: Activation is explicit rather than automatic. The override no longer sits at a path Cargo discovers on its own, it is ignored by git under whatever name it does take, and an ordinary cargo command in this tree resolves the pinned crossing and leaves Cargo.lock untouched -- checked by running one and observing the lock unchanged, not assumed. OD-PLATFORM-004 carries an amendment recording that the substantive decision is unchanged, that local substitution is still permitted and still carries no authority, and that only activation moves from implicit to opt-in, together with the exact invocation that requests it and a statement that a build made that way is development-resolved rather than reproducible. The lock guard is untouched and still green. Both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly this record, and cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: The lock guard's restore instruction names a file the opt-in refinement removes
items.why: lock_pinning.rs fails with guidance telling the reader to park .cargo/config.toml and then check the lock out. Once activation becomes opt-in that file does not exist: the override moves to a name Cargo does not discover, and an ordinary command can no longer dirty the lock at all, so the only way to reach this failure is an explicit opt-in build or a lock committed from one. The instruction would then send a reader to a path that is not there, in the one message they see at the moment they are already confused, which is the worst place in the repository for a stale name. The message is also the thing most likely to be read by somebody who did not make the change, since the whole point of the guard is to catch a lock that was dirtied by a build rather than edited by hand.
items.done_when: The guard's failure message names the situation that can actually produce it after activation is opt-in, and the command it gives works as written in that situation. It no longer instructs the reader to move a file that the opt-in refinement removed. The module documentation, which states the same mechanism in prose, agrees with the message rather than being left one refinement behind. The guard still fails on an un-pinned lock and still passes on a pinned one, checked rather than assumed, and cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

Declined.reason: Superseded by P98-THE-LOCK-GUARD-JUDGES-A-FILE-CARGO-REPAIRS-BEFORE-IT-RUNS, which carries the stale restore message together with the correctness defect that made the message the smaller of the two problems in that file.

abandoned.reason: Too narrow, and its done_when cannot be met as scoped. Checking the clause that the guard still fails on an un-pinned lock revealed that it does not: cargo re-resolves and re-pins the lock before the test body reads it, so the guard cannot fail in an ordinary run at all.

items.title: The lock guard judges a file cargo repairs before it runs, so it cannot fail in an ordinary run
items.why: The guard landed in e3d86344 reads Cargo.lock from the working tree. Any cargo invocation re-resolves and re-pins that file when no patch configuration is active, including the very cargo test invocation that runs the guard. Measured 2026-09-14: an opt-in build left zero of twelve packages pinned, and one ordinary cargo metadata call restored all twelve. So by the time the test body opens the file, cargo has repaired the thing it exists to judge. It appeared to work when it was landed only because the override was auto-discovered at that moment, so cargo test itself kept the patch applied and the lock un-pinned; the same sequence run after activation became opt-in reports the lock at zero pinned and the guard passing. Making activation explicit therefore removed the only condition under which this guard could ever fail, which means it now cannot fail in an ordinary local run or in CI. The test is also named for the committed lock while reading the working tree, and those are different artifacts: only the first is the claim anybody cares about, because only the first is what a commit publishes. Separately, its failure message still tells the reader to park a file the opt-in refinement removed.
items.done_when: The guard judges what a commit actually publishes rather than what cargo has just rewritten, reading the lock as committed rather than from the working tree, and refuses rather than passes if it cannot read that. The judging logic is a function taking lock text, so it can be exercised against a synthetic un-pinned lock as a negative control that proves the assertion can fail, rather than the guard being believed because it passes on a tree that satisfies it. Both the negative control and the real assertion over the committed lock are present and pass. The failure message names the situation that can actually produce it now that substitution is opt-in, and the command it gives works as written. The module documentation agrees with both. cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes and the gate lint step is clean.

items.title: The crossing acceptance check runs warm, so a zero exit is not evidence the crossing was exercised
items.why: Measured 2026-09-14 while verifying the pinned crossing: cargo check --workspace --all-targets exited zero in twenty seconds having compiled no xvpe crate at all, because a concurrent session had already warmed the shared target directory. The same check re-run with an isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR compiled ten xvpe crates from the git revision by name. Exit zero is therefore not evidence that the dependency crossing participated in the build; it is evidence that nothing in the workspace failed to typecheck against artifacts somebody else produced, possibly from different sources. Nothing in this repository currently distinguishes those two outcomes, and the claim that this workspace builds against a pinned XVPE is exactly the claim that needs the distinction. Making every build cold would waste a great deal of time and is not wanted. The dedicated acceptance check for this one crossing is what should be cold by construction. Note for whoever takes this: the gate has not executed a step since at least 2026-09-07 -- every run fails in seconds with a GitHub billing message and zero steps started -- so a gate step added here is correct placement but will not run until that is resolved.
items.done_when: A dedicated acceptance check builds a crossing-dependent crate into a target directory it creates fresh, and asserts from the build output that the xvpe packages actually compiled from the pinned git revision rather than inferring it from an exit code. It fails if no xvpe crate appears in that output, so a warm or short-circuited run cannot report success. It does not run as part of an ordinary cargo test invocation, because a cold build is slow and every local run must not pay for it, and it is reachable by one bare command that the gate can name. The gate names it as its own step. The check is proven by observing it distinguish the two cases rather than by passing once.

items.why: OD-CAPABILITY-017 decided that bundling a provider with its contract does not defeat the Rules boundary, and the first of its three clauses is the load-bearing one: the rule consumes the contract half only. That clause rests on a measurement taken 2026-09-14 -- nomos-rules calls no provider-side symbol of nomos-connector-coderabbit or nomos-cap-requirement-trace, every use being capability, contract version, ceiling, schema and payload parsing. A measurement is a fact about one afternoon. Nothing prevents a later edit to checks/review.rs or checks/requirement_trace.rs from calling the fetching or translation functions directly: the crates are linked and the symbols are public, so the compiler would accept it and no test would notice. That failure is silent and lands in the committed state, which is the shape this repository already decided is worth a guard rather than a convention.

The contract half is defined by something the crate itself states rather than by a list retyped in the test, or if it must be a list, the list is checked in both directions so it cannot go stale in either. items.title: A red check on a commit means the gate never ran, and nothing says so
items.why: OD-GATE-006 decided that a declaration of enforcement is incomplete until something executes it in every environment the claim needs. That condition is currently false and nothing records it. Measured 2026-09-14: gh run list shows every recent commit on dev completing as failure in two to seven seconds, the run annotation reads that the job was not started because recent account payments have failed or the spending limit needs increasing, and the jobs endpoint reports zero steps for both the ubuntu and windows runners. No gate step has executed since at least 2026-09-07. The consequence is a signal that reads as its own opposite: a red check on a nomos commit is being produced by a scheduling refusal, and a reader who sees it will conclude the gate ran and found something. The inverse error is just as bad and must be avoided in whatever is written: these commits are not unverified in any blanket sense, because each carries the local predicate its ledger item declared plus the lint step work finish runs. What they specifically lack is remote full-gate execution evidence, and that precision is the whole content of the statement. This workspace already has the vocabulary for exactly this distinction rather than needing a new one: Applicability separates MissingCapability and ProviderUnavailable from a clean result, and SynchronizationState::Unavailable already carries the note that unavailable is not agreement and is not divergence either.
items.done_when: A governing record states the remote gate availability as unavailable, names the refusal as the cause and the date from which it holds, and is explicit in both directions about what that does and does not mean: no commit after that date carries remote full-gate execution evidence, and every commit still carries whatever its own declared predicate and the lint step actually established. It names what a red check currently signifies so a reader stops misreading it, states what recovery requires and what would have to be replayed if historical remote evidence turns out to matter, and routes to this workspace's existing unavailability vocabulary rather than declaring a parallel one. The record is registered rather than only written, both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly the records this commit publishes, and cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: A verification predicate can repair or bypass the condition it is supposed to observe
items.why: Three defects found in one session share a cause that none of them looks like individually, and the cause is not bad input. In each case the verification mechanism modified or bypassed the very condition it existed to observe, and reported success. First, a workspace check exited zero in twenty seconds having compiled no crate of the dependency crossing it was run to prove, because a concurrent session had warmed the shared target directory; the same check in an isolated target directory compiled ten of them. Second, a lock guard appeared to work only because an ambient auto-discovered Cargo configuration kept the violation alive during the test run, so making that configuration opt-in removed the single condition under which the guard could ever fail. Third, the same guard read Cargo.lock from the working tree, and cargo re-resolves and re-pins that file on its way to running any test, so the test setup repaired the violation before the test body could observe it. Every one of the three passed. Two of the three were found by checking a done_when clause rather than by anything going red, which is the point: a predicate in this state cannot go red. This workspace already writes records about a check that reports the same clean result whether it verified everything or nothing, and this is that failure arriving from the environment rather than from an empty subject.
items.done_when: A governing record names the defect class, states the three measured instances as evidence rather than as illustrations, and states the obligation it puts on a predicate: that a predicate is not established until it has been observed to fail on a real violation, and that its relationship to the environment it runs in is part of what must be checked rather than assumed. It names the asymmetry that makes the class worth a record, which is that such a predicate cannot report the problem itself. It deliberately declines to build a general abstraction now and says why, and names where the class is expected to recur so a later reader recognises it rather than rediscovering it. The record is registered rather than only written, both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly the records this commit publishes, and cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Census the forward-looking implementation-state claims in module docs and governing records, and correct only the ones implementation superseded
items.why: Three stale forward-looking claims were found in two files in one session, each naming functionality that later landed correctly. gate_command.rs said compare was simply absent, not stubbed, while Compare_Gate_Runs was exported and nomos gate compare was a shipped verb (67d66b8e). nomos-api cited that same gate.rs claim as precedent after the claim had stopped existing (b42e3aa3). nomos-api then promised a follow-up increment wires a real transport over Handle_Gate_Run once one exists to design it against, while nomos-api-transport was already dispatching to it and quoting that very sentence as the hole it fills. The shape is identical each time and it is not prose drift: an increment lands, the prose that predicted it survives, and a module doc a reader is routed to as navigational authority becomes false about the state of the workspace. AGENTS.md routes every question to an authority, and OD-AGENT-001 records why an instruction file must route rather than restate; a routed-to authority asserting a state that is no longer true is the same defect one layer down. What is not yet known is the size of the population. Three instances found incidentally is evidence of a pattern and not a measurement of one, and this repository does not build a mechanism for a population it has not counted.
items.done_when: A census exists reporting every forward-looking implementation-state claim found in module docs under crates/ and in docs/records/, searched for at minimum on the phrases: not yet, nothing calls, follow-up increment, once one exists, will wire, future provider, still unbuilt, not composed, not reachable, not CLI-wired, no caller. Each hit is classified into exactly one of four buckets: still true; superseded by implementation; intentionally deferred; historical context that is explicitly dated or scoped. Only the second bucket is corrected, and each correction follows the pattern 67d66b8e established rather than deleting the reasoning: the original restraint is preserved and what eventually satisfied its trigger is stated beside it, because a decision held and then released on evidence is a stronger precedent than one still waiting and the reasoning is the part a reader cannot re-derive. Historical reasoning is NOT rewritten merely because later work happened. The census reports its own counts per bucket, and whether the superseded bucket has enough repeated structure to be mechanically checkable, but designs no rule and composes none: that decision is a separate item, authored only if this census produces the evidence for it. A count of three -- the three already corrected -- closes this item as a manual cleanup that was sufficient, and that is a real outcome rather than a failure.

items.title: OD-CONNECTOR-004 revisit condition does not distinguish a second provider from a second transport
items.why: OD-CONNECTOR-004 declines a provider-comparison mechanism until a second real review provider exists, and does not say what counts as one. The unmerged track-c-external-kwb branch carries nomos-connector-github, whose own commit message calls it ARC-CONNECTOR-001s first real connector. A session finding that branch can satisfy the revisit condition for the wrong reason, because review artifacts flow through it. Acquiring or publishing review artifacts is a transport role; producing review judgments by independently analyzing a change under the canonical review capability is a provider role, and only the second establishes the plurality the declined mechanism needs. The ambiguity is one sentence wide and is cheaper to close than the wrong reopening it invites.
items.done_when: OD-CONNECTOR-004 is amended to version 2 and states, for its revisit condition, that a second review provider means an independent analyzer capable of resolving the same canonical review capability, and that a connector, transport or artifact acquisition path does not constitute provider plurality merely because it carries review artifacts. Nothing else in the record changes, no mechanism is built, and both required projections are re-rendered from a tree holding exactly the amending commit record set.

items.title: Nothing holds a rule to the contract half of a bundled crate
items.why: OD-CAPABILITY-017 decided that bundling a provider with its contract does not defeat the Rules boundary, and the first of its three clauses is load-bearing: the rule consumes the contract half only. That clause rests on a measurement taken 2026-09-14 -- nomos-rules calls no provider-side symbol of nomos-connector-coderabbit or nomos-cap-requirement-trace, every use being capability, contract version, ceiling, schema and payload parsing. A measurement is a fact about one afternoon. Nothing prevents a later edit to checks/review.rs or checks/requirement_trace.rs from calling the fetching, translation or materialization functions directly: the crates are linked and the symbols are public, so the compiler accepts it and no test notices. That failure is silent and lands in the committed state. There is a derivation available rather than a list to invent: each bundled crate's own lib.rs re-exports every public symbol through a pub use naming the module it comes from, so which half a symbol belongs to is something the crate already states.
items.done_when: A contract test resolves every symbol nomos-rules names from each bundled capability-contract crate and refuses any that the crate re-exports from a fact-producing module, so a rule that starts calling a provider directly fails instead of compiling quietly. The halves are read from the crate's own pub use lines rather than retyped, and wherever a list is unavoidable it is checked in both directions: a named module that no longer exists fails, and a module the crate gains that is classified as neither half fails, so a new provider module cannot slip through unjudged. The guard is proven by feeding it source that names a fact-producing symbol and observing rejection, and source that names only contract symbols and observing acceptance, rather than by passing on a tree that already satisfies it. The module is registered in boundaries/main.rs and its property count there stays truthful. cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes and the gate lint step is clean.

items.title: Build the per-rule empty-population report OD-ANALYSIS-012 accepted and deliberately left unbuilt
items.why: OD-ANALYSIS-012 is accepted at version 1 and its Status section states the answer completely: an empty population is a per-rule fact reported in CheckOutcome::Judged itself, Advisory and Claim-flipping the same way ProviderUnavailable already is, computed from population sizes run_context.rs already holds. Its own What This Record Does Not Do section then says No code moves here, and names the new field, the count computed in run_context.rs and Claim_Of's extension precisely enough for a follow-up item's territory to be declared completely. That follow-up item does not exist. Grepped 2026-09-14: no ledger item names an empty population or OD-ANALYSIS-012, and nothing under crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration names a population at all. So the decision is governing and the mechanism is absent, which is the gap between a record and a build rather than a question needing another record. The present instance is real and named by the record: the four rules P43-SCRIPT-RULES-CANNOT-FIRE measured all report an empty population in this tree today, and a reader cannot tell any of them apart from a rule that judged a real population and found it clean. Note what is already built and is NOT this: crates/host/nomos-cli/src/vacuity.rs satisfies OD-GATE-003 and guards the exit code main.rs produces when a whole group saw no subject at all. That is a per-run guarantee at the CLI boundary. This item is the per-rule fact inside a run that did see subjects, which vacuity.rs's own What this does not cover section puts outside itself.
items.done_when: CheckOutcome::Judged carries the per-rule empty-population fact OD-ANALYSIS-012 names, computed in run_context.rs from population sizes it already holds, and Claim_Of reads it so an empty population flips the claim to Incomplete exactly as a coverage-debt finding already does. No variant is added to Claim and no host renderer changes: Claim is a two-variant Copy enum rendered through Display, so the flip reaches the CLI with no edit there, and any discovery that a host must change means the territory was wrong and the item is declined and re-authored rather than widened. Applicability is not touched and gains no variant, which the record forbids by name: every existing variant presupposes a subject this fact does not have. tests/contract/surface/nomos-check-orchestration.txt is re-blessed from a clean worktree for the changed public surface. A test drives a rule over a deliberately empty population and asserts it is reported apart from a rule that judged a real population clean, and is confirmed able to fail by giving that rule a real population and observing the two stop differing. The four rules P43-SCRIPT-RULES-CANNOT-FIRE measured are checked against the built mechanism and the resulting count is stated in the commit. cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-check-orchestration passes, and so does the workspace self-check.

Declined.reason: Its own done_when names this disposition: any discovery that a host must change means the territory was wrong and the item is declined and re-authored rather than widened. Three hosts must. CheckOutcome::Judged is a struct variant, so every pattern binding all three of its fields without a rest pattern stops compiling when a field is added, and every construction needs the new value. Measured 2026-09-14: nomos-api check.rs, nomos-cli check/report.rs, nomos-gate-orchestration gate_environment.rs and tests/integration calibration.rs each bind all three; gate_environment.rs also reconstructs the variant and nomos-cli gate/report.rs builds four fixtures of it. None of the eight is a rendering decision and each needs a rest pattern or one field value, but none is reachable from the five paths reserved. Separately the done_when requires Claim_Of itself to read the new fact, and Claim_Of is called by nomos-gate-orchestration's Reduced_With_Coverage over the gate's rule-and-scope-selected findings under OD-GATE-016 -- a set carrying no population information -- so extending that signature would force a decision about gate coverage policy that no record has made. Re-authored as -2 with the measured territory, with the host edits stated as mechanical and bounded, and with the Claim_Of question left to the implementer under the constraint that a gate run's disposition does not change.

abandoned.reason: Claimed to implement, grepped every site that binds or builds CheckOutcome::Judged before editing anything, and eight of them are outside the reserved five paths. The item's own done_when says that means decline and re-author rather than widen.

items.title: The architecture the dependency rules judge is 66 compiled-in nomos crate names, so the family cannot judge any other repository
items.why: Five policy families already take their criterion from a declared capability fact under OD-RULES-011, and standards.json carries naming, scripting and words keys a foreign repository supplies for itself: tests/integration/fixtures/third-party/hex-0.4.3/standards.json already declares its own naming policy and the same rules judge it. The architecture family is the exception. Check_Dependency_Direction, Check_Every_Member_Declares_A_Band and Check_Write_Authority resolve every package through Zone_Of, and ZONES is a literal of 66 entries every one of which is a nomos crate name. The dependency edges are provider-derived and generalize; the architecture they are judged against is source code in nomos-rules. In any other repository Zone_Of returns None and the family reports NotApplicable, which is honest and is also the whole family declining for every repository that is not this one. OD-RULES-024 named this as a fact this workspace does not yet produce; the missing fact is a declared architecture, not an inference engine.
items.done_when: A repository declares its architecture as data and it reaches the three existing dependency rules as a capability fact, following the OD-RULES-011 contract-plus-provider pattern the five policy families already use. No nomos crate name remains compiled into nomos-rules as architecture: deleting every such name does not reduce this workspace's ability to enforce its own architecture, because this workspace now declares what the ZONES table encoded. The same three rule implementations, unchanged in what they judge, enforce a foreign declaration with a different package vocabulary, proved against the hex-0.4.3 third-party fixture. A repository declaring no architecture still reports NotApplicable rather than passing clean, and an incomplete or unparseable declaration reports a refusal or applicability state rather than silently dropping the checks. OD-RULES-024 is amended to say the fact now exists and what it is. This item does not design an ownership, required-mechanism or general engineering-model schema; it moves the architecture topology the existing rules already judge, and nothing else.

Declined.reason: Territory omitted root Cargo.toml, which a new workspace member and its workspace-dependency entry both require, and the new crate's own tests/contract/surface snapshot. Re-authored as -2 with both added, before any claim, rather than widened mid-claim.

items.title: The security rules decide what is test material from an eight-clause hardcoded path convention, so a repository that files fixtures elsewhere gets false credential findings
items.why: Auditing all 42 SourceText rules for repository-specific criteria found exactly one family. Is_Test_Or_Fixture_Source in security_text.rs matches tests/, /tests/, /test/, /testdata/, /fixtures/, /examples/, _test.rs, _tests.rs and _test.go, and Check_A_Credential_Is_Not_Hardcoded_In_Source, Check_A_Secret_Does_Not_Travel_In_A_Url and Check_Certificate_Verification_Is_Not_Disabled all exempt a source on that basis; rust_text.rs carries the same notion in its unwrap-outside-tests-and-examples wording. Some of those clauses are toolchain-fixed and portable: Cargo owns tests/ and examples/, Go owns _test.go. testdata and fixtures are neither, they are a project convention. A repository filing its fixtures under resources or spec or samples is judged as if a fixture credential were a real one, and an exemption that is too narrow produces false positives rather than misses, which is the damaging direction for a security rule. Everything else in the 42 is language syntax, Rust module-system filenames or Go conventions; the only other repository-specific literals are five self-exemption paths naming the rule modules own source.
items.done_when: What counts as test material reaches the security rules as a declared criterion rather than a path list compiled into security_text.rs, using whatever declaration path P100-2 establishes rather than inventing a second one. The toolchain-fixed clauses may remain as defaults, and a repository declaring nothing keeps today behaviour. A repository declaring its own fixture locations has them exempted, proved against a fixture whose test material sits under none of the nine current clauses. rust_text.rs stops carrying a second independent notion of the same thing.

Declined.reason: Stranded by a stale edge, not by the work ceasing to be work: it depended on P100-...-2, which was declined and re-authored as -3. Re-added as -2 of its own name pointing at -3. The finding it records is unchanged.

items.title: Gate compare is reachable only from a terminal, and the headless surfaces are the ones a deployment drives
items.why: ARC-ROADMAP-001's constraint 5 describes the product Gate as exposed through plan, run, explain and compare over the same application-service boundary the CLI, API and MCP projections share, and IF-001 requires every user-visible query or action to have a canonical application service. Three of the four verbs have one. Measured 2026-09-14: nomos-cli serves all four, compare having been wired by P73-GATE-COMPARE-HAS-NO-CALLER; nomos-api exports Handle_Gate_Plan, Handle_Gate_Run and Handle_Gate_Explain and no compare handler at all; and nomos-api-transport's ServedMethod names GatePlan, GateRun, GateExplain and Correction. So the only way to ask what changed between two runs is a terminal, and the headless surfaces are precisely the ones a continuous-conformance deployment drives. What compare answers is the question a gate exists to answer over time rather than once: which findings are new, which are gone, and which changed bucket because a policy moved rather than because the code did. A deployment that cannot ask it can only ever see a pass or a fail, which is the linter-runner behaviour the roadmap separates a product from. The shape is already decided and needs no invention: OD-GATE-022-A settled that a compare caller re-derives both runs inside one process, builds no run-history store and serializes no GateRunResult, and left the per-host wiring to whichever item does it. Compare_Gate_Runs exists, and nomos-cli's own Compare_Verb already proves the composition.
items.done_when: nomos-api exports a gate compare handler beside its own response type, in one file, the handler-beside-its-response locality every other endpoint in that crate keeps. It composes two same-process walk-and-judge runs the way OD-GATE-022-A decided and nomos-cli already does -- each side taking its own fresh RunId from the same clock -- and hands both real results to Compare_Gate_Runs. The response is a one-way serializable projection in the shape its siblings take, and neither GateRunResult nor GateCompareResult nor FindingDisposition nor DispositionChange gains a derive, which OD-GATE-022-A refuses. It carries added, removed and changed as three distinct things rather than collapsing them into a count or a boolean, and a changed entry carries which bucket the finding was in before and which it is in after, because a finding that moved from blocking to baselined and one that moved the other way are opposite facts. The crate documentation's own enumeration of its increments stays truthful rather than stopping at the increment before this one. The public surface snapshot for nomos-api is updated in the same commit that widens the surface. cargo test -p nomos-api -p nomos-contract-tests passes and the gate lint step is clean.

items.title: OD-CAPABILITY-013 decided a per-provider classification and left its carrier undecided, and ProviderOffer is per capability
items.why: OD-CAPABILITY-013 is accepted and decides the vocabulary and the cardinality without ambiguity: a twelve-name FAMILY set and a two-value Delivery axis that classify a provider's own registration, never something a rule names, at one classification per real provider. Its What This Record Does Not Do section then names a follow-up item's territory as a Family enum and a Delivery enum in a shared location, suggesting nomos-capability alongside Registry and ProviderOffer as the natural home, plus one classification per real provider, the eight rows this record already states. Measured against the code on 2026-09-14, that shape does not fit and the record's own count is wrong. ProviderOffer is keyed per capability, not per provider: it carries provider, capability, version and guarantee, and Provider_Offer is constructed at 18 sites across 7 crates, not 8. nomos-lang-rust alone constructs three, from src/guarantee.rs, src/reachability/guarantee.rs and src/rollup/contract.rs, and nomos-repo-policy constructs five. A Family or Delivery field placed on ProviderOffer would therefore give one provider identity three to five independently writable copies of a fact the record says it has exactly one of, with nothing preventing them from disagreeing -- a second authority for a single fact, which is the shape this workspace refuses. The requirement is sound and the physical representation is underdetermined. OD-GATE-024 is the precedent for what happens when that is discovered inside an implementation claim instead of before one: P76-POLICY-ENTRIES-MATCH-BY-SUBJECT-NAME was implemented, measured against the real suite, found unsound as written, and reverted, and the record was amended with what implementing it measured. This item settles the representation from measured code first so the implementation claim that follows has one shape to build.

items.title: The headless surfaces still stop at three Gate verbs, so the compare service has no caller
items.why: P101 gave gate compare a canonical application service: nomos_api::Handle_Gate_Compare composes two same-process walk-and-judge runs the way OD-GATE-022-A decided and returns a serializable projection carrying added, removed and changed. Nothing calls it. Measured after that commit: nomos-api-transport's ServedMethod names GatePlan, GateRun, GateExplain and Correction, its dispatch has no compare arm, and the ADMITTED allow-list in tests/contract/tests/boundaries/transport_registry.rs is a fixed array of four handler names that does not include it; nomos-mcp's ServedTool wraps the same four. So a headless deployment -- the surface a continuous-conformance product is actually driven through -- still cannot ask what changed between two runs, and constraint 5's four-verb Gate is complete only in a terminal. Widening this registry is deliberately not a small edit: OD-HOST-007 required the exclusion be structural rather than advisory, so a fifth verb costs a variant, a dispatch arm, an entry in an allow-list measured against nomos-api's own blessed surface, and a tool description and schema on the MCP side. Correction is the precedent that this is admissible for a real end-user seam rather than a repo-tooling handler.
items.done_when: A headless caller can run gate compare. ServedMethod carries a fifth variant named for the method a caller spells, the dispatch reaches nomos_api::Handle_Gate_Compare, and the transport's allow-list admits that handler deliberately rather than by the registry widening alone. The wire shape carries two whole sides rather than one command and a second root, because OD-GATE-022-A's policy comparison varies the policy between them and its code comparison varies the tree, and one shape serves both. MCP publishes the tool with a sentence saying what it answers and a schema accepting that shape. The repo-tooling exclusion is untouched and still structural: no Handle_Work or Handle_Spec handler becomes reachable, and the test that measures the allow-list against nomos-api's blessed surface still refuses them. Both affected public-surface snapshots are updated in the same commit that widens the surfaces. cargo test -p nomos-api-transport -p nomos-mcp -p nomos-contract-tests passes and the gate lint step is clean.

items.title: A newly authored product Gate should not inherit a compatibility default that lets partial coverage pass
items.why: CoveragePolicy has two variants. Unset means coverage debt does not affect disposition, which is OD-COMPLETENESS-004's own default carried forward so that every construction site predating the type is unchanged in behaviour. RequireCompleteness turns a run that would otherwise report Passed into Indeterminate whenever recomputed coverage over the selected findings is incomplete. Default is Unset, and this repository declares no nomos-gate.json, so a gate whose rules could not be evaluated reports Passed today. The owner's decision is that the representation default and the product-authoring default are different questions and only the second should change: an absent field in an existing configuration still means Unset, so historical behaviour stays reproducible and no existing caller is migrated, while anything that authors a new product Gate -- scaffolding a nomos-gate.json, creating one through API or MCP -- emits require_completeness. A third variant, AllowPartial, makes wanting partial operation an explicit inspectable choice rather than the meaning of an omission, which is the principle at stake: partial coverage may pass should be a decision somebody made, not a consequence of a field nobody wrote.
items.done_when: A governing record states the three-variant model and the distinction it rests on, between the default a representation takes when a field is absent and the default a newly authored Gate is given. It records that Unset keeps its present meaning and that no existing caller is migrated by this, why redefining Unset globally would turn a compatibility decision into a silent semantic migration, and that AllowPartial exists so a deliberate choice of partial operation is inspectable rather than inferred from an omission. It states that Unset is to become visibly non-ideal in authoring and inspection output -- named as a compatibility default, with its effective behaviour and a recommended migration shown -- and that it is deliberately not made invalid, because that would force an unrelated migration across existing callers to improve a default for future use. The record is registered, both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly it, and cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes. No code changes under this item; the variant and the authoring default are separate implementation work this record unblocks.

items.title: The architecture the dependency rules judge is 66 compiled-in nomos crate names, so the family cannot judge any other repository
items.why: Five policy families already take their criterion from a declared fact under OD-RULES-011, and tests/integration/fixtures/third-party/hex-0.4.3/standards.json already declares its own naming policy for the same rules to judge. The architecture family is the exception. Check_Dependency_Direction, Check_Every_Member_Declares_A_Band and Check_Write_Authority resolve every package through Zone_Of, and ZONES is a literal of 66 entries every one of which is a nomos crate name. The dependency edges are provider-derived and generalize; the architecture they are judged against is source code in nomos-rules. In any other repository Zone_Of returns None and the family reports NotApplicable, which is honest and is also the whole family declining for every repository that is not this one. OD-RULES-024 named this as a fact this workspace does not yet produce; the missing fact is a declared architecture, not an inference engine.
items.done_when: The acceptance test is the direction of dependency between rule mechanism and project description, not the representation chosen. Concretely: if the repository-specific description changes completely while the governing rule concept stays the same, the rules crate is unchanged. A relocated table whose schema and interpretation the rules crate still owns does not satisfy this even though it looks data-driven. Which mechanism carries the description is the implementer's to determine from what already exists -- a capability payload, a repository manifest, or another existing contract -- and a new mechanism is not required. Then: no nomos crate name remains compiled into nomos-rules as architecture, and deleting every such name does not reduce this workspace's ability to enforce its own architecture, because this workspace now declares what the ZONES table encoded. The same three rule implementations, unchanged in what they judge, enforce a foreign declaration with a different package vocabulary, proved against the hex-0.4.3 third-party fixture. A repository declaring no architecture still reports NotApplicable rather than passing clean, and an incomplete or unparseable declaration reports a refusal or applicability state rather than silently dropping the checks. OD-RULES-024 is amended to say the fact now exists and what it is. This item does not design an ownership, required-mechanism or general engineering-model schema, and does not decide what a declared component with no observed implementation means.

Declined.reason: Territory reserves sixteen paths and the change provably touches at least fourteen more, measured by grepping every reader of the surface being removed rather than estimating it. Inside nomos-rules: lib.rs and checks.rs both re-export Zone, Zone_Of, Permits, ZONES, ZONE_LIST, SAME_ZONE_EDGES and WRITE_DOORS, and Cargo.toml must name whichever crate carries the declaration. Outside the check run: nomos-gate-orchestration admissibility.rs and nomos-lsp walk_outward/architectural_component.rs both call Zone_Of and Permits with no FactReader anywhere between them, so where those two get their answer is a design question the done_when never states, and their own callers move with their signatures. Registration and materialization need composition.rs, facts.rs and facts/policy_materialization.rs beside the one reserved run_context.rs. In tests/contract: completeness_universes/table.rs names ZONES, SAME_ZONE_EDGES, ALL and WRITE_DOORS by file and constant, and readme.rs reads ZONE_LIST and ZONES to check README.md own zone table. Re-authored as -4 with the measured set, and with the two consumers outside the check run named in the done_when, before any claim rather than widened mid-claim.

abandoned.reason: Claimed to implement, then measured the readers of the surface being removed before editing anything, and the reserved territory cannot carry the change. Abandoning so the item can be declined and re-authored rather than widened mid-claim.

items.title: The security rules decide what is test material from an eight-clause hardcoded path convention, so a repository that files fixtures elsewhere gets false credential findings
items.why: Auditing all 42 SourceText rules for repository-specific criteria found exactly one family. Is_Test_Or_Fixture_Source in security_text.rs matches tests/, /tests/, /test/, /testdata/, /fixtures/, /examples/, _test.rs, _tests.rs and _test.go, and the three security rules all exempt a source on that basis; rust_text.rs carries the same notion independently in its unwrap-outside-tests-and-examples wording. Some clauses are toolchain-fixed and portable: Cargo owns tests/ and examples/, Go owns _test.go. testdata and fixtures are neither, they are a project convention. A repository filing its fixtures under resources or spec or samples is judged as if a fixture credential were a real one, and an exemption that is too narrow produces false positives rather than misses, which is the damaging direction for a security rule.
items.done_when: What counts as test material reaches the security rules as a declared criterion rather than a path list compiled into security_text.rs, composed from the toolchain-fixed clauses plus whatever the repository declares, so that stable Cargo and Go semantics do not become configuration. It uses whichever declaration path P100-...-3 establishes rather than inventing a second one. A repository declaring nothing keeps today behaviour. A repository declaring its own fixture locations has them exempted, proved against a fixture whose test material sits under none of the nine current clauses. rust_text.rs stops carrying a second independent notion of the same thing.

Declined.reason: Stranded by a stale edge, not by the work ceasing to be work: it depended on P100-...-3, which was declined and re-authored as -4 after its territory was measured. Re-added as -3 of its own name pointing at -4. The finding it records is unchanged.

items.title: OD-CAPABILITY-013 defers selection on the premise that no capability has more than one admitted provider, and nomos.cap.syntax.items has two
items.why: OD-CAPABILITY-013 declines to decide P54-A-REPOSITORY-CANNOT-CHOOSE-ITS-TOOLS on a factual premise: Selection does not exist yet because no capability has more than one admitted provider. Measured 2026-09-14, that is false and has been since nomos-lang-rust-scan was composed into the production registry. crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/src/composition.rs offers nomos_lang_rust::Provider_Offer() and nomos_lang_rust_scan::Provider_Offer() in the same real composition, both against nomos.cap.syntax.items, both over Rust sources, and their guarantees differ rather than making either inapplicable: nomos-lang-rust declares FactVariant::SemanticallyResolved with completeness Assurance::Unknown, nomos-lang-rust-scan declares FactVariant::Approximate with soundness Assurance::Unsound. Two admitted providers, one capability, the same subjects. This corrects a premise and must not disturb the conclusion it was supporting, which independently holds: provider choice stays caller-owned because the existing machinery already expresses the competing case truthfully. Registry::Resolve ranks by guarantee, and Resolve_Requiring lets a caller name a provider as required rather than preferred, refusing substitution and naming who else was usable, which OD-CAPABILITY-001 reserved to the caller deliberately. What remains absent is a repository-authored preference, and nothing has asked for one, so OD-HOST-009's trigger is still unfired and that record is untouched here. Boarded apart from P99-OD-CAPABILITY-013-NAMES-THE-CARRIER-OF-A-PROVIDERS-FAMILY-AND-DELIVERY, which amended the same record at a15ef947, because the two correct independently falsifiable claims for different reasons; the ledger refused them as concurrent reservations of one record, which is Test_Two_Items_Writing_One_Record_Should_Still_Be_Refused holding.
items.done_when: OD-CAPABILITY-013 no longer asserts that no capability has more than one admitted provider. It states the measured fact instead, naming the composition that offers both providers against nomos.cap.syntax.items and the differing guarantees that make them genuine alternatives rather than one being inapplicable, and it states why the deferral it was supporting survives the correction: the ranking and Resolve_Requiring already express a truthful choice, so competition existing does not by itself call for repository-authored preference. The deferral of P54-A-REPOSITORY-CANNOT-CHOOSE-ITS-TOOLS stands and OD-HOST-009's trigger stays unfired. Governing-record correction only: no standards.json section, no selection mechanism, no capability contract, no code, and selection policy is not reopened. Followed through .claude/skills/nomos-spec-change: the round trip is read before editing, the preview is read and reports no block removed and no relation changed, and both projections are re-rendered from a worktree holding exactly the records this commit publishes, with a binary built inside it, because spec/domain-specification.md carries the same sentence as a derived projection owned by nobody per OD-GATE-005 and is fixed by rendering rather than editing. Grepped before finishing to confirm no third copy of the premise exists outside the record and that projection. The record's version is bumped.

Declined.reason: The done_when requires three statements the tree contradicts. It says the deferral of P54-A-REPOSITORY-CANNOT-CHOOSE-ITS-TOOLS stands: that item is Done on this board, verified 2026-09-05, and its product is OD-HOST-009. It says OD-HOST-009's trigger stays unfired: that record declares no trigger, is accepted at version 1, and decides outright that a repository may declare per language and per family which tool answers it or that none should run, leaving only the mechanism unbuilt. It says competition existing does not by itself call for repository-authored preference: OD-HOST-009 decided that it does. Separately the why misreads a guarantee -- nomos-lang-rust declares FactVariant::Syntactic with soundness Sound and completeness Unknown, not SemanticallyResolved, which appears in that file as what a future compiler-backed provider would offer and is not composed into the production registry. The premise being corrected is genuinely false and the correction is genuinely owed, so this is re-authored as -2 on measurements taken from the declaring sites, before any claim, rather than written to a done_when that would put three new false statements into a governing record to remove one.

items.title: Three records repeat the bare line Checked 2026-09-14, the preservation guard refuses it, and P95 already fixed this class once
items.why: Test_A_Seeded_Store_Should_Pass_Preservation_Non_Vacuously reports one violation over 9,056 subjects with the corpus set: three sections across three documents repeat an undeclared template, the bare line Checked 2026-09-14. The three are D-130, OD-CAPABILITY-017 and OD-PLATFORM-004, landed 2026-09-14 in be4ca011, 2d39b498 and 8a923e49. This is a recurrence of P95-THREE-RECORDS-REPEAT-A-BARE-MEASURED-ON-LINE, closed 2026-09-13, one phase earlier and one verb over: that item was three sections across three documents repeating the bare line Measured 2026-09-13, caught by the same rule, no_undeclared_filler_template. The rule is right and this is the wording it exists to catch. OD-SPEC-004 is the record about a filler blocklist missing the wording that hollowed v15, and a date with no object is exactly that -- it occupies the position where a reader expects to learn what was checked and against what, and says only when. The discriminator is visible in this very batch: a fourth record written the same day, ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001, carries Checked 2026-09-14, this workspace at 8503ddb3 and escapes the rule, because its object is on the same line. That is the same escape P95 measured for six records written on its own day. A red preservation guard contaminates confidence in every subsequent governing-record edit, which is why this is boarded ahead of ordinary forward work: the guard protecting the normative corpus is the thing currently failing, and a session amending a record while it is red cannot tell its own edit apart from the standing violation.
items.done_when: Each of the three records states what was checked and against what, rather than a date alone, following P95-THREE-RECORDS-REPEAT-A-BARE-MEASURED-ON-LINE's own resolution and ARC-ECOSYSTEM-001's escape in the same batch as the two worked examples. The detector is NOT weakened and no template is declared as intentional: the rule is correct, the prose is what is wrong, and an exemption would reintroduce exactly the filler OD-SPEC-004 records the cost of. No decision changes and no version is bumped on any of the three, because none says anything different afterwards -- this is wording moving, which nomos spec preview reports as its own category and which the preview must confirm rather than reporting blocks added or removed. Followed through .claude/skills/nomos-spec-change: round trip read before editing each, preview read for each, and both projections re-rendered from a worktree holding exactly the records this commit publishes, with a binary built inside it, because three record bodies move. Verified with the corpus set, not merely with a green predicate: NOMOS_V14_CORPUS, NOMOS_SPEC_ARCHIVES and NOMOS_RUST_CORPUS are exported and Test_A_Seeded_Store_Should_Pass_Preservation_Non_Vacuously reports zero violations rather than one, over a subject count in the same order as the 9,056 it reported red, since a corpus-less run of that test passes vacuously and is not evidence. items.title: Materialization restates the demand the descriptors already declare, and the two have drifted
items.why: A rule declares the fact families it needs. RuleDescriptor.requires names one of twelve RequiredFact values per rule, and rule_reassessment_cache.rs and declared_rules.rs both read it as authoritative. Materialization does not. run_context.rs decides what to materialize through hand-written guards of the form Is_Rule_Selected(A) or Is_Rule_Selected(B), one per fact family, restating the same rule-to-fact relation in a second place. Two representations of one relation drift, and these have. Measured 2026-09-14 by parsing DESCRIPTORS and the guards and comparing them: six rules declare RequiredFact::LimitsPolicy -- PARAMETER_COUNT, GO_HELPERS_PACKAGE_FIVE_INPUTS, FILE_SIZE_JUSTIFICATION_TRIGGER, ONE_THOUSAND_LINE_HARD_TRIGGER, FIVE_HUNDRED_LINE_REVIEW_TRIGGER and NESTING_DEPTH -- and the guard names five. NESTING_DEPTH appears in no guard in that file at all. A full run hides it, because the other five rules are selected and the fact is materialized anyway; a narrowed selection does not, and narrowing is exactly what RuleSelector and gate run --rule give an end user. What the rule then does is the part that matters: Check_Nesting_Depth calls Resolve_Limit with the absent fact and falls back to the built-in MAX_NESTING_DEPTH, so it silently judges against the default limit rather than the one the repository configured, reports no MissingCapability, and produces no finding saying so. This is the same duplicate-authority shape OD-GATE-020 measured going false silently twice between the gate registry and the composed rule list, which OD-RULES-027 closed by deriving one from the other rather than reconciling them by hand again.
items.done_when: Materialization derives its demand from RuleDescriptor.requires rather than restating it. For a run, the fact families materialized are the union of the RequiredFact values the selected rules declare, and the hand-written per-family Is_Rule_Selected guards that encoded the same relation are gone rather than left beside the derivation as a second authority. Two controls in both directions: a run selecting a rule proves the family that rule declares is materialized, and a run selecting rules that declare a family proves a family none of them declares is not materialized. NESTING_DEPTH selected alone materializes the limits-policy fact, which is the drift this closes, and that case is a test rather than a claim. Nothing reads cache state, provider cost or whether a fact is already materialized in deciding what to materialize -- the derivation is a union over declarations and nothing else, which is what keeps it on the near side of the demand planner OD-RULES-009 has declined across eight rounds and which run_context.rs's own documentation draws the line at. Judged_Sources stays where it is, its own doc giving the reason a capability slice is an orchestration concept. cargo test -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-contract-tests passes and the gate lint step is clean.

items.title: Nothing proves an unchanged second run through Run produces no new facts
items.why: The reuse machinery is proved correct and never proved economical. incremental_equivalence.rs asserts through the real Run that a reused workspace and store reach the claim and findings a clean recomputation reaches, and its own documentation states why that is not the same property: recomputing everything and recomputing nothing both pass an unchanged comparison. So a regression that quietly re-materialized every fact on every run would leave every existing test green. The observable already exists and needs no new abstraction. MemoryFactStore::Materializations is public and counts actual store writes, incremented inside Materialize, and Already_Current short-circuits before that call so a reused subject does not increment it. Examined.facts is deliberately not that observable and must not be made into one: Materialize_Syntax counts a subject as covered whether it was reused or produced, and its own doc says so -- a caller reusing a store pays for a real parse only for a subject whose bytes moved but still counts that subject as covered either way. Asserting zero on Examined.facts would force the wrong semantics onto a counter that answers a different question.
items.done_when: A test drives the real Run twice over an unchanged tree with the same store and workspace, and asserts three things: the first run produced facts, so the fixture is not vacuous and a store that materialized nothing at all cannot pass; the second run produced none, measured as the delta in MemoryFactStore::Materializations across it rather than by any count of subjects covered; and the second run's findings and claim equal the first's, so economy was not bought by answering a different question. Examined and its facts field are untouched and keep meaning subjects covered. The test is proved capable of failing rather than believed because it passes, by making the second run produce a fact and observing the assertion fire. cargo test -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-contract-tests passes and the gate lint step is clean.

items.title: The surface OD-RULES-009 watched for growth no longer exists, and the masking that hid a defect is worth a heuristic
items.why: OD-RULES-009 has declined the shared analysis planner across eight rounds and is at version 7. Its own closing sentence names what would make it revisit: participation varying by a second axis, or a diverging rule population resuming growth of the hand-written materialization surface past the point it stops absorbing cleanly. P102 removed that surface rather than growing it. Materialization now derives its demand from the union of RuleDescriptor.requires over the selected rules, the per-family hand-written guards are gone, and the record is entitled to know that the thing it was watching is no longer there. The evidence that a planner would now be speculative is measurable rather than argued: no duplicate rule-to-fact authority remains, since gate-orchestration's Registered already reads DESCRIPTORS and is pinned against Composed_Rules; no ordering between fact families exists to schedule; provider choice is one resolution per requirement with nothing to sequence; nothing needs a cache-aware decision, and the derivation deliberately reads no store state; Spread_Collecting_Reached has no consumer outside nomos-analysis; and Judged_Sources is orchestration-owned by a recorded decision rather than duplicated normative data. Separately, the defect P102 found is worth a heuristic rather than only a fix. NESTING_DEPTH declared LimitsPolicy, no guard named it, and a full run hid that completely because five sibling rules forced the fact into existence anyway. Full-suite success was not evidence about selective execution, and the same masking is available wherever a shared dependency has several consumers -- gates, phases, workflows, provider fallbacks, correction validation.
items.done_when: OD-RULES-009 carries an amendment recording that the hand-written materialization surface its last round named as the thing to watch has been removed rather than grown, what replaced it, and the specific measurements that make a planner speculative today rather than merely unbuilt. It states the decline as still standing and names what would change it, without restating triggers earlier rounds already found unfired. OD-GATE-028 carries an amendment recording the masking shape as a member of the class it already names: a full population exercising a shared dependency can make a narrowed consumer's dependence on it unobservable, so a green suite proves less than it appears. It states the heuristic as three populations -- the full one, the smallest consumer, and a neighbouring one that does not require the dependency -- names NESTING_DEPTH as the case that produced it, and is explicit that this needs no framework and is the ordinary shape of a negative control. Both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly these records, and cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: A temporary waiver claims a bounded period and nothing can make it stop applying
items.why: SuppressionDisposition::TemporaryWaiver documents itself as accepted for a bounded period, expected to be revisited, and distinguishes itself from AcceptedBaselineDebt as the one which names an end date this does not. No end date exists. Suppression carries rule, subject, disposition, rationale and owner and nothing else, and no file under policy/ reads a clock, a deadline or an expiry. So a TemporaryWaiver is behaviourally identical to a FormalRiskAcceptance: it suppresses forever. This is worse than a missing feature. The type name and its documentation promise a behaviour the engine does not implement, so a repository that tolerates something temporarily has in fact tolerated it permanently and has been told otherwise, which is the hiding half of the adoption question a gate exists to answer. The declared file refuses an expires key today under deny_unknown_fields, so an author reaching for one is told no rather than silently dropped -- honest, and evidence the key has been wanted. baseline_debt.rs already records the order this should follow: the key appears on the declared entry first, and the domain type grows a field to carry it.
items.done_when: A TemporaryWaiver expires. Suppression carries an expiry, the declared entry in nomos-gate.json accepts it, and a waiver without one is refused rather than accepted as permanent -- the disposition whose meaning requires an end date cannot be written without it. A disposition whose contract does not call for an end date is refused one rather than silently carrying an ignored field. Evaluation reads a time the caller supplies rather than an ambient clock read inside policy logic, so a run judged against a past moment answers as that moment and a replay is not a function of today's date; the time arrives by the same route a run's other execution facts already do rather than through a new parameter that would push Run_Gate past this workspace's own parameter-count rule. A waiver before its expiry suppresses, a waiver at or after it does not, and the second case is visible as an expired waiver rather than as a suppression that silently stopped matching -- a reader must be able to tell a finding that is blocking because a waiver lapsed from one that was never waived. The status is an enum rather than a boolean, and its documentation says what a third state would mean and why it is not invented before something produces it. Controls in both directions and at the boundary: before, at, and after the expiry instant. cargo test -p nomos-gate-orchestration -p nomos-cli -p nomos-api -p nomos-contract-tests passes, the public surface snapshot is updated in the same commit, and the gate lint step is clean.

Declined.reason: Superseded by P103-A-TEMPORARY-WAIVER-CLAIMS-A-BOUNDED-PERIOD-AND-NEVER-ENDS-2, which reserves the status module alongside the files it is exported from.

abandoned.reason: Under-scoped territory. The status taxonomy needs its own module: this workspace's file-name rule reports a file with more than one top-level public type, suppression_disposition.rs and suppression.rs each declare exactly one and export no free function, so neither can host a second type the way gate_compare.rs can. The new sibling file is not reserved.

items.title: Refresh the v14 corpus block lineage against the volumes cace351ac produced, then re-measure the figures this workspace pins
items.why: Successor to P96-THE-LIVE-V14-CORPUS-HAS-DIVERGED-FROM-THE-ARCHIVE-ITS-FIGURES-ARE-PINNED-FROM, declined 2026-09-14 for territory that could not hold it: it reserved two files and the eight failures live in five. The owner chose the resolution P96's done_when listed third, refreshing source-block-lineage.yaml, over cutting a v14.37 archive (66 files here name v14.36 or DEFAULT_REVISION) and over reverting the live tree (cace351ac resolved four architecture drifts found by a spec review, and discarding it would make the corpus less correct to quiet a harness). One cause, measured: cace351ac on 2026-08-17 edited five of ten domain volumes, 31 insertions against 21 deletions. Its volume 02 diff splits the Indexer and Identity Service table row into three and the Contract Discovery and Calibration Service heading into two, taking that document from the 202 blocks source-block-lineage.yaml records to the 204 segmentation produces, so every ordinal after the insertion shifts and 494 recorded content hashes stop matching. source-block-lineage.yaml is untouched since 2026-08-06; the volumes moved on 08-17. Nothing downstream was refreshed. The mechanism this needs does not exist yet, which is why the item is a capability and not a correction. The lineage's authored fields are disposition, authority, target_volumes and stable_ids; its mechanical ones are block_ordinal, heading_path, block_kind, content_hash and normalized_hash. Only a segmenter that agrees with nomos can produce hashes Test_I1 accepts, and the corpus's own validate_bundle.py is not one: its editorial_source_errors checks only that an entry HAS a disposition, HAS both hashes and HAS a target volume, never recomputing or comparing them, which is exactly why it reports ok while nomos reports 494 mismatches. Those are two different measurements and neither is evidence about the other. No nomos verb emits block lineage either, so the recomputed hashes have no way out of this workspace today.
items.done_when: A mechanism in this workspace emits, for the live corpus, every block's document, ordinal, heading_path, block_kind, content_hash and normalized_hash as the same segmentation Test_I1 judges against produces them -- the same segmenter, not a second implementation of it, because a reimplementation that disagreed would be a second authority for what a block is. Its first and only consumer is the corpus refresh, so it is test-gated in real_corpus.rs rather than given a spec verb ahead of a second caller. source-block-lineage.yaml is then refreshed in the code-standards repository from that emission, preserving every authored field where a block still exists and authoring disposition, authority, target_volumes and stable_ids for each genuinely new block; the corpus's own policy content_hash_change_requires_manifest_refresh_and_review is satisfied by the owner reviewing the refresh, which is recorded in the corpus commit rather than assumed here.
