items.title: A whole-crate verification predicate inherits unrelated corpus-gated obligations, and one item was verified around that rather than by it
items.why: Recorded as a candidate rather than acted on, because one instance is not yet a pattern. P99-THREE-RECORDS-REPEAT-A-BARE-CHECKED-ON-LINE declared the predicate cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-spec-validate -p nomos-spec-store, and its acceptance criterion was one thing: that Test_A_Seeded_Store_Should_Pass_Preservation_Non_Vacuously stops reporting a violation with the corpus present. Run with the corpus exported, that predicate failed -- on Test_The_Domain_Volumes_Should_Answer_282_258_And_234, which counts pipe lines in a directory outside this repository and read 286 against a pinned 282. That is the divergence P96 named and P102 now carries, and nothing in the commit could move it. So work finish ran in the default corpus-unset environment where the predicate passes, and the corpus-set obligation the done_when stated was discharged by hand. Both halves were honest and the commit says so, but the ledger's machine-recorded verification does not itself prove the corpus-set run, and that gap is the defect worth naming: a predicate naming a crate inherits every conditional obligation that lives in it, including ones whose truth drifts for reasons the item never touches. The narrower rule this suggests is that a predicate should execute the smallest command directly proving its own done_when, plus any specifically required surrounding regression check, rather than inheriting unrelated obligations by crate membership. It is deliberately NOT that a corpus-gated crate should always be addressed by --test: a whole-crate predicate is right when the item's claim really is that the crate remains valid, and the distinction is driven by done_when scope rather than by where a test happens to live.
items.done_when: Decided after P102-THE-V14-BLOCK-LINEAGE-IS-REFRESHED-AT-ITS-SOURCE finishes, not before, because that item is expected to make these whole-crate predicates clean again and the answer depends on what happens then. If another item's predicate fails for an unrelated corpus obligation after the v14 divergence is resolved, that is a second instance and enough evidence to state the narrower rule as a convention -- where it belongs, whether a record or a line in the work skill, and what it says about items whose claim genuinely is whole-crate validity. If no second instance appears, this declines with that as its reason: one occurrence caused by a single outstanding corpus divergence is a stale invariant rather than a structural defect in how predicates are declared, and a convention written from one case would be the speculative surface this workspace refuses elsewhere. Either way the outcome is recorded, so the next session finds the measurement rather than re-deriving it from the same symptom.

Declined.reason: Stranded by the decline of P102-THE-V14-BLOCK-LINEAGE-IS-REFRESHED-AT-ITS-SOURCE, which it named as a dependency. The dependency was right and only its name is stale: the question is still whether a whole-crate predicate inheriting unrelated corpus obligations is a structural defect or one stale invariant, and it still cannot be answered until the v14 divergence is fully closed. Re-authored as P103-A-LEDGER-PREDICATE-INHERITS-CORPUS-OBLIGATIONS-FROM-THE-CRATE-IT-NAMES depending on P103-THE-REGISTER-FIGURES-THE-LINEAGE-REFRESH-MOVED-ARE-RE-MEASURED instead, unchanged otherwise.

items.title: The architecture the dependency rules judge is 66 compiled-in nomos crate names, so the family cannot judge any other repository
items.why:
Five policy families already take their criterion from a declared fact under OD-RULES-011, and tests/integration/fixtures/third-party/hex-0.4.3/standards.json already declares its own naming policy for the same rules to judge. The architecture family is the exception. Check_Dependency_Direction, Check_Every_Member_Declares_A_Band and Check_Write_Authority resolve every package through Zone_Of, and ZONES is a literal of 66 entries every one of which is a nomos crate name. The dependency edges are provider-derived and generalize; the architecture they are judged against is source code in nomos-rules. In any other repository Zone_Of returns None and the family reports NotApplicable, which is honest and is also the whole family declining for every repository that is not this one. OD-RULES-024 named this as a fact this workspace does not yet produce; the missing fact is a declared architecture, not an inference engine.

OD-RULES-029 already settled two things this item must not re-decide. The declaration is read from the repository under check, per OD-RULES-003. And it is not an OD-RULES-011 sixth family, because what travels is a triple -- a finite set of named components, an order over them, and named exceptions the order alone cannot express -- so a membership map shipped without its lattice and its vocabulary externalizes nothing. That record also settled where it is not authored: the tiers array in standards.json is another tool's declared input, which this repository holds and does not own.

Version -3 of this item was declined after its territory was measured rather than estimated. The readers of the surface being removed are fourteen files beyond what -3 reserved, and two of them are why this item cannot be scoped to the check run: admissibility.rs in nomos-gate-orchestration and walk_outward/architectural_component.rs in nomos-lsp both call Zone_Of and Permits with no FactReader anywhere between them. OD-GATE-026 anticipated exactly that, saying the question admissibility asks is the same either way and that what this migration changes is where those two functions get their answer -- which makes it a thing this item has to decide, not a consequence it can leave to fall out.
items.done_when:
The acceptance test is the direction of dependency between rule mechanism and project description, not the representation chosen. Concretely: if the repository-specific description changes completely while the governing rule concept stays the same, the rules crate is unchanged. A relocated table whose schema and interpretation the rules crate still owns does not satisfy this even though it looks data-driven, and neither does moving the membership map while the category vocabulary stays a closed enum in nomos-rules: a repository dividing its architecture into Domain, Infrastructure and Api must not have to edit nomos-rules to say so. Which mechanism carries the description is the implementer's to determine from what already exists -- a capability payload, a repository manifest, or another existing contract -- and a new mechanism is not required; what it carries is the whole triple OD-RULES-029 names, not one third of it.

Then: no nomos crate name and no nomos-specific architectural category remains compiled into nomos-rules, and deleting every such name does not reduce this workspace's ability to enforce its own architecture, because this workspace now declares what the ZONES table, the Zone enum, SAME_ZONE_EDGES, Permits and WRITE_DOORS between them encoded. A name that is in today's ZONES table, with its declaration removed, resolves to unresolved rather than to its legacy zone: that is the query where a correct implementation and a surviving compiled-in fallback must disagree, and confirming the cases that already pass is not evidence about it.

The same three rule implementations, unchanged in what they judge, enforce a foreign declaration with a different package vocabulary and different category names, proved against the hex-0.4.3 third-party fixture. The two consumers outside the check run each reach the declaration through the same seam the rules do rather than through a second copy: nomos gate admits answers from the declared architecture, and the LSP architectural component resolves from it, with no path anywhere still short-circuiting to a hardcoded classification.

A repository declaring no architecture still reports NotApplicable rather than passing clean, and an incomplete or unparseable declaration reports a refusal or an applicability state rather than silently dropping the checks. OD-RULES-024 is amended to say the fact now exists and what it is, and both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly that record.

This item does not design an ownership, required-mechanism or general engineering-model schema, and does not decide what a declared component with no observed implementation means.

Declined.reason: Territory measured one indirection short. -4's set was built by grepping every reader of the symbols being removed, which found admissibility.rs and walk_outward/architectural_component.rs. A signature change does not stop at the symbol: ArchitecturalComponent::Of gains the declaration, so WalkOutward::Of does, so file_diagnostic.rs's Diagnostics_For does, so nomos_diagnostic_provider.rs and nomos-lsp's own tests/fixture_tree.rs do. Re-authored as -5 with those three added and with the LSP threading stated as a signature change and nothing more, before any claim rather than widened mid-claim.

abandoned.reason: Claimed to implement, traced the caller chain of the signature change before editing anything, and three nomos-lsp files it reaches are outside the reserved set. Abandoning so it can be declined and re-authored rather than widened mid-claim.

items.title: A temporary waiver claims a bounded period and nothing can make it stop applying
items.why: SuppressionDisposition::TemporaryWaiver documents itself as accepted for a bounded period, expected to be revisited, and distinguishes itself from AcceptedBaselineDebt as the one which names an end date this does not. No end date exists. Suppression carries rule, subject, disposition, rationale and owner and nothing else, and no file under policy/ reads a clock, a deadline or an expiry. So a TemporaryWaiver is behaviourally identical to a FormalRiskAcceptance: it suppresses forever. This is worse than a missing feature, because the type name and its documentation promise a behaviour the engine does not implement, so a repository that tolerated something temporarily has tolerated it permanently and was told otherwise. That is the hiding half of the adoption question a gate exists to answer. The declared file refuses an expires key today under deny_unknown_fields, so an author reaching for one is told no rather than silently dropped, which is honest and is evidence the key has been wanted. baseline_debt.rs already records the order this should follow: the key appears on the declared entry first, and the domain type grows a field to carry it.
items.done_when: A TemporaryWaiver expires. Suppression carries an expiry, the declared entry in nomos-gate.json accepts it, and a waiver written without one is refused rather than accepted as permanent, so the disposition whose meaning requires an end date cannot be authored without it. A disposition whose contract does not call for an end date is refused one rather than silently carrying a field nothing reads. Evaluation reads a time the caller supplies rather than an ambient clock read inside policy logic, so a run judged against a past moment answers as that moment and a replay is not a function of today's date; the time arrives through the value a run's other execution facts already travel in rather than a new parameter that would push the composing function past this workspace's own parameter-count rule. A waiver before its expiry suppresses, a waiver at or after it does not, and the second is visible as an expired waiver rather than as a suppression that quietly stopped matching, because a reader must be able to tell a finding blocking from a lapsed waiver from one never waived. The status is an enum in its own module, since the file-name rule reports a second public type in a file exporting no free function, and its documentation says what a third state would mean and why it is not invented before something produces it. Controls in both directions and at the boundary instant: before, exactly at, and after. cargo test -p nomos-gate-orchestration -p nomos-cli -p nomos-api -p nomos-contract-tests passes, the public surface snapshot is updated in the same commit, and the gate lint step is clean.

Declined.reason: Superseded by -3, which reserves every GateEnvironment construction site rather than the six a truncated grep showed.

abandoned.reason: Territory short by three GateEnvironment construction sites. The population was enumerated with a truncating head and the truncated list was treated as complete: nomos-gate-orchestration's own tests.rs and tests/check_orchestration_seam.rs, and nomos-workflow-orchestration's run.rs, all construct GateEnvironment and all need the new field. Re-added with the full population.

items.title: The security rules decide what is test material from an eight-clause hardcoded path convention, so a repository that files fixtures elsewhere gets false credential findings
items.why: Auditing all 42 SourceText rules for repository-specific criteria found exactly one family. Is_Test_Or_Fixture_Source in security_text.rs matches tests/, /tests/, /test/, /testdata/, /fixtures/, /examples/, _test.rs, _tests.rs and _test.go, and the three security rules all exempt a source on that basis; rust_text.rs carries the same notion independently in its unwrap-outside-tests-and-examples wording. Some clauses are toolchain-fixed and portable: Cargo owns tests/ and examples/, Go owns _test.go. testdata and fixtures are neither, they are a project convention. A repository filing its fixtures under resources or spec or samples is judged as if a fixture credential were a real one, and an exemption that is too narrow produces false positives rather than misses, which is the damaging direction for a security rule.
items.done_when: What counts as test material reaches the security rules as a declared criterion rather than a path list compiled into security_text.rs, composed from the toolchain-fixed clauses plus whatever the repository declares, so that stable Cargo and Go semantics do not become configuration. It uses whichever declaration path P100-...-4 establishes rather than inventing a second one. A repository declaring nothing keeps today behaviour. A repository declaring its own fixture locations has them exempted, proved against a fixture whose test material sits under none of the nine current clauses. rust_text.rs stops carrying a second independent notion of the same thing.

items.title: OD-CAPABILITY-013 defers a closed item on a false count, and names a trigger the record it points at does not have
items.why:
OD-CAPABILITY-013's "What This Record Does Not Do" defers P54-A-REPOSITORY-CANNOT-CHOOSE-ITS-TOOLS on a factual premise: Selection "does not exist yet because no capability has more than one admitted provider." Measured 2026-09-14 against the real tree, the paragraph is stale three times over, and version -1 of this item was declined because it carried two of the three staleness claims the wrong way round.

First, the count is false, which is what -1 said and is right. Declare_Syntax_Capability in crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/src/composition.rs declares nomos.cap.syntax.items and then offers three providers against it: nomos.lang.rust.syn, nomos.lang.rust.scan and nomos.lang.go.tree-sitter. It has had more than one since nomos-lang-rust-scan was composed in.

Second, the guarantees are not what -1 stated. It said nomos-lang-rust declares FactVariant::SemanticallyResolved with completeness Assurance::Unknown. Read directly at crates/languages/nomos-lang-rust/src/guarantee.rs, it declares Syntactic, soundness Sound, completeness Unknown, IncrementalGranularity::File. SemanticallyResolved appears in that file as what a future compiler-backed provider would offer, and that provider is not composed into the production registry at all. nomos-lang-rust-scan declares Approximate, Unsound, Unknown, File.

Third, and the reason -1 could not be implemented as written: P54-A-REPOSITORY-CANNOT-CHOOSE-ITS-TOOLS is Done on this board, verified 2026-09-05, and its product is OD-HOST-009, which cites OD-CAPABILITY-013 as a relation. items.title: A temporary waiver claims a bounded period and nothing can make it stop applying
items.why: SuppressionDisposition::TemporaryWaiver documents itself as accepted for a bounded period and distinguishes itself from AcceptedBaselineDebt as the one which names an end date this does not. No end date exists: Suppression carries rule, subject, disposition, rationale and owner, and no file under policy/ reads a clock, a deadline or an expiry. So a TemporaryWaiver is behaviourally identical to a FormalRiskAcceptance and suppresses forever. That is worse than a missing feature, because the type name and its documentation promise a behaviour the engine does not implement, so a repository that tolerated something temporarily has tolerated it permanently and was told otherwise. The declared file refuses an expires key today under deny_unknown_fields, so an author reaching for one is told no rather than silently dropped, and baseline_debt.rs already records the order to follow: the key appears on the declared entry first and the domain type grows a field to carry it. The evaluation moment must come from the caller rather than a clock inside policy logic, so replaying a past run answers as that run did; it rides in the two grouping values a run's execution context already travels in, GateEnvironment for a gate and Platform for a workflow step, because both composing functions are at this workspace's four-parameter limit. The constructor and call-site population was enumerated in full across both affected types after earlier attempts were re-scoped, the first from output truncated by head.
items.done_when: A TemporaryWaiver expires. Suppression carries an expiry, the declared entry accepts it, a waiver written without one is refused rather than accepted as permanent, and any other disposition carrying one is refused rather than silently ignoring it. Evaluation reads the moment the caller supplied and every construction site of both grouping values supplies one. A waiver before its expiry suppresses, at or after it does not, and the second is visible as a lapsed disposition rather than a suppression that quietly stopped matching. The status is an enum in its own module, since the file-name rule reports a second public type in a file exporting no free function, and carries only the two states something can construct -- a third, for a disposition stale by rule version, subject identity, evidence or scope, is named in its documentation and deliberately not invented before an invalidation mechanism exists. Controls in both directions and at the boundary instant: before, exactly at, and after. The predicate is cargo test over the three crates whose behaviour this changes, which is where every claim above lives. Two further facts are established outside it and stated in the finish evidence rather than smuggled into a green: both public surface snapshots are re-blessed and the public_surface guard passes, and nomos-cli is modified only at two construction sites, compiles, and passes its other tests -- two real-tree population assertions there are red at HEAD for pre-existing causes this item introduces no claim about, and the repository-wide gate remains the separate stronger check. Lint over the workspace is clean.

items.title: Build the per-rule empty-population report OD-ANALYSIS-012 accepted and deliberately left unbuilt
items.why:
OD-ANALYSIS-012 is accepted at version 1 and its Status section states the answer completely: an empty population is a per-rule fact reported in CheckOutcome::Judged itself, Advisory and Claim-flipping the same way ProviderUnavailable already is, computed from population sizes run_context.rs already holds. Its own What This Record Does Not Do section says no code moves there and names the new field, the count computed in run_context.rs and Claim_Of's extension precisely enough for a follow-up item. That follow-up did not exist. The decision is governing and the mechanism is absent, which is the gap between a record and a build rather than a question needing another record.

The present instance is real and named by the record: the four rules P43-SCRIPT-RULES-CANNOT-FIRE measured all report an empty population in this tree today, and a reader cannot tell any of them apart from a rule that judged a real population and found it clean. Note what is already built and is not this: crates/host/nomos-cli/src/vacuity.rs satisfies OD-GATE-003 and guards the exit code main.rs produces when a whole group saw no subject at all. That is a per-run guarantee at the CLI boundary. This item is the per-rule fact inside a run that did see subjects, which vacuity.rs's own "What this does not cover" section puts outside itself.

Version -1 of this item reserved five paths and forbade any host renderer from changing, saying in as many words that discovering one must change means the territory was wrong and the item is declined and re-authored. Three do, and the cause is Rust rather than design: CheckOutcome::Judged is a struct variant, and a pattern that binds all of its fields without a rest pattern stops compiling the moment a field is added. Grepped 2026-09-14, four sites bind all three fields and four more construct the variant, and none of the eight is a rendering decision: nomos-api's check.rs converts the outcome into a response, nomos-cli's check/report.rs dispatches to Report_Findings, nomos-gate-orchestration's gate_environment.rs destructures and reconstructs it to narrow findings by scope, nomos-cli's gate/report.rs builds four fixtures, and tests/integration's calibration.rs destructures one. What each of them needs is a rest pattern or one more field value. That is mechanical, it is not a renderer change in any sense the -1 wording was protecting against, and it cannot be avoided by any placement of the field the record permits.

Two things -1 got wrong beyond the count. It required Claim_Of itself to read the new fact. Claim_Of is public, and nomos-gate-orchestration's Reduced_With_Coverage calls it over the gate's own rule-and-scope-selected findings under OD-GATE-016 -- a narrowed set that carries no population information at all. Extending that signature would force a decision about whether a gate run's coverage policy also fails on an empty population, which neither OD-ANALYSIS-012 nor OD-GATE-016 has made. And -1 named tests/contract/surface/nomos-check-orchestration.txt but not the three crates whose own compilation it breaks, so the item could not have been finished from inside what it reserved.
items.done_when:
CheckOutcome::Judged carries the per-rule empty-population fact OD-ANALYSIS-012 names, computed in run_context.rs from the population sizes it already holds at the point each rule is run, at no new materialization cost. The run's own claim is Incomplete whenever any composed rule examined an empty population, exactly as a coverage-debt finding already makes it Incomplete.

Whether that flip is expressed by extending Claim_Of or by a sibling beside it is the implementer's to determine, under one constraint: nomos-gate-orchestration's Reduced_With_Coverage must keep answering exactly what it answers today. It calls Claim_Of over the gate's own rule-and-scope-selected findings under OD-GATE-016, a set that carries no population information, and whether a gate run's coverage policy should also fail on an empty population is a decision neither OD-ANALYSIS-012 nor OD-GATE-016 has made. This item does not make it, and a gate run's disposition is unchanged by this item in every case.

Applicability is not touched and gains no variant, which OD-ANALYSIS-012 forbids by name: every existing variant presupposes a subject this fact does not have. No variant is added to Claim either; it stays a two-variant Copy enum rendered through Display, so the flip reaches a reader with no rendering change anywhere.

The eight sites that bind or build CheckOutcome::Judged are updated to keep compiling and to nothing more. No renderer decides differently, no response shape gains a field, and nothing new is printed or served: whether the identity of the rules that examined nothing should reach the CLI report or the API response is a separate item this one leaves open, since the claim flip is what OD-ANALYSIS-012 decided a reader is owed.

A test drives a rule over a deliberately empty population and asserts it is reported apart from a rule that judged a real population clean, and is confirmed able to fail by giving that rule a real population and observing the two stop differing. The four rules P43-SCRIPT-RULES-CANNOT-FIRE measured are checked against the built mechanism and the resulting count is stated in the commit.

tests/contract/surface/nomos-check-orchestration.txt is re-blessed from a clean worktree for the changed public surface, and any other surface snapshot the change moves is re-blessed with it. cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-gate-orchestration -p nomos-api -p nomos-cli -p nomos-contract-tests passes, and so does the workspace self-check.

items.title: A baseline entry is treated as a perpetual exemption for a rule and subject, and continuity is unprovable
items.why: BaselinePolicy matches a finding by rule and subject against a declared list, and a match cannot fail the build. Fixing the finding does not remove the entry, so the same violation returning at the same subject re-matches and is tolerated again, silently. The crate says so itself: no new-code, diff or identity detection distinguishes tolerated debt from a reintroduced or genuinely new finding. That makes a baseline entry behave as a perpetual exemption for a rule and subject pair, when what a repository meant by adopting it was that this occurrence existed when the baseline was taken. Those are different claims and the second is the useful one. Measured 2026-09-14, and the measurement reshapes the work rather than confirming it: continuity cannot be proven with what exists. Finding carries rule, subject, subject_name, applicability, evidence, gate, summary and locations, and no occurrence or snapshot identity. No baseline entry records the snapshot it was taken at. Nothing anywhere keeps a run history, which OD-GATE-022-A deliberately deferred until a real caller needed one. So a single run can see that a finding matches a baseline entry and cannot see whether it persisted since the baseline or was fixed and returned. Building a heuristic over line or diff age would be guessing at exactly the point the product is supposed to be truthful, and the owner's direction is explicit: do not guess persistent debt, and an uncertain continuity state should remain explicit.
items.done_when: A governing record decides what a baseline entry means and what a gate may claim about one. It states that an entry is evidence that an occurrence existed at a named snapshot rather than a standing exemption for a rule and subject pair, and that the two readings differ precisely when a finding is fixed and returns. It records the measurement that continuity is unprovable today -- no occurrence identity on a finding, no snapshot on an entry, no run history -- and decides what a run reports in that state: an explicitly undetermined continuity rather than a persistence claim nothing established, because reporting persistent debt for a finding that may have been reintroduced is the hiding failure a gate exists to prevent. It names what would make continuity provable, in the order the parts would arrive, and states that a line-age or diff heuristic is refused rather than unbuilt, with the reason. It decides nothing about scope by source geometry, which baseline_debt.rs already defers. The record is registered rather than only written, both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly it, and cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests passes.

items.title: Compare collapses six suppression reasons into one bucket, so a policy change reports as no change
items.why: SuppressionDisposition has six variants and P103 gave a waiver a status besides, but GateFindings is four Vec<Finding> and Compare_Gate_Runs derives a FindingDisposition purely from which bucket a finding sits in. So a finding whose suppression reason changed compares equal to itself. A FalsePositiveDisposition becoming a FormalRiskAcceptance is a substantial engineering change -- the first says the rule was wrong here, the second says somebody owns the risk -- and compare reports nothing at all. The same is now true of expiry: a TemporaryWaiver that lapses between two runs stays in the suppressed bucket until something else moves it, so the visibility P103 just built into the run model is lost again in historical comparison, which is where a reader looks to find out what changed. The reason is discarded at partition time: Reduced_Findings asks only whether Suppressing returned something and keeps the finding, not what matched it. Compare cannot recover it, and should not learn to -- it would become a second place that understands suppression evaluation, which is how two readings of one relation drift, the shape P102 already removed once between descriptors and materialization.
items.done_when: Two finding states compare equal only when both the gate treatment and the policy reason producing it are semantically equal. The run records why a suppressed finding is suppressed -- the disposition that matched and its status at the run's own moment -- so the reason travels in the run result rather than being re-derived; compare reads that value and names no suppression-evaluation type of its own. The four top-level buckets are unchanged, because they remain right for summary counts and multiplying them would make every count answer a different question. A bucket change still reports both ends, and a reason change within one bucket now reports as changed with both reasons. Four transitions are exercised: a disposition changing within Suppressed, a waiver going Active to Expired within Suppressed, an expired waiver leaving Suppressed for Blocking, and Baselined to Blocking. Both directions guarded: a finding whose bucket and reason are both unchanged still reports as unchanged, without which a comparison that reported everything would satisfy the first four and make compare useless. Every reason recorded corresponds to a suppressed finding and every suppressed finding has one, checked both ways so the two cannot drift. The predicate covers the crates whose behaviour this changes; affected public surface snapshots are re-blessed and the surface guard passes; workspace lint is clean.

Declined.reason: Superseded by -2, which reserves policy.rs so both the new type and the one P103 left unreachable are exported.

abandoned.reason: Territory missing the export chain. policy and suppression_disposition are both private modules, so policy.rs is the only route by which a new public type reaches the crate root, and it is not reserved. The same file also carries a defect P103 left: Suppression::Status_At returns SuppressionStatus and that type is not re-exported, so the surface shows a signature naming a type a caller cannot write.

The reason is discarded at partition time, since Reduced_Findings asks only whether Suppressing returned something. Compare cannot recover it and should not learn to, because re-deriving would answer with today's policy about an earlier run, and because a second evaluator is a second reading of one relation -- the shape P102 removed once between descriptors and materialization. One further defect, in the same export chain and so in the same change: Suppression::Status_At returns SuppressionStatus and policy.rs does not re-export it, so the public surface shows a signature naming a type no caller can write.
items.done_when: Two finding states compare equal only when both the gate treatment and the policy reason producing it are semantically equal. The run records why a suppressed finding is suppressed -- the disposition that matched and its status at the run's own moment -- so the reason travels in the run result rather than being re-derived, and compare reads that value while naming no suppression-evaluation type of its own. The four top-level buckets are unchanged, because they remain right for summary counts. A bucket change still reports both ends, and a reason change within one bucket now reports as changed with both reasons. Four transitions are exercised: a disposition changing within Suppressed, a waiver going Active to Expired within Suppressed, an expired waiver leaving Suppressed for Blocking, and Baselined to Blocking. Both directions guarded: a finding whose bucket and reason are both unchanged still reports unchanged, without which a comparison that reported everything would satisfy the first four and be useless. Every recorded reason corresponds to a suppressed finding and every suppressed finding has one, checked both ways so the two cannot drift. SuppressionStatus and the new reason type are both reachable from the crate root, so no public signature names a type a caller cannot write. The predicate covers the crates whose behaviour changes, both affected surface snapshots are re-blessed and the surface guard passes, and workspace lint is clean.

Declined.reason: Superseded by -3, same territory and work, with the recording invariant stated as it actually holds.

abandoned.reason: One done_when clause is falsified by the implementation it asked for. It required that every recorded reason correspond to a suppressed finding. Recording only suppressing dispositions leaves a finding that blocks because a waiver lapsed indistinguishable from one that blocks because a violation appeared, which is the distinction P103 made visible in the run model and which comparison is where a reader looks for. So lapsed reasons are recorded too, the recorded set is deliberately not the suppressed set, and the clause must say the invariant that actually holds.

items.title: All ten v14 volumes repeat the same front-matter, and the filler-template rule reads it as undeclared boilerplate
items.why: Split out of P102, whose done_when wrongly bundled this with the block-lineage refresh because one test invocation exposes both. Measured 2026-09-14 after the refresh landed: restoration.rs reports 16 violations over 2,988 subjects and siblings.rs reports 103 over 18,873, and the rule firing in both is no_undeclared_filler_template. The subjects are not lineage at all -- they are the volumes' shared front-matter, each reported as 10 section(s) across 10 document(s): the edition line Domain-owned edition v14.19, 4 August 2026; the suite title Nomos Focused Product Design and User Story Specification; the volume-ownership sentence This volume owns the domain material collected here; and the Word navigation note. The evidence that this is pre-existing and corpus-wide rather than anything the refresh caused is direct: those strings appear in all ten domain volumes including the five cace351ac never touched, restoration.rs moved only 18 to 16 across the refresh, and siblings.rs stayed at exactly 103. This is the same rule class that was closed twice by hand on this repository's own records in two days -- P95 for a bare Measured line and P99 for a bare Checked line -- but the subject is different in a way that matters: there the repeated text was filler a author could rewrite per record, and here it is a deliberate, identical publication header that ten volumes of one suite are supposed to share. A header that every volume of a suite carries is not the defect OD-SPEC-004 describes.
items.done_when: The question is decided and recorded: whether repeated publication front-matter across the volumes of one suite is an undeclared template the rule should refuse, or a declared shared header the corpus is entitled to carry and the rule should admit. The decision names which of the two it is for each of the four repeated strings the measurement found, since they are not obviously the same case -- an edition line and a Word navigation note may not deserve the same answer as a volume-ownership sentence. Whatever is decided, the mechanism follows from it rather than being chosen first: if the strings are legitimate the corpus declares them and the rule reads the declaration, and if they are filler the corpus rewrites them per volume the way P95 and P99 each did for three records. Nothing is re-pinned and no violation count is written into a test as an accepted number, because a count accepted without a decision is the suppression this rule exists to make visible. restoration.rs and siblings.rs are reserved because whichever way it goes their assertions are what proves it; the corpus-side act, if the decision calls for one, happens in code-standards and is recorded in that commit with the owner's review, the same division the lineage refresh used.

Declined.reason: Measured 2026-09-14 with both corpora exported, and the premise is wrong in three ways. FIRST, the population is not four strings. restoration reports 16 violations over the ten domain volumes, in three structurally different shapes: four suite-wide front-matter strings at 10 sections across 10 documents; eleven volume abstracts at 3 sections across 2 documents, which is the cover line, the Document purpose section and the suite index entry, three canonical places by publication convention; and one parity note repeated 10 times inside a single volume, once under each of ten capability tables. SECOND, the 103 siblings violations are not the same phenomenon at all, and the item asserts they are. Measured over 18,873 subjects: 102 of the 103 are 40 characters or fewer. The largest is three characters of horizontal rule repeated 562 times; the rest are ordinary connective fragments -- a single downward arrow repeated 9 times, Or, or:, So:, LLM, KWB, Add:, Use:, Bad:, Why?, Then:, Good:. Not one of them is front-matter and not one is a template. The defect there is that the rule has no minimum length before repetition is allowed to mean template, which is a different defect from repeated-by-design publication text and needs a different mechanism. Bundling them is the same defect that split this item out of P102. THIRD, the territory cannot carry any landing. The done_when requires the question be decided AND recorded, and reserves only the two test files while forbidding any count be written into them, so no file this item reserves may change. The decision is an amendment to OD-SPEC-004, which decided that repetition answers is this filler and is falsified by both measurements: OD-SPEC-004 calibrated that census on the ten v14.36 volumes at 13 sections out of 482 and its own record says so, and neither the 18,873-subject sibling corpus nor a three-place publication convention was in that calibration. An amendment needs the record and its registration reserved and this item reserves neither. Replaced by P103-REPETITION-IS-NOT-SUFFICIENT-EVIDENCE-OF-FILLER-AND-OD-SPEC-004-SAYS-IT-IS, which carries both measurements and amends the record; the two mechanisms follow from that decision rather than being chosen ahead of it.

abandoned.reason: Claimed and measured; the item's premise does not survive the measurement. Abandoned to decline it.

items.title: A whole-crate verification predicate inherits unrelated corpus-gated obligations, and one item was verified around that rather than by it
items.why: Re-authored from P102-A-LEDGER-PREDICATE-INHERITS-CORPUS-OBLIGATIONS, stranded when its dependency was declined; only the dependency's name changed. P99-THREE-RECORDS-REPEAT-A-BARE-CHECKED-ON-LINE declared the predicate cargo test -p nomos-spec-validate -p nomos-spec-store, and its acceptance criterion was one thing: that Test_A_Seeded_Store_Should_Pass_Preservation_Non_Vacuously stops reporting a violation with the corpus present. Run with the corpus exported that predicate failed, on Test_The_Domain_Volumes_Should_Answer_282_258_And_234, which counts pipe lines in a directory outside this repository and read 286 against a pinned 282. Nothing in that commit could move it. So work finish ran corpus-unset where the predicate passes, and the corpus-set obligation was discharged by hand. Both halves were honest and the commit says so, but the ledger's machine-recorded verification does not itself prove the corpus-set run, and that gap is the defect worth naming: a predicate naming a crate inherits every conditional obligation living in it, including ones whose truth drifts for reasons the item never touches. The narrower rule this suggests is that a predicate should execute the smallest command directly proving its own done_when plus any specifically required regression check, rather than inheriting obligations by crate membership. It is deliberately NOT that a corpus-gated crate should always be addressed by --test: a whole-crate predicate is right when the item's claim really is that the crate remains valid, and the distinction is driven by done_when scope rather than by where a test happens to live.
items.done_when: Decided after P103-THE-REGISTER-FIGURES-THE-LINEAGE-REFRESH-MOVED-ARE-RE-MEASURED finishes, not before, because that item is expected to make these whole-crate predicates clean again and the answer depends on what happens then. If another item's predicate fails for an unrelated corpus obligation after the v14 divergence is fully resolved, that is a second instance and enough evidence to state the narrower rule as a convention, naming where it belongs and what it says about items whose claim genuinely is whole-crate validity. If no second instance appears, this declines with that as its reason: one occurrence caused by a single outstanding corpus divergence is a stale invariant rather than a structural defect in how predicates are declared, and a convention written from one case would be the speculative surface this workspace refuses elsewhere. Either way the outcome is recorded, so the next session finds the measurement rather than re-deriving it from the same symptom.

Declined.reason: Framed too narrowly to be true of its own evidence. Its why and done_when both say corpus obligation, because the only instance when it was authored was a predicate naming nomos-spec-store while the live v14 corpus had diverged. A second instance on 2026-09-14 shows corpus is incidental: P103-THE-TASK-SKILL declared cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests, changed one markdown file, and could not finish because public_surface failed on a peer's unblessed snapshot while agent_harness -- the obligation that actually governs skill text, and the only one its done_when claimed -- was green. No corpus involved, same structural failure. Keeping the corpus wording would misdirect the next reader about what the defect is, and the item cannot be edited, so it is replaced rather than read as satisfied a fortiori. Re-authored as P103-A-LEDGER-PREDICATE-MUST-NOT-INHERIT-UNRELATED-CRATE-OBLIGATIONS carrying both incidents as the evidence that crossed the generalization threshold.

items.title: Compare collapses every finding a rule makes about one subject into one, losing 41 percent of them
items.why: Compare_Gate_Runs indexes a run's findings into a BTreeMap keyed by rule and subject, with insert. A rule emits one finding per occurrence -- rules push inside per-line loops and each finding carries a single location -- while the subject is the file, so a rule that finds five violations in one file emits five findings sharing one key and the map keeps the last. Measured against this repository's own tree on 2026-09-14: 253 findings emitted, 150 distinct rule-and-subject pairs, so 103 findings -- 41 percent -- are discarded before comparison begins. Thirty-seven keys hold more than one finding; lint-diagnostics on nomos-spec-project/src/project_error.rs holds fifteen and dependency-policy holds twenty-four. The consequences are false lifecycle claims in both directions. Fixing four of five violations in a file leaves one finding before and one after, so compare reports no change and an improvement is invisible. Going from one violation to five reports no change either, so a regression is invisible. added and removed are wrong by construction wherever a key holds more than one finding. Nothing acknowledges this: the only disjointness gate_compare documents is that a finding cannot fall into more than one bucket, which is true and about something else. This is the independent owner for occurrence identity that the baseline question could not supply on its own -- a shipped consumer that infers continuity from normative plus subject identity and makes false claims because of it.
items.done_when: Two findings a rule makes about one subject are two findings to compare, not one. Comparison identifies a finding by something that distinguishes occurrences rather than by rule and subject alone, so a run emitting five findings for one key compares as five. The identity is derived from what the finding says rather than from the run that produced it -- a run identity would make every rerun manufacture new occurrences and every finding read as added, which is worse than the collapse it replaces. Measured on this repository's own tree, the number of findings entering comparison equals the number emitted, and that equality is asserted rather than stated. Four behaviours are exercised: some-but-not-all occurrences fixed reports a removal, occurrences multiplying reports additions, an unchanged multi-occurrence subject reports no change, and a subject with exactly one finding behaves as it does today. Whether suppression and baseline matching keep their deliberate rule-and-subject scope is decided rather than changed by accident, since a suppression that stopped covering every occurrence of a rule in a file would be a silent policy narrowing. The predicate covers the crates whose behaviour changes and the gate lint step is clean.

Declined.reason: Re-scoped before claiming. Territory covered only gate_compare.rs, which cannot hold a new type in nomos-model, and the measurement since found an existing identity and lifecycle vocabulary there to align with rather than duplicate.

items.title: The architecture the dependency rules judge is 66 compiled-in nomos crate names, so the family cannot judge any other repository
items.why:
Five policy families already take their criterion from a declared fact under OD-RULES-011, and tests/integration/fixtures/third-party/hex-0.4.3/standards.json already declares its own naming policy for the same rules to judge. The architecture family is the exception. Check_Dependency_Direction, Check_Every_Member_Declares_A_Band and Check_Write_Authority resolve every package through Zone_Of, and ZONES is a literal of 66 entries every one of which is a nomos crate name. The dependency edges are provider-derived and generalize; the architecture they are judged against is source code in nomos-rules. In any other repository Zone_Of returns None and the family reports NotApplicable, which is honest and is also the whole family declining for every repository that is not this one. OD-RULES-024 named this as a fact this workspace does not yet produce; the missing fact is a declared architecture, not an inference engine.

OD-RULES-029 already settled two things this item must not re-decide. The declaration is read from the repository under check, per OD-RULES-003. And it is not an OD-RULES-011 sixth family, because what travels is a triple -- a finite set of named components, an order over them, and named exceptions the order alone cannot express -- so a membership map shipped without its lattice and its vocabulary externalizes nothing. That record also settled where it is not authored: the tiers array in standards.json is another tool's declared input, which this repository holds and does not own.

Version -3 of this item was declined after its territory was measured rather than estimated. The readers of the surface being removed are fourteen files beyond what -3 reserved, and two of them are why this item cannot be scoped to the check run: admissibility.rs in nomos-gate-orchestration and walk_outward/architectural_component.rs in nomos-lsp both call Zone_Of and Permits with no FactReader anywhere between them. OD-GATE-026 anticipated exactly that, saying the question admissibility asks is the same either way and that what this migration changes is where those two functions get their answer -- which makes it a thing this item has to decide, not a consequence it can leave to fall out.

Version -4 was declined for the same class of mistake one indirection out. Its territory was measured by grepping every reader of the symbols being removed -- Zone, ZONES, ZONE_LIST, SAME_ZONE_EDGES, WRITE_DOORS, Zone_Of and Permits -- which found admissibility.rs and walk_outward/architectural_component.rs and stopped there. A signature change does not stop at the symbol: ArchitecturalComponent::Of gains the declaration, so WalkOutward::Of does, so file_diagnostic.rs's Diagnostics_For does, so nomos_diagnostic_provider.rs and nomos-lsp's own tests/fixture_tree.rs do. None of those three names a zone symbol anywhere, which is exactly why the first grep could not see them. Territory for a signature change follows the caller chain, not the symbol. Measured 2026-09-14: three files, and the chain ends there -- NomosDiagnosticProvider::New takes no arguments and the declaration is read inside the method that already holds root and a FileSystem, so the provider's own tests are untouched.
items.done_when:
The acceptance test is the direction of dependency between rule mechanism and project description, not the representation chosen. Concretely: if the repository-specific description changes completely while the governing rule concept stays the same, the rules crate is unchanged. items.title: A policy violation cannot say what it is about, so twelve of them are one fact
items.why: PolicyViolation carries severity, code and message and nothing else. cargo-deny reports a graphs array naming the package each diagnostic concerns, and nomos-lang-rust-deny's parser reads severity, code and message and drops it. So twelve violations about twelve different crates normalize into twelve byte-identical facts. Measured on this repository's own tree 2026-09-14: 253 findings emitted, 242 distinct by rule, subject, summary and locations, and the single colliding fingerprint repeats twelve times -- dependency-policy reporting a git source not explicitly allowed, once per xvpe crate P103 pinned, with no location and no way to tell which. This blocks the occurrence identity P104 needs, and not as an inconvenience: once the distinction is gone from the fact, no downstream identity function can recover it without inventing one. Letting comparison collapse those twelve knowingly would bake an upstream information loss into the new canonical mechanism and weaken its invariant from every emitted occurrence has an identity to every occurrence has one unless a provider omitted enough, which is the kind of qualification consumers accommodate and nobody removes. The field to add is not a new vocabulary: nomos-cap-dependency's own DependencyEdge already names the crate an edge points at with a plain target: String, which is provider-neutral -- a package name is not a Cargo concept -- and sits at exactly this layer.
items.done_when: Two policy violations concerning different governed dependency subjects remain distinguishable after provider normalization. PolicyViolation carries the violation's own target, spelled the way nomos-cap-dependency's DependencyEdge already spells one, and optional because a violation such as an unencountered license genuinely concerns no package rather than concerning one the provider failed to record. The contract version is raised, since a payload gaining a field is a new agreement, and the schema states it. nomos-lang-rust-deny reads the target from cargo-deny's own graphs rather than inventing one, and a diagnostic carrying no graph yields no target rather than a placeholder. The rule carries the target into the finding as structured material -- subject or geometry as fits its meaning -- rather than appending it to the summary so a later hash happens to differ, because identity must follow the semantic representation and not presentation text. Measured against this repository's own tree, the twelve colliding findings become twelve distinguishable ones, and that count is asserted rather than described. cargo test over the capability, its provider and the rule passes; affected surface snapshots are re-blessed; the gate lint step is clean.

items.title: The architecture the dependency rules judge is 66 compiled-in nomos crate names, so the family cannot judge any other repository
items.why:
Five policy families already take their criterion from a declared fact under OD-RULES-011, and tests/integration/fixtures/third-party/hex-0.4.3/standards.json already declares its own naming policy for the same rules to judge. The architecture family is the exception. Check_Dependency_Direction, Check_Every_Member_Declares_A_Band and Check_Write_Authority resolve every package through Zone_Of, and ZONES is a literal of 66 entries every one of which is a nomos crate name. The dependency edges are provider-derived and generalize; the architecture they are judged against is source code in nomos-rules. In any other repository Zone_Of returns None and the family reports NotApplicable, which is honest and is also the whole family declining for every repository that is not this one. OD-RULES-024 named this as a fact this workspace does not yet produce; the missing fact is a declared architecture, not an inference engine.

OD-RULES-029 already settled two things this item must not re-decide. The declaration is read from the repository under check, per OD-RULES-003. And it is not an OD-RULES-011 sixth family, because what travels is a triple -- a finite set of named components, an order over them, and named exceptions the order alone cannot express -- so a membership map shipped without its lattice and its vocabulary externalizes nothing. That record also settled where it is not authored: the tiers array in standards.json is another tool's declared input, which this repository holds and does not own.

Version -3 of this item was declined after its territory was measured rather than estimated. The readers of the surface being removed are fourteen files beyond what -3 reserved, and two of them are why this item cannot be scoped to the check run: admissibility.rs in nomos-gate-orchestration and walk_outward/architectural_component.rs in nomos-lsp both call Zone_Of and Permits with no FactReader anywhere between them. OD-GATE-026 anticipated exactly that, saying the question admissibility asks is the same either way and that what this migration changes is where those two functions get their answer -- which makes it a thing this item has to decide, not a consequence it can leave to fall out.

Version -4 was declined for the same class of mistake one indirection out. Its territory was measured by grepping every reader of the symbols being removed -- Zone, ZONES, ZONE_LIST, SAME_ZONE_EDGES, WRITE_DOORS, Zone_Of and Permits -- which found admissibility.rs and walk_outward/architectural_component.rs and stopped there. A signature change does not stop at the symbol: ArchitecturalComponent::Of gains the declaration, so WalkOutward::Of does, so file_diagnostic.rs's Diagnostics_For does, so nomos_diagnostic_provider.rs and nomos-lsp's own tests/fixture_tree.rs do. None of those three names a zone symbol anywhere, which is exactly why the first grep could not see them. Territory for a signature change follows the caller chain, not the symbol. Measured 2026-09-14: three files, and the chain ends there -- NomosDiagnosticProvider::New takes no arguments and the declaration is read inside the method that already holds root and a FileSystem, so the provider's own tests are untouched.

Version -5 was declined on the carrier rather than on territory. standards.json is shared, and code-standards decodes it into one Limits struct with decoder.DisallowUnknownFields at kernel/config/limits/config_loading.go line 171. Checked field by field against the live checkout on 2026-09-14: every one of this repository's thirteen top-level keys is a field that struct names, and architecture is not. The five OD-RULES-011 families do not contradict that -- each reads a key code-standards already owns and decodes, so nomos piggybacks on that tool's schema rather than extending it, and a declared architecture has no such key to piggyback on. Cargo.toml's workspace.metadata table is the idiomatic Rust extension point and is wrong for a different reason: nomos judges Go repositories, and a declaration only a Cargo workspace could carry would make this family Rust-only, which fails this item's own property harder than the collision it avoids. So the carrier is a dedicated language-neutral file at the repository root, nomos-architecture.json, by the convention nomos-gate.json already set.

Version -6 was declined on one manifest, found by compiling the whole workspace with all targets once the migration was otherwise complete rather than by another round of estimating. Every other crate builds against it -- nomos-cli, nomos-api, nomos-lsp, the integration tests -- and the single remaining error is the contract tests importing a surface that no longer exists. That crate depends on neither nomos-cap-architecture nor nomos-repo-policy. Parsing the declaration there with serde_json, which it already has, would avoid the manifest and is the wrong answer: it would make the contract tests a second reader of a format this item exists to give one reader. Their independence is in asserting against cargo metadata, not in parsing the declaration a second way.
items.done_when:
The acceptance test is the direction of dependency between rule mechanism and project description, not the representation chosen. Concretely: if the repository-specific description changes completely while the governing rule concept stays the same, the rules crate is unchanged. A relocated table whose schema and interpretation the rules crate still owns does not satisfy this even though it looks data-driven, and neither does moving the membership map while the category vocabulary stays a closed enum in nomos-rules: a repository dividing its architecture into Domain, Infrastructure and Api must not have to edit nomos-rules to say so. The declaration is authored in nomos-architecture.json at the repository root and read by one provider, and the same file is what the foreign fixture declares in. It is not authored in standards.json, which another tool decodes with unknown fields disallowed, and not in a Cargo manifest, which would make the family Rust-only. What the carrier holds is the whole triple OD-RULES-029 names, not one third of it: the components themselves, the order over them, and the named exceptions that order cannot express, plus OD-RULES-023's write authorities.

Then: no nomos crate name and no nomos-specific architectural category remains compiled into nomos-rules, and deleting every such name does not reduce this workspace's ability to enforce its own architecture, because this workspace now declares what the ZONES table, the Zone enum, SAME_ZONE_EDGES, Permits and WRITE_DOORS between them encoded. A name that is in today's ZONES table, with its declaration removed, resolves to unresolved rather than to its legacy zone: that is the query where a correct implementation and a surviving compiled-in fallback must disagree, and confirming the cases that already pass is not evidence about it.

The same three rule implementations, unchanged in what they judge, enforce a foreign declaration with a different package vocabulary and different category names, proved against the hex-0.4.3 third-party fixture. The two consumers outside the check run each reach the declaration through the same seam the rules do rather than through a second copy: nomos gate admits answers from the declared architecture, and the LSP architectural component resolves from it, with no path anywhere still short-circuiting to a hardcoded classification. Threading it to the LSP is a signature change and nothing more -- no renderer decides differently, no diagnostic gains or loses a field, and the declaration is read where a root and a FileSystem are already held rather than from ambient state, which OD-HOST-001 reserves to a composition root.

A repository declaring no architecture still reports NotApplicable rather than passing clean, and an incomplete or unparseable declaration reports a refusal or an applicability state rather than silently dropping the checks. OD-RULES-024 is amended to say the fact now exists and what it is, and both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly that record.

This item does not design an ownership, required-mechanism or general engineering-model schema, and does not decide what a declared component with no observed implementation means.

Declined.reason: OD-GATE-026 made admits the one gate verb with no --root, because a crate pair needed no tree while the architecture was compiled into nomos-rules. Once the architecture is the repository's own declaration that premise is gone, and three unreserved files in nomos-cli state it as a present fact: invocation.rs, parsing.rs's own user-facing usage text, and tests.rs, which asserts it by chdir-ing to the platform temporary directory and requiring a permitted answer from a directory that is not a repository. Outside a repository there is no architecture to answer from and NotJudged is honest. Re-authored as -8 with those three. OD-GATE-026 needs no amendment, checked rather than assumed: that sentence is in its What Was Measured section, dated context by construction, and its Decision and Status say nothing about disk.

abandoned.reason: Migration complete and the whole workspace green but for three nomos-cli files that assert a premise the migration invalidates. Abandoning to re-author with them.

items.title: The security rules decide what is test material from an eight-clause hardcoded path convention, so a repository that files fixtures elsewhere gets false credential findings
items.why: Auditing all 42 SourceText rules for repository-specific criteria found exactly one family. Is_Test_Or_Fixture_Source in security_text.rs matches tests/, /tests/, /test/, /testdata/, /fixtures/, /examples/, _test.rs, _tests.rs and _test.go, and the three security rules all exempt a source on that basis; rust_text.rs carries the same notion independently in its unwrap-outside-tests-and-examples wording. Some clauses are toolchain-fixed and portable: Cargo owns tests/ and examples/, Go owns _test.go. testdata and fixtures are neither, they are a project convention. A repository filing its fixtures under resources or spec or samples is judged as if a fixture credential were a real one, and an exemption that is too narrow produces false positives rather than misses, which is the damaging direction for a security rule.
items.done_when: What counts as test material reaches the security rules as a declared criterion rather than a path list compiled into security_text.rs, composed from the toolchain-fixed clauses plus whatever the repository declares, so that stable Cargo and Go semantics do not become configuration. It uses whichever declaration path P100-...-7 establishes rather than inventing a second one. A repository declaring nothing keeps today behaviour. A repository declaring its own fixture locations has them exempted, proved against a fixture whose test material sits under none of the nine current clauses. rust_text.rs stops carrying a second independent notion of the same thing.

Declined.reason:
Mechanically unreachable board debt, not a judgment about the work. This item depends on P100-THE-ARCHITECTURE-A-RULE-JUDGES-IS-COMPILED-INTO-THE-RULE-CRATE-INSTEAD-OF-DECLARED-BY-THE-REPOSITORY-7, which is Declined and can never become Done, so work audit reports it stranded and no retry resolves it.

The subject survived that decline. The dependency was re-authored as -8 with three more files and -8 is Done, so the declaration path this item's done_when defers to now exists and is authored in nomos-architecture.json at the repository root. The premise did not die with the dependency; only the edge is stale.

Re-authored as -7 with the dependency retargeted to -8. Why, territory, predicate and timeout are read off this item and carried forward unchanged. One word of the done_when changes: it abbreviated its dependency as P100-...-7, which now names a declined item, and reads P100-...-8.

Flagged rather than repaired, because widening another author's item is a judgment about their work and this is an edge repair. The territory is two files in nomos-rules, and the done_when requires what counts as test material to reach the rules as a declared criterion using whichever path the dependency established. That path is read in crates/repository/nomos-repo-policy/src/architecture/reading.rs and fact_context.rs and materialized in crates/orchestration/nomos-check-orchestration/src/facts/policy_materialization.rs, none of which is reserved. Measured 2026-09-14 by grep, not by running the change, so it is a prediction and not a finding. Whoever claims -7 should measure the cone before editing and expect to re-author if it escapes.

items.title: Compare collapses every finding a rule makes about one subject into one, losing 41 percent of them
items.why: Compare_Gate_Runs indexes a run's findings into a BTreeMap keyed by rule and subject, with insert. A rule emits one finding per occurrence -- rules push inside per-line loops, each finding carrying a single location -- while the subject is the file, so a rule finding five violations in one file emits five findings sharing one key and the map keeps the last. Measured 2026-09-14 before P104a: 253 findings emitted, 150 distinct rule-and-subject pairs, 103 discarded before comparison began, thirty-seven keys holding more than one. The consequences are false lifecycle claims both ways: fixing four of five violations in a file leaves one finding before and one after and reports no change, and going from one to five reports no change either. Nothing acknowledged it -- the only disjointness gate_compare documents is that a finding cannot fall into two buckets, which is true and about something else. P104a closed the upstream information loss that would have forced this fix to ship with a known exception, and the tree now measures 256 findings to 256 distinct fingerprints over rule, subject, summary and locations. A correction to an earlier measurement belongs in this item's own record: the lifecycle vocabulary is not absent, it is spelled differently. nomos-model's identity module already declares IdentityTransitionKind with ExactContinuity, ProbableMove, SignatureEvolution, SplitInto, MergedFrom, Recreated and Unresolved, and a CompositeIdentity carrying a StructuralFingerprint. All of it has zero consumers outside that crate, so it constrains nothing mechanically, but it is this repository's considered design and CompositeIdentity's own doc already rejects path and line as identity for the reason that matters here.
items.done_when: Two findings a rule makes about one subject are two findings to compare. A finding occurrence identity is derived in nomos-model as a projection over a Finding rather than a field stored on one, so no construction site changes, and it is built from rule, subject, summary and locations -- what identifies which violation instance occurred -- and from nothing describing its treatment, so applicability, gate category and any policy standing are excluded by construction. The cardinality is checked per run result before any comparison begins: a run whose findings do not yield as many distinct identities produces a typed failure naming both colliding findings, and BTreeMap::insert is never the mechanism that discovers a collision. Comparison then keys by that identity -- present in both compares standing and reason, present only before is removed, present only after is added -- with no silent overwrite. Measured on this repository's own tree, the number of findings entering comparison equals the number emitted, asserted rather than described. Four behaviours are exercised: some-but-not-all occurrences fixed reports removals, occurrences multiplying reports additions, an unchanged multi-occurrence subject reports no change, and a single-finding subject behaves as it does today. Suppression and baseline keep their rule-and-subject addressing, asserted so occurrence identity cannot narrow them by accident. The public protocol is not widened for an internal key: the identity is exposed only where a caller must already see it. The documentation states the injectivity claim narrowly -- injective over the currently representable Finding model, and a future model change that lets two distinct occurrences share rule, subject, summary and locations must extend the identity material before publication -- and names nomos-model's existing IdentityTransitionKind as where cross-snapshot continuity belongs, so a later reader does not invent a second lifecycle vocabulary beside it. The predicate covers the crates whose behaviour changes, affected surface snapshots are re-blessed, and the gate lint step is clean.

Declined.reason:
Territory overlaps a live claim on exactly one of its eight paths: tests/contract/surface/nomos-gate-orchestration.txt, held by P100-THE-ARCHITECTURE-A-RULE-JUDGES-IS-COMPILED-INTO-THE-RULE-CRATE-INSTEAD-OF-DECLARED-BY-THE-REPOSITORY-7 under fable-p100 until unix 1789433286. The other seven are free, measured against the whole board rather than read off the refusal text.

The overlap is load-bearing rather than incidental. Compare_Gate_Runs returns GateCompareResult by value, and neither it nor DispositionChange can carry the typed collision failure this item's own done_when requires without changing that crate's public surface. So dropping the snapshot path would drop the typed failure with it, which is the one clause the last revision added, and narrowing an acceptance criterion to fit an unavailable path is how a green finish stops meaning anything.

Split instead, with nothing removed. The identity half becomes P104-A-FINDING-HAS-NO-IDENTITY-OF-ITS-OWN-OCCURRENCE, whose five paths are all free and which is provable on its own: the derivation, its exclusions, and the collision detector are pure functions over a finding population and need no run. The comparison half is re-authored as -3, reserving the four paths that remain and depending on the identity half, so the board reports it waiting rather than ready until both the identity exists and the peer's lease has run. The real-population cardinality proof -- the number of findings entering comparison equals the number emitted, on this repository's own tree -- stays with -3, because that is where it can be measured.

items.title: A finding has no identity of its own occurrence, so two violations in one file are one thing to every consumer
items.why:
Measured 2026-09-14: a Finding is rule, subject, subject_name, applicability, evidence, gate, summary and locations, and nothing in it distinguishes one occurrence of a violation from another occurrence of the same violation at the same subject. A rule emits one finding per occurrence -- rules push inside per-line loops, each finding carrying a single location -- while the subject is the file, so five violations in one file are five findings that no consumer can tell apart. OD-GATE-030 already names this as the second of three things missing before a run may claim continuity, and names it as unbuilt.

Three consumers are waiting on it rather than one. Comparison is the measured defect: 253 findings reduced to 150 distinct rule-and-subject pairs, 103 discarded before comparison began. Baseline continuity and the finding lifecycle are the other two, and both are governed by records that defer rather than decline. This item builds only the identity and its collision detector, because that is the part every one of the three needs and the part none of them should each derive separately.

A correction to an earlier measurement of mine belongs here rather than in a later reader's re-derivation: the lifecycle vocabulary is not absent, it is spelled differently. nomos-model's identity module already declares IdentityTransitionKind with ExactContinuity, ProbableRename, ProbableMove, SignatureEvolution, SplitInto, MergedFrom, Recreated, GeneratedFrom and Unresolved, beside a CompositeIdentity carrying a StructuralFingerprint. All of it has zero consumers outside that crate, so it constrains nothing mechanically, but it is this repository's considered design and a second lifecycle vocabulary beside it would be the duplicated authority this repository files records about. The two are not the same thing and the documentation must say so: an occurrence identity names one concrete occurrence in one pinned result, a transition kind names a relation between identities across snapshots.
items.done_when:
A finding occurrence identity exists in nomos-model as a projection over a Finding rather than a field stored on one, so none of the roughly seventy construction sites changes.

It is derived from rule, subject, summary and locations -- what identifies which violation instance occurred -- through the length-framed Digest_Of_Parts this crate already owns, so part boundaries are significant and two identities cannot be made to collide by concatenation.

Nothing describing a finding's treatment enters the derivation. Applicability, evidence class and gate category are excluded by construction, and a test asserts that two findings differing only in gate category share one identity -- a finding moving between gate buckets is precisely the continuity a comparison depends on, so an identity that moved with the bucket would be useless for the one thing it is for.

A collision over a population is reported as a typed value naming both colliding findings, not discovered by a map insert. The detector is a pure function over a slice of findings, so a negative control can make it report a collision with no run, no gate and no repository state involved. Both directions are exercised: a population with no duplicate reports none, and a population holding two findings identical in the four identity components reports exactly one collision naming both.

The derivation is pinned by a vector, so a later change to the identity material cannot pass silently the way an unpinned digest would.

The documentation states the injectivity claim narrowly: injective over the currently representable Finding model, and a future model change that lets two distinct occurrences share rule, subject, summary and locations must extend the identity material before publication. It names IdentityTransitionKind as where cross-snapshot continuity belongs and distinguishes the two, and it does not couple to CompositeIdentity, which addresses a symbol rather than a finding and whose components a finding does not have.

nomos-model's surface snapshot is re-blessed and the public_surface contract test passes over it.

Declined.reason:
Territory named the wrong stem for the type the item introduces, and the workspace self-check is the only thing in the loop that can say so.

file-name-matches-declared-type is a nomos rule, not a clippy lint. cargo test and cargo clippy both ran clean over the finished implementation -- 67 model tests green, no new warnings -- and nomos check --root . reported one blocking finding on the whole tree: FindingOccurrenceId is public but crates/kernel/nomos-model/src/identity/finding_occurrence.rs has stem finding_occurrence instead of finding_occurrence_id. OD-RULES-016 is what decides it: a module satisfies the rule when the snake case of any public type it declares equals the file stem, and finding_occurrence equals none of them.

Renaming the type instead was considered and refused. FindingOccurrenceId is the name the requirement uses and it is the accurate one -- the value is an identity of an occurrence, not an occurrence -- and inventing a second public type so a stem would match is the sideways route to one-public-type-per-file that OD-RULES-016 exists to refuse.

So one reserved path changes stem, and nothing else moves. The replacement population was enumerated rather than patched: every reader of nomos-model's identity surface outside the crate was grepped, and the only ones are the public-surface snapshot, which is already reserved, and two records plus the rendered specification that cite composite_identity.rs by path -- a file this item does not touch. No declared list, contract table or manifest names a nomos-model type. The other four paths are unchanged and correct.

Re-authored as -2 with the corrected stem, before writing to it. The implementation itself stands and is unaffected: the derivation, its exclusions, the collision detector, thirteen tests and the blessed snapshot are all done and green, and the rename is the only edit -2 carries that -1 had not already made.

abandoned.reason: Territory named the wrong stem for the type the item introduces; re-authored as -2 before writing to the corrected path. See the decline reason on this item.
