A relocated table whose schema and interpretation the rules crate still owns does not satisfy this even though it looks data-driven, and neither does moving the membership map while the category vocabulary stays a closed enum in nomos-rules: a repository dividing its architecture into Domain, Infrastructure and Api must not have to edit nomos-rules to say so. The declaration is authored in nomos-architecture.json at the repository root and read by one provider, and the same file is what the foreign fixture declares in. It is not authored in standards.json, which another tool decodes with unknown fields disallowed, and not in a Cargo manifest, which would make the family Rust-only. What the carrier holds is the whole triple OD-RULES-029 names, not one third of it: the components themselves, the order over them, and the named exceptions that order cannot express, plus OD-RULES-023's write authorities.

Then: no nomos crate name and no nomos-specific architectural category remains compiled into nomos-rules, and deleting every such name does not reduce this workspace's ability to enforce its own architecture, because this workspace now declares what the ZONES table, the Zone enum, SAME_ZONE_EDGES, Permits and WRITE_DOORS between them encoded. A name that is in today's ZONES table, with its declaration removed, resolves to unresolved rather than to its legacy zone: that is the query where a correct implementation and a surviving compiled-in fallback must disagree, and confirming the cases that already pass is not evidence about it.

The same three rule implementations, unchanged in what they judge, enforce a foreign declaration with a different package vocabulary and different category names, proved against the hex-0.4.3 third-party fixture. The two consumers outside the check run each reach the declaration through the same seam the rules do rather than through a second copy: nomos gate admits answers from the declared architecture, and the LSP architectural component resolves from it, with no path anywhere still short-circuiting to a hardcoded classification. `nomos gate admits` keeps answering for the repository the caller is standing in, found by searching upward for the declaration the way cargo finds a manifest, so the verb works from a subdirectory; outside any repository it reports NotJudged, and the three places in nomos-cli that state the opposite as a present fact say what is true instead. Threading it to the LSP is a signature change and nothing more -- no renderer decides differently, no diagnostic gains or loses a field, and the declaration is read where a root and a FileSystem are already held rather than from ambient state, which OD-HOST-001 reserves to a composition root.

A repository declaring no architecture still reports NotApplicable rather than passing clean, and an incomplete or unparseable declaration reports a refusal or an applicability state rather than silently dropping the checks. OD-RULES-024 is amended to say the fact now exists and what it is, and both projections are re-rendered from a tree publishing exactly that record.

This item does not design an ownership, required-mechanism or general engineering-model schema, and does not decide what a declared component with no observed implementation means.

items.title: A finding has no identity of its own occurrence, so two violations in one file are one thing to every consumer
items.why:
Measured 2026-09-14: a Finding is rule, subject, subject_name, applicability, evidence, gate, summary and locations, and nothing in it distinguishes one occurrence of a violation from another occurrence of the same violation at the same subject. A rule emits one finding per occurrence -- rules push inside per-line loops, each finding carrying a single location -- while the subject is the file, so five violations in one file are five findings that no consumer can tell apart. OD-GATE-030 already names this as the second of three things missing before a run may claim continuity, and names it as unbuilt.

Three consumers are waiting on it rather than one. Comparison is the measured defect: 253 findings reduced to 150 distinct rule-and-subject pairs, 103 discarded before comparison began. Baseline continuity and the finding lifecycle are the other two, and both are governed by records that defer rather than decline. This item builds only the identity and its collision detector, because that is the part every one of the three needs and the part none of them should each derive separately.

A correction to an earlier measurement of mine belongs here rather than in a later reader's re-derivation: the lifecycle vocabulary is not absent, it is spelled differently. nomos-model's identity module already declares IdentityTransitionKind with ExactContinuity, ProbableRename, ProbableMove, SignatureEvolution, SplitInto, MergedFrom, Recreated, GeneratedFrom and Unresolved, beside a CompositeIdentity carrying a StructuralFingerprint. All of it has zero consumers outside that crate, so it constrains nothing mechanically, but it is this repository's considered design and a second lifecycle vocabulary beside it would be the duplicated authority this repository files records about. The two are not the same thing and the documentation must say so: an occurrence identity names one concrete occurrence in one pinned result, a transition kind names a relation between identities across snapshots.
items.done_when:
A finding occurrence identity exists in nomos-model as a projection over a Finding rather than a field stored on one, so none of the roughly seventy construction sites changes.

It is derived from rule, subject, summary and locations -- what identifies which violation instance occurred -- through the length-framed Digest_Of_Parts this crate already owns, so part boundaries are significant and two identities cannot be made to collide by concatenation.

Nothing describing a finding's treatment enters the derivation. Applicability, evidence class and gate category are excluded by construction, and a test asserts that two findings differing only in gate category share one identity -- a finding moving between gate buckets is precisely the continuity a comparison depends on, so an identity that moved with the bucket would be useless for the one thing it is for.

A collision over a population is reported as a typed value naming both colliding findings, not discovered by a map insert. The detector is a pure function over a slice of findings, so a negative control can make it report a collision with no run, no gate and no repository state involved. Both directions are exercised: a population with no duplicate reports none, and a population holding two findings identical in the four identity components reports exactly one collision naming both.

The derivation is pinned by a vector, so a later change to the identity material cannot pass silently the way an unpinned digest would.

The documentation states the injectivity claim narrowly: injective over the currently representable Finding model, and a future model change that lets two distinct occurrences share rule, subject, summary and locations must extend the identity material before publication. It names IdentityTransitionKind as where cross-snapshot continuity belongs and distinguishes the two, and it does not couple to CompositeIdentity, which addresses a symbol rather than a finding and whose components a finding does not have.

nomos-model's surface snapshot is re-blessed and the public_surface contract test passes over it.

Both new files satisfy file-name-matches-declared-type, measured by running the workspace self-check and reading its findings for these paths rather than by inspection -- that rule is a nomos rule and neither cargo test nor cargo clippy can see it. The self-check is deliberately not in the declared predicate: it judges the whole real tree, which peers redden and green independently of this item, and an item's predicate proves the claims that item introduces rather than repository-wide health.

items.title: Run_Reassessing and RuleReassessmentCache have no consumer and no test anywhere, so the skip they implement is unverified
items.why: Measured 2026-09-14 by grepping every .rs under crates/ and tests/: the only mentions of Run_Reassessing or RuleReassessmentCache outside run_context.rs, which defines them, are inside rule_reassessment_cache.rs's own doc comment and its definition. No caller anywhere. No test anywhere, inside the crate or out, and no Test_ function in either reassessment module. The mechanism is implemented and exported and has never been executed. That makes the accurate description of this capability today: implemented and exported, currently unverified and unused. It should not be described as an implemented capability with behaviour until this item passes, because there is no execution evidence behind its behavioural claim. The API also decides where the proof can live. RuleReassessmentCache::New is public but Record and Recorded are pub(crate) and absent from the public surface snapshot, so a caller in another crate can construct and thread the cache but cannot observe whether anything was skipped. Proving the skip therefore belongs inside nomos-check-orchestration, where pub(crate) is visible -- and the alternative, widening Recorded to public so a test in another crate can read it, would be a test dictating the public surface.
items.done_when: A test inside nomos-check-orchestration drives three runs against one retained Workspace, one retained MemoryFactStore and one retained RuleReassessmentCache, and asserts behaviour rather than construction: after run 1 an eligible rule is recorded; run 2 over unchanged sources does not run that rule again; run 3, after a change reaching a fact family the rule's own Effective_Requires names, runs it again. Which rules are eligible is read from Effective_Requires rather than assumed, since that function's own doc says the skip stops at exactly the rules where it is honest. The assertions use the pub(crate) Recorded counter from inside the crate; Recorded and Record stay pub(crate) and the public surface snapshot does not change. The test is confirmed able to fail by holding the cache across a change that should invalidate it and observing the rule wrongly skipped. If the three runs show the mechanism is incorrect rather than merely untested, that is the item's result and it is reported as a finding: this item does not redesign Run_Reassessing, and P105-THE-LSP-PERSISTS-THE-REASSESSMENT-CACHE does not start. cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-check-orchestration passes.

items.title: NomosDiagnosticProvider retains Workspace and fact store across diagnoses but builds a fresh reassessment cache every call
items.why: NomosDiagnosticProvider is this workspace's one long-lived caller of the check pipeline: it holds workspace: Option<Workspace> and store: MemoryFactStore as private fields and threads &mut self.workspace and &mut self.store into every Diagnose, so the reuse OD-ANALYSIS-009 built already has a real consumer. It calls nomos_check_orchestration::Run, which by that function's own doc always starts from an empty RuleReassessmentCache and drops it at the end of the call -- so every rule re-runs on every keystroke that reaches a didOpen or didSave, even where the facts it reads have not moved. Run_Reassessing is the identical pipeline handed a cache the caller keeps, and it has no caller anywhere. This is the first one it is waiting for. Traced before authoring rather than after: the fields are private and the public surface snapshot lists only New, Diagnose, three consts and two impls, so a private reassessment field changes no public surface and needs no constructor parameter -- tests/contract/surface/nomos-lsp.txt is deliberately NOT in this territory. All four construction sites, src/main.rs and three in the provider's own tests, go through New() and need no signature change.
items.done_when: NomosDiagnosticProvider carries a private RuleReassessmentCache alongside its existing workspace and store, initialised in New() with no new public constructor parameter, and Diagnose calls Run_Reassessing threading &mut self.reassessment instead of calling Run. The test proves only what this crate owns: one provider instance survives repeated Diagnose calls over the same tree and retains its reassessment state across them, and the diagnostics it reports are unchanged by the switch. It does NOT assert the cache skipped anything -- Recorded is pub(crate) and unreachable from here, and the proof that the cache skips is P105-THE-REASSESSMENT-CACHE-IS-EXPORTED-AND-HAS-NEVER-BEEN-EXECUTED's own subject, which is why this item depends on it. No public surface changes and the snapshot is unchanged; if it turns out one must, the territory was wrong and this declines and re-authors rather than widening. The demanded-family duplication between RuleDescriptor.requires and Materialize_Capabilities' hand-written Tracking calls is visible from this work and is deliberately left alone: it is its own item, not a cleanup this one absorbs. cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-lsp passes.

Declined.reason: Impossible as authored, found by P105-THE-REASSESSMENT-CACHE-IS-EXPORTED-AND-HAS-NEVER-BEEN-EXECUTED while proving the mechanism. Its territory is the LSP provider and its tests, on the premise that Run_Reassessing and RuleReassessmentCache were callable from another crate. They are not. mod run_context at nomos-check-orchestration/src/lib.rs:50 is private, and line 62 re-exports only Composed_Rules, Run and RunContext from it. Both names are individually pub inside that private module, which makes them unreachable from every other crate and absent from tests/contract/surface/nomos-check-orchestration.txt entirely -- the LSP cannot name Run_Reassessing today. The authoring error is precise and worth recording: pub was read as reachable without checking the module's own visibility, which is the built-versus-reachable distinction this workspace had just finished writing down. Re-authored as P105-THE-REASSESSMENT-PATH-BECOMES-REACHABLE-AND-THE-LSP-KEEPS-A-CACHE, which owns the export and the surface snapshot alongside the LSP change, because the work is two responsibilities and not one: making the path reachable across a crate boundary, and wiring the first caller that survives across requests.

items.title: Compare collapses every finding a rule makes about one subject into one, losing 41 percent of them
items.why:
Compare_Gate_Runs indexes a run's findings into a BTreeMap keyed by rule and subject, with insert. A rule emits one finding per occurrence while the subject is the file, so a rule finding five violations in one file emits five findings sharing one key and the map keeps the last. Measured 2026-09-14 before P104a: 253 findings emitted, 150 distinct rule-and-subject pairs, 103 discarded before comparison began, thirty-seven keys holding more than one, the worst dependency-policy at twenty-four.

The consequences are false lifecycle claims in both directions: fixing four of five violations in a file leaves one finding before and one after and reports no change, and going from one to five reports no change either. Nothing acknowledged it -- the only disjointness gate_compare documents is that a finding cannot fall into two buckets, which is true and about something else.

P104a closed the upstream information loss that would have forced this fix to ship with a known exception: a dependency-policy violation now says which crate it is about, and the tree measures 256 findings to 256 distinct fingerprints over rule, subject, summary and locations.

This is the second half of a split. P104-A-FINDING-HAS-NO-IDENTITY-OF-ITS-OWN-OCCURRENCE builds the identity and its collision detector in nomos-model; this item is the rewire that consumes them and the only place the real-population cardinality can be measured, because nomos-model cannot run a gate.
items.done_when:
Two findings a rule makes about one subject are two findings to compare.

Comparison keys by the occurrence identity nomos-model now derives: present in both compares standing and reason, present only before is removed, present only after is added, with no silent overwrite anywhere.

The cardinality is checked per run result before any comparison begins. A run whose findings do not yield as many distinct identities produces a typed failure naming both colliding findings, and BTreeMap::insert is never the mechanism that discovers a collision.

Measured on this repository's own tree, the number of findings entering comparison equals the number emitted, asserted rather than described.

Four behaviours are exercised: some-but-not-all occurrences fixed reports removals, occurrences multiplying reports additions, an unchanged multi-occurrence subject reports no change, and a single-finding subject behaves as it does today.

Suppression and baseline keep their rule-and-subject addressing, asserted so occurrence identity cannot narrow them by accident. The public protocol is not widened for an internal key: the identity is exposed only where a caller must already see it, and if it stays internal to compare and is not serialized, the headless response is left alone.

The predicate covers the crates whose behaviour changes, affected surface snapshots are re-blessed, and the gate lint step is clean.

items.title: The reassessment path is trapped behind a private module, and the one caller that could use it re-runs every rule per keystroke
items.why: Two responsibilities, which is why this replaces an item that assumed one. FIRST, reachability. mod run_context at nomos-check-orchestration/src/lib.rs:50 is private and line 62 re-exports Composed_Rules, Run and RunContext only. Run_Reassessing and RuleReassessmentCache are pub inside that private module, so no other crate can name them and neither appears in tests/contract/surface/nomos-check-orchestration.txt. P105-THE-REASSESSMENT-CACHE-IS-EXPORTED-AND-HAS-NEVER-BEEN-EXECUTED proved the mechanism from inside the crate at cbeb644d -- a rule recorded on run 1, skipped on an unchanged run 2, re-run after run 3 moves a family it reads, both assertions confirmed able to fail in both directions. What it could not do is make that mechanism available to anyone. SECOND, the caller. NomosDiagnosticProvider already holds workspace and store as private fields and threads them into every Diagnose, so fact reuse has a real long-lived consumer. It calls Run, which by its own doc always starts from an empty cache and drops it at the end of the call, so every composed rule re-runs on every didOpen and didSave even where nothing it reads has moved. It is the strongest available second consumer precisely because, unlike the CLI, keeping state across edits is what it is for.
items.done_when: nomos-check-orchestration's lib.rs re-exports RuleReassessmentCache and Run_Reassessing alongside the three names it already exports, and tests/contract/surface/nomos-check-orchestration.txt is re-blessed from a clean worktree for the two additions. The export is exactly those two and no wider: no incremental-session type, no builder, no re-export of Record or Recorded, which stay pub(crate) and cfg(test). NomosDiagnosticProvider then carries a private RuleReassessmentCache beside its workspace and store, initialised in New() with no new public constructor parameter, and Diagnose calls Run_Reassessing threading it. The LSP's own public surface does not change and tests/contract/surface/nomos-lsp.txt is not touched; if it must be, the territory was wrong and this declines rather than widens. The LSP test proves what that boundary actually permits: one provider instance survives repeated Diagnose calls, its diagnostics are unchanged across an unchanged tree, and they update after a real edit. It does NOT count rule invocations. Recorded is cfg(test) and pub(crate) to another crate and stays that way -- making test instrumentation public so a downstream test can read it would export the wrong thing, and the invocation proof is cbeb644d's, already done, from inside the crate that owns it. Whether any external observable can distinguish a skipped rule from a re-run one is reported in the commit as a finding either way, since that is evidence about the application-service API rather than a gap in this item. The demanded-family duplication between RuleDescriptor.requires and Materialize_Capabilities' hand-written Tracking calls is deliberately left alone. cargo test --no-fail-fast -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-lsp passes, and so does the contract suite.

Declined.reason: Right work, two defects in how it was written. FIRST, its own predicate does not establish its own done_when. The done_when requires that the contract suite pass, because the item re-blesses tests/contract/surface/nomos-check-orchestration.txt, and the declared argv is cargo test -p nomos-check-orchestration -p nomos-lsp, which never runs it. Finishing on that would record verified over a claim the ledger never checked, which is the defect P103-A recorded one commit earlier at 1301f8b3. The fix is not to widen the argv either: Test_Every_Crates_Public_Surface_Should_Match_Its_Snapshot judges every crate's snapshot in a single test and cannot be narrowed to the one crate this item moves, so putting the contract suite in the predicate would inherit every peer's unblessed snapshot, which is the same defect in the other direction. The replacement states the exception explicitly instead of leaving a predicate that silently under-covers. SECOND, the acceptance is weaker than what is required. The done_when asks the LSP test to prove only that a provider instance survives repeated Diagnose calls with unchanged diagnostics, and defers every reuse proof to cbeb644d, so an implementation that retained a cache object which was never effective would satisfy it. Measured while inspecting: MemoryFactStore::Materializations is public and counts store writes, Already_Current short-circuits before it, and the provider's own test module is a child module that can read the private store -- so demonstrable reuse, selective invalidation and clean-recompute equivalence are all provable at the LSP boundary without exporting anything. items.title: A verification predicate scoped to a crate inherits every obligation that crate owns, and an item cannot finish though its own acceptance condition passes
items.why: A work item's verification predicate must establish that item's done_when, not every independent obligation owned by the crate named in its command. Two real instances now demonstrate the failure and the second proves the first was not corpus-specific. FIRST, 2026-09-14: P99-THREE-RECORDS-REPEAT-A-BARE-CHECKED-ON-LINE declared cargo test -p nomos-spec-validate -p nomos-spec-store, and its acceptance criterion was one thing -- that Test_A_Seeded_Store_Should_Pass_Preservation_Non_Vacuously stops reporting a violation with the corpus present. Run with the corpus exported it failed on Test_The_Domain_Volumes_Should_Answer_282_258_And_234, which counts pipe lines in a directory outside this repository. The item finished corpus-unset with the real obligation discharged by hand, so the ledger's machine-recorded verification did not prove what the item claimed. SECOND, the same day: P103-THE-TASK-SKILL declared cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests and changed one markdown file. It could not finish because public_surface failed on a peer's unblessed nomos-gate-orchestration snapshot, while agent_harness -- the obligation that governs skill text and the only one the item claimed -- was green throughout. Nothing corpus-related, same shape. The invariant is about verification-predicate scope against work-item scope, and the first instance's corpus was incidental to it.
items.done_when: The convention is decided and recorded where a ledger author reads it: a verification predicate establishes the item's own done_when, and does not inherit independent sibling obligations merely because they share a crate or package unless those obligations are themselves part of the item's acceptance criterion. It is stated as scope matching rather than as breadth minimising, and the record says so explicitly: cargo test -p <crate> stays correct for an item whose claim really is that the crate remains valid, and the rule to reject is verification scope wider than claimed obligation scope, not any particular command shape. Both incidents are carried as the evidence, including which obligation each item actually claimed and which unrelated one blocked it, so a later reader can check the generalization rather than trust it. The acceptance is behavioural on both sides: an item whose claim is narrow finishes when its own claimed obligation passes even while an unrelated sibling in the same crate is failing, and an item whose claim is whole-crate correctness still fails on any crate-wide failure. Whatever carries the convention -- a record, or a line in .claude/skills/nomos-task step 3 beside the territory rule it is a sibling of -- is chosen when the item is claimed rather than predetermined here. No mechanism is built: two instances justify a convention, not a predicate-scope validator, a scope algebra, or automatic dependency analysis, and the outcome says so rather than leaving the absence to read as an oversight. The shell-status hazard found alongside the second incident, where a pipeline's exit code belonged to head rather than cargo, is deliberately NOT part of this: that is observing a verdict wrongly, and this is a correct verdict about the wrong scope.

Declined.reason: The defect is right and only the carrier was wrong. This item's done_when deliberately left the carrier to be chosen when the item was claimed, a record or a line in the task skill, but its territory reserved only docs/records/OD-LEDGER-039 and there is no work edit, so choosing the skill makes the item impossible to execute rather than merely different. Claimed and inspected 2026-09-14: the convention is procedural, not a ledger semantic. VerificationPredicate is not declared in nomos-ledger, OD-LEDGER-037 having found it ledger-agnostic and moved it to nomos-scope-verification, so this item's own predicate of cargo test -p nomos-ledger could not have established its done_when either way. Finish already keeps a failing predicate apart from one that could not be asked and Record_From_Argv already stores exactly what ran, so both incidents are the ledger honestly reporting an author's choice. The only ledger semantic about inherited obligation is OD-LEDGER-003, which makes every item inherit the gate's lint step on purpose, and gate_unknown.rs already states the cost reason the test step stays per-item. OD-GATE-028 is the nearest record about verification predicates and is the opposite polarity, a predicate green for the wrong reason. A record would therefore restate a decided semantic rather than decide a new one. Replaced by P103-A-VERIFICATION-SCOPE-MATCHES-THE-CLAIMED-OBLIGATION-AND-THE-TASK-SKILL-CARRIES-IT, which reserves .claude/skills/nomos-task/SKILL.md, carries both incidents unchanged, and declares cargo test -p nomos-contract-tests --test agent_harness, the one obligation that governs skill text and the scope this convention would have chosen. OD-LEDGER-039 is released unallocated.

abandoned.reason: Claimed to decide the carrier its own done_when deliberately left open. The inspection answered skill rather than record, and the territory reserves only docs/records/OD-LEDGER-039, so the item cannot be executed as written. Abandoned to decline it.

items.title: The compare failure type is unreachable from the crate root, so no caller can name it
items.why:
A second, disjoint claim beside P104-COMPARE-COLLAPSES-EVERY-FINDING-A-RULE-MAKES-ABOUT-ONE-SUBJECT-INTO-ONE-4, not a widening of it. That item is still valid and its four paths are still correct; the scope grew by exactly one file, which is the case the ledger answers with an additive item rather than with a decline.

Compare_Gate_Runs currently returns GateCompareResult by value. -4 makes it refuse a run whose findings do not yield as many distinct occurrence identities, which means a typed failure in its signature. A type named in a public signature has to be reachable from the crate root or callers cannot name what they are handling, and the crate root is the one place a type declared in gate_compare.rs becomes public: lib.rs line 220 is where Compare_Gate_Runs, DispositionChange, FindingDisposition and GateCompareResult are already re-exported together.

The crate root also carries prose about the verb. Its compare paragraph says the verb reports each finding’s disposition change as a DispositionChange in a GateCompareResult. That stays literally true of the success path and becomes silent about a refusal the verb can now make, which is the half a reader would act on. Measured rather than assumed: the two other doc sites naming Compare_Gate_Runs were read and are not falsified -- nomos-cli/src/gate.rs describes the two-walk composition, and gate_command.rs describes reachability from a terminal, and neither states the return shape.

Nothing else in the crate root moves. The mod list, the other re-exports and every paragraph that is not about compare are untouched.
items.done_when:
The failure type -4 introduces in gate_compare.rs is re-exported from the crate root beside Compare_Gate_Runs, DispositionChange, FindingDisposition and GateCompareResult, so a caller outside the crate can name the thing it must handle.

The crate root’s compare paragraph states that comparison can refuse and what makes it refuse, rather than describing only the shape returned when it does not. It does not restate gate_compare.rs’s own reasoning, which is that file’s to hold.

Nothing else in lib.rs changes: the mod list, the other re-export lines and every paragraph not about compare are byte-identical.

The workspace builds and nomos-gate-orchestration’s public surface snapshot accounts for the new export, which is -4’s path to bless, so the two items are verified and committed together rather than separately -- neither half compiles without the other.

items.title: The headless compare response cannot say that no comparison happened
items.why:
A third disjoint claim beside P104-COMPARE-COLLAPSES-EVERY-FINDING-A-RULE-MAKES-ABOUT-ONE-SUBJECT-INTO-ONE-4 and P104-THE-COMPARE-FAILURE-TYPE-IS-UNREACHABLE-FROM-THE-CRATE-ROOT. Both of those remain valid and correctly scoped; this is scope growing by one more file, which the ledger answers additively rather than by declining a live item.

Once Compare_Gate_Runs can refuse, nomos-api has to say so. Handle_Gate_Compare is not library-only: nomos-api-transport dispatches nomos.gate.compare to it and serializes what it returns, so a refusal that is not representable in GateCompareResponse would be representable only as a response claiming an empty difference -- indistinguishable from two runs that genuinely agree, which is the exact class of silent false claim this whole P104 line of work exists to remove.

Measured before choosing the shape rather than after. Every one of nomos-api's twenty-plus handlers returns a plain response type and not one returns a Result, so refusals in this crate live inside the response; making this the single exception would invent a second convention for one caller. deny_unknown_fields appears on the transport parameter types and on no response type, so an added response field is additive on the wire and breaks no existing consumer. The api-transport surface names only ServedMethod::GateCompare and is unaffected.

This does not contradict -4's clause about leaving the headless response alone. That clause governs the occurrence identity -- FindingOccurrenceId stays internal to compare and is serialized nowhere -- and a refusal is not the identity.
items.done_when:
GateCompareResponse can say that no comparison happened, so a wire consumer can tell a refusal from two runs that agreed. A response carrying a refusal is not also carrying differences, and a test asserts both directions: a real comparison reports no refusal, and a refused one reports no added, removed or changed entries that a reader could mistake for a result.

The shape stays minimal on purpose and the reason is stated where the field is declared: no wire consumer needs the colliding pairs today, the only caller is the transport dispatcher, and the full typed pairing is already available to a Rust caller as CollidingOccurrences. Inventing a serialized failure taxonomy ahead of a caller that reads one is the shape this crate refuses elsewhere by name.

nomos-api's public surface snapshot accounts for the added field, and nomos-api-transport still compiles and serializes without change, asserted by building it rather than by reasoning about it.

Verified and committed together with -4 and the crate-root item: none of the three compiles without the others.

items.title: The reassessment path is trapped behind a private module, and the one caller that could use it re-runs every rule per keystroke
items.why: Two responsibilities. FIRST, reachability. mod run_context at nomos-check-orchestration/src/lib.rs is private and the crate root re-exports Composed_Rules, Run and RunContext only. Run_Reassessing and RuleReassessmentCache are pub inside that private module, so no other crate can name them and neither appears in tests/contract/surface/nomos-check-orchestration.txt. cbeb644d proved the mechanism from inside the crate -- a rule recorded on run 1, skipped on an unchanged run 2, re-run after run 3 moves a family it reads, both assertions confirmed able to fail in both directions. What it could not do is make that mechanism available to anyone. SECOND, the caller. NomosDiagnosticProvider already holds workspace and store as private fields and threads them into every Diagnose, so fact reuse has a real long-lived consumer. It calls Run, which by its own doc always starts from an empty cache and drops it at the end of the call, so every composed rule re-runs on every didOpen and didSave even where nothing it reads has moved. It is the strongest available second consumer precisely because, unlike the CLI, keeping state across edits is what it is for. This replaces P105-THE-REASSESSMENT-PATH-BECOMES-REACHABLE-AND-THE-LSP-KEEPS-A-CACHE, whose predicate did not establish its own done_when and whose acceptance a never-effective cache would have satisfied. Measured while inspecting it: MemoryFactStore::Materializations is public and counts store writes, Already_Current short-circuits before that call so a reused subject does not increment it, and the provider's test module is a child module that reads the provider's private store already -- so reuse, selective invalidation and clean-recompute equivalence are provable at the LSP boundary with no new export and no test instrumentation made public.
items.done_when: nomos-check-orchestration's lib.rs re-exports RuleReassessmentCache and Run_Reassessing alongside the three names it already exports, and nothing wider: no incremental-session type, no builder, no re-export of Record or Recorded, which stay pub(crate) and cfg(test). tests/contract/surface/nomos-check-orchestration.txt is re-blessed from a clean worktree for exactly those additions. NomosDiagnosticProvider then carries a private RuleReassessmentCache beside its workspace and store, initialised in New with no new public constructor parameter, and Diagnose calls Run_Reassessing threading all three. The LSP's own public surface does not change and tests/contract/surface/nomos-lsp.txt is not touched; if it must be, the territory was wrong and this declines rather than widens. SEVEN ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, proven at the LSP boundary in the provider's own test module, which is a child module and can read the provider's private state without exporting any of it. ONE, reachability: Run_Reassessing has at least one real non-test caller and it is Diagnose. TWO, persistent state: one provider instance owns Workspace, MemoryFactStore and RuleReassessmentCache across Diagnose calls rather than reconstructing any of them per diagnostic publication. THREE, behavioural equivalence: first-run diagnostics are identical to what the clean Run path produces over the same tree, asserted against a direct Run call rather than assumed. FOUR, actual reuse: a second unchanged Diagnose performs strictly fewer materializations than the first, read from the provider's own store through the public Materializations counter, rather than an assertion that a cache object exists. FIVE, selective invalidation: editing one of two sources re-materializes that source and leaves the other's fact reused, measured as a materialization delta of one rather than two. SIX, clean-recompute equivalence: the diagnostics a reusing provider reports after the edit equal those a freshly constructed provider reports over the same resulting tree. SEVEN, no LSP-specific analysis semantics: nomos-lsp gains lifecycle and state retention only, with no judgment, ordering, invalidation policy or fact handling of its own, and nomos-check-orchestration remains the authority on analysis and reassessment. The three-step shape carries four, five and six together, because a two-run test cannot tell reuse from recomputation: run 1 over sources A and B cold, run 2 unchanged, run 3 with A alone modified. The LSP test does not count rule invocations. Recorded is cfg(test) and pub(crate) and stays that way, since making test instrumentation public so a downstream test could read it would export the wrong thing, and the rule-skip invocation proof is cbeb644d's, already done from inside the crate that owns it. The commit reports, either way, which of a skipped rule and a reused fact an external observer can actually distinguish and through what. VERIFICATION SCOPE. The predicate is the two crates whose behaviour this item claims. The re-blessed snapshot is judged by Test_Every_Crates_Public_Surface_Should_Match_Its_Snapshot, which judges every crate's snapshot in one test and cannot be narrowed to the one crate this item moves, so it is deliberately not in the predicate: including it would inherit every peer's unblessed snapshot, which is the defect recorded at 1301f8b3. It is run by hand and its outcome reported in the commit, and the exception is stated here rather than left implicit in an argv that silently under-covers. NOT IN SCOPE, and this item is not read as covering any of them: a daemon, a generalized incremental scheduler, a demand planner, a filesystem watcher, or any new cache abstraction. The demanded-family duplication between RuleDescriptor.requires and Materialize_Capabilities' hand-written Tracking calls is deliberately left alone. If retaining the three existing state objects exposes a real defect in their contracts, that concrete defect is fixed; otherwise this increment only makes already-built incremental behaviour reachable in a long-lived production surface.

items.title: The one test of the reassessment cache runs a one-rule selection, so the skip every real caller gets is unasserted
items.why: Measured at 0c3b1013 and recorded only in that commit message. Under the selection the LSP actually passes, the empty one meaning all 71 composed rules, a retained cache over two sources skips 52 of 71 rule evaluations on an unchanged second call: Recorded went 71, then plus 19, then plus 68 after one of the two sources was edited. Nothing asserts any of that. Test_A_Retained_Cache_Should_Skip_A_Rule_Whose_Families_Did_Not_Move, the only test of the cache, selects COMPLETENESS_MIRROR alone and its own doc says why -- a rule reading a policy family would prove less there, because those sections re-materialize every call. That is the right choice for the claim it makes and it leaves the production claim unmade. A regression that put SyntaxItems into changed unconditionally would take the skip from 52 to 0 and leave that test, the LSP suite, and every equivalence test in this workspace green, because skipping and re-running a deterministic rule produce identical findings. The figure is also the only evidence the cache is worth retaining at all: 0c3b1013 established that no observable outside the crate can distinguish a skipped rule from a re-run one, so if this number is not asserted inside the crate it is asserted nowhere.
items.done_when: A test in nomos-check-orchestration's own test module runs a retained RuleReassessmentCache over the empty selection, which is what every composed rule means and what NomosDiagnosticProvider passes, across the same three calls the existing narrow test uses: cold, unchanged, then one of two sources edited. It asserts that the unchanged call runs strictly fewer rules than the cold one, read from Recorded, and that the edited call runs more than the unchanged one. It does not pin 71, 19 or 68: the composed table grows, and a test that fails when a rule is added fails for the wrong reason. Both assertions are observed failing on a real violation before the item finishes -- the honest mutation is making the cache unreachable from the call, since a cache threaded and never consulted is exactly the regression this guards, and the mutation is restored byte-identically. The existing narrow test stays as it is and is not generalized into this one: it proves a different thing, that a named rule with one required family skips, and merging them would leave neither claim legible. No mechanism is added beyond the test.

items.title: The gate exit-code doc enumerates three causes of Contradictory and compare added a fourth
items.why:
ExitCode::Contradictory's own doc enumerates where the code comes from: this gate's rule composition is self-contradictory, or run's tree could not be read at all, or the check registry beneath a run was itself self-contradictory. As of P104's compare rewrite there is a fourth: Render_Compare returns Contradictory when a run's findings do not yield one occurrence identity each, so the comparison refuses rather than dropping a finding.

Reusing the existing code was deliberate and is not what this item questions. Render_Compare already reuses run's refusals rather than restating them, and a self-contradictory identity is the same kind of thing as a self-contradictory registry -- the analysis contradicting itself rather than the tree being bad. Minting a fifth code would have cost exit_code.rs, its Every_Exit_Code census and gate/tests.rs's exhaustive match, for a distinction a caller has no different action for.

What is wrong is only the enumeration. A reader who gets exit code 5 from nomos gate compare goes to this doc and finds three causes, none of which is theirs. The sentence is not false -- it does not say only these -- and it is incomplete in the one place a reader looks, which is the same defect class this repository files about its own prose elsewhere. Filed rather than folded into P104 because exit_code.rs was outside all three of that work's territories and widening a live claim mid-implementation for one sentence is the move this repository has declined five times.
items.done_when: ExitCode::Contradictory's doc names the compare refusal beside the three causes it already lists, in the same register: what happened, not how the mechanism works, which gate_compare.rs holds. The existing three are unchanged and no code is minted. Nothing else in exit_code.rs moves, including the Every_Exit_Code census, which does not change because no variant does.

items.title: A dead import sits in the headless compare response

gate_compare_response.rs imports SuppressionReason from nomos-gate-orchestration and never names it. BucketChange::From reads change.before_reason.disposition and .status, and field access needs no import, so the name has been dead for as long as that conversion has existed.

It was left alone on purpose while P104 was in flight. An item's predicate proves the claims that item introduces, and sweeping an unrelated warning into a claimed territory to make a build quieter is the opportunistic fix this repository has already been told not to make. items.title: A verification predicate need not reach the crates its own territory names
items.why:
An item can reserve a file and declare a predicate that never compiles it. Nothing refuses the combination, so the item finishes green having never built part of what it changed.

Measured on a real instance, not hypothesised. P104-COMPARE-COLLAPSES-EVERY-FINDING-A-RULE-MAKES-ABOUT-ONE-SUBJECT-INTO-ONE-4 reserved crates/host/nomos-cli/src/gate/report.rs and declared cargo test -p nomos-gate-orchestration -p nomos-api. That predicate does not build nomos-cli. The implementation added a directory walk that nested four levels, nesting-depth reported it as blocking, and two real-tree tests in nomos-cli went red -- Test_Host_Variant_Should_Compose_Into_A_Real_Run_That_Judges_This_Workspaces_Own_Tree and Test_Read_Source_Should_Underlie_A_Real_Runs_RunId_Report, both of which assert this workspace carries nothing that can fail a build. The declared predicate was green throughout. It was caught only by running a crate the item never named, and work finish would not have seen it either: the gate lint step is bare clippy with no -D warnings, and nesting-depth is a nomos rule that neither cargo test nor cargo clippy runs.

This is the mirror of a question already asked and left open. P103-A-LEDGER-PREDICATE-MUST-NOT-INHERIT-UNRELATED-CRATE-OBLIGATIONS and its two predecessors were declined, and all three are about a predicate being too *broad* -- inheriting sibling obligations because they share a crate. This is the opposite direction and does not reopen them: scope matching cuts both ways, and a predicate narrower than its own territory fails the same principle those items were trying to state.

Whether the ledger should refuse such an item mechanically, or whether this is a convention a record states and an author follows, is the open question. Proposed rather than required because the cheap mechanical version -- map each reserved path to its owning crate and check the predicate names it -- is a guess at the right strictness: a territory naming a record, a snapshot or a JSON fixture belongs to no crate, and an item may legitimately verify a shared artifact through a different package than the one that owns the file.
items.done_when:
The question is decided and recorded where a ledger author reads it: whether a verification predicate must reach every crate its territory names, and if so what happens to reserved paths that belong to no crate -- records, surface snapshots, JSON fixtures, the ledger itself.

The record states the measured instance rather than describing the shape in the abstract, names the mirror relationship to P103-A-LEDGER-PREDICATE-MUST-NOT-INHERIT-UNRELATED-CRATE-OBLIGATIONS so a reader sees both directions of one principle, and says plainly that a green predicate proved nothing about a crate it never built.

If the decision is that the ledger should refuse the combination, the record says so and the enforcement is boarded as its own item rather than folded in, because the carrier -- work add, work finish, or a contract test over the committed board -- is a separate question this record does not answer. If the decision is convention only, the record says why mechanical enforcement was refused, so the next reader does not re-derive it.

Both projections are re-rendered from a tree holding exactly the records the commit publishes, per OD-GATE-005.

Declined.reason: The done_when invited the wrong next action. It said the question is decided and recorded, which reads as an instruction to decide it now, and the evidence for deciding it is one instance. Re-authored as -2 so the item holds the measurement and explicitly waits for a second independent instance before any ledger feature is designed. The why is unchanged and still correct; only what finishing means has changed.

P104 proved those are not the same thing -- cargo test and cargo clippy were both clean over a file that nesting-depth reported as blocking.

items.title: OD-SPEC-004 decided that repetition answers whether a body is filler, and two corpora now falsify that
items.why: OD-SPEC-004 chose its option 1, a repetition census with the blocklist retained as the naming layer, and states the principle plainly: repetition answers is this filler, which no pattern list can keep up with. It calibrated that on one corpus and its own record says which -- over the ten v14.36 domain volumes the test fires on 13 sections out of 482, so it is not a test that calls ordinary prose filler. Both halves of that calibration have now been exceeded, measured 2026-09-14 with both corpora exported, and the two failures are different from each other. FIRST, length. Over the sibling suites, 18,873 subjects, NSV-PRESERVE-004 reports 103 violations and 102 of them are 40 characters or fewer. The largest is three characters of horizontal rule repeated 562 times across 2 documents. The rest are ordinary connective fragments: a single downward arrow repeated 9 times, and Or, or:, So:, LLM, KWB, Now, Add:, Use:, and:, Bad:, Not:, Why?, Then:, Good:, Today, Show:, Uses:. The rule has no minimum length, so in any corpus of ordinary authored prose short fragments collide and every collision is reported as a form letter. That is not an edge case at 102 of 103. SECOND, publication convention. Over the ten domain volumes the count is 16, not the 13 OD-SPEC-004 measured, and every one of them is contentful text repeated by design in the places the suite's own layout puts it. Four are suite-wide front-matter at 10 sections across 10 documents: the edition line, the suite title, the volume-ownership sentence, the Word navigation note. Eleven are volume abstracts at 3 sections across 2 documents, which is exactly the cover line, the Document purpose section and the suite index entry -- three canonical places, so a ten-volume suite hits the threshold of 3 by construction. One is a parity note repeated 10 times inside a single volume, once beneath each of ten capability tables. None of the sixteen is prose that says a section exists without saying what it says, which is the definition FILLER_PATTERNS carries in its own doc, and none of them hollows a restored member, which is the harm OD-SPEC-004 measured over 44 of them. The two failures need different mechanisms, which is why the declined item that bundled them could not land, and both are downstream of one decision this record currently answers the other way.
items.done_when: OD-SPEC-004 is amended to version 3 and the amendment decides, on the evidence above, that repetition is necessary but not sufficient evidence that a body is filler -- or decides the opposite explicitly and says what the 118 measured violations then are. It answers three questions separately, because the measurement shows they are not one question. ONE, the length floor: whether a body below some length may be counted as a template at all, and if so what the floor is and what it is derived from rather than guessed; the 102-of-103 figure and the 562-times horizontal rule are carried as its evidence. TWO, declared publication text: whether a corpus may declare the text its own layout repeats -- front-matter, a volume abstract in its three canonical places -- so that a declaration admits it while an undeclared repetition still violates, and if so whether that declaration is corpus-side data or a second Rust list beside FILLER_PATTERNS. The answer says explicitly whether extending FILLER_PATTERNS itself is refused, since Get_Filler_Pattern names why a block was judged filler for a lineage row and calling a volume abstract filler would make that row say something false. THREE, the parity note: whether ten identical paragraphs inside one document is the same case as an abstract appearing in three documents, or a third one, since a single-document repetition is not a cross-volume convention and the answer may differ. The amendment carries both measurements with the corpora and subject counts named, so a later reader can re-run them rather than trust them, and it states that OD-SPEC-004's original calibration was correct for the corpus it was taken over and is being extended rather than corrected. No mechanism is built here and no violation count is pinned into any test: the two mechanisms follow from this decision and are authored from it, one per defect, and restoration.rs and siblings.rs stay red until they land rather than being quieted by an accepted number, which is the suppression the rule exists to make visible. Both projections are re-rendered from a clean worktree per OD-GATE-005 and committed with the record, and the freshness check is run with both required profiles; that step is deliberately not in the predicate because work finish does not run it and AGENTS.md says why.

items.title: A judged gate run that reaches no verdict panics the binary
items.why:
Exit_Code_For in crates/host/nomos-cli/src/gate/report.rs answers GateRunOutcome::Indeterminate with an unreachable arm, on the stated invariant that Run_Gate only assigns that disposition for a CheckOutcome which never reached Judged, and that this arm is Judged own. Two independent mechanisms in gate_environment.rs falsify it, and both are deliberate.

Run_Gate assigns Indeterminate whenever Resolve_Gate_Policy returns an error, without regard to what the check outcome was; its own comment says the judging still happens and is reported after it so the answer stays as informative as it honestly can be. Separately, Reduced_With_Coverage turns a Passed into Indeterminate on a fully judged run when the declared coverage floor is require-completeness and the claim over the selected findings is Incomplete, which is OD-GATE-016 own decision.

Measured 2026-09-14 with the built binary against a three-file probe tree. Three reproductions, every one exit 101:
- a nomos-gate.json with a mis-spelled top-level key, which DeclaredPolicy refuses under deny_unknown_fields
- a nomos-gate.json that is not valid JSON
- a valid nomos-gate.json declaring coverage require-completeness over a tree where the dependency-policy capability could not be materialized

The third is the one that matters most: nothing is wrong with the repository or with its configuration. It declared the coverage floor OD-GATE-016 built, the floor did exactly what that record decided, and the product aborted. The first two are the most likely operator error there is, in the one file a repository adopting this tool authors by hand, and every run after the typo aborts identically.

Every finding is written to stdout before the abort, so the panic replaces the verdict line and nothing else. A caller reading exit status gets 101, which is not in the table exit_code.rs declares; a caller reading stdout gets a complete report with no disposition. For a repository running this verb continuously and headlessly, that is the enforcement loop stopping on the operator error it is most likely to make.
items.done_when:
Exit_Code_For has no unreachable arm. A judged run whose disposition is Indeterminate reports to stderr that the run reached no verdict, and exits Contradictory, which is the code that file own doc already assigns to every Indeterminate a run produces and says run never carries further than. No exit code is minted and Every_Exit_Code does not change. ExitCode::Contradictory own doc names the two causes this item makes reachable beside the ones it already lists.

Proved by running the built binary against the same three probe trees the why measured: each exits 5 rather than 101, and stdout still carries the findings it carried before. Proved in the crate own predicate as well, by a test in report.rs that drives Render_Run over a GateRunResult which is Judged with an Indeterminate disposition and asserts both the exit code and the stderr line, so the arm is covered by cargo test rather than only by a manual run.

Out of scope, and deliberately: saying which of the two causes produced the Indeterminate. GateRunResult carries neither the policy error nor the coverage floor, so naming a cause here would mean guessing one. Reporting that there is no verdict, without claiming to know why, is the honest answer this territory can give.

items.title: NSV-PRESERVE-004 has no minimum length, so 102 connectives and a horizontal rule are form letters
items.why: OD-SPEC-004 version 3 decided that repetition is necessary and not sufficient evidence of filler, and question one of that amendment is the length floor. Measured 2026-09-14 over the sibling suites, 18,873 subjects: NSV-PRESERVE-004 reports 103 violations and 102 of them are 30 characters or fewer. The largest single contributor is three characters of horizontal rule carried by 562 sections across 2 documents; the rest are ordinary connectives and labels, among them a single downward arrow at 9 sections, and Or, or:, So:, LLM, KWB, Add:, Use:, Bad:, Why?, Then:, Good:, Example:, For example: at 148. The rule groups prose blocks by normalized hash and has no eligibility test at all, so in any corpus of ordinary authored prose short fragments collide and every collision is reported as an undeclared form letter. The amendment derives the floor rather than guessing it: the longest accidental collision observed is 30 characters, the shortest body repeated by design is 43, the shortest entry in FILLER_PATTERNS is 50 and Get_Filler_Pattern is substring containment so every block this repository has ever declared to be filler is at least that long. The distribution is empty between 31 and 42 in both corpora and the record fixes the floor at 36.
items.done_when: A prose block shorter than the floor is not eligible to be a template, and the floor is 36 characters of normalized block text as OD-SPEC-004 version 3 fixes it. The threshold lives beside SHARED_BY rather than in the rule, because the rule already documents that the value it enforces and the value archaeology Shared_Templates reports over a revision pair must stay one constant and not two numbers somebody has to notice disagree; census.rs and sections.rs both apply it or the item has created exactly that divergence. Boundary tests assert both sides from the measurement rather than from round numbers: a body of 30 characters repeated five times is not a violation, a body of 43 characters repeated three times is, and a body at the floor itself is decided explicitly rather than left to an off-by-one. The sibling measurement is re-run with both corpora exported and the new count is reported in the commit message; it is expected to fall from 103 to 1, the survivor being a 51-character status line that is question two of the amendment and not this item to fix. Neither restoration.rs nor siblings.rs is edited and no count is pinned into either: restoration stays at 16 because every one of those bodies is past the floor, and quieting a corpus test with an accepted number is the suppression the rule exists to make visible. VERIFICATION SCOPE: the predicate is the two crates this item changes, selected as lib plus named integration targets so that it excludes nomos-spec-ingest tests restoration.rs and siblings.rs, which are red by design until the declaration mechanism lands and are not this item's obligation to turn green. That exclusion is deliberate and is the convention step 3 of the task skill carries.

Declined.reason: Territory could not carry the acceptance, measured by implementing it. The floor must be one constant applied by NSV-PRESERVE-004 in nomos-spec-validate and by the archaeology census in nomos-spec-ingest, because the rule already documents that those two must not become two numbers somebody has to notice disagree. The helper therefore has to be nameable from another crate, and archaeology is declared mod archaeology at src/lib.rs line 8, private, so the re-export in lib.rs is not a convenience but the only way the rule can reach it. The item reserved tests/contract/surface/nomos-spec-ingest.txt, which is where the export becomes visible, and not the file that produces it -- the same dependency-cone miss the territory rule was written for, on an item authored after that rule landed. Re-authored with src/lib.rs added and nothing else changed; the implementation is already written and parked as a patch.

abandoned.reason: Territory cannot carry the change. The floor has to be one constant shared by the rule and the archaeology report, and the rule is in another crate, so the helper must be re-exported from nomos-spec-ingest. That re-export is in src/lib.rs, which this item did not reserve: it reserved the surface snapshot the export shows up in but not the file that produces it. Re-authored with lib.rs added.

items.title: A corpus has no way to declare canonical text its own layout repeats, so its front matter is a form letter
items.why: OD-SPEC-004 version 3 decided that a corpus may declare the text its own layout repeats, that the declaration is corpus-side data, and that it names structural roles rather than strings. Nothing carries such a declaration today. Measured 2026-09-14 over the ten v14.19 domain volumes, 2,988 subjects: NSV-PRESERVE-004 reports 16 violations and every one is contentful text repeated where the suite format puts it. Four are suite-wide front matter at 10 sections across 10 documents, the edition line, the suite title, the volume-ownership sentence and the Word navigation note. Eleven are volume abstracts at 3 sections across 2 documents, which is the cover line, the Document purpose section and the suite index entry, so a ten-volume suite crosses SHARED_BY by construction. A seventeenth case is a 51-character status line in the sibling suites. The amendment refuses both obvious shortcuts: extending FILLER_PATTERNS would make a lineage row say a volume abstract is prose that says a section exists without saying what it says, which is false, and a second compiled-in list is this repository's opinion about another corpus's layout and goes stale the way the blocklist did when one adjective changed. A store table is forced rather than chosen: Rule Evaluate receives only a SpecificationStore, so a declaration the rule can consult has to be rows, and a new table is a bundle change because the bundle is the authority committed to git and a table that does not travel in it is content a rebuilt store cannot hold.
items.done_when: A corpus can declare that a canonical block is intentionally projected into named structural positions, the declaration is ingested into rows, and those rows survive a bundle round trip. The declaration names roles and derives expected multiplicity from them, not a whitelisted string: this is what keeps it a declaration rather than a suppression list, and an undeclared further occurrence of a declared block must remain distinguishable from the declared ones. The bundle budget is paid in full and is the part of this item that is easy to leave half-done, because none of it is reachable from the crate that owns the table: the column coverage list, an exporter, an importer, both driver lists, and the round-trip fixture that must insert at least one row per table. Expect nomos-spec-store to stay green through all of it while the bundle is still incomplete. Coverage is proved from an in-repo fixture, not from either corpus. THIS ITEM DOES NOT TURN THE TWO CORPUS TESTS GREEN and must not be judged as though it should: restoration.rs and siblings.rs go green only when the corpora themselves carry declarations, and the corpora live outside this repository and are not territory any item here can reserve. Neither file is edited and no count is pinned into either. The rule consulting these rows is the separate item that depends on this one, so nothing here changes what NSV-PRESERVE-004 reports. VERIFICATION SCOPE: the predicate is the three crates this item changes, selected as lib plus the named integration targets that judge transport, so that it excludes nomos-spec-ingest tests restoration.rs and siblings.rs, which are red by design and are not this item's obligation. That exclusion is the convention step 3 of the task skill carries.

Declined.reason: Re-authored with a sharper acceptance rather than a changed premise. The done_when required declaration rows to survive a bundle round trip, which is too weak to exclude the corruption that actually matters: multiplicity is part of what a declaration means, so an export and import that preserved the text while coalescing two declarations of the same block into one would pass that clause and destroy the rule's semantics. The replacement requires multiplicity and identity to survive exactly, and requires the round-trip fixture to be able to fail if they do not. Nothing else about the item changes.

items.title: NSV-PRESERVE-004 cannot consult a repetition declaration, so declaring one would change nothing
items.why: OD-SPEC-004 version 3 decided that a block appearing in the places its declaration names is admitted and is not filler, while a further undeclared occurrence of that same block is still a violation. The carrier item makes the declaration into rows a rule can read. This item is the half that makes reading them change an answer, and it is deliberately separate because the two have different falsifiers: the carrier is proved by a bundle round trip, and this is proved by what the rule reports. Landing the carrier alone would leave a corpus able to declare its layout and a rule that still calls it a form letter.
items.done_when: NSV-PRESERVE-004 consults the declaration rows and admits a repetition whose occurrences are the ones its declaration names. The falsifier is asserted in the same run and is the whole point of the item: a block declared for three named roles that appears a fourth time, undeclared, is still reported, and a repetition nothing declared at all is still reported. Without that assertion the mechanism is a suppression list with extra steps, which is what the amendment refused. The blocklist keeps its separate job and is not extended: Get_Filler_Pattern still names which known pattern a template matched for a lineage row, and a declared block is admitted without being called filler, so no lineage row is made to assert something false about it. Both conditions are proved from an in-repo fixture. THIS ITEM DOES NOT TURN THE TWO CORPUS TESTS GREEN either: that needs the corpora to carry declarations, and they live outside this repository. restoration.rs and siblings.rs are not edited and no count is pinned into either. If, once the rule can see declarations, the ten-times-in-one-document parity note still reports, that is correct and is the question OD-SPEC-004 version 3 deliberately left open, not a defect in this item. VERIFICATION SCOPE: the predicate is nomos-spec-validate, the one crate whose behaviour this item claims and which owns no corpus-gated test; the ingest crate is not in it though the declaration rows come from there, because this item claims what the rule does with rows and not how they arrive.

Declined.reason: Superseded to keep its dependency edge live. Its carrier is being re-authored so that the bundle round trip must prove declaration multiplicity and identity survive export and import exactly, and a dependent pointing at a declined carrier is stranded rather than waiting. Re-authored unchanged in substance as the -2 item against the new carrier id.

items.title: The corpus-gate report only speaks in a workspace run, and every item predicate is package-scoped
items.why: On 2026-09-14 a session ran the filler-template predicate with NOMOS_V14_CORPUS set and NOMOS_SPEC_ARCHIVES unset, read nine passed from crates/spec/nomos-spec-ingest/tests/siblings.rs, and recorded the sibling corpus as clean. It was not: with both variables set the same file reports 103 violations over 18,873 subjects. The mechanism that should have caught this exists and is good. tests/contract/tests/corpus_gates.rs declares every gated file, the variables it reads and how many of its tests are gated, derives the same table from the source independently, and Test_A_Run_Should_Report_What_It_Did_Not_Check prints one line per variable naming how many assertions an unset one costs. It handles the partial case correctly, which is exactly the case that occurred. The gap is where it speaks. That report is a test inside nomos-contract-tests, so it runs in a workspace run and in CI, and never in a package-scoped run. Every verification predicate on this board is package-scoped, and the predicate-scope convention step 3 of the task skill now carries makes that correct rather than accidental, so the one mechanism that would say a run was hollow is the one an item predicate structurally cannot invoke. The hazard note in AGENTS.md says a test that cannot find its corpus passes, but it says so where somebody reads it before the run, not where they read the result. SECOND AND SEPARATE: line 22 of that file calls NOMOS_V14_CORPUS the v14.36 authoring tree. The tree on this machine is v14.19, with 51 occurrences of that version string and no occurrence of v14.36 anywhere in the corpus. OD-SPEC-004 carried the same stale edition and it is why its 13-of-482 calibration could not be re-run.
items.done_when: Reading a package-scoped test result no longer requires having remembered the hazard beforehand: a run whose corpus variables are not all set says so where the result is read, not only in a workspace run that no predicate performs. What that costs is bounded deliberately, because the decision not to fail is already made and this item does not reopen it. The module doc of corpus_gates.rs states plainly that a gate which can never be green is a gate everybody learns to ignore, most machines will never hold these corpora, and the remedy is a declared and reported hole rather than a red test. Any answer here that makes an absent corpus fail contradicts that and is refused; the item is about reaching the reader, not about changing the verdict. The declared table keeps its two independent derivations and they still agree, and no test count in it moves unless the item genuinely adds a test, in which case the table is updated in the same commit. SECOND: the v14.36 reference at line 22 is corrected to the edition the corpus actually carries, or is stated as the edition the numbers in that paragraph were measured over with the note that it is not the tree present here, whichever is true. Do not repair the one and leave the other: they are one commit because they are one file, but they are two claims and the commit message says which evidence establishes each.

abandoned.reason:
Stopped rather than improvised: the first half of this item's done_when cannot be satisfied inside the territory it reserves, and I am not widening into eight packages on my own judgement.

The report is the test Test_A_Run_Should_Report_What_It_Did_Not_Check in tests/contract/tests/corpus_gates/report.rs. It compiles only into the nomos-contract-tests test binary, so a package-scoped run of any other package never builds it and can never print its line -- and every verification predicate on this board is package-scoped.

There is no smaller place to stand. No crate in this workspace depends on nomos-contract-tests, so the report cannot ride into another test binary through a linked library. The fifteen declared gated files share no choke point: each reads its corpus variable in its own local helper -- Corpus_Or_Skip in nomos-lang-rust, nomos-workspace and tests/integration, Corpus in nomos-spec-ingest, Corpus_Root in nomos-spec-model and nomos-spec-store -- so making a scoped run speak means editing eight packages, and this item reserves none of them.

A helper that prints on its own skip path does not reach the reader either. libtest captures a passing test's output, which is exactly why a skipped test prints ok in the first place; the captured line is discarded with the pass. The two mechanisms that do reach a scoped run's terminal are a build script emitting cargo::warning, which must live in each gated package, and a static initializer in a library linked into each test binary, which needs a dev-dependency added to each. Both are eight-package changes and both are a mechanism decision this item does not make.

So the item needs its mechanism decided and then its territory widened, and in that order. Suggested split, in the shape P110-A and P110-B already took here: a decision item naming the reporting mechanism and the exact packages it lands in, then this item re-scoped to that surface with the table's two independent derivations still agreeing.

The SECOND half was verified independently and deliberately left unlanded, because this item's own done_when forbids repairing one and leaving the other. Line 22's v14.36 is false: the corpus at the configured root carries v14.19 fifty times across its text files plus once inside a compiled .pyc, which reconciles this item's own figure of 51, and v14.36 appears nowhere in the tree at all. That half is small, real and in territory whenever somebody takes this up.

items.title: The predicate-scope paragraph closes on the two incidents that caused it and never says what happened after
items.why: Step 3 of the task skill closes by saying two instances justify a rule and not a validator. That is the right conclusion and it is the argument for building no mechanism, but it dates the paragraph to the day it was written and leaves a reader unable to tell whether the rule has been used since or has only been stated. The distinction matters here more than usual because the paragraph is the reason no mechanism exists: the evidence for leaving it unenforced is that the rule works when followed, and nothing in the file records whether it has been. Items authored under the rule since carry an explicit verification-scope clause naming what the predicate excludes and why, which is checkable on the board and is the behaviour the paragraph was trying to produce. That is what should be recorded, and it is deliberately not a count of declines: the ledger stores a decline as a holder and a timestamp and does not persist the reason, so a claim about how many items were declined for predicate scope cannot be checked from the board and must not be written as though it could.
items.done_when: The closing of step 3 says what has happened since the rule landed, in a form a later reader can check, and does not assert anything the ledger cannot substantiate. It stays evidence rather than becoming an endorsement: the paragraph still concludes that no mechanism is justified, and it now says what would have to change for that to stop being true. No count of declines is written, because the decline reason is not persisted. No item identifier is named anywhere in the file, since agent_harness requires any identifier in an agent surface to be declared as a TEMPORARY_HAZARD and this change is not worth one; describe an item by the obligation it claimed, the way the two incidents above it are already described. Every backticked path added must exist, for the same check. VERIFICATION SCOPE: the predicate is the one test target that judges agent surface text, and no other obligation in that package is any part of this claim.

items.title: A run that reaches no verdict discards the reason it has one
items.why:
Resolve_Gate_Policy says exactly what is wrong with a nomos-gate.json. GatePolicyError is Unreadable or Malformed and carries the message, which for a malformed file is serde's own text naming the unknown field, or the syntax error and where it is. Run_Gate reads that result as declared.is_err() and keeps nothing else, so the message is computed and dropped at the one moment a person needs it.

GateRunResult therefore has no field for why a judged run reached no verdict, and every consumer is equally blind. P106 proved that at the shell: the message it wrote can say there is no verdict, and can name the two mechanisms that produce one, and cannot say which of them happened here, because the result does not know. A repository whose policy file has one mis-spelled key is correctly sent to the policy file, and is not told that the key it wrote is basline and not baseline, which the tool worked out and threw away.

The coverage floor is the second mechanism and is different in kind: Reduced_With_Coverage turns a Passed into an Indeterminate by OD-GATE-016's design, on a run where nothing is broken at all. A reader of the result cannot tell that from a broken policy file, and the two call for opposite responses -- one is a repository doing what the record intended, the other is a typo.

Measured 2026-09-14. GateRunResult has five construction sites in this workspace: one in gate_environment.rs, one in gate_compare.rs and three in nomos-cli's own report tests, so a field costs a countable edit rather than a sweep. GatePolicyError is pub(crate) and Resolve_Gate_Policy is private to the policy module, so what reaches the public surface is this item's to decide.
items.done_when:
GateRunResult carries why this run reached no verdict, and Run_Gate fills it from both mechanisms that produce one rather than discarding either. A malformed or unreadable nomos-gate.json contributes the message GatePolicyError already carries, serde's naming of the offending key or position included. A coverage floor that downgraded an otherwise-passing run is distinguishable from it, because the two call for opposite responses.

A run that reached a verdict carries nothing there, so every existing caller reads what it reads today.

nomos-cli renders it. The message P106 wrote names both mechanisms and says the result does not record which; it is replaced by one that names the one that happened. Proved by re-running the built binary over the three probe trees P106 measured, each naming its own cause, the mis-spelled one quoting the key that was refused.

Whether serde's text reaches the public surface as a String or as a variant of a type this crate owns is decided inside the item, by measuring what a caller would match on rather than by preference. The surface snapshot moves either way and is reserved.

Out of scope: the headless response, which is its own item and is sequenced after this one; and any change to what a disposition means. Indeterminate stays exactly what it is.
