items.title: The headless run response cannot say why a run gave no clean verdict
items.why:
GateRunResponse is run, root, disposition and findings. GateRunResult is run, root, check_outcome, findings, disposition and unmatched_policy. Two fields are dropped at the wire, and nothing says why: response.rs's own module doc explains at length why each type is twinned rather than given a Serialize derive, and is silent on both omissions.

check_outcome. Render_Run's own doc states the rule it is dropped against -- the exit code for every non-Judged variant is a property of why nothing was judged, which only check_outcome carries. At the shell, Unreadable, Contradictory, NoSource and NoFacts each get their own message and land on two different exit codes. Headlessly all four arrive as disposition indeterminate with four empty finding buckets, which is also how a judged run with a broken gate policy arrives. A caller cannot tell a repository that could not be walked from one whose analysis produced no facts from one whose policy file has a typo, and those call for three different actions.

unmatched_policy. OD-GATE-024 exists because an author who writes a policy entry matching nothing gets no error, no warning and no effect, and cannot tell a mis-spelling from a finding that has since been fixed. nomos-cli reports it under a heading of its own, deliberately silent only when every entry matched. A headless caller is given nothing, which is precisely the state that record was filed to end, restored for the surface this product is meant to be run on.

Measured 2026-09-14 by reading every response type in the crate: the name unmatched_policy does not occur anywhere under crates/host/nomos-api, and neither the plan nor the explain response carries it, so there is no other headless route to it.
items.done_when:
GateRunResponse says why a run did not reach a clean verdict. A caller can tell the four non-judged causes apart from one another and from a judged run, in the terms Render_Run already distinguishes them by, without a second request. A caller is told which declared policy entries matched nothing, the same list nomos-cli prints, and the empty case stays quiet rather than serializing a header over nothing.

The reason a judged run reached no verdict, which P106-A-RUN-THAT-REACHES-NO-VERDICT-DISCARDS-THE-REASON-IT-HAS-ONE puts on GateRunResult, is carried too. This item is sequenced after that one on purpose, so the response shape is decided once rather than widened twice.

A judged run with no unmatched entries serializes to what it serializes to today, plus whatever an absent cause is spelled as, so no existing consumer breaks.

The shape follows a measured precedent rather than a preference, and the item states which before it writes one: GatePlanResponse and GateExplainResponse are both tagged enums over an outcome, GateCompareResponse carries an optional uncomparable field, and this response is a flat struct, so the crate offers two precedents and they disagree.

Proved through Handle_Gate_Run over a real tree, not only over a constructed result, because that handler is what a transport actually calls. The surface snapshot is reserved and re-blessed.

Out of scope: widening ServedMethod, and the run-history store OD-GATE-022-A defers. This item changes what one response can say, not what the product can do.

items.title: A corpus has no way to declare canonical text its own layout repeats, so its front matter is a form letter
items.why: OD-SPEC-004 version 3 decided that a corpus may declare the text its own layout repeats, that the declaration is corpus-side data, and that it names structural roles rather than strings. Nothing carries such a declaration today. Measured 2026-09-14 over the ten v14.19 domain volumes, 2,988 subjects: NSV-PRESERVE-004 reports 16 violations and every one is contentful text repeated where the suite format puts it. Four are suite-wide front matter at 10 sections across 10 documents, the edition line, the suite title, the volume-ownership sentence and the Word navigation note. Eleven are volume abstracts at 3 sections across 2 documents, which is the cover line, the Document purpose section and the suite index entry, so a ten-volume suite crosses SHARED_BY by construction. A seventeenth case is a 51-character status line in the sibling suites. The amendment refuses both obvious shortcuts: extending FILLER_PATTERNS would make a lineage row say a volume abstract is prose that says a section exists without saying what it says, which is false, and a second compiled-in list is this repository's opinion about another corpus's layout and goes stale the way the blocklist did when one adjective changed. A store table is forced rather than chosen: Rule Evaluate receives only a SpecificationStore, so a declaration the rule can consult has to be rows, and a new table is a bundle change because the bundle is the authority committed to git and a table that does not travel in it is content a rebuilt store cannot hold.
items.done_when: A corpus can declare that a canonical block is intentionally projected into named structural positions, the declaration is ingested into rows, and those rows survive a bundle round trip. The declaration identifies roles or declared repeated structures and derives expected multiplicity from them. It does not store literal strings under a better name: that is the second list the amendment refused, and an implementation that reaches the same place by a different route has not satisfied this item. MULTIPLICITY AND IDENTITY SURVIVE EXPORT AND IMPORT EXACTLY, and this is a named acceptance condition rather than a consequence of the word survive, because it is the corruption that would otherwise pass. Multiplicity is part of what a declaration means. An exporter and importer that preserved every declared text while coalescing two declarations of one block into one row, or while merging declarations that name different roles, would leave the text intact and the meaning destroyed, and a round-trip fixture that only compares text would report that as success. So the fixture distinguishes them: it carries a case where the same block is declared more than once, and a case where two declarations differ only in the roles they name, and it is observed to fail when the exporter or importer coalesces either. The bundle budget is paid in full and is the part of this item that is easy to leave half-done, because none of it is reachable from the crate that owns the table: the column coverage list, an exporter, an importer, both driver lists, and the round-trip fixture that must insert at least one row per table. Expect nomos-spec-store to stay green through all of it while the bundle is still incomplete. Coverage is proved from an in-repo fixture, not from either corpus. THIS ITEM DOES NOT TURN THE TWO CORPUS TESTS GREEN and must not be judged as though it should: restoration.rs and siblings.rs go green only when the corpora themselves carry declarations, and the corpora live outside this repository and are not territory any item here can reserve. Implementing the mechanism cannot make an undeclared corpus compliant. Neither file is edited and no count is pinned into either. The rule consulting these rows is the separate item that depends on this one, so nothing here changes what NSV-PRESERVE-004 reports. VERIFICATION SCOPE: the predicate is the three crates this item changes, selected as lib plus the named integration targets that judge transport, so that it excludes nomos-spec-ingest tests restoration.rs and siblings.rs, which are red by design and are not this item's obligation. That exclusion is the convention step 3 of the task skill carries.

items.title: NSV-PRESERVE-004 cannot consult a repetition declaration, so declaring one would change nothing
items.why: OD-SPEC-004 version 3 decided that a block appearing in the places its declaration names is admitted and is not filler, while a further undeclared occurrence of that same block is still a violation. The carrier item makes the declaration into rows a rule can read. This item is the half that makes reading them change an answer, and it is deliberately separate because the two have different failure boundaries: changing the store and bundle schema fails at transport and is proved by a round trip, while teaching one rule to read those rows fails at judgement and is proved by what the rule reports. Landing the carrier alone would leave a corpus able to declare its layout and a rule that still calls it a form letter.

The blocklist keeps its separate job and is not extended: Get_Filler_Pattern still names which known pattern a template matched for a lineage row, and a declared block is admitted without being called filler, so no lineage row is made to assert something false about it. items.title: NSV-PRESERVE-004 has no minimum length, so 102 connectives and a horizontal rule are form letters
items.why: OD-SPEC-004 version 3 decided that repetition is necessary and not sufficient evidence of filler, and question one of that amendment is the length floor. Measured 2026-09-14 over the sibling suites, 18,873 subjects: NSV-PRESERVE-004 reports 103 violations and 102 of them are 30 characters or fewer. The largest single contributor is three characters of horizontal rule carried by 562 sections across 2 documents; the rest are ordinary connectives and labels, among them a single downward arrow at 9 sections, and Or, or:, So:, LLM, KWB, Add:, Use:, Bad:, Why?, Then:, Good:, Example:, For example: at 148. The rule groups prose blocks by normalized hash and has no eligibility test at all, so in any corpus of ordinary authored prose short fragments collide and every collision is reported as an undeclared form letter. The amendment derives the floor rather than guessing it: the longest accidental collision observed is 30 characters, the shortest body repeated by design is 43, the shortest entry in FILLER_PATTERNS is 50 and Get_Filler_Pattern is substring containment so every block this repository has ever declared to be filler is at least that long. The distribution is empty between 31 and 42 in both corpora and the record fixes the floor at 36. This replaces an item whose territory could not carry the change: the helper must be nameable from nomos-spec-validate, archaeology is a private module, and the re-export lives in src/lib.rs, which the first item did not reserve.
items.done_when: A prose block shorter than the floor is not eligible to be a template, and the floor is 36 characters of normalized block text as OD-SPEC-004 version 3 fixes it. The threshold lives beside SHARED_BY rather than in the rule, because the rule already documents that the value it enforces and the value archaeology Shared_Templates reports over a revision pair must stay one constant and not two numbers somebody has to notice disagree; census.rs and sections.rs both apply it or the item has created exactly that divergence. That is also why src/lib.rs is reserved: archaeology is private, so without the re-export the rule cannot name the helper and the two would have to be written twice. Length is counted over normalized text and in characters, so one arrow is one character. Boundary tests assert both sides from the measurement rather than from round numbers: a body of 30 characters repeated five times is not a violation, a body of 43 characters repeated three times is, and a body of exactly the floor is decided explicitly rather than left to an off-by-one. THE EXISTING UNDECLARED FIXTURE IS REPAIRED IN THE SAME COMMIT: it repeats a 14-character body, which the floor makes ineligible, so left alone it would keep passing while proving nothing -- the rule dismissing it for length and the test reading that as the rule working. It must repeat something above the floor and must assert its own length so the same thing cannot recur quietly. The sibling measurement is re-run with both corpora exported and the new count is reported in the commit message; it is expected to fall from 103 to 1, the survivor being a 51-character status line that is question two of the amendment and not this item to fix. items.title: A gate comparison cannot say whether its two runs were judged alike
items.why:
Compare_Gate_Runs reports added, removed and changed findings between two runs and says nothing about whether the two were judged by the same instrument. A caller reads a difference as a fact about the repository, because that is what a gate is for. It is only that when every judgment input other than the source was compatible, and nothing checks or records that.

Measured 2026-09-14 against the tree, and the measurement narrowed the scope rather than confirming a plan.

What can actually differ between the two sides today, through nomos's own hosts: the effective gate policy, because Run_Gate resolves nomos-gate.json from command.root and compare judges two roots, so the CLI's own promise that every other flag narrows both sides alike does not reach it -- a policy file is not a flag. And which capabilities could be materialized at each root: P106 measured a probe tree where a missing deny.toml left dependency-policy unmaterialized, which changed both the findings and the claim, so two roots differing only in that produce different findings for a reason that is not the code.

What can differ through the published library surface but not through nomos's own hosts: the whole GateCommand, since Handle_Gate_Compare takes two independent ones and its own module doc names one tree under two policies as an intended case -- a narrower rules.include means that side did not look, and its absent findings are reported as added on the other. And BuildVariant and now, both GateEnvironment fields a caller supplies per Run_Gate call, with Compare_Gate_Runs public and taking two results; nomos's hosts pass one variant and one clock to both sides, and the crate publishes no constraint saying a caller must.

What cannot differ yet: the nomos build and the provider binaries, because OD-GATE-022-A has compare re-derive both runs in one process. Those arrive when a run outlives its process, which that record defers and this one does not schedule.

GateRunResult records none of it. It carries run, root, check_outcome, findings, disposition, unmatched_policy and no_verdict, and not the command, the variant, the policy, the moment, or which rules could look.

The vocabulary for this already exists and is published. nomos-contracts' domain table puts the analysis kernel -- facts, checks, findings -- at StateTemporal, CrossPlatform, BitIdentical. StateTemporal makes time a declared judgment input, and it is one: a temporary waiver expires against the run's own moment. CrossPlatform is strictly weaker than CrossBinary, so the table already says findings are not claimed to reproduce across builds of the tool, which is exactly the claim a cross-binary comparison would need.
items.done_when:
OD-GATE-031 is authored and registered, and decides three things.

What comparability means, as the invariant a person stated: a difference between two runs may be attributed to repository state only when the non-source judgment inputs were compatible, or their differences are explicitly represented. Never by the absence of evidence that they differed.

The minimum identity a run must carry for that question to be answerable at all, derived from the measurement rather than from the long-term shape: what can differ today, what cannot yet, and which of the two the identity is sized for. The record states explicitly which components it is NOT adding and why -- a provider-binary version cannot differ between two same-process runs, so recording one now would be shape ahead of a body.

That a missing or unknown provenance resolves to incomparable rather than to compatible, for the reason Applicability already keeps MissingCapability apart from a clean result and OD-GATE-030 refuses to claim continuity it cannot show: nothing could look must never read as nothing was wrong.

The record is explicit about what it does not decide: it does not schedule the run history OD-GATE-022-A defers, does not reopen OD-GATE-030's baseline continuity, and builds no mechanism. It names the follow-up items' territory precisely enough to author them and no more.

Both projections are re-rendered from a worktree holding exactly the records this commit publishes, per OD-GATE-005, and both freshness checks exit 0.

items.title: A run discards every input that decided its own judgment
items.why:
OD-GATE-031 decided that a run carries the identity of what judged it, sized to the four inputs that can differ between two sides of a comparison today, and built no mechanism. This is the value half: without it, the comparability verdict has nothing to read.

Every component is already inside Run_Gate and already discarded. The walked source is a parameter. BuildVariant and the run's moment are GateEnvironment fields. The rule selector and the scope selector are GateCommand fields. The effective policy is computed a few lines above the return. GateRunResult keeps none of them, so a finished run cannot say what judged it even though the function that produced it held all five.

Measured 2026-09-14 so the territory is right before it is written rather than after. GateRunResult has five construction sites: one in gate_environment.rs, one in gate_compare.rs and three in nomos-cli's report tests, which a new field breaks and which a compile lists in one pass. A new public type additionally needs the module that re-exports its neighbours (gate_plan.rs) and the crate root (lib.rs), neither of which a compile finds for you: the first shows up as a private-type-in-public-field error, and the second fails nothing at all -- build, clippy and test are all green while the surface snapshot silently omits the type. P106 paid for that lesson across three separate items in one session; this one reserves the whole chain up front.

Digest_Of_Parts length-prefixes every part, so a digest over an ordered sequence is injective across part boundaries rather than a concatenation that can collide. nomos_rules::DESCRIPTORS is a static table carrying each rule's id, contract record and contract record version, which is the same content Registered copies into its offers, so the instrument is computable without composing a registry and without a second failure path in Run_Gate.
items.done_when:
GateRunProvenance exists, carrying the five components OD-GATE-031 named and no others: the source judged, the effective policy judged under, the selection judged with, the instrument, and the moment. The first four are digests over ordered, length-prefixed parts; the moment is the Timestamp itself, because a moment is not an identity and a reader comparing two runs wants to see which was later.

Run_Gate fills every one from what it already holds. The source from each walked file's path and text. The policy from the effective GatePolicyFile after the declared file was resolved over the command, not from the command alone, so a difference in either shows. The selection from the rule selector and both halves of the scope selector. The instrument from BuildVariant's target, profile, toolchain and features together with every entry of nomos_rules::DESCRIPTORS.

GateRunResult::provenance is Option, and Run_Gate always fills Some. None is what an unknown run carries -- one built by hand, or one that a later increment reads back from a store that predates this field -- and OD-GATE-031 decided it resolves to incomparable rather than to compatible. Representing it is this item's job; acting on it is the comparison item's.

Proved by measurement rather than by construction: two runs over the same tree with different nomos-gate.json files produce different policy digests and identical source digests, and two runs differing only in rule selection produce different selection digests and identical everything else. A run repeated with the same inputs produces the same digests. At least one test drives Run_Gate over a real root rather than over a constructed value, since that is the function whose discarding is the defect.

No verdict is computed here and Compare_Gate_Runs is unchanged except for whatever a new field costs its own construction site. The headless response and the CLI rendering are their own items.

items.title: The task skill reads a predicted territory as authoritative and a new guard as covered
items.why:
Two disciplines in the task skill each acquired a third measured instance in one session, and neither of the two sentences that would have to change has changed.

Territory. Step 3 already says territory follows the acceptance predicate's dependency cone rather than the sites where the failure appears, and both instances it cites were authored before that rule existed. The third happened under it, authored and worked by the session that wrote it, actively applying it, and it was still wrong twice. The first escape was a re-export: the helper the predicate's own rule had to call lived in a private module, so nothing outside the crate could name it, and the file carrying the module declaration was not reserved. The skill warns about exactly that in the abstract, two paragraphs above, and the warning did not produce the reservation. The second escape was two fixtures whose bodies the new invariant invalidated -- they would have gone on passing while proving nothing, so leaving them was not an option and editing them was outside the reservation. Neither file was reachable by grepping what the predicate reads. Both were produced by running the change and reading what broke.

That does not falsify the rule. A reservation is a concurrency claim and it still has to be made before any editing, or two sessions collide. What it falsifies is the reading that a statically derived reservation is the answer rather than a proposal: the predicted cone and the actual cone differ, and the difference is only visible after the attempt.

Guards. The same increment introduced a shared eligibility predicate and mutated it five ways to prove the tests held it. Three of the five killed nothing. Two of the three applications of the threshold had no falsifier at all -- every other fixture in those modules repeated a body far past it, so removing the filter moved no test, and the divergence between the rule and the report that the shared threshold exists to prevent was unprotected while looking covered. The third was worse: a test written in the same increment specifically to pin that eligibility is counted over normalized text was vacuous, because both its fixtures cleared the threshold whichever length was counted, so it agreed with the implementation it was written to exclude. Three tests were added and the mutations then killed the right one each.

The shape is the same in both halves. There is a test and there is a test that would fail without this are different claims, and only the second is evidence -- which is the thing this repository already refuses to accept one level down, in a rule about corpora that pass having read nothing.
items.done_when:
Step 3 of the task skill states that a predicted territory is provisional until execution validates it, and says what validating it means. The reservation is still authored first and still derived from the acceptance predicate's dependency cone -- that paragraph is not weakened, because the claim has to exist before the editing does. What is added is that the derivation is a proposal: before finishing, the set actually required is compared against the set reserved, and an escape stops the finish rather than being absorbed into it.

The skill says what actually required means, because the cheap reading of it is wrong. It is the minimal set of files required for the change to be truthful and verified, which is not the same as the set that was edited: a fixture whose assumption the change invalidated is required whether or not anybody edited it, and so is a module declaration that visibility forces, a snapshot a moved surface stales, and a dependent item's acceptance condition the change falsified. Naming those four kinds is the point, since each of them is a thing a diff of edited files does not report.

The skill says what an escape costs today, honestly: there is no widen verb, so the answer is abandon, decline and re-author, which strands dependents and is why the cost is worth stating rather than glossing. It does not promise one is coming.

Step 7 carries the second principle where it bites: a guard owns a falsifier. When an increment introduces a filter, a threshold, a normalization rule, an exclusion or any other predicate, at least one test must distinguish the guarded implementation from the same implementation with that predicate removed or inverted -- and every site the guard is applied at owns its own, because a shared threshold applied in three places has three ways to diverge and one passing test about the first says nothing about the other two. The measured instance is stated, since three of five is the evidence and a rule without it is an opinion.

The frontmatter description moves too. It currently promises the skill makes an item's territory right the first time, which is the claim this item exists to retract.

No item identifier appears anywhere in the new text. The harness derives every identifier a skill names and fails on one that is not declared as a temporary hazard, the declared list is empty, and it is empty on purpose.

No mechanism is built and no governing record is written. This is authoring discipline for the board, and the record becomes the right authority level if the ledger ever computes or validates a cone itself, which is a different thing from telling an author to measure one.

items.title: A territory that execution proves insufficient costs the whole item
items.why:
A reservation is authored before the change is attempted, so it is a prediction, and a prediction is sometimes wrong by one file. The ledger has no proportionate answer to that. Territory is immutable under claim and there is no widen verb, so the only route is abandon, decline and re-author -- and declining an item strands every dependent, each of which must itself be declined and re-authored against the replacement identifier.

Measured 2026-09-14 on one item, which was declined three times for exactly this. The first escape was the crate root: the helper the item's own rule had to call sat in a private module, so nothing outside the crate could name it, and the file carrying the module declaration was not reserved. The second was two fixtures whose bodies the change made vacuous -- leaving them would have left two tests passing for a reason that was no longer the one they claimed, and editing them was outside the reservation. Neither was reachable by grepping what the predicate reads. Both appeared only when the change was run. The third attempt reserved what an actual build and test run named, and held.

The cost was not the editing. It was five ledger transitions and a dependent re-authored twice, for work whose only defect was that one file it legitimately had to touch could not be predicted before the attempt.

The immutability is not the defect and must survive. A holder who could rewrite their own reservation could take a path a peer holds, and the exclusion check would never be asked. What is wrong is that the refusal is total rather than proportionate: the ledger answers a request to add one path by ending the item.

There is a second loss, and it is the one that compounds. The board cannot say how often a predicted cone escapes its reservation. A decline stores a holder, a timestamp and free prose, so the number is not derivable and a stated one would be a figure nobody could check. The task skill now instructs an author to compare the actual cone against the reservation before finishing; nothing anywhere records the answer. A widening that is refused into a decline is evidence destroyed at the moment it is produced.

The territory below is large because a field added to an item breaks every site that constructs one. Measured rather than estimated: 29 files across five crates construct a LedgerItem, two further matches in nomos-spec-ingest are an unrelated Filler.displaced and are excluded, and a compile lists the real set in one pass. Reserving the whole chain up front is deliberate -- this is the item whose subject is what an under-reservation costs, and discovering its own escape mid-claim would cost exactly what it exists to describe.
items.done_when:
A holder can widen the territory of an item they hold, and can only widen it. The verb is authored beside the others rather than as a special case of add, because add allocates and this does not.

Each refusal has its own test and none of them is a message check:

- A widening whose new paths overlap a live claim is refused, through the same exclusion check a claim goes through -- called and not copied, so a widening cannot come to a different answer about contention than a claim would. This is the refusal the whole verb has to earn and it is the one that must not be weakened by any later convenience.
- A widening by anybody who is not the current holder is refused.
- A widening of an item that is not claimed, or that is done, or that is declined, is refused.
- A narrowing is refused. Widen takes paths to add; it does not take a replacement territory. Dropping a path drops the done_when clause that path carried, which this repository has already recorded as a rule, and a verb that accepted a whole new territory would make narrowing a typo away.

The widening is recorded on the item rather than merged into the territory silently: which paths were added, by which holder, at what moment. That record is the measurement the board cannot make today, and it is what lets an escape be counted without anybody reading a decline's prose. A widening that leaves the territory correct and the history empty does not satisfy this item.

The schema moves to 6 and every item on the board carries the new field after the same commit. That is not discretionary: a test counts the keys on a serialized item, so a field arriving without the bump is a refusal that misstates why. The field carries no serde default, for the reason kind and origin carry none -- a defaulting field is dropped silently by an older build, and dropping a recorded widening on shared coordination state is the stale-writer defect with a new field name. An older build must refuse the file outright instead. work/ledger.json is deliberately not reserved: reserving the board would block every other claim, and the migration is an obligation stated here rather than an exclusion.

show reports every widening with its paths and its holder. list does not gain a column, because list is one line per item and this is prose.

README.md carries the verb in the reference the contract routes to, and .claude/skills/nomos-task/SKILL.md loses the sentence saying no widen verb exists, which this item makes false. The skill keeps the rest of that paragraph unchanged: the comparison before finishing is still required, and a cheaper repair is not a reason to reserve carelessly.

items.title: A comparison ignores the provenance its two runs now carry
items.why:
A run now records what judged it and Compare_Gate_Runs still ignores it. OD-GATE-031's invariant is that a difference may be attributed to repository state only when the non-source judgment inputs were compatible or their differences are explicitly represented, and a comparison that never reads the provenance satisfies neither half. The value exists and nothing acts on it, which is the state OD-ANALYSIS-012 and OD-RULES-011 have both been filed about before: a schema is not a feature.

Concretely, the false story is unchanged until this lands. Comparing two checkouts compares two nomos-gate.json files, because Run_Gate resolves the policy from command.root; every finding that moved bucket for that reason still reads as movement in the code. Handle_Gate_Compare still accepts two independent GateCommands, so a narrower rules.include on one side still reports its missing findings as added on the other.

Measured 2026-09-14 for territory, before writing rather than after. GateCompareResult is re-exported from lib.rs directly with no intermediate module, so the orchestration export chain is one file. The headless twin needs a file of its own under response/, which that module's doc requires of every twin serializing one field of a response, plus response.rs and the crate root list -- the chain P106 paid for across three items and which this one reserves up front. Both surface snapshots move.
items.done_when:
Compare_Gate_Runs reports its own comparability, in the three states OD-GATE-031 named, and GateCompareResult carries it.

Compatible when both sides recorded a provenance and their policy, selection and instrument all agree: a difference is then a difference in the repository and may be read as one.

Compatible with stated differences when both recorded one and something other than the source differed, naming which of the three it was, so a reader attributes the change themselves rather than being told a story.

Incomparable when either side does not say what judged it, naming the run or runs that did not. OD-GATE-031 decided that unknown provenance resolves here rather than to compatible.

It qualifies rather than refuses, and the item says why in the code: the findings diff is still real information, and P106 established the principle one verb over -- refusing the verdict is not refusing the answer. A refusal would throw away what the caller asked for in order to report something about it.

The moment is deliberately not classified as a difference, and the reason is written down rather than left as an omission. Two runs essentially always have different moments, so reporting that as a discrepancy on every comparison is noise that teaches a reader to skip the line that matters; and deciding whether a moment difference could have changed anything needs to know whether a waiver expired between them, which the identity carries a digest of rather than the policy itself. A caller holds both runs and can read both moments. What this item must not do is imply the moments were equal.

Both surfaces show it. nomos-cli's compare rendering states the comparability before the differences it found, because a reader who takes the diff at face value has already been misled by the time they reach a footnote. The headless response carries it as a twin in a file of its own. Neither exit code changes: comparability is not a verdict, and compare is still clean whenever both sides were judged.

Proved over real runs rather than constructed ones for at least the policy case, since resolving two policies from two roots is the mechanism that makes this reachable through this workspace's own hosts. Both surface snapshots are re-blessed and confirmed green without the variable.

items.title: A territory that execution proves insufficient costs the whole item
items.why:
A reservation is authored before the change is attempted, so it is a prediction, and a prediction is sometimes wrong by one file. The ledger has no proportionate answer to that. Territory is immutable under claim and there is no widen verb, so the only route is abandon, decline and re-author -- and declining an item strands every dependent, each of which must itself be declined and re-authored against the replacement identifier.

Measured 2026-09-14 on one item, which was declined three times for exactly this. The first escape was the crate root: the helper the item's own rule had to call sat in a private module, so nothing outside the crate could name it, and the file carrying the module declaration was not reserved. The second was two fixtures whose bodies the change made vacuous -- leaving them would have left two tests passing for a reason that was no longer the one they claimed, and editing them was outside the reservation. Neither was reachable by grepping what the predicate reads. Both appeared only when the change was run. The third attempt reserved what an actual build and test run named, and held.

The cost was not the editing. It was five ledger transitions and a dependent re-authored twice, for work whose only defect was that one file it legitimately had to touch could not be predicted before the attempt.

The immutability is not the defect and must survive. A holder who could rewrite their own reservation could take a path a peer holds, and the exclusion check would never be asked. What is wrong is that the refusal is total rather than proportionate: the ledger answers a request to add one path by ending the item.

There is a second loss, and it is the one that compounds. The board cannot say how often a predicted cone escapes its reservation. A decline stores a holder, a timestamp and free prose, so the number is not derivable and a stated one would be a figure nobody could check. The task skill now instructs an author to compare the actual cone against the reservation before finishing; nothing anywhere records the answer. A widening that is refused into a decline is evidence destroyed at the moment it is produced.

The territory below is large because a field added to an item breaks every site that constructs one. Measured rather than estimated: 29 files across five crates construct a LedgerItem, two further matches in nomos-spec-ingest are an unrelated Filler.displaced and are excluded, and a compile lists the real set in one pass. Reserving the whole chain up front is deliberate -- this is the item whose subject is what an under-reservation costs, and discovering its own escape mid-claim would cost exactly what it exists to describe.
items.done_when:
A holder can widen the territory of an item they hold, and can only widen it. The verb is authored beside the others rather than as a special case of add, because add allocates and this does not.

# One mutation, not a check followed by a write

Load, holder check, enlarged territory, exclusion against every other live claim, history append, territory replacement, whole-ledger validation and the write are one mutation inside one lock acquisition, through the same guarded path the fourth board-changing verb uses. OD-LEDGER-015 is the record of what the other three cost by deciding outside the lock, and this is the fifth.

Calling the same exclusion the claim called is necessary and is not the invariant. Two simultaneous widenings can each observe a board on which their own new paths are free and jointly create the overlap the check exists to prevent, and no amount of sharing the function fixes that. Atomicity is the property, and it owns a falsifier: a test in which a second widening interleaved between the first one's read and its write is refused rather than applied.

The exclusion is re-run against the board as it is at widen time, never inherited from the claim. Independence was established when the claim was granted and the board has moved since.

# What is refused, each with its own test

- A widening whose new paths overlap a live claim, through the exclusion check a claim goes through -- called and not copied, so a widening cannot come to a different answer about contention than a claim would. This is the refusal the whole verb has to earn.
- A widening by anybody who is not the current holder.
- A widening of an item that is not claimed, or that is done, or that is declined.
- A widening by a holder whose lease has run out. This is the boundary case and it is not covered by the holder check: the name still matches and the claim is still on the item. store/refusal.rs already records that a lapsed claim stops excluding, so another item may since have been claimed over exactly the files this one reserves -- a lapsed holder enlarging a reservation that currently excludes nobody is that hazard reached through a new verb. The authorization test is therefore liveness, not name equality: Has_Active_Claim is already false once the lease has gone, and a name match on a dead lease must authorize nothing. A lapsed holder is told to take the item over first.
- A narrowing. Widen takes paths to add; it does not take a replacement territory. Dropping a path drops the done_when clause that path carried, which this repository has already recorded as a rule, and a verb accepting a whole new territory would put narrowing one typo away.

# The widening is recorded, not merged silently

Which paths were added, by which holder, at what moment, kept on the item the way a displaced claim is kept. That record is the measurement the board cannot make today: it is what lets an escape be counted without anybody reading a decline's prose, and it is the only evidence that would ever justify computing a dependency cone rather than predicting one. A widening that leaves the territory correct and the history empty does not satisfy this item.

# Compatibility, stated as two directions with two mechanisms

The schema moves to 6 and every item on the board carries the new field after the same commit. The record states both directions separately and names the mechanism for each, because attributing either to the other is how a guard comes to rest on something that does not hold it.

An older build meeting schema 6 is refused by deny_unknown_fields on LedgerItem, which is mechanical and applies to any new field. The version probe in store/document.rs is consulted after that refusal and never to decide whether to refuse; its whole job is to make the operator read Unrecognized rather than Malformed. The protection is therefore not the version bump, and OD-LEDGER-008 is why that matters: a field once arrived without the number moving, so a guard resting on the bump would report clean on the next instance of the defect it was built for. A forgotten bump costs a sentence and cannot cost a field.

A newer build meeting schema 5 is refused by the absent serde default on the missing key. That is what the absent default is for, and it is the opposite direction: it makes every historical item be migrated rather than silently read as one that was never widened. kind and origin carry none for the same reason.

The bump itself is still not discretionary -- a test counts the keys on a serialized item -- but the done_when does not claim it protects anything.

work/ledger.json is deliberately not reserved: reserving the board would block every other claim, and the migration is an obligation stated here rather than an exclusion.

# The rest of the surface

show reports every widening with its paths and its holder. list does not gain a column, because list is one line per item and this is prose.

README.md carries the verb in the reference the contract routes to, and .claude/skills/nomos-task/SKILL.md loses the sentence saying no widen verb exists, which this item makes false. The skill keeps the rest of that paragraph unchanged: the comparison before finishing is still required, and a cheaper repair is not a reason to reserve carelessly.

OD-LEDGER-039 records the decision, since every previous field on an item came with one and the semantic is the load-bearing part: territory is a concurrency claim that its holder may enlarge, under the same exclusion the claim was granted under, while the claim is still live, and the enlargement is durable history. The record says explicitly that this is not cone inference -- nothing here infers, validates or proposes a dependency cone, and an author still measures.

Not closed by a verb that mutates territory without recording the mutation, by one that accepts a replacement territory, by one that decides outside the lock, or by one that authorizes a holder whose lease has gone.

Declined.reason:
One clause missing, and it is the clause that decides whether the mechanism is worth having.

The done_when required the record to say the verb is not cone inference, and said nothing about the other direction it can decay in: a cheap repair makes reserving loosely and discovering territory incrementally the path of least resistance, which would destroy the measurement the item exists to create. An escape rate means nothing unless the reservations it is measured against were genuine attempts. The skill half of that was already required -- a cheaper repair is not a reason to reserve carelessly -- but the record and the verb's own help text were not bound by it, and the record is what governs.

Re-authored as -3 carrying the why, the territory and the predicate unchanged, with the OD-LEDGER-039 paragraph stating both things the verb is not. No dependents to strand.

This is the second decline of a ready, unclaimed item in this session whose work and territory were right and whose done_when was not. Recorded here so the population is countable from the board rather than asserted, since the question of whether the ledger should be able to amend an item's terms is one an observed count should decide and not an anecdote.

items.title: gate explain answers against a policy no real run uses
items.why: Explain_Gate reads command.adoption, command.suppressions and command.baseline and never resolves the declared nomos-gate.json, while Run_Gate resolves it and prefers the command over it. Every caller passes those three empty: crates/host/nomos-cli/src/gate/parsing.rs lines 183 to 185 hardcode all three to default, and nomos-api's Handle_Gate_Explain documents itself as using the default GateCommand narrowed only by root. So explain always answers as if nothing is tolerated. Measured 2026-09-14 against the built binary on a probe tree declaring one baseline entry: gate run reports that finding baselined and exits 0, and gate explain on the same finding in the same tree reports would block true and exits 1. Two verbs of one product contradict each other about one tree, and the tolerated side is the one a repository adopted on purpose. The function's own doc states the intent this defeats, saying those three fields are consulted because whether any applies is part of the finding's own explanation.
items.done_when: Explain_Gate resolves the declared policy under command.root and prefers the command's own policies over it, by the same Resolve_Gate_Policy plus Resolved_Over composition Run_Gate performs, so explain and run answer alike about one tree. A test in finding_query.rs's own tests module builds a scratch root holding only a nomos-gate.json with one baseline entry, passes the existing phantom-mirror source as walked, and asserts the explanation reports the finding as baselined and not blocking. That test fails before the change and passes after. The predicate deliberately does not reach tests/check_orchestration_seam.rs, this crate's integration seam, which is a separate obligation, nor the host crates' explain tests, which are unaffected because no tree they judge declares a policy file.

items.title: baseline tolerance is unbounded, and the record names the wrong first increment
items.why: OD-GATE-030 names a snapshot identity on the entry as the first buildable increment toward honest adoption. Measured 2026-09-14 against the built binary, that is the wrong first increment and it would close nothing. A baseline entry is keyed on rule and subject, and a file's subject is the digest of its normalized path rather than its content, so the entry survives every content change by construction. A snapshot digest would therefore prove continuity only while the tree is byte-identical to adoption, which is true until the first commit after adopting and false forever after. What it would not touch is the defect that is live now: adopt one entry for one violation, fix that violation, write five new ones in the same file, and a run reports five baselined and exits 0. The tolerance a repository granted for one occurrence is unbounded in quantity, which is the hiding failure this record says a gate exists to prevent. A count closes that without any of the machinery the record defers: if a scope accepted N occurrences and a run observes M greater than N, then at least M minus N of them cannot belong to the adopted population. That is exact rather than a line-age or diff-age proxy, needs no run history, needs no cross-revision occurrence matching, and is stable under reformatting, which is the objection FindingOccurrenceId's own doc raises against giving baseline occurrence scope.
items.done_when: The record is at version 2 and decides bounded baseline capacity: an adopted baseline records the maximum occurrence population accepted for a rule and subject scope, a later run may tolerate no more than that quantity, and an observed population above the accepted count is a baseline expansion the baseline must not hide. It states, in its own words rather than by implication, that a count establishes neither occurrence continuity, persistence nor reintroduction, and that those stay unresolved until historical identity evidence exists, so a reader cannot take the new bound for partial reintroduction detection. It refuses per-finding attribution within an exceeded population explicitly, because choosing which occurrences are the historical ones would manufacture the evidence the record says nobody has. It decides migration semantics for entries authored before the count existed rather than leaving them to become silently unlimited. It corrects its own What Would Make Continuity Provable list, where step 1 currently names the wrong artifact. It keeps the existing addressing scopes intact, and it names IdentityTransitionKind as the vocabulary a later continuity increment reuses rather than reinventing. The projections are re-rendered from a worktree holding exactly the records this commit publishes, per OD-GATE-005, and all four halves are committed with it.

items.title: A reservation that decayed under a peer's refactor is reported by nothing
items.why:
Territory is authored once and the tree moves under it. A reservation names repository paths; a peer's refactor renames or splits those files; the reservation is then false while continuing to look exactly like a correct one. Nothing reports that.

This is not under-reservation and it is not an authoring error. The author predicted the cone correctly and the prediction was invalidated afterwards by somebody else's commit, which is why it is worth a separate mechanism from anything about how territory is predicted.

Measured, and the measurement is already on this board rather than newly assembled. The decline of P11-AMEND-TERRITORY records it in full: the item reserved crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/store.rs, which held both the guard it was changing and the refusal wording its done_when required to change, and that was correct when it was authored. The commit ef1c93f, Give every substrate type its own file, moved AddRefusal into its own file. The guard stayed reserved and the sentence an author reads did not, so the item could implement half its done_when and could not satisfy the clause it had been reissued to carry. It was found while holding the claim, after the work had started.

The same decline states the population rather than the instance: the three refactor commits 43c5a63 to ef1c93f split 49 files into 99, and eight open items reserved a file that was split -- P11-EXEC-IDLE, P10-DECLINED-DEPENDENCY, P11-DISPATCH-SPLIT, P11-NEXT-WORK, P11-ITEM-DISCRIMINANT, P11-PREFERENCE-STRENGTH, P11-INVALIDATION-ORDER and that item. It says the failure mode is not specific to that item and is live, and no item was ever opened for it: searched 2026-09-14 across every item's title, why and done_when, and the twenty-five that mention a split or a rename are items that happened to involve one, not items about reservations going stale.

work audit is the verb that already answers this shape of question and it does not answer this one. Verified 2026-09-14 by running it: it reported a stranded item behind a declined dependency and a waiting item behind an unfinished one, exit 0, and said nothing about any reserved path. So the gap is a missing check inside an existing verb rather than a missing verb, and the composition root already holds what it needs -- crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work.rs takes a FileSystem and a root directory and already walks the record directory through it, and crates/host/nomos-api/src/work/audit_response.rs takes a directory too.
items.done_when:
work audit reports, for every item that could still be worked, each reserved path that is not in the tree. Done and declined items are not reported: their territory is history and a stale path in it is not debt.

# Detection only

The report says what it found and nothing else. It does not infer a replacement path, propose a widening, edit the item, add a field to it, or read git history. Whether the repair is a widening, a re-authoring or closing the item is a judgment about the work, and the caller is the one holding the context that decides it.

# The report must not claim to know which case it is

An absent reserved path is ambiguous and the ambiguity is not resolvable from the board. An item that reserves a file it is going to create is indistinguishable, by existence alone, from one whose file a peer moved. Both are real: P103-A-TERRITORY-EXECUTION-PROVES-INSUFFICIENT-COSTS-THE-WHOLE-ITEM-3 reserves crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/tests/widening_is_recorded.rs, which does not exist because that item creates it.

So the finding is authored as absent rather than as decayed, and the wording states both readings. A report that called the first case decay would be wrong on a board that already contains one, and an author who learned the report cries wolf would stop reading it -- which costs more than the check is worth. A test drives both shapes against one board and asserts the finding does not distinguish them, so a later change that starts guessing fails here.

# Where it lives

Both hosts render audit and neither may grow its own copy of the check. Blocking_Refusal was lifted into crates/host/nomos-cli/src/work/report.rs and is called by the CLI; the headless answer is crates/host/nomos-api/src/work/audit_response.rs. Whatever computes absent reserved paths is one function both reach, in the crate that owns territory, not two agreeing implementations.

Threading a root and a FileSystem into the audit path is expected and is this item's cost to pay: the verb currently answers from the document alone, and the question cannot be answered without the tree. It uses the FileSystem the composition root already chooses rather than std::fs, because that is what OD-HOST-001 decided and what makes the check testable against a constructed tree.

# What it is not

Not closed by a check that reports absent paths on done or declined items, which would bury the live findings under the board's whole history. Not closed by a check that runs during claim or add and refuses -- reserving a file you are about to create is legitimate and refusing it would break the ordinary case to report an occasional one. Not closed by making audit exit non-zero on an absent path: audit reports and does not fail today, a stale reservation is not a reason to stop a run, and changing the exit code would make every caller that branches on it start treating board debt as an error.

No record. This adds a report to an existing verb and decides nothing about what territory means.

items.title: The security rules decide what is test material from an eight-clause hardcoded path convention, so a repository that files fixtures elsewhere gets false credential findings
items.why: Auditing all 42 SourceText rules for repository-specific criteria found exactly one family. Is_Test_Or_Fixture_Source in security_text.rs matches tests/, /tests/, /test/, /testdata/, /fixtures/, /examples/, _test.rs, _tests.rs and _test.go, and the three security rules all exempt a source on that basis; rust_text.rs carries the same notion independently in its unwrap-outside-tests-and-examples wording. Some clauses are toolchain-fixed and portable: Cargo owns tests/ and examples/, Go owns _test.go. testdata and fixtures are neither, they are a project convention. A repository filing its fixtures under resources or spec or samples is judged as if a fixture credential were a real one, and an exemption that is too narrow produces false positives rather than misses, which is the damaging direction for a security rule.
items.done_when: What counts as test material reaches the security rules as a declared criterion rather than a path list compiled into security_text.rs, composed from the toolchain-fixed clauses plus whatever the repository declares, so that stable Cargo and Go semantics do not become configuration. It uses whichever declaration path P100-...-8 establishes rather than inventing a second one. A repository declaring nothing keeps today behaviour. A repository declaring its own fixture locations has them exempted, proved against a fixture whose test material sits under none of the nine current clauses. rust_text.rs stops carrying a second independent notion of the same thing.

Declined.reason:
Superseded by P100-WHAT-COUNTS-AS-TEST-MATERIAL-IS-A-HARDCODED-PATH-CONVENTION-INSIDE-THE-SECURITY-RULES-8, which carries the same title, why, done_when and dependency over a measured territory. Nothing had executed; the cone was measured 2026-09-15 before claiming, which is what this item's predecessor's decline directed in its own words: measure the cone before editing and expect to re-author if it escapes. It escapes by roughly an order of magnitude, so this is the re-authoring.

The measurement. The done_when's first clause requires what counts as test material to reach the three security checks as a declared criterion rather than a path list compiled into security_text.rs, and its second requires whichever declaration path the architecture item established rather than a second one. OD-RULES-029 fixes the kind of fact: a repository's policy parameters are an OD-RULES-011 family parameterizing a judgment the rule keeps making, and this is one, so it is deliberately not a description that joins nomos-architecture.json. OD-HOST-009 fixes where it travels: not standards.json, which code-standards decodes with unknown fields disallowed, but a dedicated language-neutral file at the repository root, the convention nomos-gate.json and nomos-architecture.json already set. Those two together make the work a sixth OD-RULES-011 family.

The precedent is P100-THE-ARCHITECTURE-A-RULE-JUDGES-IS-COMPILED-INTO-THE-RULE-CRATE-INSTEAD-OF-DECLARED-BY-THE-REPOSITORY-8, the structurally identical item, which shipped at 52 paths across seven crates with a 3600-second predicate: a capability contract crate, a provider module in nomos-repo-policy, a materializer in nomos-check-orchestration, a rule reading through nomos_analysis::FactReader, the workspace entries, the contract tests' enumerations, surface snapshots, and a repository-root carrier with a fixture carrying one. Measured against that, a reservation of two files in nomos-rules is short by an order of magnitude and not by a file.

Widening was refused deliberately, and the refusal is this item's own record's, not a preference. OD-LEDGER-039 says a widening is an evidence-backed repair for the case where execution disproves a prediction and is not the first move of an incremental discovery of territory, and warns that a board on which widening is routine has lost the measurement rather than gained a convenience. No execution occurred, and a twenty-eight-path enlargement discovered from a document rather than from a build is exactly the discovery that record refuses. The verb is also unavailable without first claiming a territory already known to be wrong, which is the loosely-reserved claim the same record forbids.

Nothing depends on this item, so nothing is stranded by ending it. `work list` may confirm that against the board rather than take this sentence's word for it.

items.title: a baseline entry cannot say how much it accepted
items.why: OD-GATE-030 v2 decides that an adopted baseline records the maximum occurrence population accepted for its rule and subject scope, and that a later run may tolerate no more than that quantity. Nothing can carry that quantity yet. DeclaredDebt is rule, path and rationale; BaselineDebt is rule, subject and rationale; BaselineDebtResponse is the same three. So the decision cannot be stated by an author, cannot be held by the domain, and cannot reach a headless caller. The record names the order this follows, the same order Suppression's owner field already took: the key appears on the declared entry first, and the domain type grows a field to carry it. This item carries the quantity and enforces nothing with it, which is deliberate and is why it is separable: a run that reads the field and ignores it behaves exactly as today, so the carrier can land and be reviewed before the behavior that depends on it.
items.done_when: A declared baseline entry may name the occurrence count it accepted, and the domain type carries it as a state that names itself rather than as a bare Option a reader has to interpret: an entry naming no count is Unbounded, and one naming a count is bounded by it. A count of zero is refused at resolution with a message addressed to the author, the way DeclaredSuppression::Problem already refuses a temporary waiver with no expiry, because an entry accepting zero occurrences tolerates nothing and declining to write the entry already does that. An entry naming no count keeps exactly the meaning it was written under, which OD-GATE-030 v2 requires and which the existing tests over countless entries prove by continuing to pass unchanged. The headless twin names the quantity too, as a tagged state rather than a nullable number, so a caller reads unbounded as a word and not as an absence. Both surface snapshots are re-blessed and committed. The predicate is the two crates' own lib tests. It deliberately does not reach tests/contract/tests/public_surface.rs, whose obligation is the whole workspace's surface and which goes red on any peer's unblessed snapshot, nor this crate's integration seam, nor the host CLI, which names no baseline quantity in this item.

items.title: A territory that execution proves insufficient costs the whole item
items.why:
A reservation is authored before the change is attempted, so it is a prediction, and a prediction is sometimes wrong by one file. The ledger has no proportionate answer to that. Territory is immutable under claim and there is no widen verb, so the only route is abandon, decline and re-author -- and declining an item strands every dependent, each of which must itself be declined and re-authored against the replacement identifier.

Measured 2026-09-14 on one item, which was declined three times for exactly this. The first escape was the crate root: the helper the item's own rule had to call sat in a private module, so nothing outside the crate could name it, and the file carrying the module declaration was not reserved. The second was two fixtures whose bodies the change made vacuous -- leaving them would have left two tests passing for a reason that was no longer the one they claimed, and editing them was outside the reservation. Neither was reachable by grepping what the predicate reads. Both appeared only when the change was run. The third attempt reserved what an actual build and test run named, and held.

The cost was not the editing. It was five ledger transitions and a dependent re-authored twice, for work whose only defect was that one file it legitimately had to touch could not be predicted before the attempt.

The immutability is not the defect and must survive. A holder who could rewrite their own reservation could take a path a peer holds, and the exclusion check would never be asked. What is wrong is that the refusal is total rather than proportionate: the ledger answers a request to add one path by ending the item.

There is a second loss, and it is the one that compounds. The board cannot say how often a predicted cone escapes its reservation. A decline stores a holder, a timestamp and free prose, so the number is not derivable and a stated one would be a figure nobody could check. The task skill now instructs an author to compare the actual cone against the reservation before finishing; nothing anywhere records the answer. A widening that is refused into a decline is evidence destroyed at the moment it is produced.

The territory below is large because a field added to an item breaks every site that constructs one. Measured rather than estimated: 29 files across five crates construct a LedgerItem, two further matches in nomos-spec-ingest are an unrelated Filler.displaced and are excluded, and a compile lists the real set in one pass. Reserving the whole chain up front is deliberate -- this is the item whose subject is what an under-reservation costs, and discovering its own escape mid-claim would cost exactly what it exists to describe.

The reservation was measured a second time before any editing, against the conventions this workspace actually holds rather than against the item's own subject matter, and it was short by eight files. Recorded here because this item is about that measurement and a silent correction would be the wrong shape.

Two are the type. A new public type in a substrate crate needs a file of its own -- ef1c93f gave every substrate type one, and it is the commit whose file splits the decline of P11-AMEND-TERRITORY measured -- and it needs the module root that declares it. That root is crates/substrate/nomos-ledger/src/holder.rs, reached as the item module through a #[path] attribute rather than being named item.rs, so grepping for the module's name finds the directory and not the file that declares it. This is the same escape as the crate-root re-export that declined the first predecessor of this item, one level down and wearing a different name.

Six are the verb. A ledger verb is a WorkCommand variant, the dispatch in run.rs matches that enum with no catch-all arm, the outcome is a second enum beside it, and both enums are public surface with a snapshot. The two hosts differ here and the difference is the whole reason the count is six and not nine: nomos-api reads each outcome through a refutable let rather than an exhaustive match, so a new variant does not break it and no headless response is owed, while nomos-cli renders through a match that must gain an arm.

Both were found by reading, which is worth stating precisely because it is not a counterexample to the rule this item exists to repair. Neither was predictable when the item was first authored; both were predictable once the work had been looked at closely enough to know which conventions it would meet. That is the same information execution would have produced, obtained earlier and more cheaply, and it does not make the reservation authoritative -- a build has still not been run.
items.done_when:
A holder can widen the territory of an item they hold, and can only widen it. The verb is authored beside the others rather than as a special case of add, because add allocates and this does not.

# One mutation, not a check followed by a write

Load, holder check, enlarged territory, exclusion against every other live claim, history append, territory replacement, whole-ledger validation and the write are one mutation inside one lock acquisition, through the same guarded path the fourth board-changing verb uses. OD-LEDGER-015 is the record of what the other three cost by deciding outside the lock, and this is the fifth.

Calling the same exclusion the claim called is necessary and is not the invariant. Two simultaneous widenings can each observe a board on which their own new paths are free and jointly create the overlap the check exists to prevent, and no amount of sharing the function fixes that. Atomicity is the property, and it owns a falsifier: a test in which a second widening interleaved between the first one's read and its write is refused rather than applied.

The exclusion is re-run against the board as it is at widen time, never inherited from the claim. Independence was established when the claim was granted and the board has moved since.

# What is refused, each with its own test

- A widening whose new paths overlap a live claim, through the exclusion check a claim goes through -- called and not copied, so a widening cannot come to a different answer about contention than a claim would. This is the refusal the whole verb has to earn.
- A widening by anybody who is not the current holder.
- A widening of an item that is not claimed, or that is done, or that is declined.
- A widening by a holder whose lease has run out. This is the boundary case and it is not covered by the holder check: the name still matches and the claim is still on the item. store/refusal.rs already records that a lapsed claim stops excluding, so another item may since have been claimed over exactly the files this one reserves -- a lapsed holder enlarging a reservation that currently excludes nobody is that hazard reached through a new verb. The authorization test is therefore liveness, not name equality: Has_Active_Claim is already false once the lease has gone, and a name match on a dead lease must authorize nothing. A lapsed holder is told to take the item over first.
- A narrowing. Widen takes paths to add; it does not take a replacement territory. Dropping a path drops the done_when clause that path carried, which this repository has already recorded as a rule, and a verb accepting a whole new territory would put narrowing one typo away.

# The widening is recorded, not merged silently

Which paths were added, by which holder, at what moment, kept on the item the way a displaced claim is kept. That record is the measurement the board cannot make today: it is what lets an escape be counted without anybody reading a decline's prose, and it is the only evidence that would ever justify computing a dependency cone rather than predicting one. A widening that leaves the territory correct and the history empty does not satisfy this item.

# Compatibility, stated as two directions with two mechanisms

The schema moves to 6 and every item on the board carries the new field after the same commit. The record states both directions separately and names the mechanism for each, because attributing either to the other is how a guard comes to rest on something that does not hold it.

An older build meeting schema 6 is refused by deny_unknown_fields on LedgerItem, which is mechanical and applies to any new field. The version probe in store/document.rs is consulted after that refusal and never to decide whether to refuse; its whole job is to make the operator read Unrecognized rather than Malformed. The protection is therefore not the version bump, and OD-LEDGER-008 is why that matters: a field once arrived without the number moving, so a guard resting on the bump would report clean on the next instance of the defect it was built for. A forgotten bump costs a sentence and cannot cost a field.

A newer build meeting schema 5 is refused by the absent serde default on the missing key. That is what the absent default is for, and it is the opposite direction: it makes every historical item be migrated rather than silently read as one that was never widened. kind and origin carry none for the same reason.

The bump itself is still not discretionary -- a test counts the keys on a serialized item -- but the done_when does not claim it protects anything.

work/ledger.json is deliberately not reserved: reserving the board would block every other claim, and the migration is an obligation stated here rather than an exclusion.

# The rest of the surface

show reports every widening with its paths and its holder. list does not gain a column, because list is one line per item and this is prose.

README.md carries the verb in the reference the contract routes to, and .claude/skills/nomos-task/SKILL.md loses the sentence saying no widen verb exists, which this item makes false. The skill keeps the rest of that paragraph unchanged: the comparison before finishing is still required, and a cheaper repair is not a reason to reserve carelessly.

OD-LEDGER-039 records the decision, since every previous field on an item came with one and the semantic is the load-bearing part: territory is a concurrency claim that its holder may enlarge, under the same exclusion the claim was granted under, while the claim is still live, and the enlargement is durable history.

The record states two things the verb is not, because each is a way it could decay into something worse than the gap it closes.

It is not cone inference. Nothing here infers, validates or proposes a dependency cone, and an author still measures. The recorded widenings are the only evidence that would ever justify changing that, and there are none yet.

It is not a licence to reserve loosely. A claim is the author's best pre-work reservation and a widening is an evidence-backed repair for the case where execution disproves that prediction. It is not the first move of an incremental discovery of territory, and neither the record nor the verb's own help text may read as an invitation to treat it as one. The distinction is what keeps the history worth having: a board on which widening is routine has lost the measurement rather than gained a convenience, because an escape rate says nothing unless the reservations it is measured against were genuine attempts to get the territory right.

Not closed by a verb that mutates territory without recording the mutation, by one that accepts a replacement territory, by one that decides outside the lock, or by one that authorizes a holder whose lease has gone.

items.title: a declared tolerance can name only a finding whose subject is its file
items.why: DeclaredSuppression and DeclaredDebt both compute their subject with Subject_Of_Path, so a declared nomos-gate.json can address a finding only where the file itself is the subject. A rule that subjects its findings to a qualified name cannot be suppressed or baselined from the file at all, and the author gets no error and no effect, because an entry that matches nothing is reported as unmatched rather than refused. Measured 2026-09-14: fourteen rule construction sites outside test code build their subject from a qualified name, spanning every rule in the naming family plus mirror, guarantee-exerciser and function-shape. The naming family is exactly what a repository adopting on existing code reaches for first, so the configuration language is weakest at the point adoption depends on it. gate_policy_file.rs's own module doc already states this limit and names the shape of an answer -- sub-item findings carrying an addressable name a person can write -- and says explicitly that it belongs to whichever item takes it up. This is that item. It is an addressing-model question and not a baseline-capacity one: OD-GATE-030 v2 bounds how much a tolerance may cover and changes nothing about which findings a tolerance can name, and this gap applies to suppression identically.
items.done_when: A record decides how a declared tolerance addresses a finding whose subject is not its file, or decides that it does not yet and says exactly what would settle it. It states the measured population rather than the qualitative limit the module doc already carries, and it distinguishes the two candidate answers the measurement exposes: giving such findings an addressable name a person can write, which is a change to Finding, against letting a declared entry name a subject some other way, which the module doc already refuses because a file naming a raw SubjectId digest is the unauthorable identity that module exists to compute rather than accept. It records that the gap is shared by suppression and baseline, so a later reader does not fix one and believe the other followed. It does not decide baseline capacity, which OD-GATE-030 owns. The projections are re-rendered from a worktree holding exactly the records this commit publishes, per OD-GATE-005.

items.title: a run tolerates more debt than its baseline accepted
items.why: P109-B gave a baseline entry a quantity and nothing reads it. Partitioned_Findings still tolerates a finding whenever any entry matches its rule and subject, one finding at a time, so a scope that accepted one occurrence tolerates five. Measured against the built binary on 2026-09-14: adopt one entry, fix the violation it named, write five new ones at the same subject, and the run reports five baselined and exits 0. OD-GATE-030 v2 decides that a later run may tolerate no more than the quantity adopted and that an observed population above it is a baseline expansion the baseline must not hide. The decision it also makes, and the one that shapes this item more than the bound does, is that no occurrence inside an exceeded population may be attributed: where five are observed and one was accepted, the run knows the population is over by four and does not know which four, so sorting by any stable key and calling the first one historical would manufacture the evidence the record says nobody has, and would let a reformatting commit change which occurrences a repository is said to have adopted.
items.done_when: A run groups the findings a baseline entry matched by rule and subject, compares each group's observed count against what that entry accepted, and reports the comparison as an aggregate carrying the rule, the subject, what was allowed and what was observed. A group within its allowance is tolerated exactly as today. A group above it is not tolerated at all: the whole affected population moves to a state of its own rather than being split into some findings called old and others called new, and the run fails because the group exceeds its ceiling. An entry that named no count tolerates its group whatever the count, since OD-GATE-030 v2 keeps that meaning, and the aggregate still reports the population as unbounded so a reader can see what was not bounded. Compare does not lose the new state: Population_Of walks exactly the buckets GateFindings holds, so a finding in a bucket it does not walk reads as removed between two runs, which is the false story this whole line of work exists to stop -- the disposition vocabulary gains the state and compare walks it. The CLI says what a person needs: how many occurrences are present, how many were accepted, by how much the debt exceeds the baseline, and that the historical identity of the individual occurrences is not known. The headless twin carries the aggregate as its own tagged response rather than as prose. Both surface snapshots are re-blessed. The predicate is the three packages' own lib and bin test targets. It deliberately does not reach tests/contract/tests/public_surface.rs, which goes red on any peer's unblessed snapshot, nor the nomos-cli integration tests that judge this repository's own tree, which declares no nomos-gate.json and therefore has no baseline population to report either before or after this change.

items.title: the baseline report names a digest where its author wrote a path
items.why: P109-C made the exceeded-baseline report the headline output of the whole adoption feature, and it names the scope by its SubjectId.
