A subject is deliberately content-addressed and a declared entry is deliberately authored by path, and the mapping between them runs one way only, so the reader of the message cannot get back to what they wrote. This is display material and OD-ANALYSIS-011 already separates that from identity: the finding's own subject_name is not the answer either, because for a file-subjected rule it is a file and line, which names one occurrence rather than the scope the count is about.

items.title: The security rules decide what is test material from a nine-clause hardcoded path convention, so a repository that files fixtures elsewhere gets false credential findings
items.why:
Auditing all 42 SourceText rules for repository-specific criteria found exactly one family. Is_Test_Or_Fixture_Source in security_text.rs matches tests/, /tests/, /test/, /testdata/, /fixtures/, /examples/, _test.rs, _tests.rs and _test.go, and the three security rules all exempt a source on that basis; rust_text.rs carries the same notion independently in its unwrap-outside-tests-and-examples wording. Some clauses are toolchain-fixed and portable: Cargo owns tests/ and examples/, Go owns _test.go. testdata and fixtures are neither, they are a project convention. A repository filing its fixtures under resources or spec or samples is judged as if a fixture credential were a real one, and an exemption that is too narrow produces false positives rather than misses, which is the damaging direction for a security rule.

This is the successor to P100-WHAT-COUNTS-AS-TEST-MATERIAL-IS-A-HARDCODED-PATH-CONVENTION-INSIDE-THE-SECURITY-RULES-7, which carried this why, done_when and dependency over a territory of two files. That item was declined on 2026-09-15 with the measurement below. Nothing had executed; the cone was measured before claiming, which is what P100-WHAT-COUNTS-AS-TEST-MATERIAL-IS-A-HARDCODED-PATH-CONVENTION-INSIDE-THE-SECURITY-RULES-6's own decline directed and what its text asked for. The measurement is the reason this item exists rather than a widened predecessor. OD-LEDGER-039 says a widening is an evidence-backed repair for the case where execution disproves a prediction and is not the first move of an incremental discovery of territory, and widening here would have been exactly the discovery that record refuses, over a reservation short by an order of magnitude rather than by a file.

The measurement, in two halves.

What kind of fact this is. OD-RULES-029 decides it: an OD-RULES-011 family is a repository's policy parameters, parameterizing a judgment the rule keeps making, and this is one -- the rule keeps asking whether a file is test material and the repository answers where its specimens live. The same record draws the contrast this item must respect: a declared architecture is a description the rule judges against and is therefore deliberately not a family, so this declaration does not join nomos-architecture.json.

Where it travels. OD-HOST-009 decides that: not standards.json, because code-standards decodes that file with unknown fields disallowed and a key nomos owns outright would make another tool fail to read a file it has always read, but a dedicated, language-neutral file at the repository root, the convention nomos-gate.json and nomos-architecture.json already set. So the original done_when's second clause is discharged by a record rather than by the item it named, and no second declaration path is invented: nomos-test-material.json at the root, following that convention.

Together those make the change a sixth OD-RULES-011 family. The precedent is P100-THE-ARCHITECTURE-A-RULE-JUDGES-IS-COMPILED-INTO-THE-RULE-CRATE-INSTEAD-OF-DECLARED-BY-THE-REPOSITORY-8, the structurally identical item, which shipped at 52 paths across seven crates with a 3600-second predicate: a capability contract crate, a provider module in nomos-repo-policy (a module and not a crate, because OD-PACKAGE-015 collapsed six provider crates into one), a materializer in nomos-check-orchestration, a rule that reads the fact through nomos_analysis::FactReader, the workspace member and dependency entries, the contract tests' own enumerations, five surface snapshots, and a repository declaring locations no clause of the nine already names.

The territory below is a prediction and not a measurement of the change, unlike the seven-crate predicate, which is copied from the precedent. Two clauses are why it is nonetheless broad: the fifth clause moves rust_text.rs, which changes the signature of a check whose cone follows the caller chain, and the fourth requires a repository to declare its locations, which means a carrier file and a fixture that carries one. Whoever claims this should measure the cone before editing, as the predecessor's decline directed, and expect to widen if execution disproves this one.

The original title said eight clauses while the why and the done_when both said nine. Nine is correct, and this item says so.
items.done_when: What counts as test material reaches the three security checks in security_text.rs as a declared criterion rather than a path list compiled into that file, composed from the toolchain-fixed clauses plus whatever the repository declares, so that stable Cargo and Go semantics do not become configuration. It uses the repository-root carrier OD-HOST-009 establishes -- a dedicated, language-neutral nomos-<concern>.json file at the repository root, the way nomos-gate.json and nomos-architecture.json already reach their readers -- rather than inventing a second one, and it reaches the rules as an OD-RULES-011 capability fact read through nomos_analysis::FactReader the way the five existing policy families do. A repository declaring nothing keeps today behaviour, clause for clause. A repository declaring its own fixture locations has them exempted, proved against a fixture whose test material sits under none of the nine current clauses. rust_text.rs stops carrying a second independent notion of the same thing.

items.title: a finding carries the address its rule declares
items.why: OD-GATE-032 decided a declared tolerance addresses its finding through a tagged selector with exactly one addressing mode, and that a rule which subjects its findings to something inside the file must declare an address a person can write rather than assemble a composite privately. Nothing implements that, and this is the prerequisite half: the policy side cannot resolve a name to an identity until the finding carries one. Sixteen production sites build the composite privately as SubjectId::From_Digest(Content_Digest(qualified.as_bytes())), where qualified is assembled at the site with no shared constructor and no normalization -- thirteen under checks/naming across eleven files, and three outside it in checks/function_shape.rs, checks/guarantee_exerciser.rs and checks/mirror/verdict.rs. subject_name holds the bare member name rather than the composite, so nothing Finding carries today can address one of these findings, and matching a bare display name would broaden across every symbol that shares it rather than addressing one. Measured this session: Finding is not non_exhaustive, implements no Default, and carries no field that could hold an address, so adding one edits every construction site in the workspace -- 132 in production across 80 files, 49 of them in nomos-rules alone. OD-ANALYSIS-011 permits exactly three subject derivations and this family is a fourth it does not name; tests/contract/tests/boundaries/findings.rs enforces the three, and its fixture is two fact-free rules so it cannot produce the fourth and passes over the family it exists to guard.
items.done_when: Finding carries the address its rule declares, as display and authoring material that never participates in subject identity or in matching, and the sixteen sites that assemble a qualified-name composite publish that address instead of keeping it private. Every subject value in the workspace is byte-identical to what it was before this item: the change is that the string a person would have to write is now on the finding rather than private to the rule that built it. OD-ANALYSIS-011 is amended to name the fourth derivation, and tests/contract/tests/boundaries/findings.rs permits it with its fixture extended to actually produce a finding of that shape, because a guard whose fixture cannot exercise the shape it exists for has already been written once in this repository and checks nothing. The naming family is the family that must be addressable, since it is what a repository adopting on existing code reaches for first.

items.title: a policy digest ignores the allowance that decides the judgment
items.why: Policy_Digest builds the digest a run records of the policy it judged under, and gate_compare.rs compares two runs by it: if before.policy equals after.policy the two sides were judged under the same policy and a difference is attributed to the repository. For each baseline entry the digest hashes the rule, the subject and the rationale, and it does not hash the entry allowance. Two policies differing only in accepted_occurrence_count therefore digest alike, and a comparison reads them as one policy -- so a repository that raised or lowered a tolerance between two runs gets a report saying the source changed, which is the failure class OD-GATE-031 exists to prevent. The evidence that this is an omission rather than a decision is the shape of what the digest does include: rationale is pure display material that no judgment consults, and it is hashed, while the allowance decides whether a finding is tolerated or exceeds the baseline and is not. The absence of declared_path from the same digest is correct and is not this defect -- it is display material too, and hashing it would make two spellings of one entry digest differently. The allowance is not display material; P109-C added it so a tolerance could say how much it accepted, and it is exactly what two such policies can differ by.
items.done_when: Two effective policies differing only in a baseline entry allowance digest differently, and a test asserts it on the digest rather than on the policy, because the omission is invisible in either policy and only appears in the comparison. Nothing about which findings a run tolerates changes, and the digest stays order-sensitive in authoring order as it is today: this is a change to what the identity is computed over and not to what a run does. A comparison over two runs whose only difference is the allowance reports the policy difference rather than attributing it to the repository.

items.title: Eight-phase spec-core: presumption reasons that name the fixture, not the call
items.why: spec-core landed at a6b1791f with its predicate green, and one class of reason in it is untrue at its site. In crates/spec/nomos-spec-bundle/src/import/reference.rs, 23 In_Transaction calls carry the reason 'the Fixture holds the row this lookup names'. The test Test_Optional_Suite_Uid_Should_Return_None_When_No_Suite_Is_Given calls In_Transaction with None and asserts the result is None on the very next line, so the row being absent is the outcome the test wants and the fixture holding it is not what makes the call succeed. The rule asks what would have to change for this to become a bug; the change the reason names would not. check-presumption reads only the string, so neither the rule nor the predicate can see this, and a green predicate is the only evidence either one offers.
items.done_when: Every reason attached to an unchecked extraction in this item's territory names what would make that call fail, rather than the fixture's contents or the test's assertion. The spec-core eight-phase predicate still exits zero; cargo test -p nomos-spec-bundle -p nomos-spec-project --no-fail-fast is green; nothing is added to suppressions.json and no in-code allow marker is added. The judgment is reported as prose: for each changed reason, the call it sits on and what would have to change for it to become a bug.
